BRIDGE-019.description: Build the actual relay server that sits between relay-endpoint.ts (fspec-side client) and the mobile app (fspec-mobile client). This is the missing middle piece — a WebSocket server that accepts connections from both sides, authenticates them via channel_id + api_key, and routes messages bidirectionally. Without this, npm run bridge:relay fails because relay-endpoint.ts is a client that expects to connect TO a server. The fake_relay_server.dart in fspec-mobile only returns hardcoded mock data and cannot route real fspec output to the mobile app. This server must implement the full relay protocol: auth handshake, channel-based routing, all 5 session-scoped message types (input, sessionControl, command, commandResponse, chunk), plus connected/ping/pong. rules.text: Relay server is a standalone TypeScript WebSocket server in bridge/relay-server.ts, started via npm run bridge:server
Server listens on a configurable port (default 8765) and accepts WebSocket connections at any path (including /v1/ws for mobile app compatibility)
Auth handshake: client sends {type:'auth', data:{channel_id, api_key}} → server validates and responds with {type:'authSuccess', data:{instances:[...]}} or {type:'authError', data:{code, message}}
Channel-based routing: clients on the same channel_id form a channel group. Messages from one client are forwarded to all OTHER clients in the same channel (not echoed back to sender)
Server is a pure message router — it does NOT inspect, transform, or interpret message payloads. It forwards the raw JSON to other clients in the channel.
All 5 session-scoped message types pass through: input, sessionControl, command, commandResponse, chunk — plus connected, ping/pong
Server responds to ping with pong directly (heartbeat is server-side, not forwarded to other clients)
When relay-endpoint sends a 'connected' message (indicating a new codelet session), server broadcasts it to all other clients in the channel so mobile app discovers available sessions
On authSuccess, server sends the current list of known instances/sessions for that channel so newly connecting clients get immediate state
Configuration via env vars: RELAY_SERVER_PORT (default 8765), RELAY_SERVER_API_KEY (optional — if set, clients must provide matching api_key; if unset, any api_key accepted)
Unauthenticated clients that send non-auth messages receive an error and are disconnected
Server logs client connections, disconnections, auth events, and message routing to console with [relay-server] prefix

When a client disconnects, it is removed from its channel. If it was the relay-endpoint (the one that sent 'connected' messages), the server does NOT notify remaining clients — the mobile app handles stale sessions via its own heartbeat/reconnect logic

BUG-047.description:
# Bug Report: BUG-047

## Type Mismatches in record-metric and record-tokens Commands

**Discovered during**: LOCK-002 file locking refactoring
**Date**: 2025-10-28
**Reporter**: Claude (AI Assistant)

---

## Summary

Two command files have type mismatches between their function signatures and how they're called in command registration:
- `src/commands/record-metric.ts`
- `src/commands/record-tokens.ts`

These bugs existed **before** the LOCK-002 refactoring work began.

---

## Detailed Findings

### File 1: `src/commands/record-metric.ts`

**Function Signature** (lines 19-23):
```typescript
export async function recordMetric(options: {
  workUnitId: string;
  tokens: number;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; totalTokens?: number }>
```

**Command Registration Call** (lines 66-70):
```typescript
await recordMetric({
  metric,                    // ❌ Not in function signature
  value: parseFloat(value),  // ❌ Not in function signature
  unit: options.unit,        // ❌ Not in function signature
});
```

**Command Arguments** (lines 60-62):
```typescript
.argument('<metric>', 'Metric name')
.argument('<value>', 'Metric value')
.option('--unit <unit>', 'Unit of measurement')
```

**Problem**: The function expects `{ workUnitId, tokens, cwd }` but is called with `{ metric, value, unit }`. These are completely different parameter sets.

---

### File 2: `src/commands/record-tokens.ts`

**Function Signature** (lines 19-23):
```typescript
export async function recordTokens(options: {
  workUnitId: string;
  tokens: number;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; totalTokens?: number }>
```

**Command Registration Call** (lines 76-79):
```typescript
await recordTokens({
  workUnitId,
  tokens: parseInt(tokens, 10),
  operation: options.operation,  // ❌ Not in function signature
});
```

**Command Option** (lines 65-68):
```typescript
.option(
  '--operation <operation>',
  'Operation type (e.g., specification, implementation)'
)
```

**Problem**: The function doesn't accept an `operation` parameter but the command tries to pass it anyway.

---

## Impact Analysis

### Current State
- TypeScript compilation may be passing due to the `[key: string]: unknown` index signature in the options interface
- Commands may be silently failing or ignoring parameters
- Tests may not be covering these code paths

### Expected Behavior
The function signatures should match the command registration calls exactly.

### Potential Fixes

#### Option A: Update Function Signatures (Recommended)
Match the functions to what the commands actually need:

**record-metric.ts:**
```typescript
export async function recordMetric(options: {
  metric: string;
  value: number;
  unit?: string;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean }>
```

**record-tokens.ts:**
```typescript
export async function recordTokens(options: {
  workUnitId: string;
  tokens: number;
  operation?: string;
  cwd?: string;
}): Promise<{ success: boolean; totalTokens?: number }>
```

#### Option B: Update Command Registration
Change how commands call the functions to match existing signatures (may require rethinking command purpose).

---

## Discovery Context

These bugs were discovered during LOCK-002 refactoring when:
1. Systematically refactoring command files to use `fileManager.transaction()`
2. Applied standard pattern to these files
3. Ran full test suite: **103 tests failed**
4. Investigated failures and found pre-existing type mismatches
5. Reverted changes to these files to isolate the issue

**Git References:**
- Last good commit before discovery: `efee27c`
- Files were at HEAD~1 when bug discovered

---

## Reproduction Steps

1. Review `src/commands/record-metric.ts` lines 19-23 and 66-70
2. Review `src/commands/record-tokens.ts` lines 19-23 and 76-79
3. Note the parameter mismatch between function signatures and calls
4. Run: `npm run build` - TypeScript may pass due to index signature
5. Run: `npm test` - Tests may fail or pass if not covering these paths

---

## Recommended Actions

1. **Investigate Intent**: Determine what these commands are supposed to do
   - Are they for recording metrics OR token usage?
   - Should they operate on work units?

2. **Fix Type Signatures**: Align function signatures with command usage

3. **Add Tests**: Ensure test coverage for these commands

4. **Update Documentation**: Clarify command purpose and usage

5. **Continue LOCK-002**: These files can be refactored after types are fixed

---

## Notes

- These bugs existed **before LOCK-002 refactoring**
- Type system may not catch due to index signature: `[key: string]: unknown`
- May need to check if similar patterns exist in other command files
- Should verify if commands are actually used in production

---

## Related Work Units

- **LOCK-002**: File locking refactoring (blocked by this bug for these 2 files)

Visual Basic: ' @step But the error is logged → should extract 'But the error is logged'

architectureNotes.text: Implementation uses the `diffy` crate for three-way merge (diffy::merge). Add `diffy = "1"` to codelet/git/Cargo.toml. The `similar` crate already present only supports two-way diff — not three-way merge with conflict markers.

New function `write_conflict_markers()` in session_result.rs: takes base/session/main content for each conflicting file, runs diffy::merge(), writes result to worktree file. Called BEFORE returning ConflictError in apply_session_changes().

detect_conflicts() currently compares raw bytes. For the three-way merge, we need to also consider: (1) identical changes = not a real conflict, (2) non-overlapping changes in same file = auto-merge, no conflict. diffy handles this automatically when its merge result has no conflicts.

The TypeScript layer (conflictLlmContext.ts, mergeWorktreeHandler.ts) needs NO changes. The fix is entirely in the Rust layer — write markers into worktree files so that the existing 'read file + resolve markers' instruction to the LLM actually works.

BUG-098.description:
When /merge-worktree detects conflicts, the Rust code in apply_session_changes() (session_result.rs) returns Err(GitError::ConflictError) immediately without writing conflict markers into the worktree files. The TypeScript handler then tells the LLM to 'read each conflicting file, resolve the git conflict markers (<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>)' — but the markers don't exist in the files. The LLM reads the file, finds no markers, gets confused, and enters a loop.

The root cause is that detect_conflicts() does a pure divergence check (did both session and main change the same file since base?) and returns file names only. No three-way merge is performed, so no conflict markers are ever materialized in the worktree.

Reproduced in session 9f4fec89 on 2026-02-26: user edited README.md ('The' → 'Da'), main had also diverged on README.md, /merge-worktree fired the conflict path, LLM read the worktree file — no markers found.

examples.text: Session edits line 7 of README.md ('The' → 'Da'), main also changed line 7 ('The Spec-Driven' → 'The Spec-Driven (v2.0)') → worktree README.md gets <<<<<<< session / Da Spec-Driven / ======= / The Spec-Driven (v2.0) / >>>>>>> main
Session edits src/app.ts (lines 10-15), main edits src/app.ts (lines 40-50, no overlap) → three-way merge succeeds cleanly, no conflict markers needed, file NOT in conflict list
Session adds new file utils.ts, main also adds utils.ts with different content → conflict markers written with empty base (two-way diff)
Session modifies logo.png (binary), main also modifies logo.png → binary file listed as conflicting but NO conflict markers written (binary can't be merged), error message notes binary conflicts
Session and main both change line 7 of README.md identically ('The' → 'Da') → detect_conflicts() should NOT report this as a conflict (both made same change)
After conflict markers are written, LLM reads the file, sees <<<<<<< markers, resolves them, saves, runs /merge-worktree again → second merge succeeds

rules.text: When apply_session_changes() detects conflicting files, it must perform a three-way merge and write standard git conflict markers into the worktree files BEFORE returning ConflictError
Conflict markers must follow standard git format: <<<<<<< session (your changes) / ======= / >>>>>>> main
Binary files must be skipped during three-way merge — no conflict markers written for binary content
For files added in both session and main with different content, write conflict markers with empty base (two-way conflict)
The worktree files must be overwritten with the merged content containing conflict markers — the LLM reads from the worktree path
Files where both session and main made identical changes (no actual conflict) should NOT get conflict markers
The ConflictError must still be returned after writing markers — the error signals the TypeScript handler to show conflict guidance

BUG-098.title: Merge conflict markers never written to worktree files — LLM told to resolve markers that don't exist

userStory.action: merge worktree changes when conflicts exist
userStory.benefit: see actual conflict markers in the files so I can resolve them

architectureNotes.text: The root cause is that fspec has no equivalent of `git add` to mark a conflict as resolved. Real git uses the index (staging area) — once you `git add` a conflicted file, git stops flagging it. fspec's merge system is stateless: every /merge-worktree call re-detects conflicts from scratch by comparing worktree vs base vs main. The fix adds statefulness via .fspec-pending-conflicts.

Implementation: New function check_pending_conflicts(worktree_path) in session_result.rs. Reads .fspec-pending-conflicts (JSON array of file paths). For each file, checks if worktree file content contains '<<<<<<< '. Returns (resolved: Vec<String>, still_pending: Vec<String>). Called at the TOP of apply_session_changes(), BEFORE detect_conflicts().

Flow change in apply_session_changes(): (1) Check .fspec-pending-conflicts → if exists, partition into resolved/pending. (2) If any still_pending → return ConflictError with just those files (no marker regeneration). (3) If all resolved → delete state file, exclude resolved files from detect_conflicts (they've been user-accepted), merge remaining changes normally, copy resolved worktree content directly to main.

The BUG-098 test 'test_re_merge_after_resolution_succeeds' (three_way_merge.rs:474) tests three_way_merge_text() directly with session_resolved == main — this tests the MERGE function in isolation, but the actual bug is one layer UP in apply_session_changes() where detect_conflicts() fires BEFORE the merge function is even called. New integration tests must test the full apply_session_changes() flow.

tree_utils.rs collect_worktree_files() must skip .fspec-pending-conflicts (add to is_git_or_fspec_dir or add a filename-based filter). Also add it to .gitignore pattern if using the excludes stack approach.

BUG-099.description:
After BUG-098 fixed conflict marker writing, a second bug remains: when the LLM resolves conflict markers and runs /merge-worktree again, detect_conflicts() re-reads the worktree files (now containing the resolved content), compares session-resolved vs base and main vs base, and sees both sides still differ from base — so it declares a NEW conflict. write_conflict_markers() then overwrites the LLM's resolution with fresh conflict markers. The LLM resolves again, merges again, same thing happens — infinite loop until the user kills the session.

Root cause: detect_conflicts() compares worktree (session) content against the base commit, not against main. After the LLM resolves markers, the worktree content is the resolved version which differs from base. Main also differs from base. So both sides are 'changed' → conflict detected again. The three-way merge regenerates markers because it uses the original base, the resolved worktree (as 'session'), and main — producing new conflict markers.

Reproduced in debug session bb90f15f (2026-02-26T23:51:12): README.md conflict detected 3 times in 76 seconds before user killed session. Sequences 3→25 (first conflict+resolve), 43→64 (second conflict+resolve), 80→82 (third conflict started, user exits).

examples.text: When LLM resolves worktree README.md to match main exactly (content equal), then /merge-worktree re-runs → detect_conflicts() sees worktree==main → NOT a conflict → apply_session_changes copies resolved content → merge succeeds → session cleaned up

When LLM resolves worktree README.md to a THIRD value (neither session nor main original), then /merge-worktree re-runs → detect_conflicts() sees worktree≠main AND worktree≠base → still a conflict → three-way merge runs with resolved-content as 'session' → if resolved doesn't overlap with main's changes, auto-merges cleanly; if it overlaps, new conflict markers appear (this is correct behavior — user made a bad resolution)

Exact reproduction from debug session bb90f15f: base='The', session→'Ma', main→'Those'. First merge writes markers. LLM resolves by keeping 'Ma' (session's choice). Second merge: worktree='Ma' ≠ base ✓, main='Those' ≠ base ✓ → CONFLICT AGAIN. three_way_merge(base='The', session='Ma', main='Those') → overlapping change → NEW markers written, overwriting LLM's work. Same resolution. Same conflict. Loop 3x in 76s before user kills session.

First merge of README.md: no .fspec-pending-conflicts exists → detect_conflicts finds divergence → write_conflict_markers writes markers AND creates .fspec-pending-conflicts with ['README.md'] → ConflictError returned

Re-merge after LLM resolves README.md (removes markers, keeps 'Ma'): .fspec-pending-conflicts exists listing README.md → check worktree: no <<<<<<< found → README.md is RESOLVED → skip three-way merge → use worktree content as final → apply to main → merge succeeds → NO LOOP

Re-merge with markers still in file: .fspec-pending-conflicts lists README.md → check worktree: <<<<<<< found → NOT resolved yet → return ConflictError listing README.md → LLM told 'still has markers' → no overwrite, no re-generation of markers

Multi-file conflict with partial resolution: .fspec-pending-conflicts lists [README.md, config.yml]. LLM resolves README.md (markers removed) but not config.yml (markers remain). Re-merge: README.md → resolved, config.yml → still pending → ConflictError lists only config.yml

Re-merge with unresolved markers produces DOUBLE-NESTED corruption: worktree has '<<<<<<< session
<<<<<<< session
session-v
=======
main-v
>>>>>>> main
=======
main-v
>>>>>>> main' — because detect_conflicts feeds marker-containing content as 'session' to three_way_merge, which then wraps the markers in NEW markers. This makes the file unresolvable.

rules.text: When the LLM resolves conflict markers and /merge-worktree is called again, apply_session_changes() must compare the worktree content against main content — if they match, skip that file (conflict resolved)
The fix must be in the Rust layer only (detect_conflicts in session_result.rs) — no TypeScript changes needed
The existing three-way merge logic in three_way_merge.rs must NOT be modified — the bug is in the caller (detect_conflicts), not the merge algorithm

The BUG-098 test 'test_re_merge_after_resolution_succeeds' is flawed — it passes session_resolved (matching main) which makes the three-way merge return Clean, but the REAL re-merge path goes through detect_conflicts() FIRST which still flags it as a conflict before the merge even runs

On re-merge (when .fspec-pending-conflicts exists), for each previously-conflicted file: if the worktree file no longer contains <<<<<<< markers → treat as resolved, use worktree content as final answer, skip three-way merge for that file

On re-merge, if a previously-conflicted file still contains <<<<<<< markers → user hasn't finished resolving → report as still conflicting (do NOT re-generate markers, just re-return ConflictError for that file)

Once all previously-conflicted files are resolved (none contain markers), delete .fspec-pending-conflicts and proceed with apply — the resolved worktree content is copied to main as the user's final answer
.fspec-pending-conflicts must be excluded from collect_worktree_files() so it doesn't get applied to main as a regular file

When write_conflict_markers() returns actual conflicts, apply_session_changes() must persist a .fspec-pending-conflicts state file (JSON with 'files' array) in the worktree listing those files — this distinguishes 'first conflict detection' from 're-merge after resolution'

On re-merge with unresolved markers, the current code produces DOUBLE-NESTED markers (markers inside markers) because detect_conflicts() feeds the marker-containing content as 'session' to three_way_merge — this corrupts the file and makes manual resolution impossible. The fix MUST prevent re-running three-way merge on files that already contain conflict markers

TOOL-017 and BUG-116 implemented the request_user_input HITL tool and Codex facade, but the session manager's HITL handler was wired using the wrong pattern (StreamChunk intercept via GlobalSessionStreamManager). The correct pattern is the PAUSE pattern — the HITL handler stores questions in session state, sets status to Paused, blocks on mpsc, and TypeScript polls the state via NAPI getter and renders inline UI in InputTransition.

3. useRustSessionState adds hitlRequest to snapshot
4. InputTransition renders inline multi-step question UI (↑/↓ options, Enter advance, Esc cancel)
5. AgentView keyboard handler captures input and calls sessionSendHitlResponse
6. Remove wrong-pattern code: HitlRequest StreamChunk, GlobalSessionStreamManager intercept, setHitlHandler/clearHitlHandler

BUG-119.description: Regression from TUI-079 (commit a764bd46). Switching globalStreamListener from updateWorkUnitsFromWatcher() to loadData() fixed data correctness but introduced severe flickering. Root causes: (1) loadData() acquires filesystem locks that collide with concurrent CLI/agent writes, producing 'Lock file is already being held' errors that flash the ErrorView, (2) zero JavaScript-side debouncing means multiple concurrent loadData() calls from watcher + IPC + explicit calls after move operations, (3) loadData() unconditionally clears error state before reading, causing board→error→board oscillation, (4) redundant explicit loadData() after moveWorkUnitUp/Down doubles lock contention with the watcher-triggered one.

User presses ] to move work unit down → work unit moves in the board, watcher fires once (debounced), no double-load or lock contention
Multiple rapid external changes to work-units.json within 200ms → single loadData() call executes after debounce, board updates once smoothly
loadData() is already running when watcher triggers another → second call is silently skipped, no lock contention
Real errors like permission denied or disk full still show the ErrorView — only lock contention is silenced

rules.text: Lock contention errors (ELOCKED / 'Lock file is already being held') must be treated as transient and must NOT set the error state or trigger an ErrorView render
globalStreamListener must debounce loadData() calls on the JavaScript side (on top of the Rust 100ms debounce) so that rapid watcher events coalesce into a single load
Concurrent loadData() calls must be prevented — if a loadData() is already in-flight, subsequent calls must be skipped (not queued)
loadData() must NOT clear the error state before attempting to read — error clearing must only happen on successful read
Explicit loadData() calls after moveWorkUnitUp/Down in BoardView must be removed — the file watcher already triggers a debounced loadData() after the write
All existing TUI-079 correctness behavior must be preserved — loadData() path, session context sync, deleted work unit detection, ordering from states arrays

architectureNotes.text: THREE STORES, THREE ACCESS PATTERNS: (1) HistoryStore (history.jsonl, 2.6MB) — used by Shift+↑/↓ and /search, loads ALL entries cross-session, small enough to keep in memory. (2) MessageStore (messages.jsonl, 1GB) — used by SessionSearch and session resume, content-addressed by UUID, needs index+seek+LRU. (3) SessionStore (4,586 files) — used by session list/resume, individual file reads are fine.

Per-session message file sharding was REJECTED because StoredMessage has no session_id field — it's content-addressed by UUID. Messages can be shared across sessions via Forked/Imported MessageSource. The correct approach is a binary index file (messages.idx) with on-demand seek() loading.

Binary index format: [magic:4][version:4][data_file_size:8][count:4][entries...] where each entry is [uuid:16 bytes][byte_offset:8 bytes][byte_length:4 bytes] = 28 bytes per entry. For 362K messages: ~10.1 MB index, loadable in ~15ms. Incremental: compare stored data_file_size with actual — if grew, scan only new bytes.

Key files to modify: (1) codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs — replace init_stores() with per-store lazy init functions. (2) codelet/napi/src/persistence/storage.rs — rewrite MessageStore to use index+seek+LRU instead of load_all(). (3) src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx — move persistenceGetHistory() to separate deferred useEffect.

BUG-122.description:
When entering AgentView, initSession() calls persistenceGetHistory() — a shell-style input recall feature (Shift+↑/↓) — which makes a synchronous NAPI call into Rust. The Rust persistence layer has two architectural problems:

1. **Monolithic init_stores()**: The first call to ANY persistence function triggers initialization of ALL FOUR singleton stores (MessageStore, SessionStore, HistoryStore, BlobStore), even though only HistoryStore is needed. This causes MessageStore to load as an unintended side effect.

2. **Eager MessageStore::load_all()**: MessageStore reads a single monolithic messages.jsonl (1.0 GB, 362K lines across 4,586 sessions) containing EVERY message ever stored, deserializes them all with serde_json, and stuffs them into a HashMap. This file grows without bound — startup cost is proportional to total historical usage.

The result: even starting a brand new thread with zero messages takes ~5s because the shell history feature inadvertently triggers a full message store load. The synchronous NAPI call blocks the JS event loop, preventing React from rendering the model name (already resolved in 28ms).

**Critical design constraint**: StoredMessage is content-addressed by UUID with NO session_id field. Messages can be shared across sessions via Forked/Imported MessageSource. Per-session file sharding is NOT viable — it would break content-addressing.

**Fix approach (three layers):**
1. Lazy per-store initialization in Rust — get_history() only inits HistoryStore
2. Binary index file (messages.idx) + on-demand seek() + LRU cache for MessageStore — keeps monolithic file, loads messages lazily
3. (Defense-in-depth) Move persistenceGetHistory() out of initSession() critical path in TypeScript

examples.text: Developer opens AgentView on a brand new session — model name appears in <100ms, not 5 seconds
Developer presses Shift+↑ immediately after session loads — shell history from ALL past sessions (for this project) is available, not just the current session
Developer uses /search command — results include matching entries from ALL sessions for this project, not limited to current session
LLM agent invokes SessionSearch tool to search across sessions — results come back without having loaded the entire 1GB messages.jsonl into memory first
Developer has used the tool for months with 4,586 sessions and 362K messages — startup time stays constant, does not degrade linearly with usage
Developer resumes an existing session with 200 messages — only those 200 messages are loaded from disk via index seek, not all 362K

rules.text: Each persistence store (MessageStore, SessionStore, HistoryStore, BlobStore) MUST initialize independently — calling get_history() must NOT trigger MessageStore or SessionStore initialization

The monolithic messages.jsonl file MUST be kept as-is — StoredMessage is content-addressed by UUID with no session_id field, and messages can be shared across sessions via Forked/Imported MessageSource

MessageStore MUST NOT load the entire messages.jsonl into memory at startup — instead build a persisted binary index (messages.idx) mapping UUID → (byte_offset, byte_length) and load messages on demand via seek()
MessageStore MUST use an LRU cache for recently accessed messages so repeated lookups (e.g. session resume, SessionSearch) are fast after first load
The binary index MUST support incremental updates — when messages.jsonl grows (append), only scan the new bytes from the last known file size, don't rebuild the entire index
persistenceGetHistory() (Shift+↑/↓ and /search) MUST be moved to a separate useEffect in AgentView.tsx so it does not block model name rendering
Shift+↑/↓ and /search both use HistoryStore (history.jsonl, 2.6MB) NOT MessageStore — they search command history across ALL sessions for the current project

SessionSearch tool (LLM agent) uses MessageStore via session_search_handler.rs with ripgrep regex matching — it loads messages per-session through SessionManifest.messages[] UUIDs, not by scanning the whole file

BUG-124.description:
When a supervisor session spawns more than one subordinate agent, Shift+Left/Right navigation fails to cycle through all sessions properly. The supervisor session gets duplicated in the navigation list (once per child), causing navigation to get stuck in an infinite loop between the supervisor and a single child, with all other children unreachable.

Root cause: build_navigation_list() in codelet/napi/src/navigation.rs:40-69 pushes the supervisor UUID once for every subordinate it finds, and get_next_target/get_prev_target use Vec::position() which always returns the first match — so duplicate occurrences are unreachable.

Fix: Replace the hierarchy-aware traversal with a flat IndexMap insertion-order walk. Discards the chain-of-command grouping in favor of a clean, simple, deterministic linear cycle through every session in spawn order.

Supervisor on the last session in spawn order presses Shift+Right and the create-session dialog appears
Supervisor on the first session in spawn order presses Shift+Left and lands back on the board

architectureNotes.text: Utility: src/utils/normalize-path.ts with normalizeFilePath() (sync) and resolveFilePath() (async, 3-phase: exact → normalized → dir scan). Wiring: (1) fspec-callback.ts applies normalizeFilePath to BOTH argv AND setFspecPositionalArgs. (2) add-attachment.ts replaces raw access() with resolveFilePath() for file existence checks. (3) attachment-server.ts replaces normalizeFilePath with resolveFilePath for file lookups after URL decoding. (4) BoardView.tsx uses encodeURI() for HTTP URLs, pathToFileURL() for file:// URLs. Integration tests must test through the real wiring — no faking by calling normalizeFilePath directly.

The fix must be in Rust (codelet/tools/src/validation.rs or a new codelet/tools/src/unicode_path.rs) — NOT in TypeScript — because Read/Write/Edit/Grep/Glob/Ls are all Rust tools that never touch the TypeScript normalize-path.ts

The normalization + directory scan logic must be applied in validate_and_resolve_path() (codelet/tools/src/facade/wrapper.rs) which is the single shared gateway for Read, Write, Edit — normalize the input path string BEFORE any canonicalize/exists checks

Rust-side architecture: (1) New module codelet/tools/src/unicode_path.rs — normalize_unicode_whitespace() replaces Unicode Zs category chars with U+0020, resolve_unicode_path() does async 3-phase: exact → normalized → parent dir scan. (2) wrapper.rs validate_and_resolve_path() calls normalize_unicode_whitespace() on input path string at line 1 before any PathBuf creation. (3) validation.rs require_file_exists() calls resolve_unicode_path() as fallback when try_exists returns false. (4) lib.rs exports the new module. AST research confirms 21 call sites for validate_and_resolve_path across read.rs, write.rs, edit.rs, grep.rs, ls.rs, glob.rs, astgrep.rs, astgrep_refactor.rs, apply_patch/mod.rs, and wrapper.rs facade methods.

BUG-130.description: macOS uses U+202F (NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE) before am/pm in screenshot filenames (e.g. 'Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 9.13.45\u202fam.png'). This character looks identical to a regular space but is 3 bytes (E2 80 AF) in UTF-8. When users or AI agents type/paste these paths with a regular space, all fs operations fail with ENOENT. The codebase has ZERO Unicode whitespace normalization. Affects: all CLI commands accepting file paths, NAPI callback entry point, attachment server, TUI attachment URLs, and coverage audit.

examples.text: macOS screenshot 'Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 9.13.45\u202fam.png' is referenced as 'Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 9.13.45 am.png' (regular space) — normalizeFilePath converts U+202F to U+0020, file is found
AI agent calls fspec add-attachment with path containing U+202F — the NAPI callback normalizes the path before Commander processes it, attachment is added successfully
File has regular spaces in name but user pastes path with U+00A0 (NO-BREAK SPACE) — resolveFilePath directory scan finds the correct file
Path with no Unicode whitespace passes through normalizeFilePath unchanged — zero overhead for normal paths
Attachment server receives URL with encoded U+202F (%E2%80%AF) — decodes and normalizes before file lookup, serves file correctly
add-attachment with file 'Screenshot\u202fam.png' on disk, called as addAttachment({filePath: 'Screenshot am.png'}) — resolveFilePath directory scan finds the U+202F file, copies it successfully

Real HTTP request to attachment server: GET /view/spec/attachments/AUTH-001/Screenshot%E2%80%AFam.png — server decodes, resolves via resolveFilePath directory scan, serves the actual file content with correct Content-Type

NAPI callback receives args {_: ['Screenshot\u202fam.png'], testFile: 'my\u00A0test.ts'} — both the argv array passed to Commander AND the positional args set via setFspecPositionalArgs contain normalized ASCII-space versions

User says 'Read /Users/rquast/Desktop/Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 9.13.45 am.png' (regular space before 'am') — Read tool normalizes U+0020 → finds file with U+202F on disk via directory scan — returns image content successfully
User says 'Edit /path/to/Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 9.13.45 am.png' with regular spaces — Edit tool resolves to actual file with U+202F via directory scan — edit succeeds

ReadTool.call() with file_path '/tmp/test/Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 9.13.45 am.png' (regular space) where file on disk is 'Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 9.13.45\u202fam.png' (U+202F) — tool returns image content successfully via directory scan in require_file_exists
EditTool.call() with file_path containing regular space, actual file on disk has U+202F — edit succeeds, old_string is found and replaced in the correct file

WriteTool.call() with file_path containing U+00A0 (NO-BREAK SPACE) — normalization in validate_and_resolve_path converts to regular space, file is created with regular-space filename (Write creates new files, so normalization at input is sufficient — no directory scan needed)

Ls tool with path '/Users/rquast/Desktop' — directory listing works regardless of whether the path string uses regular space or U+202F, because ls.rs:167 try_exists operates on the normalized path from validate_and_resolve_path
Path with no Unicode whitespace ('/tmp/normal/file.txt') passes through normalize_unicode_whitespace unchanged — zero overhead, no allocation, early return on ASCII-only input

rules.text: All Unicode whitespace characters (U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) in file paths must be normalized to ASCII space (U+0020) at input boundaries
Normalization must be applied at the NAPI callback entry point (fspec-callback.ts) to protect all commands when invoked via the Fspec tool
When exact path and normalized path both fail, a directory scan fallback must attempt to find a file whose normalized name matches (handles reverse case: user types regular space but file has U+202F)
Normalization must be idempotent — normalizeFilePath(normalizeFilePath(x)) === normalizeFilePath(x)
Path separators (/ and \) must NOT be affected by normalization
resolveFilePath() must be called by add-attachment command for file existence checks instead of raw access() — this is the primary consumer that encounters user-typed paths with Unicode whitespace

resolveFilePath() must be called by attachment server for file lookups (not just normalizeFilePath) — the server may receive a URL-decoded path that needs directory scan fallback when the on-disk filename has U+202F
NAPI callback must normalize BOTH the argv array AND the setFspecPositionalArgs array — currently setFspecPositionalArgs receives raw un-normalized Unicode
Integration tests MUST test actual wiring — NAPI callback test must invoke the real fspecCallback function (or its arg-processing logic), NOT just call normalizeFilePath() directly
Integration tests MUST test actual wiring — attachment server test must start a real HTTP server, make a request with Unicode-encoded path, and verify the file is served correctly

Integration tests MUST test actual wiring — add-attachment test must invoke addAttachment() with a path containing Unicode whitespace where the on-disk file has a different whitespace variant, and verify it succeeds
BoardView.tsx must use encodeURI() (not encodeURIComponent, which would break path separators) when constructing attachment HTTP URLs, and pathToFileURL() for file:// fallback URLs

Codelet Rust tools (Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Ls, AstGrep) must normalize Unicode whitespace in file_path arguments before any filesystem access — this is the PRIMARY entry point where AI agents and users encounter the bug, not just the fspec CLI commands

validation.rs require_file_exists() must attempt Unicode whitespace normalization + directory scan before returning 'File not found' — this is the shared validation layer used by Read, Write, Edit and other file tools

validate_and_resolve_path() in codelet/tools/src/facade/wrapper.rs is the SINGLE GATEWAY for all file tools — it must normalize Unicode whitespace (U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000 → U+0020) on the input path string BEFORE any canonicalize/exists checks

require_file_exists() in codelet/tools/src/validation.rs must perform a directory-scan fallback when try_exists returns false: scan the parent directory for an entry whose Unicode-normalized filename matches the target — this handles the reverse case where user types regular space but file has U+202F

Integration tests for Rust tools MUST invoke the real tool .call() method (e.g. ReadTool::new(Uuid::nil()).call(ReadArgs{...})) with a file on disk whose name contains U+202F, passing a path with regular ASCII space — the test must assert the tool returns content, not 'File not found'

The Rust normalization utility must be in a new module codelet/tools/src/unicode_path.rs (separate from the TypeScript normalize-path.ts) — it must export normalize_unicode_whitespace(s: &str) -> String (sync) and resolve_unicode_path(path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> (async, directory-scan fallback)

Tools that do their OWN try_exists checks AFTER validate_and_resolve_path — specifically ls.rs:167, glob.rs:127, astgrep.rs:271 — must also handle the Unicode fallback, either by using the shared resolve_unicode_path or by operating on the already-normalized path returned from validate_and_resolve_path

BUG-131.description: After upgrading from ink 6.4.0 to 6.8.0, mouse scroll wheel events no longer work in VirtualList, AgentView, UnifiedBoardLayout, and BoardView. The root cause is ink 6.8.0's new input-parser.ts which splits X10 mouse protocol sequences (ESC[M + 3 raw bytes) at the CSI final byte M, stripping the button/x/y data into separate events. Fix requires migrating from X10 mouse protocol (?1000h) to SGR extended mouse protocol (?1006h) which uses proper CSI parameter encoding that survives the parser intact.

User scrolls down in VirtualList — SGR event [<65;10;20M parsed correctly, view scrolls down
User clicks in VirtualList to start text selection — SGR event [<0;5;10M triggers disabling mouse tracking for native selection
User releases mouse button after text selection — SGR event [<0;5;10m triggers re-enabling mouse tracking
Mouse enable writes ESC[?1000h ESC[?1006h to stdout on component mount — verified by test assertion
Mouse disable writes ESC[?1006l ESC[?1000l to stdout on component unmount — reverse order
Non-mouse input (regular keypress like 'j') is not matched by SGR parser — parseSgrMouse returns null
Board view scroll in UnifiedBoardLayout — SGR scroll events parsed and forwarded to column scroll handlers

rules.text: Mouse protocol must use SGR extended format (ESC[?1006h) instead of X10 (ESC[?1000h only) because ink 6.8.0's CSI input parser splits X10 raw bytes into separate events
Mouse enable sequence must be ESC[?1000h ESC[?1006h (both tracking + SGR encoding) and disable must be ESC[?1006l ESC[?1000l (reverse order)
SGR mouse events use format ESC[<button;x;yM for press and ESC[<button;x;ym for release — after ink's ESC stripping they become [<button;x;yM/m
SGR button codes: 0=left, 1=middle, 2=right, 64=scroll-up, 65=scroll-down
All key.mouse dead code references must be removed — ink's Key type has never had a mouse property
Text selection (TUI-078) must detect button-down (terminator M with button 0-2) to disable mouse tracking and button-release (terminator m with button 0-2) to re-enable it
A shared mouseProtocol utility module must centralize all mouse protocol constants and parsing to avoid duplication across 5 components

BUG-132.description: Both DeepSearch and AgentManager handler closures capture the parent session's model (provider, model_id, context_window, max_output_tokens) ONCE at session creation time (session_manager.rs:4946-4996). When the user changes models mid-session via the TUI model selector (session_set_model / session_set_model_profile), neither handler is re-registered with the updated model. The main agent_loop dynamically reads the current model each iteration (line 4739-4751) and is NOT affected. But DeepSearch sub-agents and AgentManager-spawned subordinates silently use the old model. Additionally, the DeepSearch handler (line 4953) captures current_provider_name() without checking facade_override(), meaning MODEL-004 custom models with facade routing will dispatch DeepSearch sub-agents to the wrong provider backend. See spec/attachments/BUG-132/model-inheritance-research.md for full analysis.

BUG-133.description:
The [DEBUG] badge in src/tui/components/SessionHeader.tsx does not follow the Rust-authoritative, per-session, event-driven state replication pattern that other session-scoped badges (e.g. [ISOLATED]) use. Instead it relies on a local React useState in AgentView ORed with the Rust snapshot, which is not properly replicated via stream events to the Zustand sessionStore.

Everything in SessionHeader MUST be aware of the current session and be founded in Rust state replicated to Zustand via events. This bug will bring [DEBUG] into alignment with that architecture.

examples.text: Switching between two sessions where only session A has /debug enabled: [DEBUG] badge must appear only while session A is active, and disappear when switching to session B
Toggling /debug in session A must fire a Rust stream event that updates Zustand so the header re-renders without relying on local React state

Matching the isIsolated pattern treats the badge as per-session state mirroring the AtomicBool.

architectureNotes.text: RUST LAYER 1 - DebugCaptureManager ownership change: Currently codelet/common/src/debug_capture/mod.rs:25 has static OnceLock singleton. Refactor so DebugCaptureManager is stored on BackgroundSession (session_manager.rs:486+ struct). BackgroundSession already has pub id: Uuid (line 486) as a perfect key. Add a field like pub debug_capture: Arc<PoisonRecoveryMutex<DebugCaptureManager>> initialized in BackgroundSession::new() (line 628+). Remove the static OnceLock.

RUST LAYER 2 - Free function removal/refactoring: The convenience free functions in mod.rs must change: (a) get_debug_capture_manager() - remove or make private, callers must go through session, (b) capture_event(event_type, data) - remove, callers must have session context, (c) increment_debug_turn() - remove, callers must have session context, (d) handle_debug_command_with_dir(base_dir) - refactor to take a &BackgroundSession or &DebugCaptureManager and toggle only that session's manager. The global toggle_debug() NAPI (session_manager.rs:7512) should be removed since all debug toggles require a session context in multi-session mode.

RUST LAYER 3 - Capture call site migration (NAPI path). The NAPI call sites in codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs already have session_id and are easiest to migrate: session_update_debug_metadata(:7529), session_toggle_debug(:7568), session_compact(:7613/:7635/:7661). These already do get_session(session_id) so they can access session.debug_capture directly instead of the global singleton.

RUST LAYER 3 - Capture call site migration (CLI path). The CLI call sites use codelet CLI Session (NOT BackgroundSession). Files: repl_loop.rs (8 calls), stream_loop.rs (7+ calls), stream_handlers.rs (3 calls), recovery_compaction.rs (3 calls), gemini_continuation.rs (1 call). In CLI mode there is only one session so these can either: (a) keep a single-session DebugCaptureManager on the CLI Session struct, or (b) the CLI codepath may not be affected if fspec TUI always uses NAPI path. Determine which path the TUI agent loop uses.

RUST LAYER 3 - Capture call site migration (tracing layer). codelet/common/src/logging/mod.rs DebugCaptureLayer (line 28-50) is a tracing subscriber layer with NO session context. Options: (a) Make log.entry events include a session_id span field and route to the correct manager, (b) remove debug capture from the tracing layer entirely, (c) keep the tracing layer as a global fallback that writes to a shared 'system' debug log. Recommend option (a) using tracing spans.

RUST LAYER 4 - Stream event emission. After session_toggle_debug flips the per-session manager, it must emit StreamChunk::DebugStateChange { enabled: bool } on that session's stream. Add variant to StreamChunk enum in codelet/napi/src/types.rs (near IsolationStateChange at :543/:718). Emit from session_toggle_debug (session_manager.rs:7555+) using session.stream_sender if available, same pattern as IsolationStateChange emission.

BUG-134.description:
The DebugCaptureManager in codelet/common/src/debug_capture/ is currently a process-wide OnceLock<Arc<Mutex<DebugCaptureManager>>> singleton with a single open session_file. Every capture site (stream_loop.rs, stream_handlers.rs, repl_loop.rs, recovery_compaction.rs, gemini_continuation.rs, session_manager.rs) routes to this one manager, gated only by a global manager.enabled flag.

When two sessions run concurrently and session A enables /debug, session B's api.request/api.response/tool events are appended to A's JSONL file, indistinguishable from A's events (DebugEvent struct has no session_id field). When B toggles debug off, A's capture silently stops.

Debug logs are inherently per-session data. This work unit refactors the capture layer so that each BackgroundSession owns its own DebugCaptureManager (or an equivalent per-session capture sink), writing to its own file, gated by its own enable flag, with its activity never leaking into another session's log.

Blocks BUG-133 (TUI layer) going beyond a purely cosmetic fix. The TUI wiring in BUG-133 can land first against the existing AtomicBool; this card makes that wiring semantically correct.

examples.text: Session A runs /debug: capture starts writing to ~/.fspec/debug/{session_A_id}/session-{ts}.jsonl. Session B runs concurrently and makes API calls. Session A's JSONL contains ONLY session A's events; B's events are NOT captured (B has not toggled /debug)
Both session A and B run /debug: both have independent JSONL files. Toggling /debug off in A stops only A's capture. B's capture continues uninterrupted in its own file
Session A toggles /debug on: Rust emits DebugStateChange(session_A_id, true) on A's stream. TUI picks it up and shows [DEBUG] badge only for A. B's header remains unchanged

rules.text: The process-wide OnceLock singleton DebugCaptureManager (codelet/common/src/debug_capture/mod.rs:25) must be replaced with per-session managers owned by BackgroundSession
Each session's debug JSONL file MUST include the BackgroundSession.id (Uuid) in its path (e.g. ~/.fspec/debug/{session_id}/session-{timestamp}.jsonl) so files are unambiguously owned by one session
Toggling /debug in session A MUST NOT affect session B's capture state: B's manager.is_enabled() must remain unchanged, B's file must remain open/closed as it was
All capture call sites that currently use the global get_debug_capture_manager() must be refactored to route through the session's own manager
The free functions capture_event() and increment_debug_turn() in mod.rs must either be removed or gain a session_id parameter so callers route to the correct session manager
session_toggle_debug NAPI function must toggle only the requesting session's manager, not a global toggle
Rust must emit StreamChunk::DebugStateChange { session_id, enabled } when a session's debug state toggles, so the TUI layer (BUG-133) can replicate state to Zustand
The latest.jsonl symlink should remain functional: it should point to the most recently activated session's debug file (last session to toggle /debug on)

BUG-134.title: Refactor DebugCaptureManager to be truly per-session (one log file per BackgroundSession)

userStory.action: have each session's /debug capture write to its own isolated JSONL file
userStory.benefit: debug logs contain only that session's events and toggling debug in one session doesn't affect other sessions' capture state

architectureNotes.text: Regression introduced by BUG-133. Full root-cause analysis and design proposal in spec/attachments/BUG-135/design-analysis.md

Zustand sessionStore: replace flat `isDebugEnabled: boolean` field with `debugStateBySession: Map<string, boolean>`. Update setDebugState to take (sessionId, enabled). Remove the `state.isDebugEnabled = false` reset in activateSession (sessionStore.ts:157). Remove the isDebugEnabled=false reset in clearAndResetSession (sessionStore.ts:114).
useIsDebugEnabled selector: read `state.debugStateBySession.get(state.currentSessionId) ?? false`. Pure Zustand read, no NAPI calls per render.

globalSessionStreamManager: DebugStateChange handler (line ~355) must always call setDebugState(sessionId, enabled) regardless of whether sessionId equals currentSessionId — this populates the map for all sessions. The pendingDebugState map becomes unnecessary (since setDebugState now addresses any session directly) and can be removed or kept for back-compat. applyPendingDebugState remains but simply invokes setDebugState with Rust's ground truth.

AgentView session-attach paths: in resumeSessionById (AgentView.tsx:3633) and peer attach sites (1731, 3735, 3956, 4278), after applyPendingDebugState, also call useSessionStore.getState().setDebugState(sessionId, sessionGetDebugEnabled(sessionId)) as the ground-truth fallback from Rust's per-session AtomicBool.
SessionHeader.tsx requires no changes — the badge rendering at line 169-171 is correct; only its upstream state pipeline is broken.

Reference pattern divergence: isIsolated uses a flat boolean + reset-on-activate because isolation is immutable per session. Debug state is toggleable at runtime and therefore requires a per-session Map. Do NOT blindly copy the isIsolated pattern.

BUG-135.description: Regression introduced by BUG-133. After running /debug on session A to enable debug capture, cycling A → B → A via Shift+Left/Right causes the [DEBUG] badge to disappear from SessionHeader, even though Rust still has per-session debug enabled for A. Root cause: sessionStore's isDebugEnabled is a single flat boolean (not per-session Map), activateSession() resets it to false on every switch, and applyPendingDebugState consumes its Map entry on first read — so there is no rehydration path for repeat visits. The test file debug-badge-session-awareness.test.tsx actively forbids the Rust ground-truth fallback (sessionGetDebugEnabled) that useRustSessionState still provides. Fix: make Zustand's debug state per-session (Map<sessionId, boolean>) mirroring isIsolated's architecture so each session retains its own debug flag across switches, OR re-seed Zustand from Rust's authoritative per-session AtomicBool on every session activation.

examples.text: User enables /debug on session A, switches to session B (badge disappears), switches back to A — the [DEBUG] badge reappears
User enables /debug on both sessions A and B, then disables /debug on A — session B still shows [DEBUG], session A no longer shows it
User cycles Shift+Right through A→B→C→B→A without toggling debug — each session shows exactly the badge state it had when last toggled
User attaches to a session that already had debug capture enabled before the TUI was opened — the [DEBUG] badge is visible immediately on attach
While user is viewing session B, a debug toggle for session A (via a watcher or IPC) updates A's state silently — switching to A then shows the correct badge without any additional refresh

rules.text: Zustand must store debug state as a per-session Map<sessionId, boolean>, not a flat boolean
activateSession MUST NOT reset debug state; each session retains its own entry across switches
setDebugState action MUST accept (sessionId, enabled) and write into debugStateBySession map
useIsDebugEnabled selector MUST read debugStateBySession.get(currentSessionId) and return false if absent
On session attach/resume, after applyPendingDebugState, Zustand MUST be re-seeded from Rust's sessionGetDebugEnabled(sessionId) as a hydration fallback
SessionHeader.tsx itself MUST NOT be modified — the fix lives entirely in sessionStore, globalSessionStreamManager, and AgentView attach paths

userStory.benefit: the [DEBUG] badge accurately reflects each session's debug capture state regardless of how often I switch
userStory.role: TUI user running multiple concurrent sessions

architectureNotes.text: Root cause in codelet/providers/src/manager.rs: set_model_direct (line ~476) stores only model_id, whereas select_model (line ~431) stores the full provider/model composite. selected_model_string() returns this stored value verbatim, so AgentManager's handle_spawn passes an incomplete string to create_session_with_id. Fix stays Rust-only and needs the companion update in selected_model_id (line ~495) to continue returning the bare API id.

Existing BUG-132 regression test at codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs:8308-8316 asserts selected_model_string() == 'claude-opus-4-6' — this test encodes the buggy behaviour and MUST be updated to expect 'anthropic/claude-opus-4-6'.

BUG-136.description:
When user is on a custom model whose model_id contains slashes (e.g. 'accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-06-instruct' — common with Fireworks AI, OpenRouter, and similar aggregator APIs), AgentManager spawn fails with:

  Failed to select model: [registry] Configuration error: Unknown provider: 'accounts'. Available providers: meganova, moonshotai, ...

Root cause: `ProviderManager::set_model_direct()` stores only the bare `model_id` in `selected_model` (line 476), while `select_model()` stores the full `provider_id/model_id` composite (line 431). This asymmetry means `selected_model_string()` returns incomplete data for profile/codex/custom models.

When AgentManager's `register_agent_manager_handler` captures `selected_model_string()` and passes it to `create_session_with_id()` for the subordinate, the first segment of the slash-containing model_id ('accounts') is mis-parsed as the provider name. Unless 'accounts' happens to be a registered custom provider, the spawn falls through to `select_model()` which fails.

This was partially masked in BUG-132 by aligning the feature wording to the buggy behavior instead of fixing the asymmetry.

Reproduction: configure a Rhai custom provider that exposes a Fireworks or OpenRouter model whose API id contains slashes (e.g. 'accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-06-instruct'); select the model; invoke AgentManager spawn.

Fix: make `set_model_direct` store 'provider_id/model_id' so `selected_model_string()` always returns a properly-formed registry string; update `selected_model_id()` to strip the prefix when registry lookup fails.

examples.text: AgentManager spawn with a custom Rhai provider whose model id is 'accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-06-instruct' succeeds — the subordinate is created with the same provider/model and no 'Unknown provider' error is raised
After set_model_direct('my-llm', 'llama-3.1-70b', ...), selected_model_string() returns 'my-llm/llama-3.1-70b' (not 'llama-3.1-70b')

After set_model_direct('my-llm', 'accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-06-instruct', ...), selected_model_id() returns 'accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-06-instruct' (unchanged — only the 'my-llm/' prefix is stripped)
Existing Codex models (set_model_direct('codex', 'gpt-5-codex', ...)) continue to behave correctly — selected_model_string() = 'codex/gpt-5-codex', selected_model_id() = 'gpt-5-codex'

Existing Anthropic/Google/OpenAI registry selections via select_model('anthropic/claude-opus-4-6') continue to work — selected_model_string() = 'anthropic/claude-opus-4-6', selected_model_id() = resolved API id from registry (unchanged from today)

rules.text: set_model_direct MUST store the full 'provider_id/model_id' composite so selected_model_string() always returns a registry-parseable string, matching select_model()'s behaviour

selected_model_id() MUST continue to return just the bare API model id (no provider prefix) so provider-specific get_*() constructors get the id they expect — stripping the prefix when registry lookup fails and the stored string still starts with provider_id/

The stripping logic MUST only remove the FIRST slash segment (the provider prefix) so model ids that legitimately contain slashes (e.g. 'accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2-06-instruct') are preserved intact

architectureNotes.text: The ProviderManager stores the profile name in a new field (e.g. selected_profile_name: Option<String>) alongside selected_registry_provider_id and selected_model. This avoids re-parsing the composite and supports model ids containing slashes.

create_session_with_id already has the profile-model branch (checks for ':' before '/'). Fixing selected_model_string() to emit the profile-qualified form is sufficient — the subordinate path will then route through set_model_direct correctly.

BUG-137.description: When a profile-based model from `~/.fspec/fspec-config.json` (e.g. `openai:fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6`) is selected via the TUI, `sessionSetModelProfile` drops the profile name when routing to Rust — it only passes `provider_id="openai"` and `model_id="accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6"`. `ProviderManager::set_model_direct` stores those two parts; later `selected_model_string()` reconstructs `"openai/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6"` (missing the `:fireworks` profile segment). When AgentManager.spawn captures this string and calls `create_session_with_id`, the subordinate path doesn't detect it as a profile model, falls through to `select_model`, and fails with: `Failed to select model: [registry] Configuration error: Model 'accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6' not found in provider 'openai'`. The profile name must round-trip through ProviderManager so subordinate sessions spawn against the same profile endpoint.

examples.text: User selects 'openai:fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6' → ProviderManager.selected_model_string() returns 'openai:fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6' → AgentManager spawn succeeds
User selects cloud 'anthropic/claude-opus-4-6' → selected_model_string() returns 'anthropic/claude-opus-4-6' (no colon) → AgentManager spawn succeeds with registry validation

set_model_direct(provider_id='openai', model_id='accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6', profile_name=Some('fireworks')) → selected_model_string() returns 'openai:fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6'
set_model_direct without profile_name (codex, custom provider) → selected_model_string() emits 'provider/model' with no colon segment

architectureNotes.text: Root cause: rig_message_convert.rs::convert_user_message maps ToolResultContent::Image to String::new() and then filters empty strings out, so a Read tool result containing image content becomes ContentPart::ToolResult { content: "" } sent to the Rhai build_request script. The script sees nothing and the model receives an empty tool_result.

ReadTool already returns structured JSON {"type":"image","data":"<base64>","media_type":"image/png"} for supported images (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP). The rig-core patch's parse_tool_result_content converts this to ToolResultContent::Image. The custom provider's Rhai bridge drops it. Fix must happen in the Rhai bridge layer, not in ReadTool.

ContentPart::ToolResult currently has content: String — cannot carry structured (text+image) content needed for Anthropic-shape tool_result with image blocks. Design decision: introduce structured content on ContentPart::ToolResult by adding a parts field alongside the legacy string content (backward compatible: existing scripts still see content as a string).

BUG-138.description: When the Read tool is invoked from a Rhai-scripted custom provider (e.g. claude-rhai) against a PNG image (and likely other binary formats), it returns empty output instead of either (a) returning the image content as an image block the model can see, or (b) returning a clear error explaining the unsupported type. Repro: ask the agent running under claude-rhai to Read '/Users/rquast/Desktop/Screenshot 2026-04-22 at 9.13.05 am.png' — Read returns nothing, no error, no image content surfaced to the model. Root cause likely in the Rhai facade's Read tool implementation: it probably only handles text decoding and silently drops/empties binary payloads instead of emitting image content blocks or an explicit error. Action: audit the Rhai-scripted Read tool (and every other file-reading tool surface exposed to Rhai providers — e.g. attachment viewing, bash cat on binaries, Glob follow-ups) for all common file types (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images, PDFs, binaries, >size-limit text). For supported vision providers, return proper image content blocks. For unsupported cases, return an explicit structured error. Add tests covering each file type.

examples.text: Read('/tmp/icon.png') where icon.png is a 200x200 PNG under 5MB → build_request Rhai script sees ContentPart::ToolResult whose parts include an image block with media_type 'image/png' and base64 data; claude-rhai forwards it to Claude; model describes the icon.
Read('/tmp/screenshot.jpg') where screenshot.jpg is a valid JPEG — model using claude-rhai describes the screenshot contents correctly.
Read('/tmp/huge.png') where huge.png is 8MB — developer's model receives a clear 'image too large' error, not an empty result.
Read('/tmp/guide.pdf') in visual mode from claude-rhai — model receives each PDF page as an image block and can describe diagrams on each page.
Bash('cat /tmp/icon.png') from claude-rhai — the model receives an explicit structured error telling it to use Read instead, not garbled/empty output.

BUG-138 becomes umbrella.

Should I split BUG-138 into child work units now (e.g. BUG-138a extend ContentPart, BUG-138b bridge Images, BUG-138c audit Bash on binaries, BUG-138d audit Glob follow-ups) and start with the foundational type change?

rules.text: Read tool on a supported image file (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, within size/dimension limits) from a Rhai-scripted provider MUST surface the image as structured image content to the model — not an empty string, not a raw base64 JSON blob.
Read tool on an unsupported or over-limit binary file (oversized image, non-image binary, encrypted PDF) MUST return an explicit structured error to the script — not silently empty, not partial data.
ContentPart::ToolResult must carry structured content (text + image parts) without breaking serde backward compatibility for existing Rhai scripts that read `content` as a string.
rig_message_convert.rs::convert_user_message must propagate ToolResultContent::Image into the internal ContentPart::ToolResult structure rather than converting it to an empty string.
Other Rhai file-reading surfaces (attachment viewing, Bash cat on binaries, Glob follow-ups) either return structured content or an explicit error — never silent empty output.
PDFs through Read from Rhai providers return structured multi-page image content (visual mode) or structured text (text mode) — never empty.

BUG-140.description: Parent: BUG-138. Foundational type change. Add a structured parts representation to ContentPart::ToolResult in codelet_common so downstream (rig_message_convert, request_bridge, response_bridge) can carry tool_result content that includes image blocks — while existing Rhai scripts that read `content` as a string continue to work. Scope: codelet/common/src/types.rs (enum/struct + serde), feature for types, unit tests for serialisation round-trip and string-backcompat. NO consumer wiring in this unit — that's BUG-140.

examples.text: A developer constructs ContentPart::ToolResult { tool_use_id: 'tu_1', content: 'file contents', parts: [Text('file contents')], is_error: false } and serialises it — the JSON contains both `content: "file contents"` and `parts: [{"type":"text","text":"file contents"}]`.

A Rhai script author reads a tool_result entry from the messages array and sees both `content` (a plain string summary for text-only consumers) AND `parts` (a structured array) — so they can pick whichever shape fits their provider.

A Rhai script author reading a Read-tool result with an image part sees `parts: [{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":"image/png","data":"..."}}]`, and can forward it verbatim into Anthropic's tool_result.content block array.
An existing test that serialises ContentPart::ToolResult { content: "hello" } to JSON still passes — the JSON object's `content` key still equals the string "hello" (backcompat preserved).

rules.text: ContentPart::ToolResult must gain a `parts: Vec<ToolResultPart>` field (or equivalent) alongside the legacy `content: String`; ToolResultPart is a tagged enum covering Text { text } and Image { source: ImageSource }.

Backward compatibility: when a ToolResult is constructed with only text, its JSON MUST still serialise such that existing callers reading the `content` string field see the same text they always did (no break of PROV-063 tests, no break of the Rhai `messages_to_rhai` contract for text-only tool results).
ToolResultPart::Image must reuse the existing ImageSource enum (Url/Base64) introduced by PROV-091 so image wire formats stay consistent between request-side Image parts and tool_result Image parts.

Round-trip JSON serialisation: a ContentPart::ToolResult with mixed text+image parts must deserialise back into an equal value; a pure-text ContentPart::ToolResult must also round-trip losslessly under the new shape.

When constructing a ToolResult from a plain string (existing call sites), `parts` is initialised with a single ToolResultPart::Text mirroring `content`, so consumers that walk parts see the same text.

architectureNotes.text: rig_message_convert.rs::convert_user_message refactored: instead of collapsing each ToolResult's contents into a single joined string, walk the OneOrMany<ToolResultContent> and build a Vec<ToolResultPart> in order — Text → ToolResultPart::Text, Image → ToolResultPart::Image{source: image_to_source(...)}. If image_to_source returns None (Raw/Unknown), skip that entry. Use ContentPart::tool_result_text when the resulting parts vector is exactly one Text entry (preserves backcompat); otherwise use ContentPart::tool_result_parts.

messages_to_rhai requires NO change — it serialises via serde and ContentPart::ToolResult.parts already serialises to {type:'text'|'image', ...}. Will validate via integration test that the bridged Rhai value preserves the structure verbatim.

claude_rhai.rhai build_request must transform user messages whose `content` is an array of part-maps into Anthropic's wire format. Today it copies content verbatim. New logic per part-map: type='text' → {type:'text', text}; type='image' → {type:'image', source}; type='tool_use' → {type:'tool_use', id, name, input}; type='tool_result' → {type:'tool_result', tool_use_id, is_error, content: <transformed inner parts array> }. The inner content for tool_result is built by mapping each ToolResultPart entry to the Anthropic shape: Text→{type:'text',text}, Image→{type:'image',source}. When `parts` is empty/absent, fall back to the legacy `content` string.

Tests live in: codelet/providers/src/custom/rig_message_convert.rs (#[cfg(test)] for the Rust conversion side) AND a new integration test file codelet/providers/tests/tool_result_image_bridge_tests.rs that uses messages_to_rhai end-to-end. The Rhai-script-side behaviour is verified via a lightweight in-memory Rhai engine test that loads the updated claude_rhai.rhai content and asserts on the body produced by build_request — pattern follows existing custom_http_lifecycle_tests.rs.

BUG-141.description: Parent: BUG-138. Depends on BUG-140. Wire the structured ContentPart::ToolResult parts end-to-end: rig_message_convert.rs::convert_user_message must map ToolResultContent::Image → a structured image part (not empty string); messages_to_rhai must serialise it verbatim; update claude.rhai (or equivalent script) to build Anthropic-shape tool_result blocks with embedded images; add integration test exercising Read PNG → claude-rhai → request body contains Anthropic image block.

Given a rig user message whose ToolResult content is [Text('analysis complete'), Image(Base64 'BBB', JPEG)], when converted, then ContentPart::ToolResult.parts equals [ToolResultPart::Text{text:'analysis complete'}, ToolResultPart::Image{source: ImageSource::Base64{media_type:'image/jpeg', data:'BBB'}}] in that order, and ContentPart::ToolResult.content (legacy string) equals 'analysis complete\n[image]'.

Given a rig user message whose ToolResult content is [Text('only text')], when converted, then ContentPart::ToolResult is constructed via tool_result_text so legacy `content` equals 'only text' AND parts equals [ToolResultPart::Text{text:'only text'}] (preserving today's behaviour).

Given a rig user message whose ToolResult content is one ToolResultContent::Image with DocumentSourceKind::Url('https://x/y.png'), when converted, then the resulting parts vector contains a single ToolResultPart::Image{source: ImageSource::Url{url:'https://x/y.png'}}.

Given a Rust-built Vec<Message> containing one User message with a ContentPart::ToolResult (tool_use_id='tu_x', parts=[Image base64 'CCC' image/png]), when messages_to_rhai serialises it, then the resulting Rhai Dynamic value (decoded back to JSON) contains messages[0].content[0].parts[0] == {type:'image', source:{type:'base64', media_type:'image/png', data:'CCC'}}.

Given the updated claude_rhai.rhai script and a request whose messages contain one user message with a tool_result part carrying image parts, when build_request runs, then the returned body.messages[0].content equals [{type:'tool_result', tool_use_id:'tu_x', content:[{type:'image', source:{type:'base64', media_type:'image/png', data:'CCC'}}]}].

Given the updated claude_rhai.rhai script and a request whose messages contain one user message with a tool_result part carrying [Text('done'), Image base64], when build_request runs, then body.messages[0].content[0].content == [{type:'text', text:'done'}, {type:'image', source:{...}}] in that order.

Given the updated claude_rhai.rhai script and a request whose messages contain a user message with a plain text MessageContent (no tool_result), when build_request runs, then body.messages[0] equals {role:'user', content:'<the original text>'} (no transformation, backwards compatible).

rules.text: rig_messages_to_internal must map a UserContent::ToolResult containing a ToolResultContent::Image into a ContentPart::ToolResult whose parts vector contains a ToolResultPart::Image with the corresponding ImageSource (Base64 or Url) — never an empty string.

When a tool_result contains a mix of Text and Image entries, the resulting ContentPart::ToolResult parts vector preserves the original order (text and image entries appear in the same sequence as the rig source).

Image variants whose ImageSource cannot be derived (DocumentSourceKind::Raw or Unknown) are skipped (with a debug log) but never become an empty Text part — text parts that exist alongside them remain intact.

Pure-text tool_result inputs MUST continue to use the tool_result_text helper so the legacy `content` string and the single Text part remain in sync (no behavioural change for text-only tool results).

messages_to_rhai serialises the ContentPart::ToolResult parts array verbatim into Rhai so that scripts inspecting `msg.content[i].parts` see image entries with shape {type:"image", source:{type:"base64", media_type, data}} (no transformation needed — relies on serde Serialize).

claude.rhai's build_request, when emitting a user message, MUST detect tool_result entries inside `msg.content` (an array of part maps) and convert each into an Anthropic-shape `{type:"tool_result", tool_use_id, content:[…]}` block whose inner `content` array carries text and image blocks derived from the structured `parts`.

Backward compatibility: when a Rhai script sees a user message whose content is a plain string (text-only message, MessageContent::Text), the script's existing string-passthrough branch must continue to forward it to the Anthropic body unchanged (no regression for non-tool-result user messages).
