questions.answer: Yes. When a blocking hook fails (exit code != 0), fspec wraps the stderr output in a <system-reminder> block for AI agent consumption. This allows hooks to provide guidance, suggestions, and instructions to AI through plain text stderr output. Non-blocking hooks just display output normally.

questions.answer: No standard schema. Hooks output freeform text to stdout/stderr. AI agents read and interpret the text naturally. This maximizes flexibility for hook authors and keeps the framework simple. Documentation can provide examples of effective hook output patterns.
questions.text: @human: Should we provide a standard schema for hook output that includes 'suggestions', 'warnings', 'blockers', and 'insights' for AI consumption?

questions.answer: No. fspec provides the hooks framework only. Users can implement multi-agent patterns (spawning multiple Claude sessions, parallel execution, etc.) in their hook scripts using standard shell tools. This keeps fspec focused and avoids framework bloat.

Plain stdout/stderr only. Exit code determines success (0) or failure (non-zero). Hook output is displayed as-is to the user. If blocking hook fails (exit != 0), fspec shows stderr in a system-reminder block for AI agent consumption. This keeps hooks simple and works with any tool.

No dry-run mode. Users can use 'fspec list-hooks' to see configured hooks and 'fspec validate-hooks' to validate configuration syntax. To test a hook, users can temporarily make it non-blocking or run it manually outside of fspec.
CLI commands 'fspec add-hook' and 'fspec remove-hook' manage hooks in fspec-hooks.json programmatically

No chaining. Each hook receives the same original work unit context via stdin. Hooks execute sequentially but independently. If users need chaining logic, they can implement it inside their hook scripts (e.g., read files left by previous hooks or use pipes within the script).

No chaining for any hooks. All hooks (event hooks and exit hooks) receive the original context/output via stdin. Hooks execute sequentially but independently for side effects (validation, logging, notifications). The original command output is returned to the user unchanged by hooks.

Hooks inherit the parent process environment naturally (as spawned child processes). fspec does NOT set custom FSPEC_* environment variables. Hooks receive all context via stdin as JSON. Hooks are independent programs that manage their own environment.

Support optional conditions in hook configuration. Hooks can specify 'condition' object with fields like 'tags', 'prefix', 'epic', 'estimateMin', 'estimateMax'. If condition doesn't match, hook is skipped. If no condition specified, hook always runs. This allows context-aware hooks without requiring logic in every script.

Support hooks for ANY fspec command using convention: 'pre-<command-name>' and 'post-<command-name>'. Examples: pre-create-work-unit, post-add-rule, pre-link-coverage, post-generate-scenarios. Plus special lifecycle hooks: pre-start (before any command) and pre-exit (before returning output). This makes the system extensible for current and future commands.

Yes. When a blocking hook fails (exit code != 0), fspec wraps the stderr output in a <system-reminder> block for AI agent consumption. This allows hooks to provide guidance, suggestions, and instructions to AI through plain text stderr output. Non-blocking hooks just display output normally.

No standard schema. Hooks output freeform text to stdout/stderr. AI agents read and interpret the text naturally. This maximizes flexibility for hook authors and keeps the framework simple. Documentation can provide examples of effective hook output patterns.

No. fspec provides the hooks framework only. Users can implement multi-agent patterns (spawning multiple Claude sessions, parallel execution, etc.) in their hook scripts using standard shell tools. This keeps fspec focused and avoids framework bloat.

HOOK-013.description: Extend the existing fspec-hooks.json hook system to support agent lifecycle events in the Rust agent core. The TypeScript layer already has a mature hook system (spec/fspec-hooks.json) for fspec CLI command lifecycle events with pre/post event naming, condition evaluation, JSON context on stdin, blocking semantics, and system-reminder formatting. This story adds a NEW category of agent-level lifecycle events to the SAME config system: session_start, session_end, user_prompt_submit, pre_tool_use, post_tool_use, notification. The Rust engine reads from the existing two-level config hierarchy (user-level ~/.fspec/fspec-hooks.json + project-level spec/fspec-hooks.json), compiles regex matchers at startup, executes hooks as child processes with JSON payloads on stdin, and interprets structured outcomes that can allow/deny/modify/inject context into the agent loop. Must maintain Claude Code JSON response protocol compatibility. The biggest challenge is pre/post tool use hooks since rig auto-executes tools internally — recommended approach is Tool::call() wrapper middleware.

Exit code semantics: exit 0 = success; exit 2 + stderr = deny/block; exit 2 without stderr = warning (continue); timeout = deny for pre_tool_use, warning for others; any other non-zero exit = hook failure (non-blocking warning)
Hooks can inject additional context as system messages into the conversation via the additionalContext field in JSON output or via plain text stdout for session_start/user_prompt_submit events

pre_tool_use hooks short-circuit on definitive decisions: if any hook group returns Allow or Deny, remaining hook groups for that event are skipped; Continue means no opinion and evaluation continues to next group

rules.text: Hook commands execute via sh -c (or global.shell) with JSON payload serialized to stdin, stdout/stderr captured, timeout enforced via tokio::time::timeout + child.kill()
Each event type has a specific JSON payload struct (SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Notification) serialized via serde
Environment variables FSPEC_PROJECT_DIR, FSPEC_SESSION_ID, FSPEC_HOOK_EVENT, FSPEC_TRANSCRIPT_PATH are set on every hook child process
Exit code 0 = Success/Continue; Exit code 2 + non-empty stderr = Deny/Block; Exit code 2 + empty stderr = Warning; Any other non-zero = non-blocking warning
Timeout behavior differs by event type: pre_tool_use timeout = Deny (safety-first); all other timeouts = Warning
Hook stdout may contain Claude Code compatible JSON with fields: continue, suppressOutput, decision, reason, hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision, hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext

pre_tool_use JSON interpretation priority: (1) hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision → Allow/Deny/Ask, (2) continue:false → Deny, (3) decision:deny/block → Deny, (4) exit code 2+stderr → Deny, (5) else → Continue
additionalContext from JSON or plain text stdout (for session_start/user_prompt_submit) is returned for injection as system messages into the conversation
The engine returns typed outcome structs per event: SessionStartOutcome, UserPromptOutcome, PreToolOutcome, PostToolOutcome — not raw process results

HOOK-017.description: The hardest part: intercept rig's auto-execution of tools to run pre_tool_use and post_tool_use hooks. Build Tool::call() wrapper middleware (or ToolSet::call interception) that runs pre-hooks before delegating to the real tool and post-hooks after. Implement pre_tool_use short-circuit logic (Allow/Deny stops evaluation, Continue passes to next group). Integrate with existing blocklist/stage-permissions permission model.

examples.text: Two pre_tool_use groups match 'Bash': first returns Allow (exit 0 + permissionDecision:allow), second returns Deny — only first executes, tool is allowed
Two pre_tool_use groups match 'Bash': first returns Deny (exit 2 + permissionDecision:deny), second returns Allow — only first executes, tool is denied
Two pre_tool_use groups match 'Bash': first returns Continue (exit 0, no permissionDecision), second returns Deny — both execute, tool is denied by second group
BashTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, command never executes
ReadTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, file is never read
WriteTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, file is never written
EditTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, file is never modified
LsTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, directory is never listed
GlobTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, glob is never executed
GrepTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, search is never executed
AstGrepTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, AST search is never executed
AstGrepRefactorTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, refactor is never executed
FspecTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, fspec command is never executed
BridgeTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, bridge action is never executed
ApplyPatchTool.call() with a registered Deny handler → returns ToolError::Blocked, patch is never applied
BashTool.call() with Allow handler → command executes normally, output is returned
BashTool.call() with no registered handler → command executes normally (no-op path)

rules.text: When multiple pre_tool_use hook groups match a tool, they execute in order until a definitive decision (Allow/Deny) is reached
Allow decision short-circuits: stops evaluation of remaining groups and allows the tool call to proceed
Deny decision short-circuits: stops evaluation of remaining groups and prevents the tool call from executing
Continue decision does NOT short-circuit: evaluation proceeds to the next matching hook group
If all groups return Continue, the final decision is Continue (fall through to normal permission checks)
The run_pre_tool_use function takes compiled hooks and a PreToolUsePayload, returns a PreToolHookOutcome with the final decision and collected messages/context
Native tools must call pre_tool_hook_check() at the top of their call() method before any execution, so pre_tool_use hooks fire for all tools regardless of provider
The 12 native tools requiring pre_tool_hook_check: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Ls, Glob, Grep, AstGrep, AstGrepRefactor, Fspec, Bridge, ApplyPatch
If pre_tool_hook_check returns Deny, the tool must return a ToolError::Blocked with the deny reason, preventing execution
If pre_tool_hook_check returns Allow or Continue, the tool proceeds with normal execution (blocklist, stage permissions, etc.)
Each native tool must serialize its full input args as a serde_json::Value when calling pre_tool_hook_check, so the hook script receives accurate tool_input in its JSON payload

INIT-008.description:
WHAT ALREADY EXISTS:
1. Template generation time transformations (during 'fspec init'):
   - removeMetaCognitivePrompts() strips 'ultrathink', 'deeply consider' for CLI agents
   - stripSystemReminders() transforms <system-reminder> tags to bold text for non-Claude
   - Agent registry has supportsMetaCognition and supportsSystemReminders flags
   - This works great for generated files (AGENT.md, slash commands)

2. Environment variable:
   - FSPEC_DISABLE_REMINDERS=1 disables system-reminders entirely

WHAT'S MISSING (THE ACTUAL PROBLEM):
1. Runtime detection: fspec commands don't know which agent is running them
   - 'fspec validate' emits <system-reminder> for ALL agents (only Claude understands)
   - 'fspec update-work-unit-status' uses system-reminders regardless of agent
   - Error messages don't adapt (all use <system-reminder> tags)
   - Help commands don't tailor output based on agent

2. CLI output adaptation:
   - Commands should emit <system-reminder> for Claude Code
   - Commands should emit **⚠️ IMPORTANT:** for Cursor/Cline/IDE agents  
   - Commands should emit **IMPORTANT:** for CLI-only agents (Aider, Gemini)
   - Currently everything uses <system-reminder> by default

3. No detection mechanism:
   - Can't tell if it's Claude vs Cursor vs Aider running the command
   - No FSPEC_AGENT environment variable
   - No config file (~/.fspec/config.json)
   - No auto-detection from project files (.claude/, .cursor/)

Detection strategies to implement:
1. Environment variable: FSPEC_AGENT=claude (highest priority)
2. Config file: ~/.fspec/config.json with {"defaultAgent": "claude"}
3. Auto-detect from project: Check for .claude/, .cursor/, etc. in cwd
4. Fallback: Safe default (plain text, no system-reminders)

Acceptance Criteria:
- Runtime agent detection using priority chain (env > config > auto-detect > default)
- All CLI commands adapt output based on detected agent
- System-reminders only emitted for Claude Code at runtime
- Other agents get transformed output (bold text + emoji or plain)
- Detection works across all 18 supported agents
- Fallback to safe defaults if detection fails
- Documentation for FSPEC_AGENT env var and ~/.fspec/config.json

KGRAPH-001.description: Parent card for the nanograph-powered knowledge graph initiative. Goal: embed nanograph as a typed property graph to build relational memory over all agent session history, enabling a new GraphSearch tool analogous to SessionSearch but operating on concept/decision/entity relations rather than raw text.
KGRAPH-001.title: Nanograph Knowledge Graph Integration — Architecture & Research

userStory.action: build a knowledge graph over all agent session history
userStory.benefit: agents can search relational connections between concepts, decisions, and code across all past conversations

architectureNotes.text: Nanograph integrated as Rust crate via git dependency in codelet/napi/Cargo.toml. Singleton via lazy_static Mutex<Option<Database>> following same pattern as MessageStore/SessionStore in persistence/mod.rs. Schema bundled via include_str!() from codelet/napi/schemas/agent-memory.pg. Data directory: ~/.fspec/graph/agent-memory.nano/. Reset hook in persistence::set_data_directory(). Process exit cleanup via NAPI binding graph_db_close(). Feature-gated behind 'graph' Cargo feature.

Schema includes all node types (Concept, Decision, CodeEntity, WorkUnit, Session, Turn) and all edge types from the design doc
First call to GraphSearch: ~/.fspec/graph/agent-memory.nano/ is created, schema is written, Database.init() succeeds, empty graph is ready for queries

rules.text: Extractors are deterministic (regex/pattern matching) — no LLM API calls, zero token cost
Write/Edit tool calls produce CodeEntity nodes with file path, language (from extension), and Modifies edges (Turn → CodeEntity)
Fspec tool calls produce WorkUnit nodes from create-story/bug/task commands and WorksOn edges from update-work-unit-status
Entities are queued in a batch buffer and flushed periodically (threshold count or session idle), not on every single turn
Extractor functions are pure — take tool call data as input, return a list of graph entities to upsert (no side effects)
If graph DB is not available (not initialized, feature disabled), extractors are silently skipped — no errors

architectureNotes.text: Pure Rust extraction module at codelet/napi/src/graph/llm_extraction.rs. Defines prompt template, turn batching (filter user/assistant, truncate to 2000 chars), JSON response parsing with serde, validation (enums, self-refs, strength bounds). Returns Vec<GraphEntity> from extractors.rs. No DB writes — output feeds KGRAPH-006.

KGRAPH-005.description: Design extraction prompt, implement batch processing (5-10 turns per LLM call), parse structured JSON responses, extract Concept/Decision/Relation/CodeEntity entities from conversation content.

examples.text: A batch of 5 conversation turns about 'JWT authentication' produces Concept nodes for 'jwt-authentication' (technology) and 'session-management' (pattern), a Decision node for 'use-jwt-over-sessions', and a RelatesTo edge between them
LLM returns malformed JSON with a concept missing its slug field — that concept is skipped but other valid entities in the same response are still returned
LLM returns a relation where from == to (self-reference) — that relation is rejected during validation
A batch of only tool result turns (no user/assistant content) is skipped without invoking the LLM
Conversation turns longer than 2000 chars are truncated before being included in the extraction prompt
LLM returns a concept with category 'foobar' not in the schema enum — that concept is rejected during validation

rules.text: The extraction prompt must instruct the LLM to extract three entity types: Concepts (slug, name, category, summary, confidence), Decisions (slug, title, rationale, domain, confidence), and Relations (from, to, type, strength)
Conversation turns must be batched (5-10 turns per LLM call) with each turn truncated to 2000 characters
Only user and assistant message turns are sent to the LLM — tool results are skipped (handled by structural extractors in KGRAPH-004)

The LLM response must be parsed as JSON with validation: reject empty slugs/names, reject self-referencing relations (from==to), reject strength outside 0.0-1.0, skip malformed entries without failing the batch
The extraction pipeline outputs Vec<GraphEntity> (the same type used by structural extractors) so it can feed into the same merge/upsert path (KGRAPH-006)
Concept categories must be from the schema enum: architecture, convention, decision, dependency, domain_term, error_class, feature, library, pattern, person, platform, process, technology, tool
Decision domains must be from the schema enum: architecture, convention, dependency, deployment, design, implementation, process, testing
Relation types must be from the schema enum: causes, composes, conflicts_with, depends_on, extends, implements, similar_to, supersedes, uses

userStory.action: have conversation content automatically analyzed by an LLM to extract concepts, decisions, and relations

architectureNotes.text: Pure Rust module at codelet/napi/src/graph/merge.rs. Converts Vec<GraphEntity> to JSONL, loads via nanograph merge mode with @key. For increment/min/max merge semantics, implements read-before-write pattern. Watermark in ~/.fspec/graph/index-state.json written atomically.

KGRAPH-006.description: Generate JSONL for nanograph load, implement merge mode for idempotent upserts via @key, track co-occurrence counts on RelatesTo edges, maintain watermark state in index-state.json.

examples.text: 2 Concept GraphEntity nodes loaded into nanograph → 2 Concept rows visible in DB with correct slug/name/category
Same Concept slug loaded twice with different mentionCount → mentionCount is summed (not overwritten), firstSeen preserved, lastSeen updated
Concept loaded with confidence=medium, then same slug loaded with confidence=high → confidence promoted to high
Concept loaded with confidence=high, then same slug loaded with confidence=low → confidence stays high (no demotion)
After successful upsert, index-state.json updated with session watermark and lastRunAt timestamp
RelatesTo edge with coOccurrenceCount=1 loaded, then same pair loaded again → coOccurrenceCount becomes 2 and strength recalculated

rules.text: Vec<GraphEntity> from extractors/LLM pipeline must be converted to JSONL format for nanograph load
All loads use merge mode: if a node with same @key slug exists, update properties; if not, insert
mentionCount and coOccurrenceCount use increment semantics (read-before-write), not overwrite
firstSeen keeps earliest timestamp, lastSeen keeps latest timestamp on merge
confidence is promoted (low→medium→high) never demoted on merge
Watermark state stored in index-state.json tracks per-session lastIndexedTurn for incremental re-indexing
index-state.json written atomically via temp file + rename after each successful batch
RelatesTo edge strength recalculated as min(1.0, log2(coOccurrenceCount + 1) / 10.0) on each co-occurrence

KGRAPH-020.description:
Define the nanograph PG schema for the Learnings Graph, following the Residue methodology's Strategy Register pattern.

**Node types**:
- Learning (primary): convention | pattern | anti-pattern | decision | discovery | constraint | reformulation
- Exploration: structured exploration record with strategy, outcome, failure constraint, surviving structure
- Convention: established rules with enforcement levels
- Decision: explicit decisions with rationale, status, alternatives
- CodePattern: discovered patterns with example files

**Edge types**:
- Discovered (Exploration → Learning)
- Eliminates (Exploration → Learning): approach class elimination
- Supersedes (Learning → Learning)
- RelatesTo (Learning ↔ Learning): with strength and relationType
- InformedBy (Exploration → Exploration): cross-session learning chains
- Applies (Convention → CodePattern)
- Contradicts (Learning ↔ Learning): design tension tracking

Stored separately from AST graph at ~/.fspec/graph/learnings.nano/
Global scope (shared across projects on same machine).

KGRAPH-021.description:
Implement the LLM-based extraction pipeline that produces Learnings graph entities at natural session boundaries (not per-turn).

**Extraction triggers** (replacing per-turn extraction):
1. Session end / compaction — extract from DAG summary
2. Work unit completion (status → done) — extract from session history
3. Explicit GraphSearch index command
4. Periodic synthesis (scheduled job)

**Extraction prompt** follows Residue methodology structure:
- LEARNINGS: What lasting knowledge was gained?
- EXPLORATIONS: What approaches were tried? Outcomes? Failure reasons?
- REFORMULATIONS: New frameworks for understanding?
- CONSTRAINTS: Hard facts discovered?

**Volume target**: 5-20 entities per session (vs hundreds with old per-turn approach).
**Storage target**: <5MB for 1000 sessions.

Given an LLM response containing malformed JSON (not parseable), when extraction runs, then it returns Err with a parse error message — no entities produced, no panic

KGRAPH-022.description:
Implement the cross-session learning and synthesis capabilities inspired by the Residue methodology.

**Session continuity**: When starting work on a work unit, inject relevant learnings (decisions, constraints, conventions, failed approaches) from the Learnings graph into the system prompt context.

**Failure propagation**: When an approach fails and is recorded as an Exploration with an eliminated approach class, surface this in future sessions that touch the same domain. Prevents repeating the same mistakes.

**Periodic synthesis** (analogous to Residue's 'every 5 explorations' rule):
- Scheduled job scans recent Explorations for cross-strategy patterns
- Looks for structural similarities across concrete artifacts from different approaches
- Checks whether any Reformulation suggests an untried approach
- Creates synthesis entries in the graph

**Multi-agent dimension**: When AgentManager spawns subordinates, inject relevant learnings into their DeepSearch context. Learnings from subordinate sessions are extracted and merged back into the graph.

AgentManager spawns subordinate for security review — subordinate receives relevant learnings about security patterns from supervisor's domain context

KGRAPH-026.description:
When the AST extraction pipeline walks a project and encounters a TypeScript file that is both walked directly AND referenced via an import from another file, two File entities with the same `path` value are created. The nanograph schema declares `path: String @unique` on the File node type, so loading both into the graph in a single JSONL batch triggers a unique constraint violation.

Reproduction: Run `GraphSearch ast_index` on the fspec codebase. `bridge/telegram-endpoint.ts` imports from `./telegram-slash-commands`, which the TS extractor resolves to `bridge/telegram-slash-commands.ts` and creates a stub File node. The file walker also directly processes `bridge/telegram-slash-commands.ts` and creates a full File node. Both land in the same entity batch → nanograph rejects with '@unique constraint violation on File.path: duplicate value bridge/telegram-slash-commands.ts'.

Root cause: `ast_ts_extractor.rs:128-136` creates stub File nodes for every import target without checking if that file will also be walked directly. The `walk_and_extract()` function does no deduplication before loading.

The fix must deduplicate File entities by path before serializing to JSONL, preferring the full node (with language, lineCount, isTest) over the stub (with only slug and path).

examples.text: bridge/telegram-endpoint.ts imports ./telegram-slash-commands → walker also walks bridge/telegram-slash-commands.ts → two File nodes with path='bridge/telegram-slash-commands.ts' → @unique constraint violation
File A imports File B which is also in the project → after dedup only one File B node exists with full properties → graph loads successfully
Import target resolves to a file outside the project → stub File node is kept because no full node exists → no dedup collision
Multiple files all import the same target → only one stub File node for the target in the output, not N duplicates

rules.text: Import resolution in ast_ts_extractor.rs creates stub File nodes for import targets that may duplicate File nodes created by the file walker
The entity list must be deduplicated by (node_type, path) before JSONL serialization, preferring full nodes over stubs
Deduplication must happen in walk_and_extract() after all files are processed, not in individual extractors
Full File nodes (with language, lineCount, isTest) must always win over stub File nodes (with only slug, path) during deduplication
Edges must NOT be deduplicated — only Node entities with the same (node_type, slug) pair
Deduplication must preserve all edges — even if two File nodes are merged, both Imports edges from different source files must be kept

KGRAPH-027.description:
Comprehensive dead code detection requires three layers:

1. **Populate Calls edges** — The TS extractor must analyze function bodies for call expressions and emit `Calls` edges (Function→Function). Currently 0 Calls edges exist despite 8,447 Function nodes.

2. **Populate TypeRef edges** — The TS extractor must analyze function signatures and bodies for type references and emit `TypeRef` edges (Function→Type). Currently 0 TypeRef edges exist despite 1,138 Type nodes.

3. **New `ast_dead_code` GraphSearch action** — Uses nanograph `not { }` anti-join queries to find:
   - Orphan files: File nodes with no incoming Imports edges
   - Uncalled functions: Function nodes with no incoming Calls edges
   - Unreferenced types: Type nodes with no incoming TypeRef/Extends/Implements edges

Scope: TypeScript extractor only. Rust extractor Calls/TypeRef is deferred to KGRAPH-025.

examples.text: File A has `function main() { validateConfig(); }` and `import { validateConfig } from './config'` → Calls edge from A::main to config::validateConfig
File A has `function foo() { bar() }` and `function bar() {}` in same file → Calls edge from A::foo to A::bar (same-file call)
Function `handler(req: Request): Response { ... }` referencing types Request and Response → TypeRef edges from handler to Request and Response
File X is never imported by any other file → ast_dead_code returns X as orphan file
Function `helperUnused()` exists but no other function calls it → ast_dead_code returns it as uncalled function
Type `OldInterface` exists but no function references it in params or return type → ast_dead_code returns it as unreferenced type
`console.log()`, `process.exit()`, `new Error()` do NOT generate Calls edges — these are builtins/constructors, not project function calls
Test files should be excluded from dead code results by default — tests are leaf nodes, they call production code but nothing calls them

rules.text: The TS extractor must detect function call expressions (e.g. `validateConfig()`, `parseArgs(x)`) within function bodies and emit Calls edges (Function→Function) for calls that resolve to functions in the same file

The TS extractor must detect cross-file function calls by matching call names to imported identifiers — if file A imports `validateConfig` from './config' and calls `validateConfig()`, emit a Calls edge from A::callingFunction to config::validateConfig
The TS extractor must detect type references in function signatures (parameter types, return types) and emit TypeRef edges (Function→Type) for types defined in the same file or imported

Calls to non-function identifiers (e.g. constructors `new Foo()`, method chains `obj.method()`, builtins like `console.log()`) must NOT generate Calls edges — only direct named function calls that resolve to known Function nodes

A new `ast_dead_code` GraphSearch action must use nanograph `not { }` anti-join queries to find: orphan files (no incoming Imports), uncalled functions (no incoming Calls), and unreferenced types (no incoming TypeRef/Extends/Implements)
The ast_dead_code action must accept an optional `entity_type` filter (File, Function, Type) and exclude test files by default
Scope: TypeScript extractor only. Rust extractor Calls/TypeRef population is deferred to KGRAPH-025

architectureNotes.text: Reference implementation: ast_ts_extractor.rs — extract_imports(), extract_calls(), extract_type_refs(), extract_call_names_from_body(), extract_type_names_from_signature(). Each non-TS extractor needs equivalent functions adapted to that language's syntax.

The current extractors accept (source, rel_path) only. They need to be updated to also accept known_files: &HashSet<String> (matching the TS signature). This requires updating the dispatch layer in ast_dispatch.rs/mod.rs to pass the file set through.

For call extraction: use KindMatcher to find call expression nodes (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression etc.), extract the callee name, and cross-reference against known functions in the same file + import map. This avoids fragile text-scanning in function bodies.

Import resolution is language-specific: PHP uses PSR-4 namespace→path mapping, Python uses dot-delimited module paths, Go uses module paths, Rust uses crate:: paths, C/C++ use filesystem includes. Each extractor needs its own resolve_import_path() function.

KGRAPH-041.description:
Only the TypeScript extractor currently populates Calls, Imports, and TypeRef edges — all 12 other language extractors (Rust, Python, Go, Java, C, C++, C#, Ruby, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, PHP) only emit Contains and ContainsType edges. Without cross-reference edges, the ast_dead_code query returns zero results for non-TypeScript repos because every function appears unreachable.

Each language extractor needs:
1. **Imports edges** — use/import/include/require statements → File-to-File
2. **Calls edges** — function call expressions within function bodies → Function-to-Function
3. **TypeRef edges** — type annotations, extends, implements → Function-to-Type or Type-to-Type

This is a cross-cutting concern affecting all 12 non-TS extractors. The TS extractor (ast_ts_extractor.rs) is the reference implementation.

examples.text: PHP: `use Slim\Routing\RouteResolver;` in App.php → Imports edge from Slim-App-php to Slim-Routing-RouteResolver-php
PHP: `$this->getRouteResolver()` inside `addRoutingMiddleware()` in App.php → Calls edge from Slim-App-php::addRoutingMiddleware to Slim-App-php::getRouteResolver (same-file)

PHP: `public function handle(ServerRequestInterface $request): ResponseInterface` → TypeRef edges from Slim-App-php::handle to ServerRequestInterface and ResponseInterface (skipped as external unless local)
Python: `from click.core import BaseCommand` → Imports edge from source file to click-core-py (if local)
Go: `import "github.com/spf13/cobra"` is external (skip), but `import "./internal/util"` is local → Imports edge
Rust: `use crate::graph::helpers;` → Imports edge; `helpers::slugify_path(x)` in function body → Calls edge
Running ast_dead_code on php-slim returns specific uncalled functions like test helpers that exist but are never referenced from non-test code
C: `#include "jv.h"` → Imports edge to jv-h file; `jv_parse(input)` in function body → Calls edge

rules.text: Each language extractor must emit Imports edges (File→File) by parsing that language's import/use/include/require statements and resolving them to project-local files
Each language extractor must emit Calls edges (Function→Function) by scanning function bodies for call expressions and resolving them to known same-file or imported functions
Each language extractor must emit TypeRef edges (Function→Type) by parsing type annotations in function signatures (parameters, return types) — where the language supports them
External/third-party imports must NOT generate Imports or Calls edges — only project-local references should create edges (same logic as TS extractor's is_relative check)

Method calls on objects ($this->method(), self.method(), obj.method()) should emit Calls edges only when the target can be resolved to a known function in the same file — cross-file method resolution is best-effort
Shared extraction helpers (call name extraction from body, type name extraction from signatures) should be factored into helpers.rs where patterns are reusable across languages
Languages without static type systems (Ruby, Python without annotations, C) should still emit Calls and Imports edges — TypeRef edges are optional for dynamically-typed languages
Extractors must accept a known_files: HashSet<String> parameter (matching the TS extractor signature) so imports can be resolved against actual project files
After implementation, running ast_dead_code on each of the 13 tmp/ test repos must return non-empty results for at least Function orphans (proving the edge extraction works)

KGRAPH-056.description:
Add Dart as a supported language in the AstGrep (code search) and AstGrepRefactor (code refactoring) tools.

Dart was removed from upstream ast-grep-language in v0.30.0 (November 2024) because the tree-sitter-dart grammar at the time (v0.0.4 from UserNobody14/tree-sitter-dart) did not meet ast-grep's builtin language quality criteria — it had tree-sitter version incompatibilities and parser peculiarities (outputting multiple AST nodes for function declarations).

However, a new tree-sitter-dart v0.1.0 was published on March 11, 2026 by nielsenko/tree-sitter-dart. This new version uses the modern tree-sitter-language = "0.1" bridge crate (the same interface all current ast-grep parsers use) and is compatible with our tree-sitter 0.26.7 dependency chain.

Since ast-grep upstream has not re-added Dart, we need to integrate it ourselves at our tool layer in codelet/tools/src/. The approach is to add tree-sitter-dart as a direct dependency and handle Dart as a custom language case alongside the ast-grep SupportLang enum.

Scope:
1. Add tree-sitter-dart = "0.1.0" to codelet/tools/Cargo.toml
2. Extend AstGrepTool::parse_language() in astgrep.rs to recognize "dart" and return a custom Dart language
3. Extend AstGrepTool::get_extensions() to map Dart → ["dart"]
4. Extend AstGrepRefactorTool with equivalent Dart support
5. Update error messages and supported_languages() lists in both tools
6. Add Dart to the tool description enums exposed to the LLM
7. Verify pattern matching works for Dart syntax (functions, classes, constructors, mixins)

Note: Also fix missing Solidity, Nix, and Hcl entries in get_extensions() while touching these files.

examples.text: Searching a directory of .dart files with AstGrepTool for 'class $NAME { $$$BODY }' returns matching Dart classes with file, line, column
Passing language='dart' to AstGrepRefactorTool replaces a matched Dart pattern in a source file (e.g., rename a function)
Passing an unsupported language like 'brainfuck' returns an error message listing all supported languages including dart
AstGrepRefactorTool batch mode replaces all occurrences of a Dart pattern across a file
Searching for 'void $NAME($$$PARAMS)' (signature only) in a Dart file matches function signatures with correct meta-variable captures

rules.text: tree-sitter-dart v0.1.0 must be added as a direct dependency to codelet/tools since ast-grep upstream removed builtin Dart support in v0.30.0
Both AstGrepTool and AstGrepRefactorTool must recognize 'dart' as a language string and dispatch to the custom DartLang
The get_extensions() function must map Dart to ["dart"] so directory-walking file search finds .dart files
Error messages and supported_languages() lists must include 'dart' so the LLM knows Dart is available
Missing Solidity, Nix, and Hcl entries must be added to get_extensions() since they exist in SupportLang but have no file extension mapping
A custom DartLang struct must implement ast-grep-core's Language trait — no expando_char needed since $ is valid in Dart identifiers (same as Java/JS/Bash in ast-grep)
Pattern matching with $VAR meta-variables works natively for Dart syntax since $ is a valid identifier character — no expando_char substitution needed

Dart's tree-sitter grammar splits top-level function declarations into sibling nodes (function_signature + function_body), so full-function patterns like 'void $NAME() { $$$BODY }' fail — match signatures only or use class-level patterns

KGRAPH-057.description:
Add a Dart AST extractor for the GraphSearch ast_index and ast_dead_code pipelines.

This is the companion to KGRAPH-056 (which adds Dart to the AstGrep/AstGrepRefactor search and refactor tools). This card covers the knowledge graph side: when a user runs ast_index on a Flutter/Dart project, the pipeline should extract Functions, Types, File entities, and dependency information from .dart files and pubspec.yaml.

Scope:
1. Create codelet/napi/src/graph/ast_pipeline/ast_dart_extractor.rs following the established extractor pattern (see ast_kotlin_extractor.rs or ast_swift_extractor.rs as reference)
2. Extract functions (top-level functions, methods, constructors, named constructors, factory constructors)
3. Extract types (classes, abstract classes, enums, mixins, extensions, extension types, sealed classes)
4. Extract Imports edges from Dart import/export/part statements → File-to-File
5. Extract Calls edges from function call expressions within function bodies → Function-to-Function
6. Extract TypeRef edges from type annotations in function signatures → Function-to-Type
7. Create codelet/napi/src/graph/ast_pipeline/pubspec_dep_extractor.rs to extract dependencies from pubspec.yaml
8. Wire up the Dart extractor in ast_pipeline/mod.rs (add "dart" to SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS, import module, add dispatch case in extract_file())
9. Wire up pubspec dependency extractor in ast_dispatch.rs dispatch_ast_index()
10. Ensure ast_dead_code works correctly for Dart projects (functions without callers, files without importers)

Dart-specific considerations:
- Dart uses `$` in string interpolation (e.g., `'Hello $name'`), so the expando_char needs careful handling — Dart identifiers accept letters, digits, and underscores but NOT `$` in non-string contexts. Use `µ` (mu) as expando_char like Go/Python.
- Dart has named constructors (MyClass.fromJson) and factory constructors that should be extracted as Functions
- Dart mixins and extension types are unique to Dart and need proper Type classification
- Dart's import system uses package: URIs for packages (external) and relative paths for local files

examples.text: Indexing a Dart project with classes, functions, enums, and mixins produces correct File, Function, Type nodes with proper Contains/ContainsType edges
A Dart file with relative imports (import '../models/user.dart') produces Imports edges to the target file when the target exists in known_files
A Dart file with dart: and package: imports does NOT produce Imports edges (external imports are skipped)
A function calling another local function produces a Calls edge; calling an imported function from a relative import produces a cross-file Calls edge
A function with typed parameters (String name, int age) produces TypeRef edges to locally-defined types but NOT to Dart builtins
pubspec.yaml with dependencies: and dev_dependencies: sections produces Dependency nodes with correct isDev flag and version constraints
Named constructors (User.fromJson), factory constructors, and const constructors are extracted as Function nodes
ast_dead_code correctly identifies uncalled Dart functions and files without importers

rules.text: ast_dart_extractor.rs must follow the established extractor pattern: extract File, Function, Type nodes and Contains, ContainsType, Imports, Calls, TypeRef edges

Function extraction must cover: function_signature (top-level), method_signature (class methods), constructor_signature, constant_constructor_signature, factory_constructor_signature, getter_signature, setter_signature, operator_signature
Type extraction must cover: class_declaration, enum_declaration, mixin_declaration, extension_declaration, extension_type_declaration, type_alias, mixin_application_class
Import extraction must handle relative imports (../foo.dart, ./bar.dart, baz.dart) as local Imports edges, skip dart: and package: imports as external
Calls edges must be extracted from function bodies using the shared extract_call_names_from_body helper
TypeRef edges must be extracted from function signatures via colon-based type annotations (param: Type, : ReturnType)
pubspec_dep_extractor.rs must parse dependencies and dev_dependencies from pubspec.yaml and emit Dependency nodes + DependsOn edges
The .dart extension must be added to SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS and the extract_file dispatch in mod.rs
pubspec.yaml dependency extraction must be wired into ast_dispatch.rs dispatch_ast_index alongside other dep extractors

Dart uses $ for string interpolation but $ IS valid in Dart identifiers, so DartLang from codelet/tools does NOT use expando_char — the AST extractor must use DartLang directly rather than SupportLang (since Dart is not in ast-grep's SupportLang enum)

architectureNotes.text: Nanograph does NOT support variable-length path traversal (e.g. Cypher's [:CALLS*1..5]) — all .gq queries are single-hop. Multi-hop features (call chains, transitive traversal, class hierarchy) must be implemented as BFS/DFS in Rust using iterative single-hop queries

CGC uses Cypher graph DB with native multi-hop traversal — we use nanograph (Arrow/DataFusion-based) with only single-hop queries. Our implementation strategy is BFS in Rust with cached adjacency lists from existing .gq queries (function_calls, function_callers, type_extends, type_implements)

KGRAPH-060.description: Add ast_call_chain action to GraphSearch that finds the shortest call path(s) between two functions via multi-hop CALLS edge traversal. CGC equivalent: find_function_call_chain() with configurable max_depth.

examples.text: Agent asks for call chain between two unconnected functions — returns empty chains array with message 'No call path found within depth 5'
Agent asks for call chain with a non-existent function slug — returns error 'Function not found: nonexistent_function'
Agent asks for call chain with max_depth=2 but the shortest path is 3 hops — returns empty chains, but with max_depth=3 it finds the path
Agent asks GraphSearch for call chain from 'func_a' to 'func_b' — returns a single chain of length 1 (direct call)
Agent asks for call chain from function A to function D where there's a 3-hop path (A→B→C→D) — returns the full chain with all intermediate functions
Agent asks for call chain and gets back both function_chain with metadata (slug, name, path, lineStart) and call_details with edge info (callCount, isConditional) for each hop
Agent gets response with summary 'Found 2 call chains from entry to target (max depth: 5)' — human-readable summary included

rules.text: New action_type 'ast_call_chain' must accept 'from' (source function slug or name), 'to' (target function slug or name), and optional 'max_depth' (default 5)
Returns an array of chains, each chain being an ordered list of function slugs/names from source to target
Chains are ordered by length (shortest first), limited to max 20 results to prevent explosion on deeply connected graphs
Implementation uses BFS in Rust over iterative single-hop Calls edge queries — nanograph doesn't support variable-length path traversal
If no path exists between source and target within max_depth, returns empty chains array with a message
If 'from' or 'to' doesn't resolve to an existing function node, returns an error with 'not found' message

Each chain result includes both function_chain (ordered function metadata: name, path, line_number) and call_details (edge metadata per hop: callCount, isConditional) — mirroring CGC's dual-array return structure
Each chain includes a chain_length integer representing the number of hops (edges) — matching CGC's 'length(path) as chain_length'
Successful response includes a summary string with format 'Found N call chains from X to Y (max depth: D)' — matching CGC handler summary format

KGRAPH-060.title: Call Chain / Path Tracing Between Two Functions

userStory.action: trace the call chain between two functions to understand how function A reaches function B
userStory.benefit: I can perform impact analysis and understand unfamiliar code paths

architectureNotes.text: Implement ast_callers and ast_callees as two new GraphSearchAction variants sharing the BFS traversal module from KGRAPH-060. ast_callers traverses incoming Calls edges (function_callers query), ast_callees traverses outgoing Calls edges (function_calls query). Wire in graph_search_handler.rs and types.rs.

KGRAPH-061.description: Implement the reserved depth parameter on ast_neighbors for multi-hop graph traversal. Add find_all_callers and find_all_callees capabilities using variable-length CALLS path traversal. CGC equivalent: find_all_callers() / find_all_callees() with [:CALLS*] queries.

examples.text: Agent asks ast_callers for 'dispatch_ast_search' — returns dispatch_action (depth 1), create_handler closure (depth 2), and any higher-level callers
Agent asks ast_callees for a high-level entry point — returns all functions it transitively calls, each annotated with their depth from the entry point
Agent asks ast_callers for a leaf function with no callers — returns empty results array

rules.text: New action_type 'ast_callers' accepts function slug/name and optional max_depth (default 5), returns all direct and transitive callers
New action_type 'ast_callees' accepts function slug/name and optional max_depth (default 5), returns all direct and transitive callees
Results include the hop distance from the source function, so agents can see which are direct (depth 1) vs transitive (depth 2+)
Reuses BFS infrastructure from KGRAPH-060 (call chain) — same Rust BFS module, different output format (flat list with depth vs ordered chains)
Each result includes function slug, name, file path, line numbers, and depth from source — matching CGC's output format

KGRAPH-061.title: Transitive Callers / Callees (Multi-Hop Traversal)

userStory.action: find all transitive callers or callees of a function across the entire call graph
userStory.benefit: I can understand the full blast radius of changes and identify all affected code paths

architectureNotes.text: DRY approach: single complexity.rs module with data-driven per-language configs. Extend build_function_node() signature to force all 14 extractors through compile error. Single AstComplexity action handles both single-function lookup (with node_id) and top-N query (without node_id). Schema adds cyclomaticComplexity: I32? to Function node.

KGRAPH-062.description: Calculate and store cyclomatic complexity per function during AST extraction. Add ast_complexity action or enrich ast_search results. CGC equivalent: cyclomatic_complexity property on Function nodes + find_most_complex_functions() query.

examples.text: Agent asks for top 10 most complex functions — receives list sorted by cyclomatic complexity descending with function name, file path, line numbers, and complexity score
Agent asks for complexity of a specific function — receives the function's complexity score, e.g. 'dispatch_action has cyclomatic complexity 12'
A simple getter function with no branches has complexity 1. A function with 5 if/else branches has complexity 6.

rules.text: Cyclomatic complexity must be calculated during AST extraction and stored as a property on Function nodes in the graph schema
Complexity is calculated by counting decision points: if, else if, while, for, case/match arms, catch, &&, || — formula: 1 + decision_points
New action_type 'ast_complexity' accepts optional function slug (for specific function) and optional limit/sort_by for top-N most complex
The ast-code.pg schema must add a 'cyclomaticComplexity: I32?' optional property to the Function node
Single shared complexity.rs module calculates complexity for all 14 languages using data-driven keyword configs — extractors pass function source text, not per-extractor logic

KGRAPH-062.title: Cyclomatic Complexity Analysis

userStory.action: query the cyclomatic complexity of functions and find the most complex functions in a codebase
userStory.benefit: I can identify code hotspots that need refactoring and prioritize code review

architectureNotes.text: DRY approach: Create a single metadata.rs module under ast_pipeline/ with data-driven per-language configs for docstring patterns, decorator patterns, and parameter extraction. Each language extractor passes raw AST source text to shared helpers rather than implementing extraction logic. Same pattern as complexity.rs. Extend build_function_node() and build_type_node() signatures to force all 14 extractors through compile error.

KGRAPH-063.description: Store function/type source code, docstrings, parameters, start/end lines, and decorators as properties on AST graph nodes. CGC equivalent: source, docstring, args, decorators, line_number, end_line properties on Function/Class nodes.

examples.text: Agent indexes a TypeScript project and searches for 'dispatch' — results include source code (first 100 lines), JSDoc docstring, parameter names (action, options), decorators (@Injectable), and language (typescript)

Agent indexes a Rust project — Function node for 'find_all_reachable' has parameters='graph, start_id, max_depth, direction', docstring='/// BFS to find all reachable nodes...', source with actual code, decorators='' (empty since Rust uses #[attr] and this function has none), language='rust'
A function with 200 lines of source code gets its source capped at 100 lines with truncated=true — the graph doesn't bloat from huge functions
Agent indexes a Python project — Type node for class 'UserService' has lineStart=15, lineEnd=89, docstring='Service for managing user operations', decorators='@dataclass', language='python'

rules.text: Function nodes must store: parameters (String? — comma-separated names), source (String? — capped at 100 lines), docstring (String? — extracted doc comment), decorators (String? — comma-separated), language (String? — e.g. 'typescript', 'rust')
Type nodes must store: lineStart (I32?), lineEnd (I32?), source (String?), docstring (String?), decorators (String?), language (String?) — same conventions as Function nodes
Source code MUST be capped at 100 lines or 4KB (whichever is smaller) with a truncated: Bool? flag when capped — prevents graph bloat on large functions/types

build_function_node() signature must be extended to accept new fields — all 14 language extractors get compile errors forcing them to pass the new fields (same DRY pattern used for cyclomatic complexity in KGRAPH-062)
build_type_node() signature must be extended to accept lineStart, lineEnd, and the new metadata fields — all 14 language extractors get compile errors forcing them to pass them

Docstring extraction must be language-specific: JSDoc (/** ... */) for JS/TS, rustdoc (/// or //!) for Rust, triple-quoted for Python, Javadoc (/** ... */) for Java/Kotlin/Scala, XML doc (/// <summary>) for C#, GoDoc for Go, YARD for Ruby, PHPDoc for PHP, triple-slash for Dart, slash-star-star for C/C++ — use a data-driven config per language (same DRY pattern as complexity.rs)

Decorator extraction must capture language-specific decorators/annotations: @decorator for Python/TS/Dart, #[attr] for Rust, @Annotation for Java/Kotlin, [Attribute] for C#, @objc/@available for Swift, decorators for Scala — stored as comma-separated list
Parameter extraction must capture function parameter names as a comma-separated string (e.g. 'self, name, age') — excludes types to keep it concise across languages
ast_search results must include the new metadata fields when present — agents see source, docstring, parameters, decorators, language in search results without extra tool calls

KGRAPH-063.title: Source Code and Metadata Storage in Graph Nodes

userStory.action: retrieve function/type source code, docstrings, parameters, decorators, and language directly from graph nodes
userStory.benefit: I can understand code without making separate Read tool calls for every function I find

architectureNotes.text: Add AstHierarchy variant to GraphSearchAction enum. Implement in ast_hierarchy.rs using existing type_extends, type_implements, and type_container .gq queries with iterative multi-level traversal.

KGRAPH-064.description: Add ast_hierarchy action that returns full inheritance tree (parents, children, methods) for a type. Add override detection across classes. CGC equivalent: find_class_hierarchy() + find_function_overrides().

examples.text: Agent asks ast_hierarchy for 'DatabaseManager' in CGC Python codebase — returns parent classes, child classes, and methods of each class in the hierarchy
Agent asks ast_hierarchy for a type with no parents or children — returns the type itself with its methods, empty parents and children arrays

rules.text: New action_type 'ast_hierarchy' accepts a type slug/name and returns parents (via Extends edges), children (via reverse Extends), and implemented interfaces (via Implements edges)
For each class in the hierarchy, includes its methods (via Contains edges from the type's file) to support method override detection
Traversal supports multi-level hierarchies (grandparent → parent → child) via iterative Extends edge walking, same BFS approach as KGRAPH-060/061
Already have Extends and Implements edges populated by extractors — this leverages existing type_extends and type_implements .gq queries plus new multi-hop traversal

KGRAPH-064.title: Class Hierarchy and Inheritance Traversal

userStory.action: traverse class inheritance hierarchies to find parent classes, child classes, and method overrides
userStory.benefit: I can understand type relationships and navigate OOP codebases effectively

architectureNotes.text: Post-process mtime stamping on File nodes in walk_and_extract rather than changing all 14 language extractor signatures
New ast_pipeline/incremental.rs module with: collect_file_mtimes(), read_stored_mtimes(), partition_changed_files(), filter_reusable_entities() — reuses export_all_entities() from KGRAPH-069
Add incremental: Option<bool> to AstIndex variant in types.rs; pass through graph_search_handler.rs to dispatch_ast_index; add all_files_with_mtime query to ast-queries.gq

Entity ownership is determined by slug prefix — entities with slugs starting with a file slug belong to that file (e.g., src-foo-rs::main belongs to file src-foo-rs). Edges where from_slug starts with a changed file slug are considered owned by that file.

KGRAPH-065.description: Add incremental AST graph updates — track file modification times, re-extract only changed files, merge into graph instead of full overwrite. CGC equivalent: CodeWatcher with watchdog + RepositoryEventHandler for debounced incremental updates.

examples.text: Full index stores mtime on all File nodes; subsequent incremental index detects no changes and returns immediately with 0 re-extracted files
After modifying one file, incremental re-index extracts only that file and reuses all other entities from the graph
After deleting a file, incremental re-index removes the deleted file's entities (File, Function, Type nodes and edges)
After adding a new file, incremental re-index extracts it as a new file and includes it alongside reused entities
When incremental is used on an empty graph (no prior index), falls back to full extraction and loads all entities
When incremental is false or omitted, full extraction + overwrite works as before (backward compatibility)

rules.text: File modification times (mtime) are stored on File nodes in the graph using the existing lastModified DateTime property
Incremental mode compares filesystem mtimes against stored mtimes to identify changed, new, and deleted files
Only changed and new files undergo AST extraction — unchanged file entities are reused from the existing graph via export
Deleted files are excluded by not including their entities in the overwrite load
If more than 50% of files changed or no prior index exists, incremental mode falls back to full extraction
Cross-file edges from unchanged files may be stale if targets were renamed — deduplicate_entities prunes dangling edges for correctness
The full overwrite-load strategy is preserved — incremental combines reused + fresh entities then overwrites, so stale entities are always cleaned up
Dependencies (Cargo.toml, package.json, etc.) are always re-extracted in incremental mode since they are fast and small

KGRAPH-065.title: Live File Watching and Incremental Re-indexing

userStory.action: have my AST graph incrementally re-indexed when only a few files have changed
userStory.benefit: avoid the expensive full re-index on large codebases and get fast graph updates

architectureNotes.text: Extend ast-code.pg schema with Variable node type and ContainsVariable edge type
Add build_variable_node() and build_contains_variable_edge() to helpers.rs following existing patterns
Variable extraction added per-language in each extractor using ast-grep patterns to match module-level/class-level assignments, const declarations, and static fields
Add Variable to the EntityType enum in types.rs and update dispatch_ast_search in ast_dispatch.rs to include Variable node type in queries

KGRAPH-066.description: Add Variable/Constant as first-class node types in AST graph schema. Extract module-level and class-level variables during indexing. CGC equivalent: Variable node with name/value/context/line_number + find_by_variable_name() + who_modifies_variable().

examples.text: Index a TypeScript file with `export const API_KEY = 'abc123'` and `const PORT = 8080` → ast_search entity_type=Variable returns both with isConstant=true, scope=module
Index a Python file with `MAX_RETRIES = 3` at module level and `count = 0` inside a function → only MAX_RETRIES appears as Variable (function-local excluded)
Index a Rust file with `const MAX_SIZE: usize = 1024` and `static INSTANCE: Lazy<Db>` → both are Variables, MAX_SIZE has isConstant=true
Index a Java file with `public static final String DB_URL = "jdbc:..."` class field → Variable with scope=class, scopeName=Config, isConstant=true
ast_search query=API entity_type=Variable → returns all variables with 'API' in their name (e.g. API_KEY, API_URL, API_VERSION)
ast_stats after indexing includes variable count alongside function and type counts

rules.text: Variable is a new first-class node type in the AST graph schema alongside File, Function, Type, and Dependency
Variable extraction during ast_index is scoped to module-level and class-level declarations only — local function variables are excluded to avoid noise
ast_search with entity_type=Variable returns variable results — no separate action needed (DRY with existing search infrastructure)

Variable nodes have: slug (@key), name, path (file path), lineStart, value (initial value string, capped at 200 chars), scope (module|class), scopeName (containing class name or empty), isConstant (bool), language
ContainsVariable edge connects File → Variable (same pattern as Contains for Functions and ContainsType for Types)
isConstant is true for: const/final keywords, static readonly, ALL_CAPS naming convention (Python/Go), Rust const keyword
Variable extraction reuses existing ast-grep infrastructure — patterns per language, builder helpers in helpers.rs

KGRAPH-066.title: Variable and Symbol Tracking

userStory.action: search for variables and constants by name across all indexed files
userStory.benefit: locate configuration values, feature flags, module exports, and understand where key symbols are defined

architectureNotes.text: DRY approach: Reuse existing matches_fields() helper with different field lists per search_mode. Add decorator/parameter filter as post-match predicates in dispatch_ast_search. No new modules needed — extend ast_dispatch.rs and types.rs only.

KGRAPH-067.description: Add full-text search capability over function bodies and docstrings in the AST graph. Requires source storage (KGRAPH-063). CGC equivalent: Neo4j fulltext index on name/source/docstring + find_by_content() + fuzzy Lucene search.

examples.text: Agent searches query='dispatch' with search_mode='name' — returns functions named 'dispatch_ast_search', 'dispatch_ast_neighbors' but NOT functions that merely call dispatch in their body
Agent searches query='authentication' with search_mode='content' — returns functions whose source code or docstrings contain 'authentication' even if their names don't
Agent searches with decorator='@Test' — returns only Function nodes whose decorators property contains '@Test' or '@test' or '#[test]'
Agent searches with parameter='request' — returns functions whose parameters string contains 'request' (e.g. 'self, request, response')
Agent searches query='User' with decorator='@Injectable' and search_mode='name' — returns only functions named User that also have @Injectable decorator (AND logic)
Agent uses ast_search with no search_mode parameter — defaults to 'name' mode for backward compatibility, only searches name/slug/path/qualifiedName

rules.text: ast_search already searches all fields (name, slug, path, qualifiedName, source, docstring, parameters, decorators) — current behavior is effectively 'all' mode with no way to scope the search

A new 'search_mode' parameter on ast_search controls which fields are searched: 'name' (name/slug/path/qualifiedName — default, backward compatible), 'content' (source/docstring only), 'all' (every field)

A new 'decorator' filter parameter on ast_search does exact/contains matching against the decorators property — e.g. decorator='@app.route' returns only functions with that decorator (CGC: find_functions_by_decorator)

A new 'parameter' filter parameter on ast_search does contains matching against the parameters property — e.g. parameter='request' returns functions that accept a parameter named 'request' (CGC: find_functions_by_argument)
When search_mode is 'name' (default), source/docstring/parameters/decorators fields are NOT searched — prevents noisy matches when agents want to find a specific function by name
decorator and parameter filters work as AND constraints combined with the query — query='User' with decorator='@Injectable' matches functions named User that also have the @Injectable decorator
decorator matching is case-insensitive and strips leading @ for matching — searching decorator='test' matches both '@test' and '@Test' and '#[test]'

KGRAPH-067.title: Full-Text and Content Search Within Graph

userStory.action: search graph nodes by source code content, docstrings, and names with controllable search scope
userStory.benefit: find relevant code by what it does, not just by name, without noisy matches when I only want name-based results

architectureNotes.text: This feature was largely implemented across KGRAPH-063 (metadata storage/extraction) and KGRAPH-067 (decorator/parameter query filters). Remaining gap: Scala and PHP decorator styles were mapped to None instead of AtSign/HashBracket.

KGRAPH-068.description: Extract decorators/annotations during AST parsing and store as list property on Function/Type nodes. Add query capability to find functions by decorator. CGC equivalent: decorators list on Function nodes + find_functions_by_decorator() + find_functions_by_argument().

examples.text: Python function with @staticmethod and @override decorators has both stored as comma-separated string in decorators property
Scala function with @tailrec annotation is extracted as AtSign decorator style (same as Java/Kotlin)
PHP function with #[Route('/api')] attribute is extracted using HashBracket style (same as Rust)

rules.text: Decorator extraction uses a data-driven DecoratorStyle enum (AtSign, HashBracket, SquareBracket, None) mapped per language — extraction runs during ast_index pipeline via shared metadata.rs

All AtSign languages (Python, TypeScript, JS, JSX, TSX, Dart, Java, Kotlin, Swift, Scala) extract @name decorators; Rust extracts #[name] HashBracket attrs; C# extracts [Name] SquareBracket attrs; PHP extracts #[Name] HashBracket attrs
Languages without decorator syntax (C, C++, Go, Ruby) correctly produce empty decorator strings
The decorator filter on ast_search does case-insensitive matching and strips leading @/#[/[ for cross-language matching — searching 'test' matches @Test (Java), #[test] (Rust), @test (Python)
The parameter filter on ast_search does contains matching against the parameters property — parameter='request' matches functions with 'request' in their parameter list

KGRAPH-068.title: Decorator and Annotation Search

userStory.action: find functions by decorator/annotation and by parameter name across all supported languages
userStory.benefit: locate API endpoints, test functions, event handlers, and injection points without reading every file

architectureNotes.text: No new modules — add export_all_entities() and jsonl_to_entities() to graph_entities.rs, ast_export dispatch in graph_search_handler.rs, AstExport/AstImport variants in types.rs. ZIP handling uses flate2+zip crates.

KGRAPH-069.description: Add ast_export and ast_import actions to serialize/deserialize the nanograph AST database to a portable format. CGC equivalent: .cgc bundle format (ZIP with JSONL nodes + edges + metadata) + bundle registry for pre-indexed libraries.

examples.text: Export a graph with Function, File, Type, Dependency nodes and Contains, Calls, Imports edges → .astbundle file is a valid ZIP containing entities.jsonl + metadata.json + schema.pg
Import an .astbundle into an empty graph → all nodes and edges are loaded, ast_stats shows same counts as the export source
Round-trip test: export → reset graph → import → export again → second bundle has same entity count and JSONL content as first

rules.text: Bundle format is .astbundle (ZIP archive) containing: entities.jsonl (all nodes and edges in nanograph JSONL format), metadata.json (version, timestamp, languages, stats), schema.pg (nanograph schema source for compatibility check)
Export reads all nodes and edges from the graph snapshot — nodes via segment iteration (skipping internal id column), edges via edge_batch_for_save with id→slug resolution
Import supports two modes: 'overwrite' (default — replaces all existing data) and 'merge' (upserts via slug-based key matching) — reusing GraphDatabase::load_entities_overwrite and load_entities
Import validates schema compatibility before loading — compares bundle schema.pg hash against the current compiled schema, rejects with actionable error if they differ
JSONL round-trip uses existing entities_to_jsonl format for export, and a new jsonl_to_entities parser for import — ensures nodes and edges survive serialization without data loss

KGRAPH-069.title: Portable Graph Bundles — Export/Import

userStory.action: export the AST graph to a portable bundle file and import pre-built bundles
userStory.benefit: share pre-indexed codebases across sessions, teams, and machines without re-indexing

KGRAPH-070.description: KGRAPH-058 changed the Dart extractor to emit 'extension' as a typeKind value for extension_declaration and extension_type_declaration nodes (ast_dart_extractor.rs lines 42-43). However, the nanograph schema (ast-code.pg line 45) was never updated — it only allows: struct_kind, class, interface, enum_kind, trait_kind, type_alias. The ast_dispatch.rs dead code filter was updated to handle the value (line 572), but the schema rejects it during JSONL entity loading. This causes any ast_index on a Dart project with extension declarations to fail with: 'invalid enum value extension for Type.typeKind'. Fix: add 'extension' to the typeKind enum in ast-code.pg.

examples.text: ast_index on a Dart project with extension declarations succeeds after adding extension to typeKind enum in ast-code.pg
ast_index on the fspec codebase (which contains Rust files including the Dart extractor) still succeeds — no regression

rules.text: The nanograph schema typeKind enum must include 'extension' as a valid value
Only the schema needs updating — the extractor (ast_dart_extractor.rs) and dispatch filter (ast_dispatch.rs) already handle extension correctly

KGRAPH-070.title: Dart extension typeKind not in nanograph schema — ast_index crashes on Dart projects with extension declarations

userStory.action: index a Dart project with extension declarations via ast_index
userStory.benefit: the graph loads successfully without schema violations

architectureNotes.text: The schema is embedded via include_str!() at compile time — the binary always has the correct schema, but the on-disk DB preserves the schema from when it was first created
KGRAPH-010 added schema hash comparison on open but blocks breaking changes with an error — this card needs to provide the rebuild path that KGRAPH-010 is missing

Uses lazy_static! { Mutex<HashMap<String, GraphDatabase>> } as singleton registry — reset_all_graphs() already exists (clears HashMap). Need a reset_graph(name) that removes a single graph. GraphDatabase wraps Arc<Database> so Drop will clean up when all references are gone.

No schema hash comparison exists despite KGRAPH-010 claiming it was done — open_or_init simply checks if schema.ir.json exists and opens blindly. The schema_source param is ignored when opening existing DB.

AstIndex is the only action that doesn't call get_graph_or_err() first — it handles its own graph acquisition inside dispatch_ast_index(). The reset logic goes here: delete dir, remove from registry, then proceed with normal indexing which will init fresh.

DB paths: AST = <cwd>/.fspec/graph/ast-code.nano/, Learnings = ~/.fspec/graph/learnings.nano/ — resolved in registry::resolve_graph_config(). Serde enum variant: GraphSearchAction::AstIndex { path: Option<String> } — add reset: Option<bool> here.

KGRAPH-071.description: When the nanograph schema (.pg file) changes and the binary is rebuilt, existing graph databases on disk still contain the old schema. open_or_init() opens the existing DB without re-initializing with the new schema, causing enum validation errors (e.g., 'invalid enum value extension for Type.typeKind'). KGRAPH-010 added schema hash comparison that blocks breaking changes with an error, but provides no automated rebuild path. The only workaround is manually deleting database files from disk AND restarting the process to clear in-memory state. This has caused repeated frustration across 4+ sessions. Need: (1) A 'reset' flag on ast_index that deletes the on-disk database and clears in-memory graph state before re-indexing, (2) The in-memory singleton graph must also be invalidated/dropped so the fresh schema takes effect without process restart, (3) Consider auto-detecting schema mismatch and offering rebuild as part of normal ast_index flow.

examples.text: Schema changes to ast-code.pg (add 'extension' to Type.typeKind), rebuild binary, ast_index fails with 'invalid enum value extension' because old DB on disk has stale schema — reset flag deletes DB, re-indexes successfully

Schema changes to ast-code.pg (add 'pubspec' to Dependency.source), user manually deletes .nano dir, but in-memory graph singleton still has old schema — reset flag clears both disk AND memory, re-index works
ast_index without reset flag hits schema mismatch — error message says 'Schema has changed. Run ast_index with reset: true to rebuild the database' instead of cryptic enum error
After reset + re-index of fspec codebase, ast_search for 'function' immediately returns results (no process restart needed)

rules.text: ast_index with reset flag must delete the on-disk .nano directory (e.g., ast-code.nano/) before opening a fresh database
When schema hash mismatch is detected on normal ast_index (no reset flag), the error message must tell the user to re-index with the reset flag instead of just failing
After reset + re-index, subsequent ast_search/ast_neighbors/ast_dead_code queries must work without process restart
ast_index with reset flag must remove the graph from the lazy_static Mutex<HashMap> registry so the next get_graph() re-initializes with fresh schema
open_or_init must compare compiled schema hash against on-disk schema.pg hash — if mismatch, return actionable error rather than silently opening with stale schema

KGRAPH-071.title: GraphSearch ast_index has no way to force-rebuild database after schema changes — stale on-disk and in-memory graph causes repeated failures

userStory.action: force-rebuild the graph database after schema changes
userStory.benefit: I don't have to manually delete database files and restart the process every time the schema changes

LANG-001.description: Add i18n framework to fspec to support multiple languages for all user-facing text including CLI output, error messages, help text, and system-reminders

questions.text: @human: Which languages should be supported initially? (e.g., Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Chinese, etc.)
@human: How should locale/language be configured? Environment variable (LANG), config file setting, CLI flag (--lang=es), or all three with precedence order?
@human: Should Gherkin feature files remain in English (industry standard), or should they also be localizable?
@human: Should system-reminders (for AI agents) be localized, or always remain in English since AI models typically understand English best?
@human: What i18n library should be used? (e.g., i18next, FormatJS/react-intl for CLI, or custom solution)
@human: Should translation files be JSON (easy to edit), YAML (human-readable), or .po/.pot files (professional translation tooling)?
@human: Where should translation files be stored? Project-level (spec/i18n/), user-level (~/.fspec/i18n/), or both with merging?
@human: Should date/time formatting, number formatting, and pluralization rules be supported (full i18n), or just text translation?
@human: How should missing translations be handled? Fallback to English, show translation key, or throw error?
@human: Should there be a command to extract translatable strings from source code (like 'fspec extract-translations')?

LANG-001.title: Internationalization and localization support for multiple languages

userStory.action: see all CLI output, error messages, and help text in my preferred language
userStory.benefit: I can use fspec effectively without language barriers
userStory.role: developer or AI agent using fspec in a non-English language environment
