userStory.action: see accurate input/output token counts during streaming
userStory.benefit: I can monitor context window fill and avoid premature compaction

architectureNotes.text: See vtcode's 6-layer truncated tool call recovery pipeline as reference: ToolCallBuilder → parse_tool_arguments with extract_balanced_json → PreparedAssistantToolCall with error recording → dispatch error responses → turn-level recovery → post-tool LLM failure recovery

Key vtcode code references: vtcode-commons/src/llm.rs (FinishReason enum), ResponseAggregator (streaming accumulation), map_finish_reason_common() (provider normalization), ContinuationController (task-level continuation), thinking signature-gated round-tripping for truncated thinking blocks

Affected files in our codebase: codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/anthropic/streaming.rs:346-374 (stop_reason discarded), codelet/patches/rig-core/src/agent/prompt_request/streaming.rs:185-188 (FinalResponse missing field), codelet/cli/src/interactive/stream_loop.rs (zero stop_reason checks), codelet/napi/src/persistence/message_envelope.rs:299,329,537,568 (hardcoded end_turn)
Secondary bug: ProviderManager::max_output_tokens() returns compile-time constant for OpenAI (4096) instead of runtime OPENAI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS env var value — compaction threshold miscalculation

Follow vtcode's pattern: stop_reason propagates as metadata through the entire pipeline, while control flow decisions are based on structural presence of tool calls/content — not stop_reason branching

PROV-039.description: When the LLM hits max_tokens during output generation, the stop_reason is discarded in the streaming path. The agent loop, CLI, and persistence layer all treat truncated responses identically to normal end_turn completions. This means truncated file writes, truncated tool calls, and truncated text responses are silently accepted with no user notification, no retry, and no continuation logic.

examples.text: Anthropic sends message_delta with stop_reason='max_tokens' → FinalResponse contains StopReason::MaxTokens → stream_loop displays truncation warning
Model hits max_tokens mid-tool-call → JSON parse fails → error message says 'Tool call truncated due to output token limit' instead of generic JSON error → model retries
Model completes normally with end_turn → no warning shown, stop_reason persisted as 'end_turn' — baseline behavior unchanged
OpenAI model hits max_tokens → persisted stop_reason is 'max_tokens', not 'end_turn'
OPENAI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS env var set to 16384 → ProviderManager::max_output_tokens() returns 16384, not hardcoded 4096

rules.text: stop_reason must be propagated from the SSE stream through FinalResponse to the agent loop — never discarded
Each provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) must normalize its wire-format stop reason into the codelet StopReason enum
Persistence must store the real stop_reason — never hardcode end_turn
When stop_reason is max_tokens and no tool calls were made, a user-visible truncation warning must be shown in the TUI
Truncated tool calls must produce an informative error message identifying the truncation as the cause — not just generic JSON parse failure
OpenAI max_output_tokens must read runtime env var value, not compile-time constant

PROV-039.title: stop_reason lost in streaming — output truncation silently treated as normal completion

userStory.action: see when the LLM response was truncated due to max_tokens
userStory.benefit: I know the response is incomplete and can ask the model to continue

architectureNotes.text: Recovery logic goes in stream_loop.rs at the point where truncated tool call errors are received — after the PROV-039 enriched error is emitted from the provider layer but before it's sent back to the model

Key detection point: the error message from PROV-039 contains 'Tool call truncated due to output token limit' — use this as the reliable signal to trigger recovery. The truncation counter should be a turn-level variable in stream_loop (reset each new user prompt).

Reference VTCode's 6-layer recovery pipeline (architecture note [0] on PROV-039). Our implementation is simpler — we only need layer 3 (dispatch error responses with recovery guidance) and layer 5 (turn-level retry budget). We don't need layers 1-2 (JSON extraction) since we rely on PROV-039's existing detection.

The recovery prompt is injected as a new user message via prompt_streaming_with_history_and_hook() — this starts a fresh stream with the recovery guidance as the prompt. The model receives the structured alternative strategies naturally and can reformulate its approach.

PROV-040.description:
When the LLM hits max_tokens while generating a tool call (especially Write with large content), the truncated JSON is detected by PROV-039 but the error is sent back to the model as-is. The model then retries the same oversized write, hits the same limit, and enters an infinite failure loop.

The system needs a recovery layer that:
1. Detects truncated tool calls (stop_reason=max_tokens + JSON parse failure) — already done by PROV-039
2. Instead of returning a raw error, injects a structured recovery prompt telling the model to break the content into chunks (e.g., write first half, then append second half using Edit or sequential Writes)
3. For Write specifically: suggests the model use bash to write large files, or split into multiple Write calls with append semantics
4. Applies across all providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) since the recovery logic sits in the stream loop, not in provider-specific code
5. Has a retry budget (e.g., max 2 retries) to prevent infinite loops even if chunking still exceeds limits

Reference: VTCode's ContinuationController pattern for task-level continuation after truncation.

examples.text: Model tries to Write a 50KB file → hits max_tokens → truncated tool call error includes recovery instruction: 'Your Write tool call was truncated. Use Bash with cat/heredoc to write large files, or split into multiple smaller Write calls.' → model retries using Bash heredoc → file written successfully

Model tries to Write a 50KB file → hits max_tokens → recovery instruction sent → model retries same oversized Write → hits max_tokens again → retry budget exhausted → error displayed to user: 'Tool call truncated twice, retry budget exhausted. Manually break this write into smaller chunks.'
Model completes a normal Write of 5KB file → no truncation → no recovery prompt injected → behavior identical to pre-PROV-040 baseline
Gemini model hits max_tokens on a Bash tool call → same recovery logic fires as Anthropic — provider-agnostic behavior verified
Model hits max_tokens on a text-only response (no tool call) → existing PROV-039 warning displayed → no recovery prompt injected (text truncation doesn't need chunking strategy)

rules.text: When a tool call is truncated (max_tokens + JSON parse failure), the error sent back to the model MUST include a structured recovery instruction — not just the raw error
The recovery instruction must tell the model to use an alternative strategy: use Bash with heredoc/echo, split into multiple smaller Write calls, or use Write+Edit append pattern
A truncation retry budget (max 2 consecutive truncation errors per turn) must prevent infinite retry loops — after budget exhausted, report failure to user
Recovery logic must live in the stream loop (provider-agnostic) — not in provider-specific streaming code — so it works identically for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini
The recovery prompt must include the truncated tool name and partial arguments so the model knows exactly what failed and can reformulate
Normal end_turn completions and non-truncation errors must be completely unaffected by the recovery logic

PROV-040.title: Truncated tool call recovery — auto-chunk large writes and retry on max_tokens

userStory.action: write large files without hitting an infinite truncation error loop
userStory.benefit: I can complete file operations reliably regardless of content size

architectureNotes.text: VTCode's 6-level ReasoningEffortLevel enum (None/Minimal/Low/Medium/High/XHigh) maps to provider-specific values: Anthropic → explicit token counts (1024/4096/8192/16384/32768), OpenAI → effort strings (low/medium/high/xhigh), Gemini → thinking_level strings (minimal/low/medium/high). Our implementation should mirror this abstraction.

Detection heuristic: FinishReason::Length + (reasoning_tokens > 0 && output_tokens < threshold). Threshold should be configurable but default to ~50 tokens. The key insight is that thinking exhaustion produces a response where the model 'thought a lot but said almost nothing'.

Recovery logic should live in the stream loop (provider-agnostic layer) — same location as PROV-040's truncated tool call recovery. The thinking exhaustion counter and session-level reasoning effort tracker are turn-level and session-level state respectively.

VTCode uses budget clamping as primary prevention: effective_budget = min(budget, max_tokens - 100). This should be our first line of defense too, but unlike VTCode, we add active recovery as a second line when prevention fails.

For context preservation: VTCode's SessionMemoryEnvelope pattern (grounded facts + task summary + touched files + history artifact path) is the gold standard. On thinking exhaustion near context limits, persist a memory envelope BEFORE retrying, ensuring recovery via SessionSearch even if the retry fails.

Anthropic Opus 4.6 uses ThinkingConfig::Adaptive (model self-manages budget). For Adaptive models, the retry strategy should NOT try to set explicit budgets — instead, inject a system hint like 'Keep your thinking concise for this request' and rely on the model's own budget management.

PROV-041.description:
When the LLM exhausts its thinking/reasoning token budget, the response terminates with FinishReason::Length (or equivalent). Unlike regular output truncation (PROV-039/PROV-040 which handle tool call truncation), thinking token exhaustion has unique characteristics:

1. The model may produce NO useful output at all — it spent all tokens thinking and had nothing left for the actual response
2. The thinking content itself may be valuable context that shouldn't be lost
3. Different providers signal this differently and have different budget control mechanisms
4. Context is lost because the truncated turn consumes context window space without producing useful output

The system needs:
1. Provider-specific detection of thinking token exhaustion vs regular output truncation
2. Recovery that preserves the thinking content and re-issues the request with adjusted budget (lower thinking, higher output)
3. Context preservation using SessionSearch/session history when hitting overall context window limits
4. A general solution that works across Anthropic (ThinkingConfig budget_tokens/Adaptive), OpenAI (reasoning effort levels), Gemini (thinking_level), and local models (TagStreamSanitizer <think> extraction)
5. Graceful degradation: if thinking exhaustion keeps happening, progressively reduce thinking budget or disable thinking entirely for the remainder of the task

Reference: VTCode's approach is purely preventive (budget clamping to max_tokens-100, Adaptive thinking for Opus 4.6) with NO explicit recovery mechanism for thinking exhaustion. This card aims to go beyond VTCode by adding active recovery.

examples.text: Anthropic model with thinking_budget=8192 and max_tokens=16000 spends all 8192 tokens on thinking → response has 7800 thinking tokens, 12 output tokens → detected as thinking exhaustion → retry with thinking_budget=4096, max_tokens=16000 → model produces full response successfully

OpenAI model with reasoning_effort=High hits length finish_reason → response has reasoning_content but empty choices[0].message.content → detected as thinking exhaustion → retry with reasoning_effort=Medium → model produces complete response

Gemini model generates long <think>...</think> block consuming most of MAX_TOKENS → regular content after </think> is truncated → detected as thinking exhaustion → retry with thinking_level downgraded from 'high' to 'medium' → model produces useful response

Model hits thinking exhaustion → retry 1 with reduced budget → hits thinking exhaustion again → retry 2 with further reduced budget → still exhausts → retry budget exhausted → thinking disabled entirely for this turn → model produces response without reasoning → warning shown to user
Model completes normally with thinking (FinishReason::Stop, has both reasoning and content) → no thinking exhaustion detection fires → zero overhead → behavior identical to pre-PROV-041 baseline

Context window at 92% utilization when thinking exhaustion occurs → system persists full conversation to session archive BEFORE retrying → thinking-reduced retry triggers compaction → even if session crashes during compaction, the pre-compaction state is recoverable via SessionSearch

Thinking exhaustion happens 3 times across different turns (not retries) → session-level reasoning effort auto-downgrades from High to Medium → user notified 'Reasoning effort automatically reduced to Medium due to repeated thinking budget exhaustion' → subsequent turns use Medium reasoning

Regular output truncation (model has useful content but hit token limit, no thinking content) → NOT classified as thinking exhaustion → handled by existing PROV-039/PROV-040 truncation recovery instead

rules.text: When a response terminates with FinishReason::Length AND the response has reasoning/thinking content but empty or near-empty output content, the system MUST detect this as 'thinking exhaustion' (distinct from regular output truncation)
On thinking exhaustion detection, the system MUST preserve the captured thinking content (reasoning field from LLMResponse) as context for the retry — not discard it

On retry after thinking exhaustion, the system MUST reduce the thinking budget (e.g., halve it or drop one ReasoningEffortLevel) and increase max_tokens for output — the ratio must shift toward output

A thinking exhaustion retry budget (max 2 consecutive thinking-exhaustion retries per turn) MUST prevent infinite retry loops — after budget exhausted, use the best partial response available or disable thinking for the turn

Detection and recovery MUST work for all providers: Anthropic (ThinkingDelta + max_tokens stop_reason), OpenAI (reasoning_content + length finish_reason), Gemini (TagStreamSanitizer <think> extraction + MAX_TOKENS), and local models (TagStreamSanitizer + length)

When context window utilization exceeds 90%, the system MUST persist conversation state via session archive BEFORE any compaction or retry — ensuring context can be recovered even if the session is interrupted
Normal completions (FinishReason::Stop, FinishReason::ToolCalls) MUST be completely unaffected — zero performance overhead on the happy path
If thinking exhaustion happens repeatedly across turns (not just retries), the system MUST progressively downgrade reasoning effort for subsequent turns: XHigh→High→Medium→Low→Minimal→None

PROV-041.title: Thinking token exhaustion recovery — detect budget depletion and preserve context across all providers

userStory.action: have thinking token exhaustion detected and recovered from automatically
userStory.benefit: my agent doesn't lose context or produce empty responses when the model spends too many tokens reasoning

PROV-042.description: Parent card for a set of improvements to codelet's stream loop resilience, drawing on patterns observed in the VTCode codebase. Currently codelet handles semantic errors well (thinking exhaustion, truncation recovery) but lacks operational resilience patterns: no retry backoff, no circuit breaker, no error classification, no history persistence before compaction, no response loop detection. VTCode implements all of these. This parent tracks the implementation of each pattern as a separate child work unit.
PROV-042.title: Stream loop resilience — structured retry, circuit breaker, error classification, and operational hardening inspired by VTCode patterns

PROV-043.description: Add a RetryPolicy with exponential backoff to PROV-040 (truncation) and PROV-041 (thinking exhaustion) retry paths. Currently both retry immediately with zero delay, which can worsen rate limit or overloaded-server situations. VTCode uses a RetryPolicy struct with configurable initial_delay, max_delay, multiplier, and jitter.
PROV-043.title: Structured retry with exponential backoff for stream loop recovery paths

PROV-044.description: Add an ApiFailureTracker to Session that counts consecutive API failures across turns. After N consecutive failures (default 3), apply exponential backoff before the next API call. Reset counter on success. VTCode implements this as a simple struct with record_failure(), reset(), should_circuit_break(), and backoff_duration() methods.
PROV-044.title: Circuit breaker and API failure tracker for cross-turn error resilience

PROV-045.description: Replace the scattered is_prompt_too_long_error(), is_truncated_tool_call_error(), is_thinking_exhaustion(), is_image_content_error(), and is_compaction_cancelled() string-matching functions with a single StreamErrorKind enum and classify_stream_error() function. VTCode uses ErrorCategory + ErrorCode enums with typed downcasting for clean error routing.
PROV-045.title: Stream error classification enum replacing string-matching detection functions

PROV-046.description: Before execute_compaction() replaces conversation with a summary, write the full conversation to .codelet/history/session_{id}_{turn}.jsonl. Include the file path in the compaction summary message so agents can recover lost details via SessionSearch/Read. VTCode implements this in persist_history_before_summarization() with a HistoryFileManager that handles JSONL serialization and file rotation.
PROV-046.title: Persist full conversation history to JSONL before compaction

PROV-047.description: Detect when the model enters a repetitive response loop (same assistant message 2+ times consecutively). Normalize whitespace and compare against last 2 assistant messages in session.messages. Emit a warning and break the loop. VTCode implements this in check_for_response_loop() with TaskOutcome::LoopDetected.
PROV-047.title: Response loop detection — break infinite assistant repetition cycles

PROV-048.description: Track consecutive streaming failures separately from general API errors. After MAX_STREAMING_FAILURES, log a diagnostic warning about streaming reliability. After a cooldown period, reset the counter. VTCode tracks streaming_failures and streaming_last_failure on the AgentRunner, with a STREAMING_COOLDOWN_SECS constant for re-enablement.
PROV-048.title: Streaming failure tracking with cooldown and diagnostic warnings

PROV-049.description: When API returns a rate limit error (429), parse the Retry-After header value and sleep for that duration before retrying transparently. Currently rate limit errors terminate the stream and are reported to the user. VTCode implements parse_retry_after_header() which handles both integer and float seconds, and the RetryDecision uses retry_after to override computed backoff.
PROV-049.title: Parse Retry-After header for transparent rate limit recovery

PROV-050.description: Add a find_safe_split_point() function to compaction logic that walks backward from the proposed split point to ensure no tool call is separated from its tool result. VTCode implements HistoryValidationReport with missing_outputs and orphan_outputs detection, and uses find_safe_split_point() during summarization to preserve tool call/output pairing invariants.
PROV-050.title: Split-safe compaction — ensure tool call/result pairs are never broken

architectureNotes.text: Uses a CacheOptimizationFacade in codelet/providers/src/cache_optimization.rs to encapsulate session affinity header logic. Facade pattern separates cache optimization concern from provider construction. SessionAffinityConfig struct holds session_id + optional env var override. get_openai(session_id) threads UUID through to from_api_key_with_options which delegates header building to the facade. No rig-core changes needed — uses existing http_headers() API.

PROV-051.description: Add x-session-affinity header support to OpenAI-compatible provider when using Fireworks.ai endpoints, maximizing prompt cache hit rates and reducing latency/cost.

examples.text: User sets OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.fireworks.ai/inference and OPENAI_API_KEY=fw-xxx, starts a session — requests include x-session-affinity header with the session UUID, Fireworks routes all requests to the same replica, cache hit rate is high
User sets OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8888 (vLLM local server) — requests are sent normally, header is present but ignored by vLLM, no behavior change

rules.text: When OPENAI_BASE_URL points to a Fireworks.ai endpoint, an x-session-affinity header MUST be sent with every request
The session affinity value MUST be stable per codelet session (use the session UUID)
The header MUST be set at client construction time via rig's http_headers() so it applies to all requests (both streaming and non-streaming)
Send unconditionally for all custom base URL endpoints — the header is harmless, servers that don't understand it will ignore it
Cached token counts from Fireworks responses MUST be captured in usage metrics (already handled by rig-core's PromptTokensDetails.cached_tokens deserialization)
The session affinity identifier can optionally be configured via OPENAI_SESSION_AFFINITY env var, defaulting to the codelet session UUID
Thread the session_id from the caller into get_openai() — the session UUID is already available at all call sites (session.id in NAPI, uuid::Uuid::new_v4() in CLI)

PROV-051.title: Fireworks.ai Session Affinity for Prompt Cache Optimization

userStory.action: have session affinity headers sent with API requests
userStory.benefit: prompt cache hit rates are maximized, reducing latency and cost

PROV-052.description: Address multiple gaps in fspec's Z.AI GLM provider integration that hurt tool-calling accuracy and limit flexibility. Identified through comparison with the official GLM-5 reference repository (zai-org/GLM-5). Key areas: (1) inconsistent tool naming — 9 of 16 tools use PascalCase instead of GLM-preferred snake_case, (2) unused thinking_config parameter, (3) hardcoded max_output_tokens/context_window with no env var overrides, (4) supports_reasoning() won't match GLM-5 models, (5) no tool_choice configuration, (6) no ZAI web search facade, (7) hardcoded generation config.

PROV-053.description: Add a new GitHub Copilot provider to fspec, authenticated via the GitHub OAuth device flow, using the stored access token as a Bearer credential against the Copilot API (api.githubcopilot.com or copilot-api.<enterprise-domain>). Covers login UX, token storage, model catalog fetching, chat/completions and responses API routing, and provider-options mapping. Research sourced from anomalyco/opencode — see attached research document for full technical citations.

items.text: Prompt for enterprise URL when enterprise selected
Begin polling once device code is issued
Continue polling on authorization_pending after interval+3s
Increase polling interval by 5s on slow_down per RFC 8628 §3.5
Persist credential to disk on successful access token issuance
Refresh model catalog after successful credential persistence
Merge remote model catalog with static catalog after fetch
Inject Copilot-Vision-Request header when vision request is detected
Force x-initiator: agent header when agent context detected
Route GPT-5+ models (except gpt-5-mini) to /responses endpoint
Round-trip reasoning_opaque field across multi-turn conversation
Strip lowercase authorization and x-api-key headers before request
Filter out models where model_picker_enabled is false
Resolve enterprise base URL when enterprise URL persisted

items.concern: Should we register our own GitHub OAuth App or reuse opencode's public client_id Ov23li8tweQw6odWQebz? Reusing couples our TOS to theirs.
Use new ~/.fspec/credentials/copilot_auth.json (slice 1 recommendation) or unify into existing credentials.json? Current credentials.json is API-key-only.
How permissive should normalizeDomain be? Strip scheme and trailing slash like opencode, or stricter URL validation?
Should the GitHub access token be stored in the macOS keychain instead of a 0600 file for defense-in-depth?
opencode polls forever. Should we cap the device-flow wait at e.g. 15 minutes and return a clean timeout error?
How is the user informed when GitHub revokes a token mid-session? opencode lets the next API call fail. We could detect 401 and prompt re-login.
opencode has zero retry logic on the data plane. Should we add exponential backoff for 429/503 to be a better citizen?
opencode fetches /models on every loader call. Should we cache with stale-while-revalidate, refresh on TUI open, or something else?
Does the rig crate support OpenAI's /responses endpoint, or do we hand-roll a raw reqwest path for GPT-5+ models?
opencode's chat.headers hook reads parts and parentID via SDK. fspec has no equivalent session model. How do we promote x-initiator: agent for compaction/sub-agent contexts?
items.text: compaction detection without opencode session model

items.concern: GitHub Copilot TOS restricts usage to approved editor integrations. Document the risk in foundation.json before shipping.
Not all GHE installs have copilot-api.<domain> configured. How do we surface DNS verification failure cleanly?
opencode date-gates xhigh on release_date >= 2025-12-04. Where do we get release_date from? Hard-code or fetch?
opencode vendors a 20-file fork of @ai-sdk/openai-compatible. fspec uses Rust + rig. Should we copy the rig OpenAI client and patch it, or hand-roll just the chat/responses endpoints we need?

PROV-055.title: GitHub Copilot HTTP middleware, facades & endpoint routing

userStory.action: send chat requests to Copilot models from the codelet TUI

architectureNotes.text: Wire format is always OpenAI-shaped — reuse existing OpenAIFspecFacade for wire translation; only the reasoning-variant selection and options transformation differs per family

CopilotModelCatalogService lives at codelet/providers/src/copilot/models.rs; exposes fetch_models(base_url, token) -> Result<Vec<ModelInfo>>; the function calls /models, parses the response, filters by model_picker_enabled, and maps each entry to ModelInfo via build_model_info — there is NO merge step and NO existing parameter

CopilotProvider::list_models() (from PROV-055) calls CopilotModelCatalogService.fetch_models() and returns the resulting Vec<ModelInfo>; the TUI model picker consumes this list via the existing provider registry — no models.dev fallback, no static catalog merge

Provider-level zero-retention enforcement (store: false) lives at codelet/providers/src/copilot/provider_options.rs as a single pure function apply_store_false(options) that is called for ALL Copilot requests irrespective of model — there is no per-model branching

Reasoning-variant emission lives at codelet/providers/src/copilot/models.rs as part of build_model_info(remote_entry) → ModelInfo: it copies capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort verbatim from the response into ModelInfo.reasoning_variants (Vec<String>); empty/missing → empty Vec; no transformation, no filtering, no family branching

PROV-056.description: Implement CopilotModelCatalogService that fetches the Copilot /models endpoint and exposes the response verbatim as a Vec<ModelInfo>. The /models endpoint is the SOLE source of every model field — there is NO hardcoded catalog, NO models.dev fallback, NO static model list, NO hardcoded small-model priority, NO per-model special-casing in code. Provider options enforce store: false at the provider level (zero retention, all Copilot requests). Reasoning effort variants per model are emitted directly from capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort in the response (one variant per tier, in order); if the array is missing or empty, no variants are emitted. sdkKey() mapping @ai-sdk/github-copilot → copilot. Wire-format-specific extras (e.g. Responses-API metadata for GPT-5 family) are handled at request time by the wire-format facades from PROV-055 based on capabilities.family from the response — not at catalog time. Integrates with the TUI model picker via CopilotProvider::list_models() from PROV-055. Parent: PROV-053.

examples.text: /models response includes a model whose capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort is ['low','medium','high','xhigh']; the catalog exposes that model with exactly 4 reasoning variants in tier order low→medium→high→xhigh, each carrying only (model_id, reasoning_effort_tier)

/models response includes a model with no capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort field at all; the catalog exposes that model with zero reasoning variants — no fallback inference, no synthesized tiers
/models response includes a model whose capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort is an empty array []; the catalog exposes that model with zero reasoning variants

/models response includes a model whose version field is 'whatever-model-2025-09-15'; the catalog exposes that model with release_date '2025-09-15' (derived purely by stripping the '{id}-' prefix from the version returned by the endpoint — no model-specific knowledge)

/models response returns one entry with model_picker_enabled=true and another entry with model_picker_enabled=false; the catalog exposed to callers contains only the entry whose model_picker_enabled is true

First fetch from /models returns two models; the second fetch from /models returns only one of them; after the second fetch the catalog contains only that one model — the missing model is gone, with no merging or fallback to the prior fetch

rules.text: CopilotModelCatalogService fetches /models from the configured base URL (github.com or enterprise), parses the Zod-equivalent schema, and times out at 5000ms with a single attempt (no retry)
release_date is parsed by stripping the `{id}-` prefix from version (e.g. `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` -> `2024-05-13`); if version does not start with id, use version verbatim
sdkKey() mapping: @ai-sdk/github-copilot -> copilot; providerOptions keyed under github-copilot are remapped to the copilot key when building outgoing requests
store: false is forced in provider options when providerID=github-copilot or api.npm=@ai-sdk/github-copilot (zero-retention enforcement with client-side reasoning replay)
The Copilot /models endpoint is the SOLE source of truth for the model catalog: there is no merge with models.dev or any prior cache; each fetch fully replaces the catalog
Only remote models with model_picker_enabled=true are included in the catalog returned to callers; entries with model_picker_enabled=false are filtered out

ModelInfo build mapping reads exclusively from the remote response: api.id from id, name from name, family from capabilities.family, limits from capabilities.limits, capabilities from capabilities.supports, release_date derived from version; cost is hard-coded to zero; providerID is github-copilot; api.npm is @ai-sdk/github-copilot
If capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort is missing or empty for a model, no reasoning variants are emitted (no id-pattern fallback, no date-gating heuristic)

Reasoning variants per model are emitted directly from capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort in the /models response: one variant per array entry, in the same order; each variant carries (model_id, reasoning_effort_tier) only — wire-format-specific metadata (e.g. Responses-API extras for GPT-5 family) is added at request time by the PROV-055 wire facades based on capabilities.family from the response, not at catalog time

PROV-057.description: PROV-053 through PROV-056 were marked done but the GitHub Copilot provider does not work end-to-end. Investigation by a 5-agent parallel deep search identified three independent layers of brokenness: (1) wrong OAuth client_id (uses opencode's `Ov23li8tweQw6odWQebz` instead of the well-known Copilot client `Iv1.b507a08c87ecfe98`), (2) missing token-exchange step against `/copilot_internal/v2/token` so the GitHub OAuth `gho_*` token is sent directly to `api.githubcopilot.com` and always returns 401, and (3) no `"github-copilot"` arm in the `run_with_provider!` macro at `codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs:5019-5073` so even after fixing auth the agent loop falls through to `_ => Unsupported provider`. Plus a stale credential cache bug where `ProviderManager` snapshots `ProviderCredentials::detect()` once and never re-detects after OAuth login writes the file. See attached investigation document for the full call chain, wiring matrix, and ordered fix plan.

PROV-058.description: fspec's Rust agent core (codelet) makes LLM API calls through GitHub Copilot's proxy. Currently it does not send any prompt caching hints on these connections. Both the official Copilot CLI and opencode use copilot_cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'} on messages and tools to get server-side prompt caching through the Copilot proxy. We need to add equivalent support so that multi-turn conversations benefit from cached prefixes, reducing latency and token costs.

architectureNotes.text: The existing PROV-055 three-layer architecture (CopilotRequestClassifier → CopilotHeaderFacade → CopilotHttpClient) is correct and does not need changes. The fix injects metadata.mode='agent' into the request body at the call sites that construct API requests.

Fix points: (1) CopilotProvider needs an is_agent parameter on complete_with_tools to inject additional_params metadata. (2) The LlmProvider trait needs to propagate an agent-mode flag. (3) The stream loop / agent loop must track iteration number (0=user-initiated, 1+=agent). (4) DeepSearch, AgentManager, and scheduler must mark their sessions as agent-initiated.

Implementation diverged from arch note[1]: instead of adding is_agent to complete_with_tools/LlmProvider, the classifier was enhanced with tool-result heuristic (role=tool) and DeepSearch injects metadata.mode=agent via additional_params. Cleaner — no trait changes needed.

PROV-059.description: The CopilotRequestClassifier/CopilotHeaderFacade/CopilotHttpClient three-layer infrastructure (PROV-055) is fully built and tested, but no production code path ever sets metadata.mode = 'agent' in the request body. This means every Copilot API request — including tool-call follow-ups, DeepSearch sub-agents, compaction continuations, subordinate sessions, and scheduled jobs — is sent with x-initiator: user, consuming premium quota unnecessarily. This mirrors the exact same bug reported in opencode issue #8030.

PROV-060.description:
Extract shared OAuth patterns across Copilot, Codex, and Claude providers into generic Rust building blocks (CredentialStore, RefreshingHttpClient, DeviceCodeFlow

, OAuthCallbackServer), then add Rhai scripting integration to enable user-defined custom OAuth providers without recompilation. Hybrid approach: native providers keep full Rust performance, custom providers use sandboxed .rhai scripts. Estimated ~750 lines of duplication to eliminate across 3 providers.

examples.text: Copilot, Codex, and Claude credential read/write all go through CredentialStore<T> with provider-specific T types, eliminating 3 separate read/write function pairs
RefreshingCodexClient and RefreshingClaudeClient are replaced by RefreshingHttpClient<CodexTokenStrategy> and RefreshingHttpClient<ClaudeTokenStrategy> sharing the same double-check locking logic
Copilot and Codex device code polling loops are replaced by DeviceCodeFlow<CopilotDeviceCode> and DeviceCodeFlow<CodexDeviceCode> sharing the same RFC 8628 polling logic
A .rhai script can define build_authorization_request, exchange_code, refresh_token, poll_for_token, needs_refresh and the sandboxed engine executes them via spawn_blocking
All 103+ unit tests and 49+ integration tests in codelet/providers continue to pass after refactoring

rules.text: A generic CredentialStore<T> must handle read/write/resolve for any provider's auth JSON file
A generic RefreshingHttpClient<S: TokenStrategy> must unify the double-check locking token refresh pattern used by Codex and Claude
A generic DeviceCodeFlow<P: DeviceCodeProvider> must unify the RFC 8628 device authorization grant polling loops used by Copilot and Codex
A generic OAuthCallbackServer<H: CodeExchangeHandler> must unify the local HTTP PKCE callback servers used by Codex and Claude
All existing provider tests (unit + integration) must continue to pass after refactoring — zero regressions
New shared oauth/ module files must each be under 300 lines
A sandboxed Rhai engine (Engine::new_raw) with operation limits, call depth limits, and registered building block modules must be provided for scripted OAuth flows
Rhai building block modules (http, crypto, json, oauth) must be registered so scripts can call http::post, crypto::sha256, json::parse, oauth::generate_pkce etc.
A ScriptedOAuthProvider that loads .rhai files and executes build_authorization_request, exchange_code, refresh_token, poll_for_token, needs_refresh must be provided
Rhai scripts run synchronously inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking; HTTP calls in scripts use ureq (sync), not reqwest (async)
The engine factory must accept extensible module lists (build_sandboxed_engine(modules)) to support PROV-061 adding time::, env:: etc.
All clippy warnings and errors across the entire workspace must be resolved, regardless of origin

PROV-061.description:
Implement a new 'custom' provider type that uses Rhai scripts to control the FULL provider lifecycle:

1. **HTTP Request/Response** (7 required Rhai functions): endpoint URLs, HTTP headers, request body construction, response deserialization, stop reason mapping, tool call extraction, streaming SSE parsing, and error handling.

2. **System Prompts** (3 optional Rhai functions): identity prefix, preamble transformation, and API-format system prompt construction. Allows custom providers to define how system prompts are formatted (plain string, array with cache_control blocks, etc.) — replacing hardcoded Rust SystemPromptFacade structs.

3. **Tool Facades** (2 optional Rhai functions): custom tool names, parameter schemas, and parameter mapping. Allows custom providers to define what tools the LLM sees (e.g., `read_file` vs `Read`) and how parameters map to internal types — replacing hardcoded Rust ToolFacade structs. Includes `define_tools()` for tool definitions and `map_tool_params()` for custom parameter transformation, plus `tool_style` presets for common patterns (claude, openai, gemini, codex).

Users define a .rhai script + JSON config to create providers for ANY LLM API without recompiling. Built on the shared OAuth building blocks from PROV-060.

examples.text: Developer creates ~/.fspec/providers/my-llm.json with name, base_url, auth.type='bearer', and models config → provider is auto-discovered and selectable
Custom Rhai script defines build_request() that converts messages to OpenAI-compatible format → HTTP POST sent with correct body
Custom Rhai script defines parse_response() that extracts tool_calls from response → tool calls correctly parsed and executed
Custom Rhai script defines parse_stream_chunk() for SSE events → streaming text appears incrementally in the terminal
Rhai script has a syntax error in build_request() → clear error message shown at provider load time, not at request time
Rhai script's parse_response() throws a runtime error → ProviderError::Api returned with script error details, no crash
Custom provider defines identity_prefix() returning 'You are MyBot' → system prompt starts with 'You are MyBot' prefix
Custom provider defines format_system_prompt() returning #{format:'array', blocks:[...]} → API receives structured array with cache_control metadata
Custom provider does NOT define any system prompt functions → defaults used: plain string, fspec guidance prepended, no prefix
Custom provider defines define_tools() returning [{name:'read_file', maps_to:'file:read', ...}] → LLM sees 'read_file' tool, calls routed to ReadTool internally
Custom provider defines map_tool_params() that renames 'filepath' to 'file_path' → custom param names transparently mapped to internal types
Custom provider config sets tool_style:'openai' without define_tools() → snake_case tool names (read_file, write_file, etc.) auto-generated
Custom provider defines define_tools() with only file:read and bash targets → LLM only sees read and execute tools, no search/web/ls tools exposed
map_tool_params() returns () for a tool → default mapping used, parameter names matched directly to Internal*Params fields
Custom provider's transform_preamble() references config.resolved_tools to list available tool names in system prompt → system prompt mentions custom tool names, not internal names

rules.text: A custom provider is defined by a JSON config file + a .rhai script, located in ~/.fspec/providers/ (user-global) or .fspec/providers/ (project-local)
The Rhai script MUST define 7 required functions for HTTP lifecycle: build_request, build_headers, build_url, parse_response, parse_stream_chunk, build_stream_request, map_error
The Rhai script MAY define 3 optional system prompt functions: identity_prefix(config), transform_preamble(config, preamble, fspec_guidance), format_system_prompt(config, preamble, fspec_guidance)

The Rhai script MAY define 2 optional tool facade functions: define_tools(config) returning tool definitions with maps_to targets, and map_tool_params(config, tool_name, maps_to, params) for custom parameter transformation
If system prompt functions are not defined, defaults apply: no identity prefix, fspec guidance prepended to preamble, plain string format
If define_tools() is not defined, the tool set falls back to a tool_style config preset ('claude', 'openai', 'gemini', 'codex') with 'claude' as default
Tool facades use maps_to string identifiers (file:read, file:write, file:edit, bash, search:grep, search:glob, ls, web_search:search, fspec, bridge, exec:run, hitl) to target internal tool types
The JSON config defines provider metadata (name, base_url, auth), model configs (context_window, max_output_tokens, supports_*), and optional system_prompt/tool settings
Auth supports bearer, api_key_header, oauth_device_code, oauth_pkce, and custom (Rhai-scriptable) types, integrating with PROV-060 shared OAuth building blocks
Rhai scripts run sandboxed (Engine::new_raw) with operation limits and only have access to registered building block modules (http, json, crypto, oauth, time, env)
Streaming uses Rhai only at the SSE-event level (not per-byte) — SSE frame parsing stays in Rust, Rhai interprets each data payload
Rhai script errors are caught and mapped to ProviderError — scripts must never panic or crash the process
Custom providers integrate with ProviderManager and are selectable via 'codelet model <provider-name>/<model-id>' syntax
format_system_prompt() can return either a plain string or a structured map with format:'array' and blocks containing cache_control metadata
map_tool_params() returning () (Rhai unit) means 'use default mapping' — parameter names are matched directly to Internal*Params fields

rules.text: RhaiCustomProvider implements the LlmProvider trait by delegating to the 7 required Rhai functions from PROV-062

An SSE event with finish_reason:'tool_calls' produces a StopReason(ToolUse) chunk
parse_stream_chunk returning {kind:'ignore'} for a keepalive event produces NO emitted chunk
When parse_stream_chunk throws a runtime error, the stream yields a single Err(ProviderError::Api) and then terminates
A streaming HTTP request returning 401 Unauthorized yields a single Err(ProviderError::Auth) before any Ok chunk
build_stream_request returns a body with 'stream':true which is sent to the wiremock SSE endpoint
End-to-end streaming against a wiremock SSE server returning 3 content deltas + 1 stop event yields 4 stream chunks (3 TextDelta, 1 StopReason) in order

rules.text: SSE frame parsing stays in Rust (reqwest + eventsource-stream); Rhai only interprets each data payload
parse_stream_chunk(config, event_data_string) returns a map describing one of: text_delta, tool_call_delta, stop, ignore, or error
build_stream_request(config, messages, tools, model) returns the JSON body used for streaming requests (may set stream:true flag)
SSE events with data == '[DONE]' are treated as end-of-stream without invoking parse_stream_chunk
Tool call deltas are accumulated in Rust: partial JSON input strings are concatenated until a tool call's arguments parse successfully
Each parse_stream_chunk runs inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking so the async runtime is never blocked
The streaming bridge yields an async Stream<Item = Result<StreamChunk, ProviderError>> where StreamChunk variants cover TextDelta, ToolCallStart, ToolCallArgsDelta, ToolCallComplete, StopReason
A parse_stream_chunk runtime error does NOT kill the whole stream — it is surfaced as a single StreamChunk Err and streaming terminates gracefully
HTTP error responses (>=400) during streaming requests still flow through map_error and produce ProviderError before any stream item is yielded

architectureNotes.text: RhaiSystemPromptFacade struct in codelet/providers/src/custom/system_prompt.rs; implements SystemPromptFacade trait from codelet/tools/src/facade/system_prompt.rs
OnceCell<&'static str> per facade instance caches the leaked identity_prefix so identity_prefix() can return Option<&'static str> as required by the trait
Defaults: identity_prefix=None; transform_preamble uses prepend_fspec_guidance from codelet/tools; format_for_api wraps transformed preamble in serde_json::Value::String

PROV-065.description: Implement RhaiSystemPromptFacade that implements the SystemPromptFacade trait and delegates to 3 optional Rhai functions: identity_prefix(config), transform_preamble(config, preamble, fspec_guidance), format_system_prompt(config, preamble, fspec_guidance). Includes support for plain string and structured array (with cache_control) return formats, and sensible defaults when functions are not defined.

examples.text: A script defining identity_prefix returning 'You are MyBot' yields facade.identity_prefix() == Some("You are MyBot")
A script without identity_prefix yields facade.identity_prefix() == None
With no transform_preamble defined, facade.transform_preamble('user text') returns FSPEC_WORKFLOW_GUIDANCE + '\n\n' + 'user text'
A script defining transform_preamble that returns 'PREFIX: ' + preamble yields facade.transform_preamble('body') == 'PREFIX: body'
A script without format_system_prompt produces facade.format_for_api('body') == JSON string '<fspec_guidance>\n\nbody'

A script defining format_system_prompt returning #{format:'array', blocks:[#{type:'text', text:'prefix'}, #{type:'text', text:'body', cache_control:#{type:'ephemeral'}}]} produces a JSON array with the blocks and cache_control preserved
A script defining format_system_prompt returning a plain string 'abc' produces facade.format_for_api('body') == JSON string 'abc'
facade.provider() returns the custom provider's name string matching ProviderConfig.name
A script throwing a runtime error from format_system_prompt causes facade.format_for_api to return a fallback JSON string rather than panicking

rules.text: RhaiSystemPromptFacade implements the SystemPromptFacade trait and delegates to 3 optional Rhai functions: identity_prefix, transform_preamble, format_system_prompt
If identity_prefix(config) is defined it returns a String that becomes the facade's identity prefix; otherwise no prefix is applied
If transform_preamble(config, preamble, fspec_guidance) is defined it returns the fully composed preamble; otherwise the default is fspec_guidance prepended to preamble
If format_system_prompt(config, preamble, fspec_guidance) is defined it returns either a plain string (String variant) or a structured map with format:'array' and blocks for API output
When format_system_prompt is not defined the default produces a plain JSON string containing fspec_guidance + preamble
When format_system_prompt returns a map with format='array' the facade produces a JSON array of block objects preserving cache_control metadata
All Rhai system prompt function invocations run inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking since facade methods are sync but must be safe from async contexts
Rhai runtime errors during system prompt formatting surface as facade errors that are converted to the upstream ProviderError pathway and do not panic
The identity_prefix() trait method returns Option<&'static str>; Rhai-returned strings are stored once via a OnceCell<&'static str> leak so the trait's static lifetime is upheld
provider() trait method returns the custom provider's name as a 'static leaked str derived from ProviderConfig.name

architectureNotes.text: Tool style presets (claude/openai/gemini/codex) are static lookup tables (lazy_static or Vec built per call) mapping preset name -> Vec<RhaiToolDef> with appropriate names and schemas

PROV-066.description: Implement RhaiToolFacadeAdapter — a single generic Rust struct implementing rig::Tool that adapts ALL Rhai-defined tools. Includes define_tools(config) for custom tool names/schemas, map_tool_params(config, tool_name, maps_to, params) for custom parameter transformation, maps_to routing to internal tool types, tool_style presets (claude, openai, gemini, codex), and tool visibility control.

examples.text: A script defining define_tools that returns a list including {name:'read_file', maps_to:'file:read', description:'...', parameters:{...}} produces a RhaiToolFacadeAdapter whose tool definition uses name 'read_file' with maps_to 'file:read'
A config with tool_style 'openai' and no define_tools produces default tools: read_file, write_file, edit_file, run_bash, grep_search, glob_search, list_dir, web_search
A config with no tool_style and no define_tools uses the 'claude' preset tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, LS, WebSearch)
A script defining map_tool_params that renames 'filepath' to 'file_path' produces InternalFileParams::Read with correct file_path when called
A script's map_tool_params returning () uses default field-by-field mapping (tool params JSON fed directly to serde_json::from_value for InternalFileParams)
A Rhai script whose define_tools throws a runtime error surfaces as a ToolError and falls back to the tool_style preset
A tool definition with unknown maps_to identifier 'mystery:foo' is rejected at resolve time with a clear error listing valid identifiers
Resolving tools stores the final list on a shared cache accessible via ProviderConfig.resolved_tools so system prompt functions can introspect tool names
A define_tools returning only file:read and bash maps_to entries exposes exactly two RhaiToolDef entries and thus two adapter instances to the LLM
RhaiToolFacadeAdapter.name() returns the tool name from the RhaiToolDef and .parameters_schema() returns the JSON schema that came from the Rhai script

rules.text: define_tools(config) Rhai function returns an array of tool definitions each with name, description, parameters (JSON schema), and maps_to string identifier
maps_to identifiers include: file:read, file:write, file:edit, bash, search:grep, search:glob, ls, web_search:search, fspec, bridge, exec:run, hitl
When define_tools is not defined, a tool_style preset (claude, openai, gemini, codex) determines the default tool set; default tool_style is claude
tool_style preset 'openai' yields snake_case tool names (read_file, write_file, edit_file, run_bash, etc.)
map_tool_params(config, tool_name, maps_to, params) Rhai function transforms LLM-supplied params; returning () (Rhai unit) means use default field-by-field mapping
If define_tools returns tools only for file:read and bash maps_to targets, the LLM only sees read and bash tools; other categories are hidden
Rhai errors in define_tools or map_tool_params are logged and surface as ToolError rather than panicking
Resolving the tool list caches the final Vec<RhaiToolDef> on ProviderConfig (resolved_tools) so system prompt functions can reference it

RhaiToolFacadeAdapter is a getters-only Rust struct (not a full rig::Tool impl) whose name()/parameters_schema()/maps_to() getters surface the RhaiToolDef so downstream code can bridge into rig-compatible request builders

A tool with maps_to search:grep and params {pattern: foo, path: src} dispatches to InternalSearchParams::Grep

PROV-081.description:
The codelet OpenAI provider (rig-core patches) silently drops reasoning/thinking tokens when talking to vLLM because vLLM emits reasoning on the field named `reasoning` while the client only looks for `reasoning_content` (the Z.AI/GLM convention).

=== STREAMING PATH ===
File: codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/streaming.rs
- Lines 35-44: `StreamingDelta` only declares `reasoning_content`, no `reasoning` field, no serde alias.
- Lines 297-303: consumption branch reads `delta.reasoning_content` only.
- Result: vLLM chunks `{delta:{reasoning:"..."}}` are deserialized into serde's ignored-extras bucket and silently lost.

=== NON-STREAMING PATH ===
File: codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs
- `Message::Assistant` (lines 113-144) exposes content / refusal / audio / name / tool_calls — NO reasoning field at all.
- `AssistantContent` enum (lines 180-185) has only `Text` and `Refusal` variants.
- Grep for `reasoning_content` returns zero matches; neither field is captured.
- `TryFrom<CompletionResponse>` extraction (lines 757-791) only emits Text and Refusal content plus tool calls.
- Today reasoning-token COUNTS are surfaced via `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` (lines 881-884, 948-950) but reasoning TEXT is dropped.
- Note: mod.rs:541 has a panic on the outbound direction refusing to serialize assistant-side reasoning — intentional, leave alone.

=== SERVER-SIDE EVIDENCE (vLLM) ===
- DeltaMessage.reasoning: vllm/entrypoints/openai/engine/protocol.py:258-262
- ChatMessage.reasoning: vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py:54-64
- Qwen3 parser: vllm/reasoning/qwen3_reasoning_parser.py (enable_thinking default True)
- include_reasoning request flag: protocol.py:184 (default true — don't override)

=== REQUEST-SIDE GUARDRAILS ===
Client MUST NOT send:
- `include_reasoning: false` (vLLM strips reasoning when set false)
- `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` (Qwen3 template-level kill-switch)

=== OUT OF SCOPE ===
- Image/multimodal delivery: moved to PROV-082 (spike). OpenAI provider DOES construct `{type:"image_url",image_url:{url:...}}` parts end-to-end; if images aren't reaching vLLM the root cause is elsewhere and needs reproduction first.
- vllm.sh `--limit-mm-per-prompt.image`: deployment runbook note tracked under PROV-082. Server launcher is in $HOME/vllm.sh, not in-project.

=== RESEARCH ATTACHMENT ===
spec/attachments/PROV-081/vllm-research.md (updated to reflect verification — see §3.1-3.2).

examples.text: Streaming chunk with only {delta:{content:'hello'}} and no reasoning fields streams through unchanged — no ReasoningDelta emitted, no error.

Non-streaming response {choices:[{message:{role:'assistant',reasoning:'analysis',content:'answer'}}]} deserializes successfully AND the caller-visible CompletionResponse exposes reasoning text 'analysis' alongside content 'answer'.
Non-streaming response {message:{role:'assistant',reasoning_content:'analysis',content:'answer'}} (Z.AI shape) also surfaces reasoning text 'analysis' to the caller — both field names work.
Non-streaming response with {message:{role:'assistant',content:'answer'}} (no reasoning fields) deserializes and works exactly as before — no reasoning surfaced, no error.
Outgoing request body serialized from a caller request contains NO `include_reasoning` key and NO `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` key (assert on the JSON payload sent to /chat/completions).

A user streams a chat completion from their local vLLM Qwen3 server and sees thinking tokens arrive in the reasoning channel before the final answer arrives in the content channel (previously: thinking tokens vanished silently).
A user pointed at a Z.AI/GLM endpoint still sees reasoning exactly as before — switching field names between servers is transparent, no regression.
A user talks to a hypothetical proxy that sends both field names at once; they see all of the reasoning concatenated, nothing is dropped.
A user talks to a plain OpenAI endpoint that emits no reasoning at all; their content streams exactly as before — no error, no empty reasoning noise.
A user issues a NON-streaming request to vLLM Qwen3 and the CompletionResponse they receive carries both the final answer content and the reasoning text (previously: only content returned).
A user issues a non-streaming request to a Z.AI endpoint and receives reasoning text via the `reasoning_content` field shape — same caller-visible surface.

A user inspects the HTTP request body sent for any Chat Completion and sees NO `include_reasoning: false` key and NO `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` key (the client never suppresses server-side reasoning).

rules.text: Streaming deserialization must accept both `reasoning` (vLLM) and `reasoning_content` (Z.AI/GLM) on the delta object and surface whichever arrives as a ReasoningDelta to the downstream stream.

Non-streaming assistant message must capture reasoning text from either `reasoning` or `reasoning_content` on the message object and expose it to callers (today neither field is captured — the extraction in TryFrom<CompletionResponse> only emits Text and Refusal).
If both `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` arrive on the same payload, their content must be concatenated (reasoning_content first, then reasoning) so nothing is silently lost.
Absence of both reasoning fields must not break normal content streaming or non-streaming responses (no regression on providers that don't emit reasoning).
Outgoing OpenAI Chat Completion request bodies must NOT contain `include_reasoning: false` (vLLM strips reasoning when this is false; default true is correct).

Outgoing OpenAI Chat Completion request bodies must NOT contain `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` on Qwen3 requests (this is the template-level kill-switch that suppresses <think> generation at the model level).

PROV-082.description:
SPIKE (diagnostic, not a bug yet). The initial PROV-081 diagnosis claimed images were not being sent to vLLM, but verification shows the OpenAI provider DOES construct and serialize `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"..."}}` content parts end-to-end (see codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs:196-216, 404-440, and round-trip unit test in client.rs:277-300).

Given that, the original user-reported symptom ("images never reach vLLM") points somewhere else. This task is to reproduce and diagnose.

## Suspects to eliminate
1. Caller never populates `message::UserContent::Image` — upstream message-building in codelet may not be routing image inputs into the provider at all.
2. Base64 inputs without `detail` silently return `ConversionError` at mod.rs:433-435 before serialization.
3. Responses API path (`responses_api/mod.rs`) is being used instead of Chat Completions.
4. Something in codelet's message plumbing strips images before they hit the provider.

## Acceptance for this spike
- Capture an actual HTTP request body sent to a local vLLM server from codelet when the user attaches an image (e.g., via a test harness + curl replay or tcpdump/mitmproxy).
- Determine: (a) does the body contain `image_url` parts, or (b) is it plain text only?
- If (a): the client side is fine. Write up a deployment-runbook note stating that `$HOME/vllm.sh` must be launched with `--limit-mm-per-prompt.image N` (currently missing) to allow multi-image prompts and close the spike.
- If (b): identify the exact point in codelet where the image was dropped and open a concrete bug work unit with the file/line/fix.

## Out of scope
- Any server-side vLLM changes.
- Editing $HOME/vllm.sh (not in project repo).
- Fixing reasoning tokens (tracked under PROV-081).

## Deliverables
- Wire capture attached to this work unit (spec/attachments/PROV-082/request-body.json).
- Written findings attachment (spec/attachments/PROV-082/findings.md) with conclusion and next-step recommendation.
- If a new bug is identified, create a follow-up work unit with precise scope.
PROV-082.title: Diagnose multimodal image delivery to vLLM Qwen3.5

architectureNotes.text: Fix location: codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs line 445-447. Current code returns ConversionError if detail is None. Replace `let detail = detail.ok_or(...)?` with `let detail = detail.unwrap_or_default();` to match the URL branch at line 431. `ImageDetail::default()` = `Auto` (verified at completion/mod.rs:218-228 where the enum is defined with #[serde(rename_all="lowercase")]). No other sites changed.

Tests live alongside existing PROV-081 tests in codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs (`#[cfg(test)] mod prov_083_tests`). Each test deserializes or constructs a rig message, runs it through `<Vec<openai::Message> as TryFrom<rig::Message>>::try_from`, and asserts either (a) success with the expected serialized `image_url.url` / `image_url.detail`, or (b) the specific pre-existing error for negative cases (media_type=None path).

PROV-083.description: Break A in PROV-082 diagnosis. codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs:445-447 requires ImageDetail to be Some(_) for DocumentSourceKind::Base64, returning ConversionError("OpenAI image URI must have image detail") otherwise. Every base64 image-building call in codelet passes detail=None (e.g., codelet/cli/src/interactive/multimodal.rs:63). Result: user-attached base64 images (bridge/Telegram/paste) never reach vLLM — the provider short-circuits with an error before building the HTTP request. Confirmed live via harness at codelet/patches/rig-core/examples/prov_082_wire_capture.rs (Scenario A). Fix: match the URL path at line 431 and use detail.unwrap_or_default() — OpenAI itself defaults detail to "auto".

examples.text: A user pastes an inline PNG into the CLI bridge. codelet builds a UserContent::Image with base64 data, media_type=image/png, detail=None. The Chat Completion request is POSTed successfully to the OpenAI-compatible server with `image_url.detail="auto"`.
A user pastes an inline JPEG with media_type=image/jpeg and detail=None — the server describes the image; no conversion error.
A user attaches a base64 image and explicitly requests high-detail processing (detail=High). The request is POSTed with `image_url.detail="high"` — explicit values are preserved.
A user attaches a URL image (not base64). Behaviour is unchanged — URL path already defaulted detail correctly, no regression from this fix.

A user attaches a base64 image but codelet failed to detect the media type (media_type=None, detail=None). Today this errors with "image MIME type required"; that behaviour is PRESERVED — we only fix the detail case, not the media-type case.

rules.text: Base64 UserContent::Image with detail=None must convert successfully into an OpenAI `image_url` content part whose `detail` defaults to Auto (mirrors the URL path behaviour at completion/mod.rs:431 and OpenAI's own default).
Base64 UserContent::Image with detail=Some(Low|High|Auto) must still honour the explicit value (backward-compat — existing callers that set detail must not regress).
The resulting OpenAI content part must use `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` as the `image_url.url` with the supplied `media_type` — no truncation, no re-encoding, no extra prefix.
If `media_type` is None, the existing ConversionError behaviour stays — we are only fixing the missing-detail case, not guessing MIME types.

architectureNotes.text: Reference implementation: the Responses API path at codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/responses_api/mod.rs:295-322 already handles mixed text+image tool results correctly using `ToolResultOutput::ContentItems`. We do NOT copy that wholesale (Chat Completions uses a different message shape), but the same pattern — iterate parts, partition into text vs image, emit appropriately — applies. Similar reference: Anthropic at anthropic/completion.rs:485-499 which uses content blocks.

Tests in codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs (`#[cfg(test)] mod prov_084_tests`). Each test builds a rig `message::Message::User { content: OneOrMany<UserContent::ToolResult(...)> }`, converts to Vec<Message> via `TryFrom`, and asserts the shape of the result: number of messages, roles, tool_call_ids, content parts. Serialize to JSON and spot-check `image_url.url` prefix. Reuse base64 decoding helpers from PROV-081's test infrastructure if needed.

Dependency on PROV-083: Once PROV-084 emits image_url parts for base64 tool-result images, those parts go through the same `UserContent::try_from` at mod.rs:416-470 → DocumentSourceKind::Base64 branch. If PROV-083 is NOT merged first, image tool results will fail with the PROV-083 ConversionError instead of Break B, and the follow-up user message will panic. PROV-084 must NOT land until PROV-083 is in.

Primary fix location: codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs. Legacy `impl TryFrom<message::ToolResult> for Message` at lines 393-414 is preserved and returns a single Message (now an unreachable path for image inputs — still returns ConversionError on image tool-result content). New helper `tool_result_to_messages(tool_result) -> Result<Vec<Message>, MessageError>` at lines 429-520 partitions text parts from image parts, returns [tool_message] for text-only and [tool_message, user_image_message] for image-bearing results. Integration site `TryFrom<OneOrMany<message::UserContent>> for Vec<Message>` at lines 611-653 routes the tool-results branch through this helper and flattens the per-tool-result Vec<Message> into the output Vec<Message> via extend.

PROV-084.description: Break B in PROV-082 diagnosis. codelet/patches/rig-core/src/providers/openai/completion/mod.rs:393-413 (`TryFrom<message::ToolResult> for Message`) only accepts ToolResultContent::Text and returns ConversionError("Tool result content does not support non-text") for ToolResultContent::Image. The rig streaming loop at codelet/patches/rig-core/src/agent/prompt_request/streaming.rs:200 correctly builds ToolResultContent::Image when the Read tool returns an image, but the provider rejects it. Confirmed live via harness (Scenario B). Affects: Read on PNG/JPG files, PDF visual-mode pages, MCP tools returning {"type":"image"}. Fix options: (a) split tool result into a tool-role message for text + follow-up user-role message with image_url content (OpenAI-compliant, matches Anthropic pattern at anthropic/completion.rs:485-499 and Responses API at responses_api/mod.rs:295-322), or (b) upgrade return type so a single ToolResult can produce Vec<Message>. vLLM accepts the split pattern — verified by task-context curl.

examples.text: A user asks the model to read a PNG file. codelet's Read tool returns an image tool result. The next Chat Completion request contains: (1) the tool-call assistant message, (2) a `tool` role message with a short placeholder like "[image attached below]" and the correct tool_call_id, (3) a `user` role message whose content array holds one `image_url` part pointing at `data:image/png;base64,...`. The model describes the image.
A user asks the model to read a text file. Read returns only text. The next request contains the existing single `tool` role message with the text content — no follow-up user message, no regression.

A user asks the model to read a PDF in visual mode with 3 pages. Read returns 3 image tool-result parts. The request contains: (1) tool-call, (2) one `tool` message with the tool_call_id, (3) one `user` message with 3 `image_url` parts in page order. The model describes all pages.

An MCP tool returns mixed content: a text summary and an image. The tool message carries the text summary; the follow-up user message carries the image. Ordering is text-first tool message, image-bearing user message immediately after.

rules.text: A rig `message::ToolResult` whose content contains any `ToolResultContent::Image` must convert into a sequence of OpenAI messages that delivers BOTH the tool-result acknowledgement AND the image(s) to the model — no silent drop, no ConversionError.

Because the OpenAI Chat Completions `tool` role only accepts string content, image parts MUST be delivered via a follow-up `user` role message immediately after the `tool` message. The `tool` message carries the text parts joined by newlines (or a non-empty placeholder like "[image attached below]" if all parts are images).

Image parts on a ToolResult must serialize as `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"data:<mime>;base64,<payload>"}}` in the follow-up user message (base64 path reuses the PROV-083 fix) or as `{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"<url>"}}` (URL path).
Text-only ToolResults must convert exactly as they do today — one OpenAI `tool` message with joined text content. Existing behaviour is PRESERVED for the non-image path.

When the tool-result contains multiple images, ALL images must appear in the single follow-up user message (one user message with multiple image content parts) — not one user message per image. This keeps message count minimal and preserves ordering.
The `tool_call_id` on the emitted OpenAI `tool` message must match the rig `ToolResult.id` — caller correlation must be preserved.

architectureNotes.text: Add pub fn build_cred_module(provider_name: String) -> RhaiModule in oauth/building_blocks.rs. Each registered native fn captures provider_name by clone and enforces name == provider_name before I/O.

Add pub fn register_all_modules_for_provider(provider_name: &str) -> Vec<RhaiModule> that returns the default four modules plus build_cred_module(provider_name). register_all_modules() keeps its current no-cred signature for backward compatibility.
Add pub fn build_provider_engine(provider_name: &str) -> Engine in oauth/engine.rs that calls build_sandboxed_engine(register_all_modules_for_provider(...)).

Add pub fn fspec_home() -> PathBuf in oauth/building_blocks.rs mirroring claude_auth::get_fspec_home — honours FSPEC_HOME env, else $HOME/.fspec/credentials. Shared helper used by cred::path computation.

cred::write uses std::fs::write + std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt to set_mode(0o600) on Unix. On non-Unix, permission setting is a no-op. Matches the sync-context approach of credential_store::write_sync + enforce_mode_0600.

Name validation: return EvalAltResult::ErrorRuntime('cred:: access denied: <requested> does not match active provider <provider_name>') when name != provider_name. No path traversal escape since the name is rejected outright before any PathBuf construction.

PROV-086.description: Expose the existing CredentialStore to Rhai scripts via a new cred:: namespace in oauth/building_blocks.rs. New functions: cred::read(name) -> Map|(), cred::write(name, map), cred::delete(name), cred::path(name) -> string. Security constraints: (1) filename scoped to active provider so script A cannot read provider B's tokens, (2) all sync I/O in spawn_blocking, (3) write uses 0600 permissions via write_secure. Path resolution uses the shared fspec_home() helper. Enables Rhai-driven OAuth flows to persist access/refresh tokens without exposing arbitrary filesystem access.

examples.text: Script for provider 'acme' calls cred::write('acme', #{access_token: 'abc', refresh_token: 'def'}) — file ~/.fspec/credentials/acme.json is created with 0600 permissions and contains the JSON map
Script for provider 'acme' calls cred::read('acme') after writing — receives a Map with access_token and refresh_token fields
Script for provider 'acme' calls cred::read('acme') before writing — receives unit () indicating no credentials exist yet
Script for provider 'acme' attempts cred::read('other_provider_auth') — the call returns an error because the requested name does not match the active provider 'acme'
Script for provider 'acme' attempts cred::write('../../etc/passwd', #{}) — the call returns an error because the name does not match the active provider
Script for provider 'acme' calls cred::path('acme') — receives the absolute path string ending in credentials/acme.json based on FSPEC_HOME
Script for provider 'acme' calls cred::delete('acme') on a non-existent file — the call succeeds (idempotent) and returns unit
build_default_engine() (which has no bound provider) does NOT register a cred:: module — scripts compiled against the default engine cannot access credential functions
build_provider_engine('acme') registers the cred:: module bound to provider name 'acme' in addition to http::, crypto::, json::, oauth::

rules.text: A cred:: Rhai namespace is registered in the default sandboxed engine alongside http::, crypto::, json::, and oauth::
cred::read(name) returns a Map when the credential file exists and parses as JSON, or unit () when it does not exist
cred::write(name, map) persists the map as JSON to ~/.fspec/credentials/<name>.json with 0600 permissions on Unix
cred::delete(name) removes the credential file and is idempotent — it succeeds when the file is absent
cred::path(name) returns the absolute string path to the credential file without touching the filesystem

The cred:: module is scoped to the active provider name — the provider name is bound at module build time and the name argument is used only as a filename component, never as a way to escape the active provider's credential file

All credential I/O (read, write, delete) runs inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking when invoked from async host code; from Rhai scripts the calls are synchronous and safe because they use std::fs with Unix permission setting via std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt
Path resolution for credential files honours FSPEC_HOME when set, otherwise falls back to $HOME/.fspec/credentials, matching claude_auth.rs::get_fspec_home()

PROV-087.description: Wire ScriptedOAuthProvider into NAPI for the browser-loopback PKCE flow. parse_stream_chunk returns #{ kind: 'thinking_delta', text: 'computing...' } → bridge yields StreamChunk::ReasoningDelta("computing...")

parse_stream_chunk returns #{ kind: 'reasoning_delta' } (no text field) → bridge yields no chunk

architectureNotes.text: Uses the new optional Rhai function `get_model_limits(config) -> Map` with shape `#{ context_window?: i64, max_output_tokens?: i64, compaction_threshold?: #{ type: "tokens"|"percentage", value: i64 } }`.

Implemented in codelet/providers/src/custom/provider.rs (RhaiCustomProvider::new invokes the script) and codelet/providers/src/custom/rhai_call.rs or similar. Missing function is detected via rhai::Engine::call_fn returning FunctionNotFound — treated as 'no-op, use JSON defaults'.

New accessor `RhaiCustomProvider::script_compaction_threshold() -> Option<(String, u64)>` exposes the parsed threshold so the NAPI session-creation path (codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs) can call `ProviderManager::set_compaction_threshold_override` at the same moment it calls `override_model_limits`.

PROV-095.description: The Rhai custom provider script (e.g. ~/.fspec/providers/claude_rhai.rhai) MUST be able to set per-model limits (context_window, max_output_tokens) from within the script itself — not only via the sibling .json config. Today the `RhaiCustomProvider` reads `context_window` / `max_output_tokens` exclusively from the deserialized `ProviderConfig.models[alias]` ModelDef (see codelet/providers/src/custom/provider.rs:68-69). There is no Rhai hook for the script to influence those numbers, and the TUI badge shows a stale/default value (e.g. 120k) that does not reflect what the script expects. Acceptance criteria: (1) expose an optional Rhai function (e.g. `get_model_limits(config) -> #{ context_window: N, max_output_tokens: M }`) that the provider invokes at construction time; (2) when present, its values override the JSON ModelDef values; (3) when absent, fall back to the JSON values (backward compatible); (4) the overridden value propagates end-to-end to the TUI SessionHeader badge.

examples.text: A claude-rhai.rhai script defines `fn get_model_limits(config) { #{ context_window: 400000, max_output_tokens: 128000 } }`; the JSON ModelDef for `opus-4.7` has `context_window: 128000`; the constructed RhaiCustomProvider reports `context_window() == 400000` and `max_output_tokens() == 128000`

A legacy claude-rhai.rhai script does NOT define `get_model_limits`; the JSON ModelDef says `context_window: 200000`; the constructed RhaiCustomProvider still reports `context_window() == 200000` (backward-compatible fallback)

A script returns `#{ context_window: 400000 }` (no max_output_tokens key); the JSON ModelDef has `context_window: 128000` and `max_output_tokens: 4096`; the provider reports `context_window() == 400000` and `max_output_tokens() == 4096`
