RIG-001.description:
Master story for replacing the rig-core dependency with a purpose-built LLM abstraction layer.

Motivation:
- We maintain a full patched fork of rig-core (~180+ files) but use only ~10% of it
- The patch adds Anthropic cache token support, OAuth handling, and other customizations to ~5-10 files
- rig-core compiles 20+ unused providers, embeddings/RAG, pipelines, vector stores, MCP, loaders, etc.
- rig is at v0.28, still rapidly evolving — every upstream release risks breaking our patches
- We already have our own provider abstractions (LlmProvider trait, ProviderAdapter, etc.)

Scope:
1. Define custom Tool trait + ToolSet (replacing rig::tool::Tool)
2. Define custom message types (replacing rig::message::Message, UserContent, AssistantContent, etc.)
3. Define CompletionModel trait + streaming response types
4. Implement multi-turn streaming agent loop (replacing rig::agent::Agent)
5. Implement StreamingPromptHook equivalent for compaction/history hooks
6. Migrate Anthropic provider HTTP client (SSE streaming, cache tokens, OAuth, thinking)
7. Migrate OpenAI provider HTTP client (SSE streaming, custom base URL)
8. Migrate Gemini provider HTTP client (SSE streaming, history format)
9. Remove rig-core dependency and patches/ directory
10. Update all tests

Approach: Incremental migration — define own traits, make tools implement both temporarily, swap providers one at a time, then remove rig.
RIG-001.title: Replace rig-core with custom LLM abstraction layer

RIG-002.description:
Define the custom Tool trait, ToolDyn wrapper, ToolSet collection, and ToolDefinition struct that replace rig::tool::*.

The trait interface is nearly identical to rig's — NAME const, Error/Args/Output associated types, definition() and call() async methods. The key difference is removing WasmCompat bounds (we don't target WASM) and simplifying the ToolEmbedding/RAG parts we don't use.

This is the foundation — all 12+ tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Ls, AstGrep, AstGrepRefactor, WebSearch, Fspec, Bridge + facade wrappers) must implement this trait.

Approach: Define the new trait alongside rig's. Temporarily make tools implement both via a blanket impl or wrapper. This enables incremental migration.
RIG-002.title: Core trait definitions — Tool, ToolSet, ToolDefinition

RIG-003.description:
Define custom message types replacing rig::message::* and rig::completion::*.

Message types needed:
- Message (role + content, with User/Assistant variants)
- UserContent (Text, ToolResult)
- AssistantContent (Text, ToolCall, Reasoning, Image)
- ToolCall, ToolFunction, ToolResult, ToolResultContent
- OneOrMany<T> utility type
- Usage (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read, cache_creation)
- CompletionResponse<T> (choice + raw_response + usage)
- ToolDefinition (name, description, parameters)
- CompletionModel trait (complete, stream)
- GetTokenUsage trait

These types are used pervasively across codelet-core, codelet-providers, and the streaming display. The key is maintaining API compatibility so the migration in consuming code is mechanical find-and-replace of import paths.
RIG-003.title: Message types and completion model trait

RIG-004.description:
Implement the multi-turn streaming agent loop that replaces rig::agent::Agent.

This is the most complex component — the core loop that:
1. Sends prompt + history + tool definitions to the LLM
2. Streams response chunks via SSE
3. Detects tool_use stop reason in the response
4. Deserializes tool call arguments and dispatches to ToolSet
5. Feeds tool results back as the next user message
6. Repeats until end_turn or max_depth reached
7. Calls hooks before/after each API call (StreamingPromptHook equivalent)
8. Supports CancelSignal for interruption
9. Emits MultiTurnStreamItem variants (text chunks, tool calls, tool results, final response)

Approach: Extract and simplify rig's agent/prompt_request/streaming.rs implementation. Remove WASM compat, enum dispatch, RAG tool selection, and other unused features. Keep only the three-provider streaming loop.

Dependencies: RIG-002 (Tool trait), RIG-003 (Message types)
RIG-004.title: Multi-turn streaming agent loop

RIG-005.description:
Implement direct Anthropic API client replacing rig::providers::anthropic.

This is the most feature-rich provider, requiring:
- POST /v1/messages with streaming (stream: true)
- SSE event parsing (message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta, content_block_stop, message_delta, message_stop)
- Tool use detection in content blocks (type: tool_use)
- Extended thinking / adaptive thinking support
- Prompt caching with cache_control metadata and ephemeral markers
- Cache token extraction from usage (cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens) 
- OAuth mode (Authorization: Bearer) vs API key mode (x-api-key)
- Beta headers (prompt-caching, interleaved-thinking, context-1m, claude-code, oauth)
- Model-aware beta header selection (PROV-005)
- Stop reason mapping (tool_use, end_turn, max_tokens)

All of this is currently split between patched rig-core, caching_client.rs, cache_token_extractor.rs, and claude.rs. Consolidation into a single clean client will eliminate the need for the patched fork entirely.

Dependencies: RIG-003 (Message types)
RIG-005.title: Anthropic provider HTTP client with SSE streaming

RIG-006.description:
Implement direct OpenAI API client replacing rig::providers::openai.

Features needed:
- POST /v1/chat/completions with streaming (stream: true)
- SSE event parsing (data: {json} lines, [DONE] sentinel)
- Tool call detection (finish_reason: tool_calls, tool_calls array in delta)
- Custom base URL support via OPENAI_BASE_URL (for vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio)
- URL normalization (ensure /v1 suffix)
- Configurable context window and max output tokens via env vars
- Stop reason mapping
- Usage extraction from stream_options: {include_usage: true}

Simpler than Anthropic — no caching, no OAuth, no thinking. The OpenAI streaming format is well-documented and widely implemented.

Dependencies: RIG-003 (Message types)
RIG-006.title: OpenAI provider HTTP client with SSE streaming

RIG-007.description:
Implement direct Gemini API client replacing rig::providers::gemini.

Features needed:
- POST /v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent with SSE
- Gemini-specific content format (parts array with text/functionCall/functionResponse)
- Tool declaration format (function_declarations)
- History format conversion (Gemini uses 'user'/'model' roles, requires alternating turns)
- GeminiHistoryHook equivalent (ensure thought signatures, handle continuation)
- Usage extraction from usageMetadata
- Stop reason mapping (STOP, MAX_TOKENS, etc.)

Gemini has the most different API format from the others. The GeminiTurnCompletionFacade and GeminiHistoryHook in codelet-core handle the quirks of Gemini's turn structure.

Dependencies: RIG-003 (Message types)
RIG-007.title: Gemini provider HTTP client with SSE streaming

RIG-008.title: Migrate all tools to custom Tool trait

RIG-009.description:
Migrate codelet-core from rig agent types to the custom agent loop and hook system.

Files to migrate:
- rig_agent.rs → Use custom Agent instead of rig::agent::Agent
- compaction_hook.rs → Implement custom StreamingPromptHook equivalent instead of rig::agent::StreamingPromptHook

RIG-010.description:
Final cleanup story — remove all rig-core references from the codebase.

Tasks:
1. Remove `rig-core` from all Cargo.toml files (workspace, codelet-core, codelet-providers, codelet-tools)
2. Remove `[patch.crates-io] rig-core = { path = "patches/rig-core" }` from workspace Cargo.toml

RIG-013.description: Implement a three-layer message queuing and cooperative interruption system for the codelet agent loop, enabling users to submit messages while the agent is running, intelligently interrupt in-progress LLM generation or tool execution, and seamlessly resume or continue the loop after interruption. Based on comprehensive research of VTCode's architecture (github.com/vinhnx/VTCode).

examples.text: User types a message and presses Enter while agent is mid-turn → message is queued → agent finishes current turn → queued message is immediately dequeued and starts a new turn without waiting
User types 3 messages while agent is busy → first dequeue takes the NEWEST message (prefer_latest_once), subsequent dequeues take remaining messages in FIFO order
User presses ESC once during LLM generation → generation is cancelled cleanly, conversation history is rolled back to before the turn, user can type a new message
User presses ESC twice within 1 second → session exits entirely (double-tap escalation)
User presses ESC during tool execution (bash command running) → command is terminated, PTY session killed, no orphaned processes
Bridge sends a follow-up message via WebSocket while agent is mid-turn → message is queued in steering channel → turn completes → follow-up starts immediately as next turn
AgentManager sends a message to a subordinate session while it's running → message queued via steering → subordinate finishes current work → processes the message as next turn
Scheduled task fires while agent is idle → task prompt injected, turn starts immediately. Scheduled task fires while agent is busy → task prompt queued, starts after current turn completes
Two concurrent sessions — user cancels session A → only session A's LLM request is cancelled, session B continues unaffected (per-session isolation)
User cancels during compaction → compaction is cleanly aborted, session returns to interaction loop without corrupted state

rules.text: Per-session message queue using VecDeque<String> with smart dequeue — newest-first once (prefer_latest_once) then FIFO
Per-session CtrlCState atomic state machine: Idle → CancelRequested → ExitArmed → ExitRequested with 1-second double-tap escalation window
RuntimeSteering channel (tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel) for external control: pause, resume, stop, follow-up input injection from bridges/schedules/subordinates
Cooperative cancellation — never drop async tasks arbitrarily; use tokio::select! racing against Notify to cleanly cancel LLM requests
History checkpoint before each turn with rollback on cancel — no half-written conversation state after interruption
Three-level nested loop: Session loop (steering drain) → Interaction loop (idle polling with biased select!) → Turn loop (non-blocking try_recv at top of every step)
All queues and state machines MUST be per-session (not global) — consistent with BUG-126 through BUG-129 fixes
Follow-up inputs from steering skip the interaction loop entirely — new turn starts immediately without waiting for user interaction
Queued submissions checked BEFORE waiting for new events in interaction loop — instant drain without blocking
NAPI bindings must expose: queue_input(session_id, text), cancel_session(session_id), get_queue_depth(session_id) for TUI integration
Force-terminate all PTY/exec sessions on cancel or exit — no orphaned processes

RIG-013.title: Message Queuing and Cooperative Agent Loop Interruption — VTCode-Inspired Three-Layer Architecture

userStory.action: submit messages while the agent is running and have them queued and processed intelligently, cancel in-progress work cleanly, and inject follow-up inputs from external sources
userStory.benefit: I never lose my train of thought, the agent responds to my latest intent, and external integrations (bridges, schedules, subordinate agents) can steer the agent without waiting for it to become idle

architectureNotes.text: Tool is wired into all 5 providers' create_rig_agent() — same pattern as SessionSearch: import DeepSearchTool from codelet_tools, add .tool(DeepSearchTool::new(session_id)) to each provider's AgentBuilder chain. Verified locations: claude.rs:530, openai.rs:338, gemini.rs:172, codex/mod.rs:364, zai.rs:247.

AMGR-001 (SessionSearch) provides the foundation for session history access. The implementation pattern: (1) Tool struct in codelet/tools/src/session_search/ with types.rs (SessionSearchAction enum, args, results), handler.rs (per-session handler storage via static RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, Handler>>), reassembly.rs (streaming chunk reconstruction). (2) Handler registered in session_manager.rs via set_session_search_handler(session_id, handler) before agent run, cleaned up after. (3) The handler closure captures project_path AND compaction_trimming: Arc<AtomicBool> — the compaction_trimming flag controls whether Layer 0 trimming (CMPCT-010) is applied to SessionSearch results during agent-controlled compaction. (4) inject_summary (CMPCT-008/009) follows the exact same handler pattern — InjectSummaryTool in codelet/tools/src/inject_summary.rs with set_inject_summary_handler/has_inject_summary_handler. DeepSearch should follow this same module pattern for its tool structure but does NOT need inject_summary (read-only sub-agent).

DeepSearch's SessionSearch handler is created via codelet/napi/src/session_search_handler.rs::create_handler(project_path, compaction_trimming). The project_path comes from the parent session's project context (same as the parent agent's handler). compaction_trimming must be Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)) since the ephemeral sub-agent never does compaction. This avoids the NAPI boundary problem since the handler is pure Rust — no ThreadsafeFunction needed.

RLM-001.description: Implement a DeepSearch tool that spawns an ephemeral sub-agent to answer questions over arbitrarily large, user-scoped corpora (files, conversation histories, logs). Based on the RLM paper (MIT CSAIL, arXiv:2512.24601). Key insight: this is NOT a BackgroundSession and NOT a REPL environment — it's a simple tool that builds a rig Agent with scoped read-only tools (Read, Grep, AstGrep, Glob, Ls, Bash) PLUS SessionSearch (from AMGR-001) for conversation history access, injects an RLM-adapted system prompt, calls RigAgent::prompt() (non-streaming, multi-turn), and returns the final answer string as the tool result. ~100-150 lines of core code. Code scoping is first-class: caller specifies paths/globs. Session history is accessible via the sub-agent's SessionSearch tool — no temp file serialization needed. Can use a cheaper model for the sub-agent. No persistence, no UI streaming, no custom stream loop — pure Rust, blocking call from the parent tool execution context.

examples.text: Parent agent calls DeepSearch(query='How is authentication handled?', scope=['src/auth/']) and gets back a text answer synthesized from reading the auth source files
DeepSearch with narrow scope=['codelet/tools/src/read.rs'] only lets the sub-agent read that one file — it can't wander into unrelated code
DeepSearch with scope=['src/'] + max_depth=5 returns partial answer with note that depth limit was reached before exhaustive exploration

Parent agent calls DeepSearch(query='What changed in session 7e0358a4?', scope=['src/auth/']) — the sub-agent uses SessionSearch(action='show', session_id='7e0358a4') to load the conversation, then uses Read/Grep on src/auth/ to correlate what was discussed with what's in the code

Parent agent calls DeepSearch(query='Find all sessions where we discussed compaction strategy') — the sub-agent uses SessionSearch(action='search', query='compaction') to find relevant sessions, then SessionSearch(action='show') to drill into the most relevant ones, building up an answer across multiple sessions

DeepSearch sub-agent's system prompt describes: 'You have SessionSearch to explore conversation history (use recent/search/show actions) and Read/Grep/AstGrep/Glob/Ls/Bash to explore code files scoped to [src/]'. The sub-agent iteratively calls SessionSearch(search) → SessionSearch(show) → Read/Grep, building context before answering

DeepSearch called with no scope and no query returns an error — at minimum a query is required. Scope (code paths) is optional: when omitted, the sub-agent has only SessionSearch for session history exploration. When scope is provided, Read/Grep/AstGrep/Glob/Ls/Bash are guided to those paths via the system prompt

questions.answer: Scope is typed facets, not a flat path list. Code gets paths/globs + git refs (branch, commit range, changed-files-only). Sessions get time range + topic keyword + specific IDs + project filter. Spec artifacts covered by code paths. Each content type has its own natural scoping dimensions that compose together.
questions.text: What granularity levels should scope support? e.g., (1) whole codebase, (2) specific directories, (3) specific files, (4) session history, (5) combined — and should there be a 'guided' mode that narrows scope progressively?

questions.answer: Two-pronged approach: (a) system prompt guardrails describe the code scope (paths/globs) and tell the sub-agent to stay within them, (b) SessionSearch naturally scopes session exploration to the project. For v1, system prompt is sufficient since the sub-agent has no motivation to look elsewhere. For v2, tool-level path restriction can be added as a wrapper
questions.text: How do we prevent the sub-agent from going down the wrong path? Options: (a) system prompt guardrails only, (b) actually restrict tool paths at the tool level, (c) phased search — start broad with Grep, narrow with Read

questions.answer: The sub-agent gets SessionSearch as a native tool — it uses SessionSearch(action='search') for keyword matching across sessions, SessionSearch(action='show') to load full conversations, and SessionSearch(action='recent') for discovery. No pre-processing or serialization needed. SessionSearch already handles blob resolution, streaming chunk reassembly, time filtering, and project scoping internally
questions.text: For session history scope — should the sub-agent get raw messages.jsonl + blobs, or a pre-processed/filtered summary? The session-search.sh script already has context/show/search modes — should the serializer mirror those levels?

questions.answer: Yes — scope is naturally composable. DeepSearch params specify code paths (for Read/Grep/AstGrep), and SessionSearch is always available as a tool. The sub-agent decides how to use each based on the query. Example: DeepSearch(query='How was auth refactored?', scope=['src/auth/']) — sub-agent uses Grep on src/auth/ for current state AND SessionSearch to find sessions discussing the refactor
questions.text: Should scope levels be composable? e.g., DeepSearch(scope={code: ['src/auth/'], sessions: ['7e0358a4'], depth: 'shallow'}) vs DeepSearch(scope={code: ['**/*.rs'], sessions: 'current', depth: 'deep'})

rules.text: DeepSearch is a rig Tool (implements rig::tool::Tool trait) that the parent agent calls like any other tool
DeepSearch scope must support both codebase files AND session history (previous conversation context from ~/.fspec/sessions)
The sub-agent uses RigAgent::prompt() (non-streaming, blocking) — NOT the streaming loop, NOT BackgroundSession
Sub-agent is ephemeral — no persistence, no session resume, no worktree, no NAPI boundary. Fresh Uuid::new_v4() for tool session_id
Must use public provider accessors: provider.client() and provider.model() — private fields rig_client/model_name are inaccessible from outside the provider impl
v1 is Claude-only. Multi-provider support (OpenAI, Gemini, Codex, ZAI) deferred to v2
max_depth must be bounded (default 50, not usize::MAX) to prevent runaway sub-agents
Credentials come from env vars already set by the parent session — sub-agent creates a new ProviderManager which reads them

Session history scope uses SessionSearch tool directly — the sub-agent gets its own SessionSearch instance with a registered handler (via set_session_search_handler). No temp file serialization needed. SessionSearch's native parameters (time range, project filter, keyword search, context turns) replace the custom scope facets from the original design

Scope is two composable dimensions: (a) code scope — paths/globs for Read/Grep/AstGrep/Glob/Ls to explore, (b) session scope — the sub-agent has SessionSearch with full access to recent/search/show actions. The caller specifies code paths in the tool params; session access is always available via SessionSearch. The system prompt describes both scopes to guide the sub-agent's exploration strategy

Two-pronged approach: (a) system prompt guardrails describe the code scope (paths/globs) and tell the sub-agent to stay within them, (b) SessionSearch naturally scopes session exploration to the project. For v1, system prompt is sufficient since the sub-agent has no motivation to look elsewhere. For v2, tool-level path restriction can be added as a wrapper

The sub-agent gets SessionSearch as a native tool — it uses SessionSearch(action='search') for keyword matching across sessions, SessionSearch(action='show') to load full conversations, and SessionSearch(action='recent') for discovery. No pre-processing or serialization needed. SessionSearch already handles blob resolution, streaming chunk reassembly, time filtering, and project scoping internally

The sub-agent's SessionSearch handler must be registered (via set_session_search_handler) with a fresh ephemeral session_id before calling RigAgent::prompt(), and cleaned up after — following the same lifecycle pattern as session_manager.rs lines 5378-5384 (register) and 5648-5649 (cleanup)

Sub-agent's SessionSearch handler must be created via create_handler(project_path, Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false))) — compaction_trimming is always false because the ephemeral sub-agent never performs compaction. The compaction_trimming: Arc<AtomicBool> parameter was added to create_handler in CMPCT-010 and controls whether Layer 0 trimming is applied to SessionSearch results

Scope is naturally composable. DeepSearch params specify code paths (for Read/Grep/AstGrep), and SessionSearch is always available as a tool. The sub-agent decides how to use each based on the query. Example: DeepSearch(query='How was auth refactored?', scope=['src/auth/']) — sub-agent uses Grep on src/auth/ for current state AND SessionSearch to find sessions discussing the refactor
Sub-agent gets read-only search tools plus SessionSearch: Read, Grep, AstGrep, Glob, Ls, Bash, SessionSearch — NO Write, Edit, Bridge, Fspec, WebSearch, ConnectMcp, AstGrepRefactor, inject_summary

Code scope (paths/globs) is optional — when provided, the system prompt guides the sub-agent to explore those paths. When omitted, the sub-agent relies on SessionSearch only. The caller controls granularity: specific files, directories, or glob patterns

RLM-001.title: Deep Search Tool — Ephemeral Sub-Agent for Scoped Corpus Analysis

userStory.action: invoke a DeepSearch tool that spawns an ephemeral sub-agent to explore a scoped corpus
userStory.benefit: I can get answers about large codebases without manually reading hundreds of files

architectureNotes.text: DeepSearchTool struct gets a depth field. The handler chain passes depth through: parent handler registration (depth=0) → execute_deep_search(depth) → build_and_run_agent conditionally adds DeepSearchTool::new(session_id).with_depth(depth+1) when depth < max_recursion_depth.

Recursive children register their own DeepSearch handler (wrapping execute_deep_search with depth+1) so their sub-agents can also invoke DeepSearch. Cleanup chain: each level's drop guard removes its own handlers.

The compile-time SUB_AGENT_TOOL_COUNT assertion (currently == 7) must become dynamic or split into two constants: BASE_TOOL_COUNT (7) and RECURSIVE_TOOL_COUNT (8). The assertion checks the correct count based on whether recursion is enabled at that depth.

RLM-002.description:
The current DeepSearch tool (RLM-001) is an iterative sub-agent that cannot call itself — it is not actually recursive despite being inspired by the RLM paper (arXiv:2512.24601). The sub-agent's tool set explicitly excludes DeepSearch, so it cannot decompose large corpora via divide-and-conquer. Additionally, the system prompt is a generic research assistant prompt rather than the RLM paper's decomposition-oriented prompt that teaches programmatic chunking, delegation via sub-calls, and aggregation.

Three changes:
1. Add DeepSearchTool to the sub-agent's tool set with depth-1 recursion (depth=0 means the sub-agent answers directly without tools — degenerating to a plain llm_query). This single change gives both llm_query() and rlm_query() from the paper.
2. Rewrite the system prompt to teach the sub-agent the RLM decomposition strategy: chunk → delegate via recursive DeepSearch calls → aggregate results.
3. Leverage Bash/inline code in the system prompt guidance to enable programmatic orchestration of sub-calls where possible.

examples.text: Parent calls DeepSearch(query='How does auth work?', scope=['src/']). Sub-agent at depth=0 uses Grep to find 47 auth files, then calls DeepSearch(query='Analyze login flow', scope=['src/auth/login.rs']) at depth=1. The depth=1 child reads the file, uses AstGrep, and returns a synthesized answer. Parent aggregates.

Sub-agent at depth=1 with max_recursion_depth=2 calls DeepSearch(query='Summarize this function', no scope). The depth=2 child has NO DeepSearch in its tools — it just answers the question directly as a single LLM call and returns. This is the llm_query() equivalent.

DeepSearch at depth=0 uses Bash to run python3 -c to split a file list into chunks, then calls DeepSearch once per chunk to analyze each independently, then aggregates the child answers into a final response.
DeepSearch at max_recursion_depth still has Read, Grep, AstGrep, Glob, Ls, Bash, SessionSearch — it just can't spawn further DeepSearch children. It's still a functional sub-agent, not a bare LLM.

Parent agent calls DeepSearch(query='Find all sessions where we discussed compaction'). Depth=0 sub-agent uses SessionSearch to find 5 sessions, then calls DeepSearch(query='What was decided about compaction in session X?') for each — each child uses SessionSearch(show) to read the session and returns a summary. Parent aggregates into a timeline.

rules.text: The sub-agent's tool set must include DeepSearchTool when recursion depth < max_recursion_depth
When recursion depth >= max_recursion_depth, the sub-agent is built WITHOUT DeepSearchTool (base case — tools only, no further recursion)
Default max_recursion_depth is 2 — parent calls depth=0, child at depth=1 can still recurse, grandchild at depth=2 cannot
max_recursion_depth is separate from max_depth (tool-call rounds per agent) — they control different things
Each recursive DeepSearch child must register its own SessionSearch AND DeepSearch handlers with ephemeral UUIDs, and clean up on exit
The system prompt must teach the decompose-delegate-aggregate strategy from the RLM paper: explore scope, chunk via Bash/python3, delegate via recursive DeepSearch, aggregate results
The system prompt must explain that DeepSearch with a simple query and no scope degenerates to a plain LLM call (the llm_query equivalent from the paper)
The system prompt should conditionally include DeepSearch in the tools section only when the sub-agent actually has recursion capability at its depth
Provider-specific config and streaming/non-streaming execution paths must work unchanged for recursive children

RLM-002.title: Make DeepSearch truly recursive with self-invocation and RLM-aligned system prompt

userStory.action: have DeepSearch recursively spawn sub-agents to decompose and explore large corpora
userStory.benefit: I get accurate answers over codebases and histories that are too large for a single agent pass

architectureNotes.text: Workspace integration: 4 new crates added to codelet/Cargo.toml workspace.members alongside existing cli/common/core/git/napi/providers/tools/tui — codelet/rpc-types, codelet/rpc, codelet/rpc-embedded, codelet/rpc-server. tarpc and bincode added to workspace.dependencies; tokio-tungstenite already present (BRIDGE-001).

WorkUnitInfo lift strategy: codelet/rpc-types defines the canonical WorkUnitInfo struct (fields id, title, work_type, status, description, estimate, epic) with serde Serialize/Deserialize/PartialEq derives. codelet/napi/src/types.rs:182 currently owns it with #[napi(object)] derives — this card replaces the local definition with a re-export from rpc-types using a NAPI wrapper newtype OR a feature gate that applies #[napi(object)] when the napi feature is enabled on rpc-types. TS naming preserved: workType (camelCase) via #[napi(js_name = ...)] on the wrapper.

Tarpc service definition: codelet/rpc defines #[tarpc::service] trait FspecService { async fn list_work_units() -> Vec<WorkUnitInfo>; } — the trait macro expands to FspecServiceClient (used by both transports) and stub generators. Single shared service impl: a struct (e.g. SharedFspecService { state: Arc<TestFixture>, counter: Arc<AtomicU64> }) implements FspecService once; both rpc-embedded and rpc-server construct an instance and serve it via tarpc::server::BaseChannel.respond_with.

Embedded transport: codelet/rpc-embedded exposes EmbeddedTransport::new(handle: tokio::runtime::Handle, service_impl: SharedFspecService) — uses tarpc::transport::channel::unbounded() for in-process Stream+Sink, spawns the server task on the provided Handle (NOT a fresh Runtime — invariant from RPC-002 Q9). WebSocket transport: codelet/rpc-server is a binary that binds 127.0.0.1:0, prints port to stdout (single line: PORT=<n>\n), wraps tokio-tungstenite WebSocketStream in an Envelope codec (bincode-serialized Envelope::Rpc { ... }), adapts to tarpc Stream+Sink via futures::StreamExt/SinkExt mapping. Reserved variants (Event/LogEvent/WorkUnitsUpdate/CmdReq/CmdRes) match-rejected with tracing::warn!.

Test layout: Rust integration tests in codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/embedded_happy_path.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/ws_happy_path.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/parity.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/shared_impl_counter.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/bincode_wire_format.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/reserved_variants_rejected.rs. Source-shape tests (no runtime spawn) using cargo metadata + ast-grep / grep on codelet/napi/src/**/*.rs for the WorkUnitInfo-defined-once and runtime-Handle-required scenarios. Vitest smoke test in codelet/napi or root TS test dir for the get_all_work_units shape assertion.

RPC-005.description:
FIRST card under RPC-002. Establishes the four scaffolding crates from the feasibility doc and proves the dual-transport architecture end-to-end with ONE round-trip RPC. No ratatui in this card.

GOAL
Prove the foundational architecture: ONE business-logic implementation in codelet/core is reachable via TWO interchangeable tarpc transports (embedded in-memory + remote WebSocket), AND the existing codelet/napi crate continues to expose the same types to the TS frontend by re-exporting from rpc-types so we never maintain two parallel type/impl trees.

SCOPE (small)

1. New crates added to codelet/Cargo.toml workspace:
 - codelet/rpc-types: pure-serde shared types (NAPI re-exports from here)
 - codelet/rpc: tarpc service trait FspecService
 - codelet/rpc-embedded: in-memory tarpc transport channel impl + service impl
 - codelet/rpc-server: WebSocket daemon binary; same service impl, tokio-tungstenite frame envelope

2. Lift exactly ONE NAPI type into rpc-types to prove the pattern (suggested: WorkUnitInfo or any equivalently small read-only struct). codelet/napi must re-export it so the TS frontend sees no change. Pure-serde derives only in rpc-types; any NAPI-specific derives applied in codelet/napi (wrapper or feature-gated).

3. Define exactly ONE method on the FspecService tarpc trait. Suggested: list_work_units(ctx) returning a Vec of WorkUnitInfo, or any equally trivial read-only RPC. Implementation delegates to existing codelet/core business logic. Implementation is written ONCE and shared between the two transports.

4. codelet/rpc-embedded returns an FspecServiceClient backed by tarpc::transport::channel: no serialization, no network. Accepts a tokio runtime Handle (per resolved Q9: share via Handle, don't spawn own runtime when embedded).

5. codelet/rpc-server is a binary that:
 - Binds a WebSocket listener (tokio-tungstenite)
 - Defines an Envelope enum per feasibility section 5.2 (Rpc variant only at this stage; Event/LogEvent/WorkUnitsUpdate/CmdReq/CmdRes deferred to later cards)
 - Forwards Rpc-variant frames to a tarpc transport adapter
 - Wire format: bincode default (JSON debug envelope deferred)

6. Integration test (in codelet/tests/) that:
 - Spins up the embedded transport and calls list_work_units; asserts the result
 - Spins up the rpc-server binary, connects a WS client, calls list_work_units; asserts the result is byte-identical to the embedded path
 - Verifies both calls hit the SAME underlying codelet/core function (single source of truth)

7. codelet/napi continues to compile and expose the lifted type unchanged (npm test on the TS side stays green).

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (deferred to later cards)
- Lifting the rest of the ~76 NAPI types into rpc-types (Phase 1 of the feasibility doc - its own card)
- Mirroring the rest of the ~191 NAPI functions on FspecService (Phase 2 - its own card, mostly mechanical)
- Streaming / push channels: StreamChunk fan-out, log events, work-units watcher (Event/LogEvent/WorkUnitsUpdate envelope variants). Single round-trip RPC only in this card.
- Reverse callbacks (callFspecCommand). Feasibility section 8 - its own card.
- Daemon topology: per-project vs per-user, lifecycle, authentication. Separate work units.
- OAuth flows in remote mode. Feasibility section 7.
- ratatui app, Compositor, any TUI scaffolding - Slice 01 of the dossier breakdown is its own card (depends on this one).
- JSON debug envelope behind a feature flag - defer until needed.

ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS THIS CARD ESTABLISHES
- ONE source of truth for shared types: codelet/rpc-types. codelet/napi MUST re-export, never redefine. Any future NAPI-only field is a wrapper around an rpc-types struct, not a fork.
- ONE source of truth for business logic: codelet/core (and friends). Both transports' service impls delegate; neither inlines logic.
- BOTH transports must reach feature parity over time. Integration tests cover both paths from this point onward; no RPC method is 'embedded only' or 'WebSocket only' without explicit written justification.
- Embedded transport accepts a tokio runtime Handle from the host; it does NOT spawn its own runtime when in-process (per resolved Q9).
- Wire format default = bincode for performance; envelope schema versioned.

REFERENCES
- spec/attachments/RPC-002/rpc-002-feasibility.md sections 4, 5, 6, 9
- spec/attachments/RPC-002/07-recommended-architecture.md section 7
- spec/attachments/RPC-002/11-open-questions-and-risks.md Q9 (resolved)

examples.text: Embedded happy path: a Rust caller obtains an EmbeddedTransport from a tokio Handle, gets an FspecServiceClient, calls list_work_units and receives a Vec<WorkUnitInfo> matching what the underlying business logic returns directly
WebSocket happy path: developer starts the rpc-server binary, connects with a WebSocket client, calls list_work_units and receives the same Vec<WorkUnitInfo> as the embedded path
Cross-transport parity: developer runs the same list_work_units call through both transports against the same underlying state and observes equal Vec<WorkUnitInfo> values
TS frontend unchanged: TypeScript developer runs npm test after the lift; existing get_all_work_units NAPI export still returns the same shape and all tests pass
Runtime sharing: developer constructing an EmbeddedTransport without supplying a tokio Handle gets a compile-time error (constructor signature requires Handle)
Bincode wire format: developer captures a WS frame on the wire and confirms it is bincode-encoded, not JSON

Reserved envelope variants rejected: developer sends a WS frame tagged Event/LogEvent/CmdReq to the server in this card; server logs an error and ignores or closes the connection (defensive default for unimplemented variants)

Both transports reach the same business-logic function: developer adds a tracing span/counter inside the shared service impl; both embedded and WS calls increment it once each (single source of truth, no inlined duplicate logic)

rules.text: Four new crates exist as members of the codelet workspace: rpc-types, rpc, rpc-embedded, rpc-server
Shared serde types are defined ONLY in codelet/rpc-types; codelet/napi re-exports them and never redefines
The FspecService tarpc trait is defined ONLY in codelet/rpc; embedded and WebSocket transports both implement it
The service implementation is written ONCE in a shared module; both transports delegate to it rather than duplicating logic
The embedded transport accepts a tokio::runtime::Handle from its host and must NOT spawn its own runtime
The WebSocket transport uses bincode as its default wire format
The WebSocket Envelope enum has only the Rpc variant in this card; Event, LogEvent, WorkUnitsUpdate, CmdReq, CmdRes are reserved but unimplemented (server rejects or ignores them)
Integration tests cover BOTH transport paths for every RPC method introduced; no method is embedded-only or WS-only
Both transport paths produce semantically identical results for the same input (parity assertion in tests)
The TS frontend continues to work unchanged: codelet/napi compiles, npm test stays green, no NAPI breaking changes

Test-only in-memory state for THIS card. Shared service impl reads from a tiny in-memory fixture; a follow-up card moves the real work-units watcher from codelet/napi into codelet/core. Keeps RPC-005 a true scaffolding spike.

Minimal test-spawnable binary: binds 127.0.0.1:0 (ephemeral port reported on stdout), tracing-to-stderr, ctrl_c shutdown only. Hardening (SIGTERM, graceful disconnect, configurable bind, daemon mode) deferred to a 'productionize rpc-server' follow-up card.

RPC-005.title: Foundation: dual-transport tarpc service (embedded + WebSocket) sharing one impl with NAPI

userStory.action: reach one tarpc service trait via either an embedded in-memory transport or a remote WebSocket transport, both backed by a single shared implementation that the existing NAPI crate also re-exports types from
userStory.benefit: the TUI can run in-process or over the network without forking the type system or business logic
userStory.role: Rust developer building the new fspec frontend

architectureNotes.text: Watcher lift target: codelet/core/src/work_units.rs (NEW module). Dependency arrow becomes rpc → core (forbidden: rpc → napi). The notify-based watcher logic currently in codelet/napi/src/work_units_watcher.rs is moved verbatim, less the ThreadsafeFunction Node bridge.

Watcher public API (codelet/core::work_units): `pub fn read_snapshot(workspace: &Path) -> Result<Vec<WorkUnitInfo>>` (one-shot reader); `pub struct WorkUnitsWatcher` with `pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Result<Self>`, `pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Vec<WorkUnitInfo>`, `pub fn subscribe(&self) -> tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<Vec<WorkUnitInfo>>`.

SharedFspecService constructor changes from `new(Vec<WorkUnitInfo>)` to `new(watcher: Arc<WorkUnitsWatcher>)`. The existing `list_work_units_calls` parity counter is retained. `FspecServiceImpl::list_work_units` body becomes `self.inner.watcher.snapshot()`.

default_fixture() at codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs:93-114 is renamed to test_fixture() and gated behind `#[cfg(test)]` (or moved into a `#[cfg(test)] mod`). All RPC-005 tests that imported it switch to the cfg-test path.

Envelope variant shape change in codelet/rpc-server/src/envelope.rs: `WorkUnitsUpdate` is no longer a unit variant — it carries `Vec<WorkUnitInfo>`. `Envelope::variant_name()` updated. ServerStats no longer counts WorkUnitsUpdate as a rejected/reserved variant; reserved-variants regression test list narrows to {Event, LogEvent, CmdReq, CmdRes}.

Server-side fan-out (codelet/rpc-server/src/server.rs::handle_connection): per-connection task subscribes to the shared `watcher` via `service.watcher_rx()` (or equivalent), sends an initial snapshot frame immediately, then forwards every broadcast event as a bincode-encoded `Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate(snapshot)` onto the WS sink. ChannelTransport remains unchanged — broadcast runs alongside it, not through it.

Client-side demux (codelet/rpc-server/src/pump.rs::ClientInbound): inbound envelope pump grows a second outbound channel — WorkUnitsUpdate frames are decoded and forwarded to a `tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<Vec<WorkUnitInfo>>` exposed via the client struct. Rpc envelopes continue to flow into the existing tarpc transport.

ws_client_connect return shape: `FspecWsClient { rpc: FspecServiceClient, work_units_rx: broadcast::Receiver<Vec<WorkUnitInfo>> }`. Existing RPC-005 call sites that used the bare client update to `.rpc`. Method `FspecWsClient::work_units_rx()` clones a fresh receiver from the broadcast sender.

Embedded zero-cost push: `EmbeddedTransport::work_units_rx() -> broadcast::Receiver<Vec<WorkUnitInfo>>` returns `service.watcher.subscribe()` directly — no envelope encoding, no fan-out task on the embedded read path. Any fan-out spawning that DOES occur uses `self.handle.spawn(...)` (the host's tokio Handle from RPC-005 Q9), never `Runtime::new`.

rpc-server binary main.rs: replace `default_fixture()` construction with `WorkUnitsWatcher::new(workspace)`. Workspace resolution: accept `--workspace <path>` clap arg, defaulting to `std::env::current_dir()`. Stdout contract (`PORT=<n>\n`) and ctrl_c shutdown contract from RPC-005 are unchanged.

NAPI compatibility shim (codelet/napi/src/work_units_watcher.rs): keep the existing exported NAPI surface (startWorkUnitsWatcher with ThreadsafeFunction). Internally, replace the local watcher implementation with a wrapper around `codelet_core::work_units::WorkUnitsWatcher` that calls `subscribe()` and forwards each broadcast event into the existing ThreadsafeFunction callback. TS frontend behaviour is preserved — Vitest smoke gains an assertion that the callback still fires on file mutation.

Source-shape regression updates: RPC-005 `scenario_10_*` (no `codelet-core` dep on the rpc crate) WIDENS to: `codelet/rpc/Cargo.toml` may depend on `codelet-core` but MUST NOT depend on `codelet-napi`. The other RPC-005 source-shape regressions (`WorkUnitInfo` defined exactly once, EmbeddedTransport requires Handle, rpc-server binds 127.0.0.1) stay green unchanged.

Broadcast capacity: bounded `tokio::sync::broadcast::channel(N)` — N=64 chosen as a small headroom default; lagging subscribers receive RecvError::Lagged and skip ahead (acceptable for a snapshot-replacement payload). Per-subscription filtering, ack/nack, configurable capacity all explicitly deferred to RPC-011.

Test layout: NEW Rust integration tests at codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/embedded_push.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/ws_initial_snapshot.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/ws_push_on_mutation.rs, codelet/rpc-server/tests/cross_transport_push_parity.rs. UPDATED tests at codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/architecture_invariants.rs (scenario_10 widening) and codelet/rpc-server/tests/reserved_variants_rejected.rs (WorkUnitsUpdate removed from rejected list). Vitest smoke at src/__tests__/napi-workunitinfo-shape.test.ts gains the watcher-callback-still-fires assertion.

RPC-006.description:
Replace the test-only default_fixture() introduced in RPC-005 with a real WorkUnitsWatcher reachable from the shared service crate, AND add the first non-Rpc envelope variant — Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate(Vec<WorkUnitInfo>) — so push events flow over both transports.

See spec/attachments/RPC-006/plan.md for the full plan.

Follows RPC-005. Unblocks RPC-007 (StreamChunk push) and RPC-009 (live work-unit list view).

examples.text: Embedded happy path: a Rust caller constructs a WorkUnitsWatcher over a temp workspace, builds an EmbeddedTransport from a tokio Handle, calls list_work_units() and receives the live snapshot (not the RPC-005 fixture)
Embedded push: a caller subscribes via EmbeddedTransport::work_units_rx(), mutates spec/work-units.json in the temp workspace, and observes the new Vec<WorkUnitInfo> arrive on the broadcast receiver
WebSocket happy path: developer starts rpc-server bound to a temp workspace, connects a WS client, calls list_work_units() and receives the same live snapshot as the embedded path
WebSocket initial snapshot: developer connects to rpc-server and immediately receives one Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate(Vec<WorkUnitInfo>) frame on connection — before any file mutation

WebSocket push: client subscribes via FspecWsClient::work_units_rx(), the temp spec/work-units.json is mutated, and the client receives a bincode-encoded Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate frame carrying the new snapshot
Bincode wire format for WorkUnitsUpdate: developer captures the on-the-wire frame and confirms it decodes as bincode of Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate(Vec<WorkUnitInfo>) — not JSON, not a custom shape
Cross-transport parity: same workspace mutation on both transports produces equal Vec<WorkUnitInfo> payloads byte-for-byte (bincode encoding stable)
Multiple subscribers: two callers each call work_units_rx() on the same EmbeddedTransport and both receive every broadcast on file mutation

Reserved variants still rejected: developer sends Envelope::Event / Envelope::LogEvent / Envelope::CmdReq / Envelope::CmdRes to the server; server logs and rejects each (regression of RPC-005 scenario 6, with WorkUnitsUpdate now removed from the rejected list)

TS frontend unchanged: TypeScript developer runs `npm test` after the watcher lift; existing getAllWorkUnits() NAPI export still returns the same WorkUnitInfo shape AND the existing startWorkUnitsWatcher callback still fires when work-units.json changes
Source-shape regression: ast-grep / grep over codelet/rpc/Cargo.toml confirms no codelet-napi import; codelet-core import is now permitted (RPC-005 scenario_10 widened)
default_fixture unreachable from production: cargo metadata + grep confirms default_fixture (or test_fixture) is gated behind #[cfg(test)] and only referenced from test modules
Loopback bind preserved: integration test confirms rpc-server still binds 127.0.0.1:0 only — no changes from RPC-005
Embedded fan-out uses host runtime: source-shape test confirms EmbeddedTransport's fan-out task is `self.handle.spawn(...)` — not `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new`

rules.text: default_fixture() becomes #[cfg(test)]-only — production SharedFspecService MUST NOT reach the fixture path
list_work_units() returns the live snapshot from a real WorkUnitsWatcher observing the project's spec/work-units.json file
WorkUnitsWatcher lives in codelet/core/src/work_units.rs (NOT in codelet/rpc) so the dependency arrow stays rpc → core (rpc → napi remains forbidden)
WorkUnitsWatcher exposes exactly three public surfaces: new(workspace), snapshot() -> Vec<WorkUnitInfo>, subscribe() -> broadcast::Receiver<Vec<WorkUnitInfo>>
Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate variant changes shape from unit to WorkUnitsUpdate(Vec<WorkUnitInfo>) and rides bincode-of-Envelope on the WS wire — no JSON debug envelope, no separate channel
Push events ride tokio::sync::broadcast — NOT a tarpc stream return — preserving strict tarpc req/res semantics (RPC-002 §5.1, §5.2 verbatim)
Both transports expose an identical work_units_rx() -> broadcast::Receiver<Vec<WorkUnitInfo>> API surface so the UI is transport-agnostic
Embedded transport returns the watcher's broadcast subscription directly with NO envelope encoding (zero-cost path)
Embedded fan-out task spawns on the host-supplied tokio::runtime::Handle — NEVER constructs its own Runtime (RPC-005 Q9 invariant preserved)
WS server sends an initial WorkUnitsUpdate frame immediately on connection (before any file mutation) — no explicit subscribe RPC required
Reserved envelope variants (Event, LogEvent, CmdReq, CmdRes) remain rejected by the server — only Rpc and WorkUnitsUpdate are now legitimate
WorkUnitInfo remains defined exactly once in codelet/rpc-types and is reused verbatim as the WorkUnitsUpdate payload — no NAPI fork, no shadowed type
codelet/napi keeps a thin shim that forwards each broadcast event into the existing ThreadsafeFunction callback — TS frontend behaviour and getAllWorkUnits() shape are unchanged
