RPC-006.title: Real work-units backing + first streaming envelope variant (WorkUnitsUpdate)

userStory.action: have list_work_units() return real project work units AND push WorkUnitsUpdate envelope frames on file changes over both transports
userStory.benefit: I can build a live work-units list view in RPC-009 with parity between embedded and WebSocket modes

architectureNotes.text: Type lift target: codelet/rpc-types gains five new types (SessionId newtype String, SessionInfo, SessionStatus enum, StreamChunk tagged enum, LogRecord). All carry serde Serialize/Deserialize derives and the #[cfg_attr(feature = "napi", napi_derive::napi(...))] gating per the existing WorkUnitInfo pattern at codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs:25-36. NAPI re-exports them with #[napi(js_name = ...)] preserved on every renamed field (correlationId, observedCorrelationIds, toolCall, etc.) so the TS frontend sees zero change.

FspecService trait additions in codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs:25-36: five new async methods (list_sessions, create_session(role: Option<String>) -> SessionId, send_input(session_id: SessionId, text: String), interrupt(session_id: SessionId), get_session_status(session_id: SessionId) -> SessionStatus). The tarpc macro regenerates FspecServiceClient for both transports automatically — no transport-specific stubs.

Envelope variant changes in codelet/rpc-server/src/envelope.rs: Event changes from unit `Event` to struct-variant `Event { session_id: SessionId, chunk: StreamChunk }`; LogEvent changes from unit `LogEvent` to tuple-variant `LogEvent(LogRecord)`. CmdReq and CmdRes remain unit variants. Envelope::variant_name() updated. The pump's run_envelope_pump match arms grow two new "forward to inbound handler" cases for Event and LogEvent — server-side handlers reject inbound Event/LogEvent (clients never push), client-side handlers demux them onto chunks_tx/logs_tx watch+broadcast pairs (same pattern as ClientInbound::on_work_units_update in pump.rs:95-101).

Server-side fan-out (handle_connection in codelet/rpc-server/src/server.rs:71-125): the existing work_units_fanout task is joined by two siblings — chunks_fanout (drains service.chunks_rx() and emits Envelope::Event { session_id, chunk } via envelope_out_tx) and logs_fanout (drains service.logs_rx() and emits Envelope::LogEvent(record)). Both honour the same RecvError::Lagged debug-log-and-resync pattern as work_units_fanout. All three tasks abort on connection drop.

Client-side demux (codelet/rpc-server/src/client.rs): FspecWsClient grows two more sibling fields — work_units_watch_tx is joined by chunks_tx (broadcast::Sender<(SessionId, StreamChunk)>) and logs_tx (broadcast::Sender<LogRecord>). The chunks/logs path uses raw broadcast (NOT the watch-replay pattern used for WorkUnitsUpdate) because StreamChunks are delta events whose history matters in order — a fresh subscriber that misses prior chunks needs them replayed via a separate read-back RPC, NOT via broadcast replay. Public methods chunks_rx() and logs_rx() return broadcast::Receivers.

Embedded transport (codelet/rpc-embedded/src/lib.rs): EmbeddedTransport gains two sibling methods chunks_rx() and logs_rx() returning the watcher's broadcast subscriptions DIRECTLY (no envelope encoding, zero-cost path). Same shape as RPC-006's work_units_rx at codelet/rpc-embedded/src/lib.rs:89-91. Source-shape regression: tests/rpc_006_source_shape.rs gains a sibling assertion that the new chunks/logs paths also contain no bincode::serialize call.

tracing::Layer for LogRecord broadcast: codelet-rpc-server's main.rs (and EmbeddedTransport::new for embedded hosts that opt in) registers a custom tracing_subscriber::Layer (analogous to codelet/napi/src/lib.rs:152-205 TypeScriptLayer) that captures level, target, message, timestamp into a LogRecord and pushes onto SharedFspecService::logs_tx. NAPI's existing setRustLogCallback path is preserved unchanged — the Layer in NAPI keeps forwarding to the ThreadsafeFunction, while the rpc-server's Layer is a sibling subscriber on the registry.

NAPI compatibility shim (the equivalent of codelet/napi/src/work_units_watcher.rs after RPC-006): once the SessionManager streaming path is reachable from codelet/rpc, codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs keeps its existing GLOBAL_CHUNK_CALLBACK + GlobalChunkCallback pattern (codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs:55-87) — it now reads from the SAME broadcast::Sender housed in SharedFspecService and forwards each (session_id, chunk) tuple into the existing ThreadsafeFunction. Vitest smoke test gains an assertion that sessionSetGlobalChunkCallback callbacks still fire after the lift.

Test layout: NEW Rust integration tests under codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/ (embedded_session_repl.rs, embedded_log_event.rs) and codelet/rpc-server/tests/ (ws_session_repl.rs, ws_log_event.rs, ws_multi_client_chunks.rs, cross_transport_chunk_parity.rs). UPDATED tests: codelet/rpc-server/tests/ws_reserved_variants_after_rpc006.rs narrows expected-rejected list from {Event, LogEvent, CmdReq, CmdRes} to {CmdReq, CmdRes}. Source-shape: codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/rpc_006_source_shape.rs widens the no-bincode-on-embedded-push assertion to cover chunks_rx and logs_rx. Vitest smoke at src/__tests__/napi-workunitinfo-shape.test.ts gains a sibling test that creates a session via sessionManagerCreate and asserts at least one chunk is delivered to the global callback.

SharedFspecService grows three fields beyond RPC-006: an Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle> (the trait lives in codelet/core; concrete SessionManager remains in codelet/napi per rule [17] — NO concrete Arc<SessionManager> in SharedFspecService, the trait object is the only allowed type so codelet/rpc never imports codelet-napi), a tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<(SessionId, StreamChunk)> chunks_tx with bounded capacity (suggested 256 to absorb token-delta storms), and a tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<LogRecord> logs_tx with bounded capacity (suggested 1024). The host (rpc-server main.rs and EmbeddedTransport hosts) constructs the concrete SessionManager and hands it to SharedFspecService::new as Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle>. Existing list_work_units_calls counter and Arc<WorkUnitsWatcher> from RPC-006 are retained.

RPC-007.description:
Add the minimum viable session-layer RPCs (list_sessions, create_session, send_input, interrupt, get_session_status) AND light up two more envelope variants — Envelope::Event(SessionStreamChunk) and Envelope::LogEvent(LogRecord) — so the agent REPL has full backend support on both transports.

See spec/attachments/RPC-007/plan.md for the full plan.

Follows RPC-006. Unblocks RPC-009 (basic UI with REPL).

examples.text: Embedded list_sessions: a Rust caller constructs an EmbeddedTransport from a tokio Handle, calls list_sessions(context::current()) and observes the same Vec<SessionInfo> the underlying SessionManager singleton already exposes via NAPI list_sessions
WS list_sessions: developer starts rpc-server bound to a workspace, connects a WS client, calls list_sessions and receives the same Vec<SessionInfo> as the embedded path (cross-transport parity)

Embedded create_session + send_input + chunks_rx: developer creates a session with a stub-provider model, subscribes to chunks_rx() before send_input, sends "hi", and observes at least one StreamChunk::Text (or AssistantTextDelta-equivalent) on the receiver within 5s — without ever holding a tarpc stream

WS create_session + send_input + chunks_rx: same input, same stub provider, both transports yield the same chunk sequence end-to-end (parity); WS frames are bincode-encoded Envelope::Event { session_id, chunk } values

LogEvent on both transports: the host emits tracing::info!("hello") on the rpc-server (or the embedded host); WS clients observe an Envelope::LogEvent(LogRecord) frame and embedded callers observe a LogRecord on logs_rx() with matching message and level

interrupt(session_id): developer calls interrupt during a streaming response on either transport; the session moves to interrupted state and a StreamChunk::Interrupted (or equivalent) arrives on chunks_rx(), confirming the no-op return value of the RPC was paired with side-effect observation via the push channel

get_session_status: developer queries get_session_status(session_id) on either transport before, during, and after a stub-provider response; the returned SessionStatus reflects Idle → Running → Idle transitions consistent with the session's lifecycle (and equal across both transports)

Multi-client unfiltered fan-out: two WS clients attach to the same rpc-server; one client creates a session and sends input; BOTH clients observe the same StreamChunks on their respective chunks_rx() channels (no per-client filter in this card)

NAPI co-listener parity: TS frontend developer runs npm test after the lift; the existing sessionSetGlobalChunkCallback callback continues to fire for new sessions (unchanged shape) AND a Rust embedded subscriber created against the SAME SessionManager instance observes byte-equal StreamChunks on its chunks_rx()

Reserved variants narrowed: developer sends Envelope::CmdReq and Envelope::CmdRes to the WS server; both are still rejected and counted in ServerStats.rejected_envelopes/rejected_variants — but Envelope::Event and Envelope::LogEvent are NO LONGER on the rejected list (regression of RPC-005 scenario 6 widened beyond RPC-006's narrowing)

Bincode wire format for Event and LogEvent: developer captures a WS frame on the wire and confirms it decodes as bincode of Envelope::Event { session_id, chunk } or Envelope::LogEvent(LogRecord) — not JSON, not a custom shape (RPC-005 architecture rule [5] preserved)

Source-shape regression: ast-grep / cargo metadata over codelet/rpc/Cargo.toml confirms NO codelet-napi import; type-uniqueness regression confirms StreamChunk, SessionInfo, SessionStatus, SessionId, LogRecord are each defined exactly ONCE across the workspace (in codelet/rpc-types) and re-exported by codelet/napi

questions.answer: Trait + Handle in codelet/core, impl stays in napi: define a SessionManagerHandle trait (and a per-session Handle type) in codelet/core; codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs SessionManager keeps its existing 8,649 LOC implementation and implements the trait; SharedFspecService takes Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle>; this preserves the rpc → napi forbidden invariant via DI from the host (rpc-server main.rs / EmbeddedTransport::new) and avoids a 21+ point full lift
questions.text: @human: SessionManager lifting strategy. The plan says "the session manager dependency lives behind a re-export shim — same pattern as the watcher in RPC-006". RPC-006's watcher was ~250 LOC moved into codelet/core. SessionManager today is 8649 LOC in codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs and pulls in codelet-cli, codelet-git, codelet-tools, codelet-providers, codelet-common, persistence, ThreadsafeFunctions, OAuth, ghost commits, scheduler, etc. Three options: (A) full lift of SessionManager into codelet/core (likely 21+ points on its own — requires breaking RPC-007 down); (B) introduce a thin SessionManagerHandle trait in codelet/core, implement it in codelet/napi, and have the embedded-test path use a minimal in-process implementation while the WS server path bridges via NAPI re-export — keeps RPC-007 at 8 points but defers the real co-listener invariant; (C) lift only a SessionManager skeleton into codelet/core that owns the PER-SESSION broadcast::Sender<StreamChunk> + the Status enum + the spawn task, and leave NAPI-only concerns (persistence, ghost commits, OAuth, blocklist) on a parallel NAPI-owned wrapper that delegates streaming to the lifted skeleton. Which path do you want?

questions.answer: Lift ALL 23 variants of StreamChunk verbatim from codelet/napi/src/types.rs:217 into codelet/rpc-types as the single source of truth, behind feature "napi" with #[napi(discriminant="type")] and every #[napi(js_name=...)] rename preserved (correlationId, observedCorrelationIds, toolCall, etc.); codelet/napi re-exports the lifted enum so the TS shape sees zero change; both transports use the same enum on the wire — no WireStreamChunk subset, no per-card narrowing, no From<> bridge
questions.text: @human: StreamChunk lift fidelity. NAPI's StreamChunk in codelet/napi/src/types.rs:217 has 23 variants today (Text, Thinking, ToolCall, ToolResult, ToolProgress, SessionStateChange, UserNotification, Interrupted, TokenUpdate, ContextFillUpdate, Done, Error, UserInput, IncomingMessage, SupervisorPendingInjection, CompactionComplete, FspecCommandRequest, FspecCommandResult, WorkUnitsUpdate, IsolationStateChange, FooterStateUpdate, DebugStateChange, ...) plus #[napi(discriminant="type")] and many #[napi(js_name=...)] attributes. Three options for the lift: (1) lift ALL 23 variants verbatim into rpc-types under feature "napi" — preserves TS shape but exposes the full surface immediately on the wire; (2) lift only the REPL-relevant subset (Text, Thinking, ToolCall, ToolResult, ToolProgress, Interrupted, Done, Error, UserInput, SessionStateChange, TokenUpdate) and keep the rest as NAPI-only types behind a re-export-or-wrap pattern; (3) introduce a separate WireStreamChunk in rpc-types with only the variants the WS transport needs and have NAPI's StreamChunk be a SUPERSET (sourced from a From<WireStreamChunk> impl). Which?

questions.answer: Introduce a new minimal StubProvider in codelet/providers gated behind a `test-support` Cargo feature; on any send_input it emits a deterministic chunk sequence [StreamChunk::Text("hi back"), StreamChunk::Done]; both transports' integration tests enable this feature and assert byte-equal chunks across embedded and WS paths; no real model credentials in CI; any pre-existing mock in codelet/providers stays untouched
questions.text: @human: Test-stub provider ergonomics. The plan says "reuse the test-stub-provider that already exists in codelet/providers". I have not yet found a stub provider in codelet/providers — the closest may be a feature-gated mock for the registry. Should I (a) scout the providers crate and adapt whatever's there, (b) introduce a new minimal StubProvider in codelet/providers that emits a deterministic `[Text("hi back"), Done]` sequence on any send_input, gated behind a `test-support` feature, or (c) use Rig's own no-op provider if one exists?

questions.answer: Keep RPC-007 as a single card and re-estimate to 13 points (the architectural-rule upper limit). The trait+handle SessionManager strategy and the verbatim 23-variant StreamChunk lift each shrink one axis of risk but the remaining surface (5 new RPCs + 2 new envelope variants + 5 type lifts + tracing::Layer for LogEvent + StubProvider behind test-support + ~6–10 cross-transport integration tests + NAPI co-listener parity + source-shape regressions) is honestly 13 points, not 8. If during testing/implementing it becomes clear we need to split, we move backward to specifying and break out children then.
questions.text: @human: Estimate sanity check. The plan estimates 8 points (4-8 hours). Given the scale — five RPCs, two new envelope variants, lifting 5+ types into rpc-types, lifting some subset of SessionManager into core, two new fan-out tasks per WS connection, NAPI co-listener wiring, a tracing_subscriber::Layer for LogEvent, a stub-provider integration test, and ~6-10 new integration tests across both transports — should this card stay at 8 or should we BREAK IT DOWN now into (i) a SessionManager lift card, (ii) a StreamChunk type lift card, (iii) the actual session RPCs + Event/LogEvent envelope card? The current dependency chain has RPC-008/RPC-009 waiting on RPC-007, so breakdown delays the REPL but keeps each card at the architectural-rule limit of 13 points.

rules.text: FspecService gains exactly five new async methods — list_sessions, create_session, send_input, interrupt, get_session_status — defined ONCE in codelet/rpc; both transports implement them via the single FspecServiceImpl adapter (no method is embedded-only or WS-only)

Five new types are lifted into codelet/rpc-types as the single source of truth: SessionId (newtype around String), SessionInfo, SessionStatus, StreamChunk (tagged enum), LogRecord — defined exactly once and re-exported by codelet/napi via the existing #[cfg_attr(feature = "napi", napi(...))] pattern so the TS shape (sessionStateChange, toolCall, etc.) is preserved

Envelope::Event variant changes from unit to Event { session_id: SessionId, chunk: StreamChunk } and Envelope::LogEvent changes from unit to LogEvent(LogRecord); both are now legitimate variants and ride bincode-of-Envelope on the WS wire — no JSON debug envelope, no separate channel

CmdReq and CmdRes envelope variants remain reserved-and-rejected — server still counts them in ServerStats.rejected_envelopes/rejected_variants, only Rpc, WorkUnitsUpdate, Event, and LogEvent are now legitimate

Streaming events ride a sibling tokio::sync::broadcast — NOT a tarpc stream return; send_input() returns () immediately and the caller observes streaming output via chunks_rx() (RPC-002 §5.1, §5.2 verbatim — strict tarpc req/res semantics preserved)

Both transports expose identical sibling subscription methods — chunks_rx() -> broadcast::Receiver<(SessionId, StreamChunk)> and logs_rx() -> broadcast::Receiver<LogRecord> — so the future ratatui frontend (RPC-008/RPC-009) is transport-agnostic

Embedded transport returns the broadcast subscriptions DIRECTLY (no envelope encoding, zero-cost path); the WS server's per-connection handle_connection grows two more fan-out tasks — chunks and logs — alongside the existing work-units fan-out from RPC-006

Multi-client fan-out is unfiltered in this card: every connected client receives every session's chunks AND every log record; per-client subscription filters and read-only observer mode are explicitly deferred to a follow-up card (RPC-002 §11 risks list)

LogEvent uses a separate broadcast channel populated by a custom tracing_subscriber::Layer registered at codelet-rpc-server startup (and at EmbeddedTransport::new when the host opts in) — replacing the ad-hoc setRustLogCallback path on the rust-frontend backend (NAPI keeps its existing setRustLogCallback unchanged)

NAPI behaviour is unchanged: existing sessionManagerCreate / sessionManagerList / sessionSendInput / sessionInterrupt / sessionGetStatus / sessionSetGlobalChunkCallback / setRustLogCallback exports keep their TS shape and continue to fire — NAPI becomes ONE listener on the same broadcast senders, not the only listener (RPC-002 §6 verbatim)

rpc → napi remains FORBIDDEN (RPC-006 source-shape invariant preserved): codelet/rpc/Cargo.toml has no codelet-napi import; the SessionManager dependency lives behind a re-export shim reachable from codelet/rpc the same way the WorkUnitsWatcher does (rpc → core is permitted; rpc → napi is not)

Q9 embedded runtime invariant preserved: the two new fan-out tasks (chunks, logs) spawn on the host-supplied tokio::runtime::Handle — NEVER construct a new Runtime — so the RPC-005 source-shape regression test remains green
rpc-server binary continues to bind 127.0.0.1 loopback only (RPC-005 invariant preserved); no auth/TLS in this card — explicitly out of scope per the plan
Cancellation propagation via tarpc context::Context is OUT OF SCOPE for this card: interrupt(session_id) is a normal RPC, not a context.deadline story (RPC-005 architecture rule [14] preserved)

Reverse callbacks (callFspecCommand) are OUT OF SCOPE: CmdReq/CmdRes envelope variants stay reserved-and-rejected; the decision between two services and envelope frames with correlation IDs is made in RPC-011 or its own dedicated card (RPC-002 §8)

Tests use a stub LLM provider (the test-stub-provider that already exists in codelet/providers) — no real model credentials in CI; both transports must observe at least one StreamChunk::AssistantTextDelta within 5s of send_input

Trait + Handle in codelet/core, impl stays in napi: define a SessionManagerHandle trait (and a per-session Handle type) in codelet/core; codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs SessionManager keeps its existing 8,649 LOC implementation and implements the trait; SharedFspecService takes Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle>; this preserves the rpc → napi forbidden invariant via DI from the host (rpc-server main.rs / EmbeddedTransport::new) and avoids a 21+ point full lift

Lift ALL 23 variants of StreamChunk verbatim from codelet/napi/src/types.rs:217 into codelet/rpc-types as the single source of truth, behind feature "napi" with #[napi(discriminant="type")] and every #[napi(js_name=...)] rename preserved (correlationId, observedCorrelationIds, toolCall, etc.); codelet/napi re-exports the lifted enum so the TS shape sees zero change; both transports use the same enum on the wire — no WireStreamChunk subset, no per-card narrowing, no From<> bridge

Introduce a new minimal StubProvider in codelet/providers gated behind a `test-support` Cargo feature; on any send_input it emits a deterministic chunk sequence [StreamChunk::Text("hi back"), StreamChunk::Done]; both transports' integration tests enable this feature and assert byte-equal chunks across embedded and WS paths; no real model credentials in CI; any pre-existing mock in codelet/providers stays untouched

Keep RPC-007 as a single card and re-estimate to 13 points (the architectural-rule upper limit). The trait+handle SessionManager strategy and the verbatim 23-variant StreamChunk lift each shrink one axis of risk but the remaining surface (5 new RPCs + 2 new envelope variants + 5 type lifts + tracing::Layer for LogEvent + StubProvider behind test-support + ~6–10 cross-transport integration tests + NAPI co-listener parity + source-shape regressions) is honestly 13 points, not 8. If during testing/implementing it becomes clear we need to split, we move backward to specifying and break out children then.

Shared NAPI contract invariant: the SessionManagerHandle trait + the five new types in codelet/rpc-types ARE the contract that all three frontends consume identically — (a) the JS fspec frontend sees them via codelet/napi's existing #[napi] re-exports (TS shape preserved verbatim), (b) the built-in ratatui fspec frontend sees them via EmbeddedTransport calling Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle> directly, (c) the WebSocket fspec frontend sees them via tarpc-generated FspecServiceClient over bincode-encoded Envelope. The trait surface, the type shapes, and the StreamChunk variants are byte-equal across all three paths — no transport-specific divergence, no JS-only or Rust-only fields. NAPI annotations live ONLY at the codelet/napi re-export layer; the trait and types in codelet/core/codelet/rpc-types are NAPI-free Rust. This is the architectural line that lets RPC-009's ratatui REPL and the existing TS REPL behave identically against the same SessionManager singleton.

SharedFspecService gains Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle> (trait object — concrete SessionManager stays in codelet/napi per rule [17]), broadcast::Sender<(SessionId, StreamChunk)>, and broadcast::Sender<LogRecord>; the existing list_work_units_calls counter and the WorkUnitsWatcher from RPC-006 are retained for parity tests. Hosts (rpc-server bin, EmbeddedTransport host) inject the concrete SessionManager via Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle>; codelet/rpc itself never depends on codelet/napi.

stateHistory.reason: 1:1 feature-to-test-file rule requires splitting RPC-007 spec into 8 features along test-file boundaries

RPC-007.title: Session RPCs + StreamChunk/LogEvent push channels (REPL backend)

userStory.action: drive a session over either transport (embedded or WebSocket) — create it, send input, observe streaming chunks and structured log events, query its status, and interrupt it — using the same FspecService trait and the same broadcast push channels
userStory.benefit: the basic ratatui REPL in RPC-009 can be wired up against a single transport-agnostic backend without depending on NAPI or hard-coding either transport
userStory.role: developer integrating the future ratatui agent REPL

architectureNotes.text: RPC-002 architecture conformance is locked: doc 11 §Q1 (alt-screen), §Q2 (~30-LoC homegrown Compositor — NOT rat-event/rat-salsa), §Q3 (bare ratatui — NOT tui-realm), §Q5 (USE tui-popup — production code path is the adapter, hand-rolled centered_rect lives only in tests/comments as fallback), and §Q9 (host-supplied Handle preserved at the trait boundary). Q4/Q6/Q7/Q8 are explicitly NOT pre-decided here — those belong to RPC-002 Slices 03–06.

Crate layout (codelet/fspec-tui/src/): lib.rs (exports App, FspecBackend, EmbeddedFspecBackend, WebSocketFspecBackend, Theme); app/{mod.rs (App + run loop), compositor.rs (~30 LoC dispatcher), event.rs (AppEvent enum), action.rs (Action enum)}; components/{mod.rs (Component trait + Priority + EventResult + Callback type), hello.rs (Background-priority placeholder), help_dialog.rs (Critical-priority dialog with tui-popup adapter)}; tui/mod.rs (crossterm init/teardown + panic hook + terminal guard); transport/{mod.rs (FspecBackend trait), embedded.rs, websocket.rs}; theme.rs. NO views/, input/, mouse/ subdirs in this card — those arrive in later slices.

Adopted dependency stack (codelet/fspec-tui/Cargo.toml — locked by RPC-002 doc 03 §C): ratatui (workspace; features='all-widgets'), crossterm (workspace), tui-popup = '0.6', tokio (workspace; features='full'), async-trait (workspace), codelet-rpc, codelet-rpc-types, codelet-rpc-embedded, codelet-rpc-server (all via workspace), anyhow (workspace), tracing (workspace). dev-dependencies: insta (workspace; features='yaml') + tempfile (workspace) + url (workspace) + tokio-tungstenite (workspace; required by WS smoke test). The ratatui workspace dependency must be added to codelet/Cargo.toml's [workspace.dependencies] block since it does not exist there yet.

Compositor implementation (~30 LoC core, codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/compositor.rs): `pub struct Compositor { layers: Vec<Box<dyn Component>>, registration_counter: u64 }`. push() bumps the counter and re-sorts; sort uses stable `sort_by_key(|a| a.priority())`; handle_event walks `iter_mut().rev()` skipping inactive layers and short-circuits on Consumed; render walks `iter_mut()` (forward) so highest priority paints last; update fans Action across ALL layers; pop() and remove(id) return Option<Box<dyn Component>>. handle_paste(text) is a stub that synthesises a key-event sequence and dispatches via handle_event — proper paste semantics arrive in Slice 06 with tui-textarea.

App run loop (codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/mod.rs): `App { compositor, action_tx, action_rx, backend: Arc<dyn FspecBackend>, theme: Arc<Theme>, should_quit, should_render }`. `App::new(backend)` constructs a Compositor pre-populated with HelloComponent at Background priority and an mpsc::unbounded_channel() Action bus. `App::run(self) -> Result<()>` initialises the terminal via the tui::TerminalGuard (which runs ratatui::init() + EnableMouseCapture + EnableBracketedPaste and registers the panic hook), enters a tokio::select! over (a) crossterm EventStream::new(), (b) action_rx.recv(), (c) tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_millis(16)) gated by self.should_render. Key events route through compositor.handle_event(); Resize sets should_render=true; Paste(text) calls compositor.handle_paste(&text); the `?` key at App-level pushes a HelpDialog onto the compositor; the `q` key sets should_quit=true. On exit, ratatui::restore() + DisableMouseCapture + DisableBracketedPaste run via the TerminalGuard's Drop.

EmbeddedFspecBackend (codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/embedded.rs): `pub struct EmbeddedFspecBackend { transport: EmbeddedTransport, client: FspecServiceClient }` with `pub fn new(handle: tokio::runtime::Handle, service: Arc<SharedFspecService>) -> Self` — non-defaulted on Handle to preserve RPC-005 Q9 at the trait boundary. The constructor builds the EmbeddedTransport and immediately calls `transport.client()` to spawn the in-process tarpc server task on the host's runtime; subsequent RPC method bodies are one-line delegates `self.client.<rpc>(context::current(), args).await`. Subscription methods are zero-cost passthroughs to `transport.work_units_rx()`, `transport.chunks_rx()`, `transport.logs_rx()`.

WebSocketFspecBackend (codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/websocket.rs): `pub struct WebSocketFspecBackend { client: FspecWsClient }` with `pub async fn connect(url: url::Url) -> Result<Self>`. The constructor calls `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(url)`, hands the resulting WebSocketStream to `codelet_rpc_server::ws_client_connect()`, and stores the FspecWsClient. RPC method bodies delegate `self.client.rpc.<rpc>(context::current(), args).await`. Subscription methods delegate to `self.client.work_units_rx()` / `chunks_rx()` / `logs_rx()`. Envelope framing remains entirely encapsulated inside codelet-rpc-server — no envelope code lives in codelet/fspec-tui.

Terminal lifecycle + panic hook (codelet/fspec-tui/src/tui/mod.rs): `pub struct TerminalGuard { terminal: Terminal<CrosstermBackend<Stdout>> }` exposes `TerminalGuard::init() -> Result<Self>` that calls ratatui::init() + crossterm::execute!(stdout(), EnableMouseCapture, EnableBracketedPaste) and registers a `std::panic::set_hook` that runs `ratatui::restore()` + DisableMouseCapture + DisableBracketedPaste before delegating to the previous panic hook. `impl Drop for TerminalGuard` performs the same restoration. The hook is registered idempotently — repeated calls re-use the existing previous hook chain and do not nest forever (use `Once` to guard registration).

Existing source-shape test widening (codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/architecture_invariants.rs::scenario_7_*): the existing scan loop must extend its directory list from `["rpc-embedded/src"]` to `["rpc-embedded/src", "fspec-tui/src"]` with the same forbidden-string set (Builder, Runtime::new, etc.). Same test crate; the assertion message gains the new path so failures are obviously attributable to either crate. RPC-008 owns this widening — it is part of the card.

Out of scope (referenced for future cards, not implemented here): VirtualList, MultiLineInput, dialogs beyond HelpDialog, theme light variant, MouseTrackingToggle (RPC-002 Slices 03-06); binary entry points fspec/fspec daemon/fspec client (RPC-010); real list view + REPL (RPC-009); per-client subscription filtering and read-only observer mode (RPC-002 §11 follow-ups); cancellation propagation via tarpc context::Context (deliberately deferred per RPC-005 architecture rule [14]); reverse callbacks / CmdReq-CmdRes (RPC-011 or its own card per RPC-002 §8).

FILE LAYOUT (locked Q-FILE-1): Split per RPC-002 doc 11 — codelet/fspec-tui/src/{lib.rs, app.rs, terminal.rs, compositor.rs, transport/{mod.rs, embedded.rs, websocket.rs}, components/{mod.rs, hello.rs, help_dialog.rs}}. Each file kept well under 300 LoC. Tests live in codelet/fspec-tui/tests/ for integration + per-module #[cfg(test)] for units.

SNAPSHOTS (locked Q-SNAP-1): Use `insta` crate as a dev-dependency. Three scenarios produce snapshots: (a) App-with-mock-backend after Key('?') → "help_dialog_visible"; (b) App-with-mock-backend after Key(Esc) → "help_dialog_dismissed"; (c) Isolated HelpDialog 80x24 → "help_dialog__centered_popup_80x24". Use `insta::assert_yaml_snapshot!` over a serialised cell-grid representation of the ratatui Buffer (cell.symbol() per row). Reviewer workflow: `cargo insta review`.

FIXTURE-CENTRIC INTEGRATION TESTING (locked Q-FIX-1): codelet/fspec-tui/tests/common/mod.rs hosts 5 reusable fixtures used by every integration test: (1) `temp_service() -> (TempDir, Arc<SharedFspecService>)` builds a real codelet_core::work_units::WorkUnitsWatcher in a tempdir + real SharedFspecService; (2) `start_ws_server(service) -> (SocketAddr, JoinHandle<()>)` calls real codelet_rpc_server::bind_and_serve("127.0.0.1:0", service); (3) `MockBackend` is a hand-rolled `impl FspecBackend` with seedable in-memory data + broadcast::Sender handles tests use to push synthetic events; (4) `test_app(backend) -> (App, Terminal<TestBackend>)` constructs App + 80x24 TestBackend pair; (5) `render_one_frame(&mut terminal, &mut app) -> Buffer` drives a single render cycle and returns a clone of the Buffer for snapshotting. Every integration test imports `mod common;` and uses these — zero duplicate setup code. Per Q-DEV-CORE-1 below, real services flow through the fixtures.

DEV-DEPENDENCY POLICY (locked Q-DEV-CORE-1): codelet/fspec-tui/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies] MAY include codelet-core because integration fixtures need to construct a real WorkUnitsWatcher (in codelet_core::work_units) to round-trip a real SharedFspecService through both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend smoke tests. This matches the existing pattern at codelet/rpc-embedded/Cargo.toml:23. Production [dependencies] of codelet/fspec-tui MUST NOT include codelet-core or codelet-napi — the shipped TUI binary path stays clean. Source-shape regression test enforces the asymmetry: zero codelet-core/codelet-napi in [dependencies], zero codelet-napi in [dev-dependencies], codelet-core ALLOWED in [dev-dependencies].

TEST FILE LAYOUT (locked): Per-module #[cfg(test)] units inside src/: compositor.rs has 12 inline unit tests per RPC-002 doc 09 §A.7 + §D.1; components/help_dialog.rs has an inline snapshot test using ratatui::backend::TestBackend + insta::assert_yaml_snapshot!; components/hello.rs has an inline rendering test asserting centered placement. Integration tests live in codelet/fspec-tui/tests/: common/mod.rs (5 fixtures per Q-FIX-1); embedded_backend_smoke.rs (uses temp_service fixture, asserts list_work_units + work_units_rx); ws_backend_smoke.rs (uses temp_service + start_ws_server fixtures, builds WebSocketFspecBackend); app_with_mock_backend.rs (uses MockBackend + test_app fixtures, snapshots through `?` then ESC); source_shape.rs (scans src/ for forbidden patterns + parses Cargo.toml dependency tables); panic_hook.rs (verifies raw mode is disabled after a forced panic via catch_unwind). Each integration test file declares `#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]` at the top to mirror the rpc-embedded pattern.

RPC-008.description:
Create a new codelet/fspec-tui crate hosting the ratatui app shell (Compositor + Component + EventResult + App) plus a transport-agnostic FspecBackend trait with embedded and WebSocket implementations. Renders only a placeholder Hello component and an ESC-dismiss dialog — no real UI. Implements RPC-002 Slice 01 (foundation) and parts of Slice 02.

See spec/attachments/RPC-008/plan.md for the full plan.

Follows RPC-007. Unblocks RPC-009 (real UI) and RPC-010 (binary entry points).

examples.text: Crate scaffolding compiles: developer adds `codelet/fspec-tui` to `codelet/Cargo.toml`'s `members` list, copies the dependency block from the plan into `codelet/fspec-tui/Cargo.toml`, runs `cargo build -p codelet-fspec-tui`, and the crate compiles clean with no warnings

FspecBackend trait compiles: developer writes a fresh consumer that asks for `Arc<dyn FspecBackend>`, swaps the concrete type between `Arc::new(EmbeddedFspecBackend::new(handle, service))` and `Arc::new(WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(url).await?)`, and the consumer code is byte-identical in both arms — the only difference is the constructor

Embedded backend smoke test: a Rust integration test constructs an `EmbeddedFspecBackend` from `tokio::runtime::Handle::current()` plus a `SharedFspecService::new(watcher)`, calls `backend.list_work_units().await`, observes the same Vec<WorkUnitInfo> the underlying watcher's snapshot returns, then subscribes to `backend.work_units_rx()` and observes a fresh snapshot after the watcher receives a filesystem event

WebSocket backend smoke test: a Rust integration test starts a `bind_and_serve` rpc-server on 127.0.0.1:0, constructs a `WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/).await?`, calls `backend.list_work_units().await`, observes the same Vec<WorkUnitInfo> the embedded backend would have returned (cross-transport parity), then subscribes to `backend.work_units_rx()` and observes the initial WorkUnitsUpdate snapshot frame from RPC-006

Compositor priority routing: a Compositor unit test pushes a Background-priority HelloComponent then a Critical-priority HelpDialog, dispatches a synthetic key event, and observes the HelpDialog's handle_event was invoked but HelloComponent's was NOT — proving the priority sort routed first to Critical

FIFO tiebreak: a Compositor unit test pushes two Medium-priority components A then B, dispatches an event, and observes B::handle_event was called BEFORE A::handle_event — proving last-registered wins at equal priority

Deferred-callback removal: a Compositor unit test pushes a HelpDialog, dispatches an ESC key, observes the dispatch returns `Consumed(Some(callback))`, then runs the callback against the compositor and observes the dialog is gone (`compositor.layers.len() == 0`)

App-with-mock-backend: an integration test constructs `App::new(Arc::new(MockBackend::default()))` against an 80x24 TestBackend terminal, drives the app loop with the synthetic key sequence `?` then `ESC`, snapshots the frame buffer after `?` (HelpDialog visible) and after `ESC` (HelpDialog gone), and both snapshots match insta golden files

Help dialog snapshot: a snapshot test renders just `HelpDialog` against an 80x24 TestBackend, calls `insta::assert_yaml_snapshot!` on the resulting Buffer, and the captured cell grid shows the rounded-border popup centered on the screen with the three keybinding lines (`?`, `ESC`, `q`) — re-runs against the golden file are byte-equal

Panic-hook terminal restoration: a Rust unit test installs the panic hook, deliberately panics from inside a `terminal.draw(|f| panic!())`, catches the panic via `std::panic::catch_unwind`, and asserts that `crossterm::terminal::is_raw_mode_enabled()` returns false afterwards — proving the panic hook restored the terminal even though Drop did not run on the App's terminal guard

Source-shape regression: a Rust integration test scans `codelet/fspec-tui/src/` and asserts no file contains `tokio::runtime::Builder`, `runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread`, `runtime::Builder::new_current_thread`, `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new`, or `Runtime::new()` — preserving RPC-005 Q9. A sibling assertion parses `codelet/fspec-tui/Cargo.toml` and confirms `[dependencies]` lists neither `codelet-napi` nor `codelet-core`, AND `[dev-dependencies]` does not list `codelet-napi` (but MAY list `codelet-core` for real-service fixtures).

questions.answer: Use tokio_tungstenite::connect_async directly inside WebSocketFspecBackend::connect — the plan section 'Existing RPC-005/006/007 artifacts this card builds on' explicitly says 'WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(url) opens the WebSocket via tokio_tungstenite::connect_async, hands the resulting WebSocketStream to ws_client_connect, and stores the FspecWsClient.' No new helper required in codelet-rpc-server. If RPC-009/RPC-010 later finds the connect+ws_client_connect dance is repeated, that future card can extract a helper without breaking the FspecBackend trait surface.
questions.text: @human: Should we use `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async` directly inside `WebSocketFspecBackend::connect` even though the existing tests in codelet/rpc-server/tests/ use it indirectly via test helpers, or should we expose a thin `codelet_rpc_server::ws_client_dial(url)` helper that does the connect_async + ws_client_connect together?

rules.text: A new codelet/fspec-tui crate is added to the workspace as the FIFTH RPC-family crate (alongside rpc, rpc-types, rpc-embedded, rpc-server) and is registered as a workspace member in codelet/Cargo.toml; it has NO [[bin]] section in this card — only a [lib]

An async_trait `FspecBackend: Send + Sync` is defined in codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs with exactly five RPC methods (list_work_units, list_sessions, create_session, send_input, interrupt) and three subscription methods returning broadcast::Receiver (work_units_rx, chunks_rx, logs_rx) — the trait surface is intentionally a near-1:1 of the tarpc surface so it exists only to enable `Arc<dyn FspecBackend>` polymorphism, not to add abstraction

Two FspecBackend implementations exist: EmbeddedFspecBackend (wraps EmbeddedTransport from codelet-rpc-embedded — its constructor takes a non-defaulted `tokio::runtime::Handle` plus `Arc<SharedFspecService>` so the RPC-005 Q9 invariant of host-supplied runtime is preserved at the trait boundary) and WebSocketFspecBackend (wraps FspecWsClient from codelet-rpc-server — its constructor takes a `Url`, opens the connection via `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async`, then delegates to `ws_client_connect`)

Both FspecBackend RPC method bodies are one-line delegates to `self.client.<rpc>(context::current()).await` and both subscription methods are zero-cost passthroughs of the underlying broadcast::Receiver — no TUI-side caching, fan-out, or envelope decoding (envelope framing remains entirely encapsulated within codelet-rpc-server)
The Priority enum is defined VERBATIM as in RPC-002 doc 09 §A.1 with `#[repr(u32)]` discriminants Background=100, Low=200, Medium=500, High=800, Critical=1000 — no additional priorities, no renaming

EventResult enum has exactly two variants: `Ignored(Option<Callback>)` and `Consumed(Option<Callback>)` where Callback = `Box<dyn FnOnce(&mut Compositor) + Send>` — the optional callback enables deferred compositor mutations (so a layer can request its own removal AFTER event-handling completes, avoiding borrow conflicts with iterating `self.layers`)

The Component trait exposes `priority(&self) -> Priority` (default Medium), `is_active(&self) -> bool` (default true), `id(&self) -> &str`, `handle_event(&mut self, &Event) -> EventResult` (default Ignored(None)), `update(&mut self, Action) -> Option<Action>` (default None), and `render(&mut self, Rect, &mut Buffer)` (no default) — Send-bound, no Sync

Compositor handles event dispatch in priority order — highest priority first via `iter_mut().rev()` after stable sort by priority — and at equal priority preserves FIFO order by tracking a `registration_counter` so newer pushes win the tiebreak; iteration short-circuits on first Consumed; layers with `is_active() == false` are skipped without consuming
Compositor renders bottom-up (lowest priority first) so highest-priority layers paint LAST and end up visually on top — render order is the inverse of event-dispatch order

Compositor exposes `push(Box<dyn Component>)`, `pop() -> Option<Box<dyn Component>>`, `remove(id: &str) -> Option<Box<dyn Component>>`, `handle_event`, `update`, and `render` — and Action propagation in `update` fans out across ALL layers (top-down), unlike event dispatch

App struct holds a Compositor, an mpsc Action bus (UnboundedSender + UnboundedReceiver), an `Arc<dyn FspecBackend>`, an `Arc<Theme>` (default dark variant only — light variant is deferred to its own card), and `should_quit` / `should_render` flags; `App::new(backend: Arc<dyn FspecBackend>) -> Self` and `App::run(self) -> Result<()>`

App::run drives a `tokio::select!` over the crossterm EventStream, the action mpsc receiver, and a 16ms render-tick interval (~60fps cap); paste events forward to a stub `Compositor::handle_paste` that delegates to the active layer's handle_event (proper paste semantics arrive in Slice 06 with tui-textarea)

Terminal init enters alt-screen + raw mode via `ratatui::init()` AND additionally calls `crossterm::execute!(stdout, EnableMouseCapture, EnableBracketedPaste)`; restoration via `ratatui::restore()` AND paired `DisableMouseCapture` + `DisableBracketedPaste` happens in BOTH the App-owned terminal guard's Drop AND a `std::panic::set_hook` so a panic mid-render never leaves the terminal in raw mode

HelloComponent registers at `Priority::Background` and renders a centered static text via `Layout::vertical([Min, Length, Min])` + `Layout::horizontal([Min, Length, Min])` — the doc 06 centered-modal helper pattern — and never consumes events

HelpDialog registers at `Priority::Critical`, is triggered by the `?` key (which is intercepted at the App level — NOT inside HelloComponent — and pushes the dialog onto the compositor), and its body is a static `Paragraph` listing only `?`, ESC, and `q` keybindings — wrapped via a small `SizedWidgetRef` adapter around `tui_popup::Popup` (per RPC-002 Q5 resolved override) — the production code path is tui-popup, not a hand-rolled centered_rect

ESC pressed while the HelpDialog is on top returns `EventResult::Consumed(Some(Box::new(move |c| { c.remove(&id); })))` — the deferred-callback pattern — so the App processes the consumption first and then runs the callback to remove the dialog from the compositor

Each FspecBackend implementation has a smoke test that constructs the backend, calls `list_work_units()` and observes a `Vec<WorkUnitInfo>`, then subscribes via `work_units_rx()` and observes at least one event after the watcher is bumped — covering both the embedded path (no envelope) and the WS path (Envelope::Rpc + Envelope::WorkUnitsUpdate over bincode-of-Envelope)
