RPC-008.title: FspecBackend trait + transport selector + ratatui app shell (codelet/fspec-tui crate)

userStory.action: scaffold a new codelet/fspec-tui crate with a transport-agnostic FspecBackend trait, two backend implementations (embedded + WebSocket), and a minimal Compositor-based ratatui app shell that renders a Hello placeholder + ESC-dismissible HelpDialog
userStory.benefit: RPC-009 can immediately add the real list view + REPL on top of an already-tested foundation, RPC-010 can introduce binary entry points without re-shaping any of this, and the dual-transport seam from RPC-005/006/007 has its first concrete consumer
userStory.role: fspec developer building the ratatui frontend

architectureNotes.text: Crate layout (codelet/fspec-tui/src/): NEW directory `views/` with `mod.rs` exporting `WorkUnitsListView`, `AgentReplView`, `RootView`, `FooterView`; one file per view (`work_units_list.rs`, `agent_repl.rs`, `root.rs`, `footer.rs`); each kept well under 300 LoC. Existing `components/hello.rs` stays in place but is no longer pre-populated by `App::new` — RootView replaces it as the App's root layer (priority Background). Existing `components/help_dialog.rs` body text updates per architecture rule [13]; everything else in components/ stays untouched.

App bootstrap delta from RPC-008: `App::new(backend)` constructs RootView (containing WorkUnitsListView + AgentReplView + FooterView) and pushes it at Background priority — replacing HelloComponent. `App::run()` then performs the explicit bootstrap sequence (list_work_units → seed left pane; create_session → seed right pane's active session; spawn three subscriber tasks). The `?`/`q` App-level shortcuts and the deferred-callback ESC path from RPC-008 are unchanged. Tab is intercepted at the App level and emits Action::FocusNext (analogous to how `?` is handled). Ctrl+C and Ctrl+D are routed to AgentReplView and the App respectively when the REPL has focus.

Subscriber task pattern (matches RPC-002 doc 06 §Async-work and templates/component from doc 03 §D): `tokio::spawn({ let tx = action_tx.clone(); let mut rx = backend.work_units_rx(); async move { while let Ok(units) = rx.recv().await { let _ = tx.send(Action::WorkUnitsLoaded(units)); } } });` — analogous spawns for chunks_rx (filter by active session id) and logs_rx. The three task handles are stored on the App so a future card can abort them on shutdown; in this card they're spawned-and-forgotten (subscriber tasks are cancellation-safe because broadcast::Receiver::recv returns RecvError::Closed when senders drop).

Action enum delta in src/components/mod.rs: extend `pub enum Action` with `LoadWorkUnits`, `WorkUnitsLoaded(Vec<WorkUnitInfo>)`, `SessionCreated(SessionId)`, `ChunkReceived(SessionId, StreamChunk)`, `InputSubmitted(String)`, `Interrupt`, `FocusNext`. The existing `Quit`, `Redraw`, `Custom(String)` variants stay. Imports for `WorkUnitInfo`, `SessionId`, `StreamChunk` come from `codelet_rpc_types` (already a dependency). The enum's `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq` derives stay; for variants carrying `StreamChunk` (which has 23 variants) the Clone derive expects StreamChunk: Clone — confirmed in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs.

Dependency delta: codelet/Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] gains `tui-input = "0.10"` in the `# === Terminal & UI ===` block alongside the existing `crossterm`, `ratatui`, `tui-popup` entries. codelet/fspec-tui/Cargo.toml [dependencies] gains `tui-input.workspace = true` in the `# Terminal & UI` block. No other workspace.dependencies changes; no other dev-dependency changes. The source-shape regression test from RPC-008 (tests/source_shape_cargo.rs) is widened to assert tui-input is present in [dependencies] AND no codelet-napi/codelet-core appear in [dependencies] AND no codelet-napi appears in [dev-dependencies].

Test layout (per RPC-008 Q-FIX-1 + Q-SNAP-1 patterns): per-view #[cfg(test)] inline unit tests inside each new src/views/*.rs file (rendering smoke + focused/unfocused gating + j/k navigation + stick_to_bottom flip + Tab cycling). NEW integration tests at codelet/fspec-tui/tests/: app_with_mock_backend_repl.rs (drives the full App with MockBackend through bootstrap → first chunk → submit → snapshot the three checkpoints); embedded_app_smoke.rs (real EmbeddedFspecBackend + real WorkUnitsWatcher, observe live left-pane update); ws_app_smoke.rs (real bind_and_serve rpc-server + WebSocketFspecBackend, observe live left-pane update — same observable behaviour as embedded). Existing source_shape_*.rs tests widen their scans to cover src/views/.

RootView design: `RootView { work_units: WorkUnitsListView, repl: AgentReplView, footer: FooterView, focused_pane: FocusedPane }` where `enum FocusedPane { WorkUnits, Repl }`. RootView implements `Component` with `priority() -> Background`, `is_active() -> true`, `id() -> "root"`. Its `handle_event` first checks for Tab → emits FocusNext on the action bus and returns Consumed (no callback); otherwise forwards to whichever sub-pane is focused. Its `render` performs the horizontal+vertical Layout split and dispatches to each sub-pane's render against the sliced Rect — sub-panes are NOT separate compositor layers, they are children of RootView (only the help dialog uses the compositor's modal layering).

WorkUnitsListView design: `WorkUnitsListView { items: Vec<WorkUnitInfo>, state: ratatui::widgets::ListState, focused: bool }`. `update(Action::WorkUnitsLoaded(units))` replaces `items`, clamps the selection if needed, returns None. `handle_event` dispatches j/Down → `state.select(Some((i+1).min(items.len().saturating_sub(1))))` and k/Up → `state.select(Some(i.saturating_sub(1)))` ONLY when `focused == true`; otherwise returns Ignored. `render` builds `List::new(items.iter().map(|u| ListItem::new(format!("{} {}", u.id, u.status))))` styled by status, wraps in `Block::default().borders(Borders::ALL)` with a focused/unfocused border style, and renders via `StatefulWidget::render` with `state`.

AgentReplView design: `AgentReplView { active_session: Option<SessionId>, scrollback: Vec<RenderedChunk>, input: tui_input::Input, scroll_offset: u16, stick_to_bottom: bool, focused: bool, action_tx: UnboundedSender<Action> }` where `RenderedChunk { seq: u64, lines: Vec<Line<'static>> }`. `update(Action::SessionCreated(id))` → set active_session. `update(Action::ChunkReceived(id, chunk))` → if id matches active_session, push a RenderedChunk; if stick_to_bottom, advance scroll_offset to keep the last line in view. `handle_event` (only when focused): KeyCode::Enter with non-empty input → emit `Action::InputSubmitted(input.value().to_string())`, then `input.reset()`; KeyCode::Char('c') with KeyModifiers::CONTROL → emit Action::Interrupt; everything else → forward to `input.handle_event(event.into())` from tui-input.

App-side action handling: the App's run loop drains `action_rx` and runs `compositor.update(action.clone())` to fan top-down across all layers (RPC-008 contract). Special-case dispatch BEFORE compositor.update: `Action::InputSubmitted(text)` → spawn `backend.send_input(active_session, text)` on the host runtime; `Action::Interrupt` → spawn `backend.interrupt(active_session)` on the host runtime; `Action::FocusNext` → mutate the RootView's focused_pane field. The compositor.update path then lets each view react (e.g. WorkUnitsListView reacts to WorkUnitsLoaded, AgentReplView reacts to ChunkReceived/SessionCreated). The action.clone() on InputSubmitted/Interrupt is intentional so layers can still observe them if needed.

MockBackend (RPC-008 fixture) gains: `seed_sessions(...)`, `push_chunk(SessionId, StreamChunk)`, scripted `create_session(role)` returning a fresh SessionId and broadcasting nothing (creation is observable via the App calling it during bootstrap), scripted `send_input` that increments a per-session call counter AND optionally pushes a deterministic chunk sequence (Text("hi back"), Done) onto chunks_tx for tests that want a synthetic round-trip, scripted `interrupt` that increments a per-session interrupt counter. Existing `bail!` stubs are replaced with these implementations. New fixture helper `mock_with_two_seeded_units()` in tests/common/mod.rs returns a `MockBackend` already seeded with AUTH-001/AUTH-002 for the bootstrap snapshot test.

Snapshot strategy (locked Q-SNAP-2): each integration test using insta builds an 80x24 TestBackend, drives the App's bootstrap on a #[tokio::test] runtime, awaits at most 100ms of real time per scripted broadcast event so subscriber tasks have a chance to drain (use `tokio::task::yield_now()` + a bounded `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(100), rx.recv())` in tests, NOT `sleep`), drives `App::handle_event` for synthetic key events synchronously (no real terminal), drives one render cycle via the Q-FIX-1 `render_one_frame` fixture, snapshots the buffer's row text via `insta::assert_yaml_snapshot!`. The three checkpoint snapshots are `repl_bootstrap`, `repl_after_first_chunk`, `repl_after_submit` — file names live alongside RPC-008's existing `help_dialog_visible` / `help_dialog_dismissed` snapshots in tests/snapshots/.

RPC-009.description:
First user-visible iteration of the new ratatui frontend. Two panes: a naive work-units list (live-updates via work_units_rx) on the left, and a naive agent REPL (input box + scrollback rendered from chunks_rx) on the right. No virtualisation, no theming, no advanced widgets — just proof that real data and a real session flow through the dual-transport seam end-to-end. Both transports produce identical behaviour.

See spec/attachments/RPC-009/plan.md for the full plan.

Follows RPC-008. Unblocks RPC-010 (binary entry points).

examples.text: Initial bootstrap snapshot: developer constructs `App::new(Arc::new(MockBackend::seeded([AUTH-001 done, AUTH-002 implementing])))` against an 80x24 TestBackend, drives one render cycle, and observes a snapshot showing the left pane listing both work units with statuses styled, the right pane showing an empty scrollback + bordered input box with cursor at column 1, and a 1-row footer at the bottom rendering `?` `q` `Tab` hints

Live work-units update: with the App constructed against MockBackend, the test calls `mock.push_work_units(updated_list)` to fire the broadcast; the work_units_rx subscriber task converts it into `Action::WorkUnitsLoaded(updated_list)`; the App's run loop drains the action; the WorkUnitsListView's update receives it and replaces its in-memory list; the next render shows the updated left pane with the new entries

First chunk arrives snapshot: with the App constructed against MockBackend with a session pre-created (SessionId("s-1")), the test fires a `(SessionId("s-1"), StreamChunk::Text("Hello!"))` onto the chunks broadcast; the chunks_rx subscriber filters by session id and converts to `Action::ChunkReceived`; the AgentReplView appends the rendered chunk to its scrollback; the next render snapshot shows the assistant's text in the right pane scrollback area

User submits input snapshot: developer types "hi" in the focused agent REPL input box (Tab cycled focus there, then 'h' 'i' Char keys), presses Enter, and observes (a) the input box clears (cursor returns to column 1), (b) the scrollback gains a `user> hi` line styled per Theme, (c) `backend.send_input(active_session, "hi")` was invoked exactly once on the MockBackend (call counter assertion)

Tab cycles focus between panes: developer presses Tab on a freshly bootstrapped App; the App emits Action::FocusNext; the WorkUnitsListView's `focused` flips false and the AgentReplView's `focused` flips true; the next render shows the focused border style on the right pane and the unfocused border style on the left pane; pressing Tab again returns focus to the WorkUnitsListView

Ctrl+C interrupts (does NOT quit): developer presses Ctrl+C while the agent REPL is focused and the chunks stream is mid-flight; the App invokes `backend.interrupt(active_session)` on the MockBackend (call counter assertion); the App's `should_quit` flag remains false; pressing Ctrl+D OR `q` from the footer afterwards is what actually quits

j/k navigation in the work-units list: with the WorkUnitsListView focused and three items seeded (AUTH-001, AUTH-002, AUTH-003), pressing 'j' or Down moves the selection from index 0 → 1 → 2 (clamped at 2); pressing 'k' or Up moves it back; Enter does nothing visible (selection-only navigation per the plan)

stick_to_bottom flips false on scroll-up: developer fills the scrollback with 50 chunks (forced larger than the visible area), scrolls up by some amount (PageUp or 'k' if the REPL takes them — for this card just by directly pushing chunks beyond the viewport); the AgentReplView's stick_to_bottom flag flips false; new chunks arriving still append to the buffer but the viewport stays where it is; scrolling back to the bottom flips stick_to_bottom back to true

Cross-transport parity at the App layer: the test runs the same scripted sequence (mutate work-units.json on disk, observe the left pane update) against an App built on EmbeddedFspecBackend and another App built on WebSocketFspecBackend (real bind_and_serve rpc-server on 127.0.0.1:0); both Apps' rendered left-pane buffers (post-mutation, post-render) are byte-identical (or at minimum semantically identical — same set of work-unit ids/statuses)

Subscriber tasks honour Lagged: a chunks broadcast subscriber receives `RecvError::Lagged(n)` when slow renders cause the broadcast channel to drop messages; the subscriber logs at debug level (per RPC-006 pattern) and resyncs by calling `backend.list_work_units()` for work_units (and continues the loop for chunks/logs since chunks are deltas without a snapshot fallback) — the App does NOT crash on Lagged

HelpDialog body update: with the App bootstrapped and `?` pressed, the rendered popup body lists EXACTLY one line per key for `j`, `k`, `Tab`, `?`, `q`, `Enter`, `Ctrl+C` — verified via insta snapshot of the post-`?` frame; ESC dismisses the dialog (RPC-008 deferred-callback path) and the next render snapshot returns to the bootstrap frame

Source-shape regression after the new files: tests/source_shape_trait.rs scans codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/{work_units_list,agent_repl,root,footer}.rs and asserts: (a) NO `tokio::runtime::Builder` / `Runtime::new` / `Runtime::new()` calls in any new file (Q9 invariant preserved); (b) NO direct import of `codelet_napi`, `codelet_core`, `tarpc`, or `tokio_tungstenite` in the new view files (everything goes through the FspecBackend trait)

rules.text: Both new views (work_units_list and agent_repl) take `Arc<dyn FspecBackend>` in their constructor — they MUST NOT call into NAPI, codelet-core, tarpc, or tokio_tungstenite directly; every interaction goes through the FspecBackend trait introduced in RPC-008

tui-input = "0.10" is the ONLY new production dependency added to codelet/fspec-tui — no tui-textarea (Slice 06), no tui-widget-list (Slices 03/04), no tui-tree-widget, no throbber-widgets-tui, no reedline; tui-input must be added to codelet/Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] and consumed by codelet/fspec-tui/Cargo.toml as a workspace dependency

Production [dependencies] of codelet/fspec-tui MUST continue to NOT include codelet-napi or codelet-core; the source-shape regression test from RPC-008 (tests/source_shape_cargo.rs) is widened to assert the dependency table now lists tui-input alongside the existing entries and still excludes codelet-napi/codelet-core in [dependencies]

The Action enum in codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs is extended with EXACTLY these new variants (all in addition to the existing Quit/Redraw/Custom): LoadWorkUnits, WorkUnitsLoaded(Vec<WorkUnitInfo>), SessionCreated(SessionId), ChunkReceived(SessionId, StreamChunk), InputSubmitted(String), Interrupt, FocusNext — no others in this card

WorkUnitsListView is rendered via ratatui core `List` + `ListState` + `Block::default().borders(Borders::ALL)` — NOT virtualised, NOT a `tui-widget-list`; selection is single-item via `ListState::select(Some(idx))`; each item is `ListItem::new(format!("{} {}", id, status))` styled by status from the existing Theme; the view reads `backend.work_units_rx()` for live updates and seeds via `backend.list_work_units()` in App bootstrap

AgentReplView holds two sub-areas: (a) a scrollback rendered as `Paragraph::new(Text::from_iter(...)).scroll((y_offset, 0)).wrap(Wrap { trim: false })` against an alt-screen Rect — NOT a virtualised list, NOT a custom BubbleList, NOT a HistoryCell trait; (b) a single-line input rendered as `Paragraph::new(input.value()).block(Block::default().borders(Borders::ALL))` with cursor positioned via `frame.set_cursor_position` based on `input.visual_cursor()` from the `tui_input::Input` field

AgentReplView has a `stick_to_bottom: bool` field (tenere pattern — plain bool, not AtomicBool; mutated only on the App task) initialised to true; flipped to false when the user scrolls up; flipped back to true when the scroll position reaches the end

AgentReplView caches scrollback as a `Vec<RenderedChunk>` keyed by chunk seq, where `RenderedChunk` is a pre-rendered `Vec<Line<'static>>` produced when `Action::ChunkReceived` arrives — early oatmeal-style nod, no caching machinery, just owned Lines so the per-frame render loop doesn't re-format

AgentReplView's chunks_rx subscriber filters by the active session id — chunks for OTHER sessions are silently dropped; only `(session_id, chunk)` tuples whose session_id equals the view's active session are converted into `Action::ChunkReceived`

AgentReplView Enter on the input pane calls `backend.send_input(active_session, input.value().to_string())` and clears the input via `input.reset()`; Ctrl+C on the input pane sends `Action::Interrupt` (which dispatches `backend.interrupt(active_session)`) — Ctrl+C is NOT a quit; quit is App-level Ctrl+D OR `q` (footer hint bar)

RootView is the new top-level Component implementing the two-pane horizontal layout via `Layout::horizontal([Constraint::Length(32), Constraint::Min(0)])`; the right pane is split vertically via `Layout::vertical([Constraint::Min(0), Constraint::Length(3)])` into scrollback + 3-row input box; the very bottom of the root layout reserves `Constraint::Length(1)` for the footer hint bar

Tab cycles a `focused: bool` field across the two pane structs (work-units list ↔ agent REPL); the unfocused pane returns `EventResult::Ignored(None)` from `handle_event` while still returning true from `is_active` — useInputCompat-style per-event gating preserves the doc 09 §A.6 + doc 02 §1.4 contract that inactive panes don't consume; the App reads each pane's `focused` field to render the focused border style on the matching pane

Footer hint bar is a 1-row Component rendering keybinding hints `?`-help, `q`-quit, `Tab`-switch-pane via styled `Spans` against the existing Theme — NO `tui-prompts`, NO `throbber-widgets-tui` (those are deferred to later slices)

On `App::run()` bootstrap performs EXACTLY this sequence in order: (1) `backend.list_work_units()` → seeds the left pane (also primes `stick_to_bottom = true` and selects index 0); (2) `backend.create_session(None)` → seeds the right pane's active session; (3) spawn THREE subscriber tasks reading `backend.work_units_rx()`, `backend.chunks_rx()`, and `backend.logs_rx()` and converting each message into an `Action::*` on the existing `mpsc::UnboundedSender<Action>` action bus — each spawn is `tokio::spawn` on the host runtime; subscriber tasks NEVER touch component state directly

The HelpDialog body text changes from the RPC-008 placeholder to one-line-per-key listing exactly: `j`/`k` (navigate), `Tab` (switch pane), `?` (toggle this help), `q` (quit), `Enter` (send), `Ctrl+C` (interrupt) — same `Priority::Critical` Component, same tui-popup adapter, NO new dialog widget code

Crate layout adds EXACTLY these new files: src/views/mod.rs, src/views/work_units_list.rs, src/views/agent_repl.rs, src/views/root.rs, src/views/footer.rs — each kept well under 300 LoC; the existing components/hello.rs is no longer pre-populated by `App::new` (replaced by RootView in the App bootstrap), but the source file remains untouched for now (deletion is RPC-010's concern)
Layout stays inside the alt-screen canvas (Q1 alt-screen) — the REPL is rendered INSIDE the alt-screen Rect, NOT into native scrollback like Codex (per doc 04 §1 'Codex is not the model to copy')

Q9 host-supplied tokio runtime invariant is preserved: the three new subscriber tasks (work_units_rx, chunks_rx, logs_rx) are spawned via `tokio::spawn` on the host's runtime — NOT via `tokio::runtime::Builder` or `Runtime::new()`; the source-shape regression test from RPC-008 (tests/source_shape_trait.rs) continues to pass after the new files are added

Three insta snapshot checkpoints pin the screen rendering against an 80x24 TestBackend driven by MockBackend: (a) initial frame after bootstrap (left pane shows seeded work units, right pane shows the empty REPL with cursor in input box, footer shows hint bar); (b) frame after first ChunkReceived arrives (scrollback shows assistant text); (c) frame after the user types text and presses Enter (input box cleared, scrollback shows the user message)

Embedded smoke test: a Rust integration test constructs the EmbeddedFspecBackend wrapping a real tempdir-backed WorkUnitsWatcher hosting a real SharedFspecService, builds an App against it, drives one render cycle, mutates the spec/work-units.json file, drives another render cycle, and asserts the rendered left pane reflects the new work-units state — SAME observable behaviour as the WS smoke test

WS smoke test: a Rust integration test spawns a real `bind_and_serve` rpc-server bound to 127.0.0.1:0 against a tempdir-backed WorkUnitsWatcher, builds a WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(ws_url), wraps it in App, and asserts the same observable left-pane behaviour as the embedded smoke test (cross-transport parity at the App layer — not just at the FspecBackend trait surface)

Out-of-scope deferrals (must NOT be implemented in this card; each is its own future card): tui-textarea-based MultiLineInput (RPC-002 Slice 06), VirtualList (Slices 03–04), BoardView (Slice 07), theming beyond the existing dark variant, status bar, role banner, multi-session tabs, slash commands, file mentions, attachments, mouse beyond crossterm defaults, group selection / scroll-vs-item / scrollToEnd / mouse-wheel velocity, native text-selection toggle / MouseTrackingToggle, get_session_status RPC on the FspecBackend trait surface (still intentionally absent — added in a future card if needed)

Existing tests must remain green: cargo test -p codelet-rpc-embedded -p codelet-rpc-server -p codelet-fspec-tui passes at end of card; the Vitest smoke at src/__tests__/napi-workunitinfo-shape.test.ts is untouched; the existing reserved-variant + source-shape regression tests pass unchanged

MockBackend (in tests/common/mod.rs from RPC-008) gains a scripted send_input + create_session implementation (replacing the current `bail!`s) AND a chunks broadcast publisher so App-level integration tests can drive scripted (Action::ChunkReceived) sequences deterministically — pattern mirrors `codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs::SharedFspecService` (atomic counters, scripted responses) so snapshot tests are byte-equal across runs

RPC-009.title: Basic frontend: work-units list pane + agent REPL pane (FIRST visible UI)

userStory.action: see a basic two-pane TUI — work-units list (live updates) on the left + agent REPL (single-line input + streaming scrollback) on the right — with both panes wired through `Arc<dyn FspecBackend>` and producing identical observable behaviour on both transports
userStory.benefit: the dual-transport seam from RPC-005..008 is proven end-to-end with the FIRST visible UI before binary entry points (RPC-010) and richer widgets (RPC-002 Slices 03+) layer on top
userStory.role: fspec developer building the ratatui frontend

architectureNotes.text: Architecture conformance with RPC-002: combined mode and client mode both call `ratatui::init()` (alt-screen + raw mode per Q1); daemon mode does NOT. RPC-002 doc 11 §Q9 (host-supplied tokio runtime Handle) is preserved at the binary boundary by `#[tokio::main]` driving the runtime and `tokio::runtime::Handle::current()` being the ONLY source for `EmbeddedFspecBackend::new`.

Three separate code paths in `codelet/fspec/src/`: (1) `combined.rs::run(args) -> Result<()>` builds service, calls `bind_and_serve`, prints `PORT=<n>` to stderr, writes daemon.json, builds EmbeddedFspecBackend, runs App, on exit removes daemon.json; (2) `daemon.rs::run(args) -> Result<()>` builds service, calls `bind_and_serve`, prints port to stdout (RPC-005 contract), optionally writes pidfile, ALSO writes daemon.json, blocks on `tokio::select!(ctrl_c, sigterm)`, removes pidfile + daemon.json on shutdown; (3) `client.rs::run(args) -> Result<()>` resolves connect URL (explicit `--connect` OR daemon.json autodiscovery), constructs `WebSocketFspecBackend::connect`, runs App, on disconnect surfaces critical-priority dialog.

`common.rs` exports: `build_service(workspace: &Path) -> Result<Arc<SharedFspecService>>` (constructs WorkUnitsWatcher + SharedFspecService — single instance per process), `init_tracing_combined()` (file appender + LogEvent broadcast layer; NO stderr fmt subscriber), `init_tracing_daemon()` (RPC-005 stderr fmt subscriber + LogEvent broadcast layer), `init_tracing_client()` (~/.fspec/client.log appender + passthrough to LogEvent broadcast it OWNS), `install_panic_hook()` (idempotent ratatui::restore + DisableMouseCapture/BracketedPaste; uses `Once` per RPC-008 pattern), `resolve_workspace(opt: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<PathBuf>` (defaults to CWD), `daemon_json_path() -> PathBuf` (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR else ~/.fspec), `write_daemon_json(path, port, pid, workspace)` (atomic temp+rename), `remove_daemon_json(path)` (idempotent).

Cargo dependencies for `codelet/fspec/Cargo.toml [dependencies]`: `clap.workspace = true`, `tokio.workspace = true` (full features for `#[tokio::main]` + signal), `anyhow.workspace = true`, `tracing.workspace = true`, `tracing-subscriber.workspace = true`, `tracing-appender.workspace = true`, `dirs.workspace = true` (for ~/.fspec resolution), `serde.workspace = true` + `serde_json.workspace = true` (daemon.json), `url.workspace = true`, `codelet-rpc.workspace = true`, `codelet-rpc-types.workspace = true`, `codelet-rpc-embedded.workspace = true`, `codelet-rpc-server.workspace = true`, `codelet-fspec-tui.workspace = true`, `codelet-core.workspace = true` (for WorkUnitsWatcher). NOT included: `codelet-napi` (forbidden — both [dependencies] and [dev-dependencies]). [dev-dependencies]: `tempfile.workspace = true`, `tokio-tungstenite.workspace = true` (for the test-side WS client in subprocess smokes), `assert_cmd.workspace = true` (for spawning the binary).

Test layout under `codelet/fspec/tests/`: `combined_smoke.rs` (spawn fspec, parse stderr PORT, attach 2nd WS client, assert list_work_units), `daemon_smoke.rs` (spawn fspec daemon, parse stdout port, attach WS client, assert list_work_units + reuse the existing RPC-005 pattern), `client_autodiscovery_smoke.rs` (spawn daemon → daemon.json → spawn bare client; HOME pinned to a tempdir), `client_explicit_connect_smoke.rs` (spawn daemon, capture port, spawn `fspec client --connect ws://127.0.0.1:<port>`), `daemon_signals.rs` (SIGTERM extension test), `daemon_pidfile.rs` (--pidfile contents + cleanup), `daemon_json_lifecycle.rs` (combined writes + removes daemon.json on shutdown), `source_shape.rs` (scans codelet/fspec/src/ for forbidden runtime calls + parses Cargo.toml dependency tables for codelet-napi absence). Each test declares `#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]` matching the RPC-005/006/007/008 pattern.

Existing artifacts this card builds on (NO duplication): `codelet_rpc_server::bind_and_serve(addr, service) -> (SocketAddr, ServerStats, JoinHandle)` from RPC-005 is called by BOTH combined.rs AND daemon.rs (single source of truth); `codelet_rpc::SharedFspecService::new(watcher)` from RPC-006 constructed exactly once via `common::build_service`; `codelet_rpc_embedded::EmbeddedFspecBackend::new(handle, service)` from RPC-008 used only by combined.rs; `codelet_fspec_tui::WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(url)` from RPC-008 used only by client.rs; `codelet_fspec_tui::App::new(backend).run()` from RPC-008/009 used by combined.rs AND client.rs; `codelet_core::work_units::WorkUnitsWatcher` from RPC-006 constructed inside common::build_service; `register_log_layer` from RPC-007 (codelet-rpc) registers the LogEvent tracing layer in init_tracing_*.

Out of scope (each is its own future card): auth / TLS / non-loopback binds, multi-tenancy, observer-mode read-only clients, daemon install-as-service helpers (systemd/launchd unit files), replacing the TS `fspec` on the npm `bin` install path (needs platform-specific binary distribution), daemon-per-user vs daemon-per-project routing, daemon.json staleness check / PID-liveness validation (RPC-011), full reconnect retry/backoff (RPC-011), `fspec status` subcommand + health RPC (RPC-011), broadcast channel sizing (RPC-011).

`init_tracing_daemon` ORDER GOTCHA (codelet-rpc::register_log_layer semantics): `register_log_layer(service)` does two things — (a) pushes `service.logs_tx()` onto the codelet-rpc process-global Vec<broadcast::Sender<LogRecord>> (unconditional), and (b) calls `tracing_subscriber::registry().with(BroadcastLogLayer).try_init()` (no-op if a global subscriber already exists). To get BOTH a stderr fmt subscriber AND the LogEvent broadcast in daemon mode, `init_tracing_daemon` MUST build the registry itself FIRST as `registry().with(BroadcastLogLayer).with(fmt::layer().with_writer(std::io::stderr).with_filter(env_filter)).init()`, THEN call `register_log_layer(service)` AFTER — at which point only the sender-push side-effect lands (the try_init is a no-op). `BroadcastLogLayer` is already `pub` in codelet-rpc — no codelet-rpc refactor required. Same pattern applies in reverse to `init_tracing_combined` (registry uses `tracing_appender::rolling` file appender layer + `BroadcastLogLayer`, NO stderr fmt layer) and `init_tracing_client` (registry uses a `~/.fspec/client.log` rolling appender only — no BroadcastLogLayer, client process has no SharedFspecService to push into).

App ownership pattern (RPC-009 inherited): combined.rs and client.rs both follow the THREE-CALL sequence `let mut app = App::new(Arc::new(backend)); app.bootstrap().await?; app.run().await?;`. App::new() constructs the App with an empty Compositor + RootView and a fresh action bus; App::bootstrap() performs `list_work_units` + `create_session(None)` + `spawn_subscriber_tasks` (the RPC-009 three-step bootstrap that seeds the left pane, opens an active REPL session, and spawns the work_units/chunks/logs subscriber tasks); App::run() initializes the TerminalGuard (alt-screen + raw mode) and enters the render loop. NEITHER combined.rs NOR client.rs calls `ratatui::init()` directly — App::run() owns the TerminalGuard. Daemon mode does NOT construct an App at all and therefore performs none of these three calls.

RPC-010.description:
New codelet/fspec/ binary crate that produces codelet/target/release/fspec — the long-term replacement for the TS fspec CLI. Three modes via clap subcommands:

  fspec           — combined: shared service + always-on WS server + ratatui frontend (embedded backend)
  fspec daemon    — headless: shared service + WS server only (suitable for systemd/launchd)
  fspec client    — frontend only: WebSocketFspecBackend connecting to a running daemon

WebSocket server is ALWAYS on in combined and daemon modes (per user requirement). daemon.json autodiscovery so plain `fspec client` works against a sibling daemon. Loopback-only bind (RPC-005 invariant preserved).

See spec/attachments/RPC-010/plan.md for the full plan.

Follows RPC-009.

examples.text: Combined-mode subprocess smoke: developer spawns `fspec --workspace <tempdir>` as a subprocess (with stdin/stdout/stderr piped), parses the `PORT=<n>` line from STDERR (NOT stdout — stdout is the alt-screen TUI canvas), constructs a SECOND `WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(ws://127.0.0.1:<n>)` client in the test process, calls `list_work_units().await`, observes a non-empty `Vec<WorkUnitInfo>` matching the tempdir's seeded `spec/work-units.json`; on test teardown the ChildGuard kills the child and the daemon.json file is gone

Daemon-mode subprocess smoke: developer spawns `fspec daemon --workspace <tempdir>` as a subprocess, reads exactly one line from STDOUT (a bare integer port — RPC-005 contract verbatim, so the existing `spawn_rpc_server` test harness pattern works unmodified), connects a `WebSocketFspecBackend` to it, calls `list_work_units().await`, observes the same non-empty `Vec<WorkUnitInfo>` as the combined-mode test

Client-mode autodiscovery smoke: developer spawns `fspec daemon --workspace <tempdir>` (which writes `<XDG_RUNTIME_DIR | ~/.fspec>/daemon.json` containing `{port, pid, workspace, version}`), THEN spawns plain `fspec client` (no `--connect` flag) with HOME pointed at the same tempdir; the client reads daemon.json, opens the WS connection, the test drives a few synthetic keypresses through the client's stdin via `tui-test`-style harness, asserts the work-units list pane renders the seeded units

Client-mode explicit connect: developer spawns `fspec daemon` (capturing port from stdout = 12345), THEN spawns `fspec client --connect ws://127.0.0.1:12345` (NO daemon.json read needed); the client opens the WS connection successfully and renders the same work-units list — proving `--connect` overrides autodiscovery

Combined mode does NOT corrupt the alt-screen TUI canvas: developer spawns `fspec` and pipes stdout to a buffer; after bootstrap completes, the buffer captured from stdout contains ONLY ratatui control codes / cell drawing — it does NOT contain the literal text `PORT=` anywhere (proving the port banner went to stderr instead)

Combined-mode shutdown removes daemon.json: developer spawns `fspec`, asserts the daemon.json file appears at the resolved path, sends SIGINT (ctrl_c equivalent) to the child, waits for graceful exit, then asserts the daemon.json file is GONE (clean teardown)

Daemon mode handles SIGTERM (extension over RPC-005's ctrl_c-only): developer spawns `fspec daemon`, sends SIGTERM (NOT SIGINT), the daemon shuts down cleanly within 5s, removes its pidfile (if `--pidfile` was passed) and daemon.json, then exits with code 0

Daemon `--pidfile` writes pid + port: developer spawns `fspec daemon --pidfile /tmp/fspec.pid`, the file content is parseable as `pid=<u32>\nport=<u16>` (or equivalent simple key=value), and after SIGTERM the file is removed

Client mode disconnect dialog: developer spawns `fspec daemon`, then `fspec client --connect ws://...`, drives the client until it has rendered the work-units list, then KILLS the daemon process; the WebSocketFspecBackend's underlying connection drops; the App surfaces a `Priority::Critical` dialog whose body contains the strings `daemon disconnected`, `q to quit`, and `r to reconnect`; pressing `q` exits the App; pressing `r` triggers a SINGLE reconnect attempt (best-effort — no backoff loop in this card)

Workspace detection: developer runs `fspec` (combined) from inside `/path/to/project` (containing `spec/work-units.json`) with NO `--workspace` flag; the WorkUnitsWatcher is constructed rooted at `/path/to/project` (CWD); running `fspec --workspace /other/path` overrides this and the watcher is rooted at `/other/path` instead — both modes (combined AND daemon) honour the same `--workspace` resolution

Source-shape regression: an integration test scans `codelet/fspec/src/` (newly added) and asserts (a) NO file contains `tokio::runtime::Builder`, `runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread`, `runtime::Builder::new_current_thread`, `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new`, or `Runtime::new()` — preserving RPC-005 Q9; (b) `codelet/fspec/Cargo.toml`'s `[dependencies]` table does NOT list `codelet-napi`; (c) `[dev-dependencies]` ALSO does not list `codelet-napi`

Build artifact at the right path: developer runs `cargo build -p fspec --release` and observes `codelet/target/release/fspec` exists, is executable, and `--version` prints the workspace version; running `npm run build:rust:fspec` (or `make build:rust:fspec`) ALSO copies the artifact to `dist/fspec` for parity with the TS layout

Existing test harnesses keep working: the existing `codelet/rpc-server/tests/websocket_transport.rs::spawn_rpc_server` helper that spawns the OLD `codelet-rpc-server` binary continues to pass unchanged (the dev-helper binary stays); a NEW sibling helper `spawn_fspec_daemon` reuses the same `BufReader::read_line` pattern against `fspec daemon` and ALSO succeeds — proving the port-line stdout contract is verbatim across both binaries

Vitest + Rust test suites green: developer runs `npm test` and the existing Vitest smoke at `src/__tests__/napi-workunitinfo-shape.test.ts` passes unchanged; developer runs `cargo test --workspace` from `codelet/` and every existing test in `codelet/rpc-embedded`, `codelet/rpc-server`, `codelet/fspec-tui` plus the new `codelet/fspec` tests passes

Loopback bind invariant preserved (REJECT non-loopback): developer spawns `fspec daemon` with no `--bind` flag, observes the listening socket address printed to stdout is `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>` (NEVER `0.0.0.0`, NEVER an external interface). When the same developer spawns `fspec daemon --bind 0.0.0.0:8080`, the binary EXITS with a non-zero code BEFORE binding any socket, and its stderr contains the string `error: --bind must be a loopback address` plus a reference to `auth/TLS for external binds is out of scope`. `fspec daemon --bind 127.0.0.1:8080` and `fspec daemon --bind ::1:8080` both succeed.

Reconnect = full bootstrap (no stale session): test spawns `fspec daemon` (port 30000), spawns `fspec client --connect ws://127.0.0.1:30000`, waits for client bootstrap to register on daemon's ServerStats (list_work_units_calls = 1, sessions_created = 1), records the session id; then KILLS the daemon and RESTARTS a fresh daemon at the SAME port; the client surfaces the disconnect dialog; user presses `r`; the client opens a NEW WebSocketFspecBackend, calls list_work_units (daemon ServerStats list_work_units_calls jumps to 1 on the new instance), calls create_session (new session id, distinct from pre-disconnect id), and respawns the three subscriber tasks — verified by App accessor `subscriber_task_count() == 3` post-reconnect

Combined-mode WS server teardown order: developer spawns `fspec`, attaches an external WS client that subscribes to work_units_rx, then sends SIGINT to the fspec child; the order of observable side-effects is (1) App::run returns, (2) the WS server's JoinHandle is aborted (external client observes a connection-closed error rather than a hang), (3) daemon.json is removed, (4) the child process exits with code 0; daemon.json never lingers past the child's exit

Client-mode daemon-side observability assertion (no pty): test spawns `fspec daemon`, captures port from stdout AND retains an external WS client subscribed to ServerStats observability (the daemon's list_work_units_calls counter); spawns `fspec client --connect ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` as a subprocess WITHOUT a pty harness, just attached pipes; within 5s the external observer sees list_work_units_calls increment by exactly 1 (from the client's bootstrap RPC) — proving the client connected and performed bootstrap WITHOUT requiring terminal-buffer cell parsing

questions.answer: Reconnect on `r` keypress = FULL BOOTSTRAP: drop the old WebSocketFspecBackend, abort the three subscriber tasks, construct a fresh `WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(url)` (using the same URL the client originally resolved), call the same bootstrap sequence as RPC-009 (`backend.list_work_units()` → `backend.create_session(None)` → spawn three new subscriber tasks) — the old session_id is discarded; any pre-disconnect conversation is lost; full retry/backoff and session-preservation are still RPC-011's concern; this single-attempt bootstrap is what unblocks the user from a transient daemon restart without leaving them with a session-not-found error from the daemon
questions.text: @human: When `fspec daemon --bind 0.0.0.0:0` is passed (a non-loopback address), should the binary (a) REJECT at clap-arg validation with a non-zero exit code and an error message, OR (b) CLAMP the host portion to `127.0.0.1` and emit a warning, OR (c) ACCEPT it but only in this card (since auth is out of scope, this is risky)? The plan says non-loopback binds are 'future-card territory' but doesn't specify the rejection mechanism for the half-step where `--bind` exists in this card.

rules.text: A NEW binary crate codelet/fspec/ exists as a workspace member with [[bin]] name = "fspec", path = "src/main.rs"; cargo build -p fspec --release produces codelet/target/release/fspec

The clap CLI surface is exactly: `fspec [--workspace <path>]` (combined mode, default), `fspec daemon [--bind <addr>] [--workspace <path>] [--pidfile <path>]`, `fspec client [--connect <url>] [--workspace <path>]`, plus `fspec --version` / `fspec --help`

Combined mode (`fspec`) starts the SAME `bind_and_serve` WebSocket server that daemon mode starts — there is NO second WS server, NO separate "embedded server" code path; the WS server is ALWAYS on in combined mode (per user requirement)

Combined mode and daemon mode both call `common::build_service(workspace)` exactly once per process invocation, producing one `Arc<SharedFspecService>` that is shared between `bind_and_serve` and (in combined mode) `EmbeddedFspecBackend::new` — single-instance invariant from RPC-005 preserved at the binary boundary

Combined mode emits the `PORT=<n>` line on STDERR (not stdout — stdout is reserved for the alt-screen TUI canvas), and ALSO writes a `daemon.json` autodiscovery file; client mode emits NOTHING on either stream; daemon mode keeps the existing RPC-005 stdout port-line contract verbatim (`<n>\n` flushed) so existing `ChildGuard` + `BufReader::read_line` test harnesses work unmodified

Combined and client modes both call `ratatui::init()` (alt-screen + raw mode) AND install a `std::panic::set_hook` that runs `ratatui::restore()` + `crossterm::execute!(stdout, DisableMouseCapture, DisableBracketedPaste)` BEFORE the panic propagates; daemon mode does NEITHER (no TUI to restore)

Combined mode's `init_tracing` routes tracing events to a `tracing_appender::rolling` file under `~/.fspec/logs/` AND to the `LogEvent` broadcast inside `SharedFspecService` (RPC-007); it does NOT register a stderr/fmt subscriber (stderr is reserved for the single PORT line and panic backtraces). Daemon mode keeps a stderr fmt subscriber (no TUI to corrupt). Client mode writes logs to `~/.fspec/client.log`.

Combined mode constructs `EmbeddedFspecBackend::new(tokio::runtime::Handle::current(), service.clone())` — using ONLY the `#[tokio::main]` runtime; `codelet/fspec/src/` contains NO `tokio::runtime::Builder` and NO `Runtime::new` calls; the existing RPC-005 source-shape regression at `codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/architecture_invariants.rs` is widened to scan `codelet/fspec/src/` for these forbidden patterns

`--bind` for `fspec daemon` defaults to `127.0.0.1:0` (loopback only — RPC-005 invariant 13 preserved); a configurable bind address is allowed as a clap arg in this card (escapes the RPC-005 hardcode), but auth, TLS, and non-loopback binds are explicitly out of scope

`fspec daemon` blocks on BOTH `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` AND SIGTERM (extending RPC-005's ctrl_c-only handling); on shutdown it removes its pidfile and (if it wrote one) its daemon.json. Combined mode tears down the WS server cleanly on TUI exit and removes daemon.json

`fspec client --connect <url>` is optional; without it, the client resolves the daemon URL by reading `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fspec/daemon.json` (if set) else `~/.fspec/daemon.json` — so plain `fspec client` works against a sibling running daemon

Client mode wraps `WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(url).await` and passes the result to `App::new(Arc::new(ws_backend)).run().await` — the SAME `App` used by combined mode; daemon mode does NOT construct an App at all (it only blocks on signals)

On WS disconnect mid-session in client mode, the App surfaces a `Priority::Critical` dialog reading roughly `daemon disconnected — q to quit, r to reconnect`; reconnect logic is best-effort in this card (a single retry on `r`); full retry/backoff is RPC-011's concern

`codelet/fspec/Cargo.toml` does NOT depend on `codelet-napi` (the production binary path stays NAPI-free, preserving the RPC-006 `rpc → napi forbidden` arrow at the binary level); the source-shape regression test asserts this in [dependencies] AND in [dev-dependencies]

The existing `codelet-rpc-server` binary at `codelet/rpc-server/src/main.rs` is REPLACED for production purposes by `fspec daemon`, but it is allowed to REMAIN as a development helper (its stdout port-line contract is preserved verbatim by `fspec daemon`); the npm `bin` entry stays on the TS shim — replacing the npm install path is a separate distribution-strategy card

An npm script (or top-level Makefile target) named `build:rust:fspec` runs `cargo build -p fspec --release` and copies `codelet/target/release/fspec` to `dist/fspec` for parity with the existing TS dist layout; this does NOT swap the TS `fspec` on the npm `bin` install path

Crate file layout is exactly: `codelet/fspec/Cargo.toml` (with `[[bin]] name = "fspec"` and `path = "src/main.rs"`), `codelet/fspec/src/main.rs` (clap dispatcher), `combined.rs`, `daemon.rs`, `client.rs`, `common.rs` (shared startup: tracing, panic hook, workspace detection, `build_service`); each file kept well under 300 LoC

`daemon.json` content is a small JSON object with at minimum `{ "port": <u16>, "pid": <u32>, "workspace": "<absolute-path>", "version": "<crate-version>" }`; it is written atomically (write-to-temp-then-rename) and removed on clean shutdown; daemon-staleness/PID-liveness validation is OUT OF SCOPE (RPC-011)

Both `fspec` (combined) AND `fspec daemon` write `daemon.json` (so a sibling `fspec client` works against either); the file location is the SAME for both modes (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fspec/daemon.json` if set, else `~/.fspec/daemon.json`); a future card per-workspace routing is explicitly out of scope

Three subprocess-spawn integration smoke tests live under `codelet/fspec/tests/`: combined-mode smoke (parse stderr PORT line, attach a second WS client, assert list_work_units returns non-empty), daemon-mode smoke (parse stdout port, attach WS client, assert same), client-mode autodiscovery smoke (`fspec daemon` → daemon.json → bare `fspec client` connects); each test cleans up its child processes via a ChildGuard

All existing tests must remain green: `cargo test -p codelet-rpc-embedded -p codelet-rpc-server -p codelet-fspec-tui -p fspec` passes; the Vitest smoke at `src/__tests__/napi-workunitinfo-shape.test.ts` is untouched; the existing reserved-variant + source-shape regression tests pass unchanged

REJECT at clap-arg validation: if `--bind` is passed with a non-loopback host (anything other than 127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost), the binary exits with a non-zero code and prints `error: --bind must be a loopback address (127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost); auth/TLS for external binds is out of scope (future card)` — preserves RPC-005 invariant 13 explicitly

Client-mode subprocess smoke test uses DAEMON-SIDE OBSERVABILITY ONLY (option c): the test spawns `fspec daemon`, captures port from stdout, retains a handle to the daemon's `ServerStats` via a sibling test-only API OR via an external WS client that observes the daemon's list_work_units count, then spawns `fspec client --connect ws://...`, waits for the client to perform its bootstrap (list_work_units RPC), and asserts the daemon-side ServerStats.service.list_work_units_calls counter incremented by 1 — NO terminal-buffer cell parsing, NO portable-pty harness, NO Vitest involvement

On clean exit of `fspec` (combined mode): ABORT the `JoinHandle` returned by `bind_and_serve` BEFORE removing daemon.json — combined.rs stores the JoinHandle, the run sequence is `App::run().await` → `join_handle.abort()` → `remove_daemon_json(path)` → return Ok(()) → `#[tokio::main]` returns → runtime drops; the RPC-005 `bind_and_serve` signature is preserved unchanged (no shutdown channel plumbing); any in-flight external client RPCs get a connection-closed error which is acceptable behaviour for a TUI-driven exit

ONLY `fspec daemon` accepts `--pidfile`. Combined mode (`fspec`) does NOT expose `--pidfile` — pidfile semantics are tied to supervised-process lifecycles (systemd / launchd) which are only relevant for daemon mode. Combined mode writes only `daemon.json` (which carries the pid field anyway for autodiscovery). This keeps the clap CLI surface minimal and matches the plan

Reconnect on `r` keypress = FULL BOOTSTRAP: drop the old WebSocketFspecBackend, abort the three subscriber tasks, construct a fresh `WebSocketFspecBackend::connect(url)` (using the same URL the client originally resolved), call the same bootstrap sequence as RPC-009 (`backend.list_work_units()` → `backend.create_session(None)` → spawn three new subscriber tasks) — the old session_id is discarded; any pre-disconnect conversation is lost; full retry/backoff and session-preservation are still RPC-011's concern; this single-attempt bootstrap is what unblocks the user from a transient daemon restart without leaving them with a session-not-found error from the daemon

RPC-010.title: fspec binary: combined frontend+server, plus fspec daemon and fspec client subcommands

userStory.action: run a single `fspec` binary in three modes — combined (default TUI + always-on WS), `fspec daemon` (headless server), and `fspec client` (frontend-only WS attach)
userStory.benefit: I have ONE production entry point at codelet/target/release/fspec that progressively replaces the TS fspec CLI, with the WS server always-on so external clients (chrome extension, bridge, sibling fspec client) can attach

architectureNotes.text: Reconnect supervisor lives at the transport layer (codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/websocket.rs). It owns an Arc<RwLock<Option<FspecWsClient>>> and an UnboundedSender<Action>. A background tokio task wraps tokio_tungstenite::connect_async in a loop with exponential backoff; on success it stores the new FspecWsClient and emits Action::Reconnected; on failure (or initial connect) it emits Action::Reconnecting(attempt) before the next sleep.

Compositor + Action enum extension (codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs): add Action::Disconnected, Action::Reconnecting(u32), Action::Reconnected. Add components/disconnect_dialog.rs implementing Component with priority()=Critical. App.dispatch() pushes DisconnectDialog on Action::Disconnected, mutates dialog state on Action::Reconnecting(n), pops on Action::Reconnected. Same tui-popup widget RPC-008's HelpDialog uses — NO new dialog framework.

ServerStats extensions (codelet/rpc-server/src/lib.rs): add `connected_clients: Arc<AtomicU64>`, `last_watcher_event_at: Arc<Mutex<Option<Instant>>>`, `lag_chunks: Arc<AtomicU64>`, `lag_logs: Arc<AtomicU64>`, `lag_work_units: Arc<AtomicU64>`, `started_at: Instant`, `shutdown_signal: Arc<tokio::sync::Notify>`. ConnectedClientGuard RAII wraps connected_clients. Lag counters incremented in the three fanout tasks when RecvError::Lagged fires. last_watcher_event_at updated in work_units_fanout on each Ok(snapshot).

daemon.json schema upgrade (codelet/fspec/src/common.rs): write_daemon_json signature changes to `pub fn write_daemon_json(path, port: u16, pid: u32, workspace: &Path, started_at: SystemTime) -> Result<()>`. JSON now includes started_at (ISO 8601) and version (CARGO_PKG_VERSION). New `pub fn read_and_verify_daemon_json(path) -> Result<DaemonHandshake>` does: read → parse → kill(pid, None) on unix / OpenProcess on windows → on ESRCH/INVALID delete file and return Err with stable text 'no daemon.json found …'. Signal handling extension (codelet/fspec/src/common.rs build_shutdown_future): grows from (sigint OR sigterm) -> Ok(()) to an enum return: pub enum ShutdownReason { Sigint, Sigterm, Sighup }. examples.text: WS drop mid-session: client is in REPL, daemon is killed; WebSocketFspecBackend detects drop, emits Action::Disconnected; DisconnectDialog renders 'daemon disconnected | r to reconnect | q to quit' at Priority::Critical within one render tick

While the disconnect dialog is up, pressing 'j' or 'k' or '?' or Tab does NOTHING (no scroll, no help dialog, no focus change). Pressing 'q' exits the client cleanly (exit 0). Pressing 'r' triggers a manual reconnect attempt (resets backoff)

Auto-reconnect happy path: daemon is killed, dialog appears at attempt 1 (250ms wait), daemon is restarted within 5s; client reconnects on attempt 2 or 3; dialog updates to 'auto-reconnecting (attempt N)…' between attempts, then disappears when reconnected; work-units list re-seeds from the new daemon

Auto-reconnect backoff cap: daemon stays dead for 60 seconds; backoff schedule observed is 250ms → 500ms → 1s → 2s → 5s → 5s → 5s … (capped); each attempt fires Action::Reconnecting(attempt) with monotonically increasing attempt number

Manual r-press during backoff: while waiting 5s, user presses 'r'; the supervisor cancels the current sleep, attempts connect immediately, and resets the backoff schedule so the NEXT failure starts at 250ms again

SIGTERM graceful drain: external observer sends SIGTERM to a running fspec daemon; daemon emits ServerGoingAway (WS Close with reason 'going_away') to all connected clients BEFORE the process exits; clients see Action::Disconnected within 100ms and the dialog shows the same 'daemon disconnected' text

SIGHUP workspace re-read: fspec daemon receives SIGHUP after the user edits their workspace path; daemon logs 'SIGHUP: re-reading workspace' at info level and continues running (does NOT exit); watcher is rebuilt against the new workspace path

Stale daemon.json: file points at PID 99999 (dead) at port 12345; user runs 'fspec client'; client calls verify_daemon_alive(99999), kill returns ESRCH, deletes the file, prints 'no daemon.json found … start `fspec daemon` first' and exits 1

fspec status against live daemon: user runs 'fspec status'; output is multi-line table with 'fspec daemon: alive', 'uptime: 14m 32s', 'connected_clients: 2', 'last_watcher_event: 3s ago', 'broadcast_lag: chunks=0 logs=0 work_units=0'; exit code 0
fspec status against no daemon: no daemon.json exists; user runs 'fspec status'; stderr prints 'fspec daemon: not running (no daemon.json at <path>)'; exit code 1
fspec status against stale daemon.json: file points at dead PID; status deletes the file (same logic as fspec client) and reports 'fspec daemon: not running (stale daemon.json removed)'; exit code 1

Two-client attach: integration test spawns daemon, opens WS-A and WS-B; A calls create_session(None) and send_input('hi'); WS-B observes the SAME (session_id, chunk) frames from chunks_rx in the same order. ServerStats.connected_clients reads 2 throughout

Broadcast capacity tuning: chunks broadcast is sized 1024; a slow subscriber that doesn't drain hits RecvError::Lagged after 1025 chunks, daemon emits tracing::warn that surfaces as a LogRecord on the logs broadcast that ALL clients see

health() RPC: embedded backend returns HealthInfo { uptime_secs: t_now - service.started_at, connected_clients: stats.connected_clients.load(), last_watcher_event_at: stats.last_watcher_event_at.lock(), lag_chunks/lag_logs/lag_work_units }; WS backend gets the same struct via tarpc

Tracing client_id span: daemon log captured during a two-client test contains lines tagged client_id=127.0.0.1:54321 AND client_id=127.0.0.1:54322 (different ephemeral ports); a grep for the first ID yields ONLY frames from that client

All earlier tests still pass: cargo test -p codelet-rpc-server -p codelet-rpc-embedded -p codelet-fspec-tui -p codelet-fspec --release is green; existing Vitest NAPI smoke (src/__tests__/napi-workunitinfo-shape.test.ts) still passes; architecture_invariants.rs still passes (RPC-011 does NOT loosen RPC-005 invariants)

questions.answer: Drain protocol: (1) on SIGTERM, set a `shutdown: AtomicBool` on ServerStats; (2) the accept-loop in bind_and_serve checks the flag and stops accepting new connections; (3) each connection task observes the flag and triggers its envelope-out channel to send a Close frame with reason=going_away then break; (4) the daemon awaits join (with a 5-second timeout — if it doesn't finish we abort()). This is more work than 'just join.await' — RPC-005 designed bind_and_serve to be shutdown via abort, not graceful. The simplest minimum-viable drain is option B: skip the accept-stop step and just (1) broadcast Close to existing clients via a new on-demand channel pulled by handle_connection's outer select, (2) abort the join handle (existing path). Adopt option B for RPC-011; record option A as a follow-up under 'graceful-accept-stop'.

rules.text: CR-1 BASELINE: WebSocketFspecBackend MUST surface WS disconnect as an Action::Disconnected on the App action bus (no silent Err returns from RPC methods after a drop)

CR-1 BASELINE: a DisconnectDialog Component is pushed onto the Compositor at Priority::Critical when Action::Disconnected fires; content includes the literal strings 'daemon disconnected', 'q to quit', 'r to reconnect'
CR-1 BASELINE: while DisconnectDialog is topmost (Critical), j/k/?/Tab are no-ops; ONLY 'q' (quit App) and 'r' (manual reconnect trigger) are honoured
Auto-reconnect: WebSocketFspecBackend owns a reconnect supervisor task with exponential backoff (250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s cap; reset on first successful frame)
Auto-reconnect: each retry attempt emits Action::Reconnecting(attempt: u32); the DisconnectDialog renders 'auto-reconnecting (attempt N)…' inline
On successful reconnect: re-issue list_work_units + create_session(None) + resubscribe to chunks/logs/work_units broadcasts, then emit Action::Reconnected so the App pops the dialog
fspec daemon handles SIGTERM AND SIGHUP in addition to SIGINT (existing). SIGTERM = graceful drain + exit; SIGHUP = re-read workspace path then continue
Graceful drain on shutdown: stop accepting new connections, wait for in-flight RPCs to complete, broadcast ServerGoingAway (WS Close with reason 'going_away' — NO new envelope variant), then exit

daemon.json gains 'pid' + 'started_at' + 'version' fields; clients (fspec client AND fspec status) call verify_daemon_alive(pid) via nix::sys::signal::kill(pid, None) BEFORE trusting the URL; on failure delete the stale file and treat as no-daemon

Broadcast channel capacities are explicit: chunks-per-session 1024, work-units 256, logs 4096. RecvError::Lagged surfaces via tracing::warn! which rides the existing LogEvent broadcast so connected clients see lag in real time

FspecService gains one new RPC: health() -> HealthInfo. HealthInfo (new lifted type in codelet-rpc-types, cfg-gated napi(object) like its siblings) carries: uptime_secs, connected_clients, last_watcher_event_at, broadcast_lag counters (chunks/logs/work_units)

ServerStats grows connected_clients: AtomicU64, last_watcher_event_at: Mutex<Option<Instant>>, and per-broadcast lag counters. health() reads these. NO new struct — ServerStats is the existing channel
FspecBackend trait gains health() -> Result<HealthInfo>; both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend implement it (embedded reads ServerStats directly; WS goes through tarpc)
New subcommand `fspec status` pretty-prints health() against the autodiscovered (or --connect'd) daemon. Exit 0 if alive, exit 1 if no daemon found / stale daemon.json / connect failure
Two-client integration test: spawn fspec daemon, attach TWO WebSocketFspecBackends, exercise create_session + send_input from client A, assert client B receives the SAME chunk stream in order
Tracing spans on per-connection handler tasks carry client_id (peer addr) and session_id fields so a `grep client_id=…` against the daemon's log filters one client's traffic

RPC-011 is ADDITIVE only: bind_and_serve signature unchanged, WebSocketFspecBackend::connect signature unchanged, build_service unchanged, no second App / no second envelope format / no rat-dialog framework

Use the WS Close frame with `reason='going_away'` (RFC 6455 close code 1001). NO new Envelope variant — that's a wire-format bump for the cost of a single observable event. The client's WebSocketFspecBackend already sees the underlying stream close; we just inspect the close frame reason when present. Decided by plan.md: 'preferred because it does NOT require a wire-format bump'.

Lives at the transport layer inside WebSocketFspecBackend (codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/websocket.rs). The supervisor owns `Arc<RwLock<Option<FspecWsClient>>>`; FspecBackend trait method bodies grab a read-lock and delegate; if the client is `None` they return `Err(BackendError::Disconnected)` so the UI renders the dialog. The supervisor publishes Action::Reconnecting/Reconnected onto an `UnboundedSender<Action>` that App passes in at connect time. Decided by plan.md table row 1 ('Wraps the existing connect in a reconnect supervisor task').

DEFER --background fork-and-detach to its own card. The plan.md marks it as 'Optional --foreground flag (default true) and a real fork-and-detach mode behind --background'. Real daemonization is a meaningful surface (PID detachment, stdio close, setsid, double-fork) and pulls in nix::unistd::daemon or similar. Out of scope for RPC-011 polish; keep --foreground=true as the only mode. systemd/launchd users use Type=simple which works fine with the current foreground process.

In codelet/fspec/src/common.rs alongside daemon_json_path() and read_daemon_json_port() — both client.rs and status.rs are siblings of common.rs. Function signature: pub fn read_and_verify_daemon_json(path: &Path) -> Result<DaemonHandshake> where DaemonHandshake = { port, pid, started_at, version }. Internal kill-probe uses nix::sys::signal::kill on unix, GetExitCodeProcess via windows-sys on windows. On stale, the function deletes the file and returns Err with a stable error string callers can match on.

Add a SECOND constructor on WebSocketFspecBackend: `connect_with_supervisor(url, action_tx: UnboundedSender<Action>) -> Result<Self>` that spawns the supervisor task wired to the action bus. The existing `connect(url)` stays as a no-supervisor convenience for tests; it returns a backend whose RPC methods just fail with BackendError::Disconnected on drop (no auto-reconnect). client.rs is updated to call connect_with_supervisor(url, app.action_tx_clone()) — App grows a pub action_tx_clone() accessor. This keeps the trait-surface unchanged and avoids upcasting an Arc<dyn FspecBackend> after the App owns it.

Upgrade to ratatui TestBackend + synth_key (already exported by app.rs for RPC-009 tests) for the App-level scenarios. That gives us a real Buffer we can scan for the literal strings 'daemon disconnected' / 'auto-reconnecting (attempt N)' — exactly what CR-1 review found missing in RPC-010. The daemon-side surrogate (subprocess-stays-alive) stays as the OUTER assertion in the end-to-end reconnect test (because we still can't pty-drive the released binary in CI), but every assertion that's about RENDERING happens against the in-process TestBackend.

Re-issue create_session(None) and replace the active session id. Reason: the new daemon has no record of the OLD session id; chunks for it will never arrive. Old session id stays in the REPL transcript (no destructive truncation) — the App emits Action::SessionCreated(new_id) which the AgentReplView treats as a NEW REPL pane. This matches the plan.md scope: 'On reconnect: re-issue list_work_units + list_sessions + resubscribe to push channels; emit a Reconnected Action'. Edit: plan.md says list_sessions; we use create_session(None) per the existing RPC-009 bootstrap pattern.

Subcommand on the existing fspec binary's Cli enum. Add `Mode::Status { connect: Option<String> }` next to Daemon and Client; implementation lives in codelet/fspec/src/status.rs. NO new binary — rule [13] still applies (codelet-napi-free). status.rs uses WebSocketFspecBackend::connect (no supervisor needed, it's a one-shot RPC then exit), calls health(), pretty-prints, exits.

SIGHUP triggers a watcher rebuild against the SAME workspace path (the path is fixed at process startup — clap doesn't expose runtime mutation). 'Re-read workspace' in plan.md scope means: drop the current WorkUnitsWatcher, build a fresh one for the same path, swap it into SharedFspecService. Use case: user committed a change that messed with fs-watch state (rename of spec/, etc.) and wants the watcher to re-walk. NOT exposed as a config-reload primitive in RPC-011 — that's its own card.

Yes — wrap the watcher in `ArcSwap<WorkUnitsWatcher>` (arc-swap crate) inside SharedFspecService. ArcSwap gives lock-free reads (cheaper than RwLock) and atomic pointer swaps; SIGHUP handler calls `service.watcher.store(Arc::new(WorkUnitsWatcher::new(path)?))`. list_work_units_snapshot() and watcher_rx() use `service.watcher.load()` to grab the current Arc. Cost: one extra dep (arc-swap is tiny, used by tracing) and one accessor change. Out-of-scope for RPC-005 invariants check — watcher slot still exists once, just behind a different Arc-flavored container.

Use a small RAII guard `ConnectedClientGuard { stats: ServerStats }`. Construct it inside handle_connection() right after ws upgrade succeeds (incrementing stats.connected_clients.fetch_add(1)); store it on the stack so Drop decrements automatically on ANY exit path (clean close, error, abort). Cleaner than manual try/finally and survives the chunks_fanout/logs_fanout abort sequence at lines 145-147 of server.rs.

Drain protocol: (1) on SIGTERM, set a `shutdown: AtomicBool` on ServerStats; (2) the accept-loop in bind_and_serve checks the flag and stops accepting new connections; (3) each connection task observes the flag and triggers its envelope-out channel to send a Close frame with reason=going_away then break; (4) the daemon awaits join (with a 5-second timeout — if it doesn't finish we abort()). This is more work than 'just join.await' — RPC-005 designed bind_and_serve to be shutdown via abort, not graceful. The simplest minimum-viable drain is option B: skip the accept-stop step and just (1) broadcast Close to existing clients via a new on-demand channel pulled by handle_connection's outer select, (2) abort the join handle (existing path). Adopt option B for RPC-011; record option A as a follow-up under 'graceful-accept-stop'.

Option (a): change u64 → i64 in HealthInfo. Rationale: (1) matches existing pattern (LogRecord.timestamp_ms is i64); (2) napi-derive v3 with napi4 feature supports i64 directly (maps to JS number; same caveat as u64 about >2^53 but realistic counters/uptime fit easily); (3) preserves the cfg-gated napi(object) without changing the napi feature level or adding BigInt to the JS surface; (4) wire format (tarpc bincode) is unchanged in width (both 8 bytes signed/unsigned); (5) zero conceptual cost for uptime/lag counters which never go negative anyway.

RPC-012.description:
Restructure codelet/fspec-tui to match the TypeScript TUI's top-level shape so future slices can layer on full Kanban rendering, work-unit details, multi-session AgentView, slash commands, etc.

GOAL
Replace the current fixed two-pane RootView with a top-level navigator that owns two dedicated state stores and can switch between a BoardView (first landing) and an AgentView. The new stores are the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for everything those views render — views become near-pure presentation against store snapshots fed via the existing Action bus.

THE TS TARGET (REFERENCE)
- src/tui/components/UnifiedBoardLayout.tsx — 7-column Kanban (backlog → specifying → testing → implementing → validating → done → blocked) with per-column scroll, a work-unit details strip, [ / ] priority reorder, session-attached indicator, last-changed indicator. Sources state via useFspecStore (Zustand).
- src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx — full-screen agent interactions; entered via Enter on a work unit in BoardView OR Shift+Right (navigate to first attached session OR open create-session dialog). Sources state via useSessionStore + useFspecStore + useModelStore (Zustand).
- src/tui/store/fspecStore.ts — work units, epics, checkpoint counts, file status, session attachments map (workUnitId → sessionId).
- src/tui/store/sessionStore.ts — currentSessionId, navigationTargetSessionId, currentWorkUnitId, currentWorkUnitStatus, isolation state, navigation handoff helpers (navigateToNewSession, setNavigationTarget).

WHAT THIS STORY DELIVERS (BASE ONLY — NOT THE FULL UI)
1. New module codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/ with:
   - BoardStore — owns: work_units: Vec<WorkUnitInfo> grouped by status into 7 columns; focused_column: usize; selected_index_per_column: HashMap<String, usize>; session_attachments: HashMap<String, SessionId> (work_unit_id → session_id); last_changed_id: Option<String>. Receives Action::WorkUnitsLoaded; exposes view-friendly read-only accessors. NOT a Zustand port — a Rust struct held in a single owning location (Mutex-free; mutated only on the App task per RPC-009 plan §single-task model). Tenere-pattern plain types.
   - AgentViewStore — owns: current_session: Option<SessionId>; navigation_target_session: Option<SessionId>; current_work_unit_id: Option<String>; current_work_unit_status: Option<String>; show_create_session_dialog: bool; should_auto_create_session: bool. Replaces AgentReplView's internal active_session field as the canonical place.
2. Refactor RootView from a fixed two-pane layout into a navigator that holds an active_view: ViewMode { Board, Agent } and a single owned BoardView | AgentView child. App::bootstrap drives the BoardView seed (board.replace_work_units(units)) and the AgentViewStore handoff (no longer pre-creates a session at bootstrap — sessions are created lazily on first navigation).
3. New BoardView component (REPLACES the current bottom-row footer + two-pane layout, but only renders a MINIMAL placeholder Kanban skeleton for now — the rich 7-column UnifiedBoardLayout port is a downstream slice). Reads from BoardStore; emits Action::EnterWorkUnit(id) on Enter, Action::OpenAgentView(target: Option<SessionId>) on Shift+Right, Action::ReorderUp/Down on [/]. The richer rendering, mouse handling, viewport scroll math, etc. are deferred.
4. AgentView wrapper (REPLACES the current AgentReplView as the right pane child of RootView; in the new world it is a top-level view shown only when ViewMode == Agent). Pulls active_session from AgentViewStore (not from its own field). Single-session for now; the multi-session/slash-command/model-picker work is downstream.
5. New Action variants — EnterWorkUnit(String), OpenAgentView(Option<SessionId>), BackToBoard, NavigationTargetSet(Option<SessionId>) — and the existing FocusNext is REPURPOSED (or replaced) for the navigator level.
6. Wiring: App::dispatch routes the new actions; on EnterWorkUnit it sets AgentViewStore.current_work_unit_id and switches RootView.active_view = Agent; on OpenAgentView with Some(sid) it sets navigation_target_session and switches view; with None it sets show_create_session_dialog = true (the dialog itself ships in a downstream slice — for now we just record the intent).
7. NO Zustand-equivalent reactive subscription machinery. The single-owner store pattern + Action bus already gives Rust a simpler equivalent of Zustand's selectors: views just read from the store on each render. The existing render-tick cadence (16ms cap) bounds re-renders.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (each is a downstream slice)
- The full 7-column UnifiedBoardLayout render (column headers, viewport math, per-column scroll arrows, last-changed ⏩ animation, work-unit details strip, [ ] priority reorder UX, mouse SGR scroll, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, etc.) — this story only ships a placeholder Kanban skeleton that proves the BoardStore wiring.
- The full AgentView port (multi-session, slash commands, file search, model picker, thinking-level dialog, history navigation, isolation, blocklist, role banner, etc.).
- Per-session BoardStore mutations (attach/detach session, last-changed timestamp tracking via stateHistory) — those land when their UI counterparts ship.
- Checkpoint counts, file status, epics, stashes — none are needed for the placeholder skeleton; add when the rich rendering arrives.
- Persistent store between runs (the TS Zustand state is also in-memory only; nothing to persist).

ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS THIS STORY MUST PRESERVE
- RPC-005 Q9 host-supplied tokio runtime Handle (tokio::spawn only; no Builder/Runtime::new).
- RPC-008 FspecBackend trait surface — every store mutation that requires backend data still goes through Arc<dyn FspecBackend>.
- Loopback-only bind, codelet-napi NOT a dep of codelet-fspec-tui [dependencies] or [dev-dependencies].
- File size — each new module file kept well under 300 LoC. The existing 300-LoC drifts in app.rs / agent_repl.rs / work_units_list.rs MUST be addressed as part of this story (extraction of the navigator, BoardStore, AgentViewStore, and stripped-down AgentView gives natural seams).
- RPC-009 critical drifts get ABSORBED: BoardView's render format and width are restated for the new Kanban skeleton; Action enum's PartialEq/Eq is reconsidered (StreamChunk's 23 variants block automatic PartialEq — confirm or use a derive-less manual impl per RPC-009).

architectureNotes.text: [0] SharedFspecService construction needs the workspace cwd so checkpoint_counts() knows where to look for refs/fspec-checkpoints/. Two options: (a) add a `cwd: PathBuf` to SharedFspecService and a `with_cwd(...)` constructor variant alongside the existing `new` / `with_session_manager`; or (b) introduce a separate trait or accessor passed at service construction. We picked (a): add an optional cwd field that defaults to None — when None, `checkpoint_counts()` returns the zero default. Hosts that want real counts (the rpc-server bin, the embedded ratatui host, the NAPI factory) pass a Some(cwd).

[1] The new `count_checkpoints` helper iterates `repo.references()` and matches names starting with `refs/fspec-checkpoints/`. Existing `list_ghost_checkpoints` filters by a single work_unit_id prefix so we cannot reuse it directly — we extract the last path segment of each ref name and pass it to a shared `is_automatic_checkpoint` helper (`name.contains("-auto-")`) that mirrors TS `AUTO_CHECKPOINT_PATTERN`.

[2] Cross-transport parity tests follow the RPC-009 pattern — co-locate one embedded + one WS variant in `tests/checkpoint_counts_rpc015.rs`. The WS test uses `tests/common::ws_server_for(...)` (already established in `ws_backend_smoke.rs` / `auto_reconnect_slice2_rpc011.rs`). The embedded test reuses the standard SharedFspecService::with_cwd pattern.

[3] BoardStore.set_checkpoint_counts only changes the new field — it does not invalidate column groupings or selections so existing replace_work_units bookkeeping is untouched. The new field default (`{0,0}`) flows through `Default::default()` so existing test fixtures need no churn.

[4] The render path in views/board.rs grows by one new Layout split (+5 rows total: 4-row header + 1-row separator) inserted between top border and the existing 5-row details strip. The `paint_side_borders` + `inner_rect` helpers are reused for the new strip. The header itself is rendered by a single new helper `paint_header(area, buf, &theme, &store)` that internally fans out into `logo::render`, `checkpoint_status::render`, `keybinding_shortcuts::render`.

assumptions: [0] The RPC-015 card description and master plan are unambiguous about implementation — the FspecService surface, the new shared type, the storage on git refs, and the header layout are all dictated. No human input needed.
RPC-015.description: Port the 4-row UnifiedBoardLayout header (src/tui/components/UnifiedBoardLayout.tsx:360-380): FSPEC ASCII art logo (left), Checkpoints: N Manual, M Auto (right, row 1), and 'C Checkpoints ◆ F Changed Files ◆ D FOUNDATION.md ◆ / New Agent' chord row (right, row 2). Requires new RPC method `checkpoint_counts()` plus shared `CheckpointCounts` type, delegating to codelet_git::ghost_commit::count_checkpoints. Additive NAPI export `count_checkpoints(cwd)` lets TS converge on the same backend without changing TS code today. Keybinding C/F/D/slash are visible hints only — wiring lands in future RPC-002 children. See spec/attachments/RPC-015/typescript-reference.md.

examples.text: [0] Given a temp git repo with 2 refs `refs/fspec-checkpoints/AUTH-001/baseline` and `refs/fspec-checkpoints/AUTH-001/AUTH-001-auto-testing`, when `codelet_git::ghost_commit::count_checkpoints` is called, it returns `{ manual: 1, auto: 1 }`

[1] Given a temp directory that is NOT a git repo, when `count_checkpoints` is called, it returns `{ manual: 0, auto: 0 }` without error (graceful no-repo path matches TS `listCheckpointIndexFiles` ENOENT behavior)
[2] Given a temp git repo with no checkpoint refs, when `count_checkpoints` is called, it returns `{ manual: 0, auto: 0 }`

[3] Given a temp git repo with checkpoint refs spread across two work units (AUTH-001 has baseline + AUTH-001-auto-testing; BUG-002 has BUG-002-auto-specifying), when `count_checkpoints` is called, it returns `{ manual: 1, auto: 2 }` aggregating across all work units

[4] When `EmbeddedFspecBackend::checkpoint_counts()` is called against a SharedFspecService constructed with a temp git repo containing 1 manual + 1 auto ref, the awaited result is `{ manual: 1, auto: 1 }`

[5] When `WebSocketFspecBackend::checkpoint_counts()` is called against an rpc-server bound to the SAME temp repo, the awaited result is `{ manual: 1, auto: 1 }` (cross-transport parity per RPC-009 pattern)

[6] When the App bootstraps against an EmbeddedFspecBackend whose service was built with a repo containing 2 manual + 3 auto refs, after `App::bootstrap().await` completes and the bootstrap task delivers its action, `app.board_store().checkpoint_counts()` returns `{ manual: 2, auto: 3 }`

[8] When BoardView renders against a 120x24 TestBackend with `set_checkpoint_counts({ manual: 2, auto: 5 })`, the header strip contains the substring `Checkpoints: 2 Manual, 5 Auto`
[9] When BoardView renders at 120x24, the rendered buffer contains the keybinding chord substring `C Checkpoints ◆ F Changed Files ◆ D FOUNDATION.md ◆ / New Agent`
