[11] After this card lands, the file `codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board/logo.rs` exists and has fewer than 300 lines; `codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board/checkpoint_status.rs` exists and has fewer than 300 lines; `codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board/keybinding_shortcuts.rs` exists and has fewer than 300 lines; `codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board.rs` still has fewer than 300 lines

[12] After this card lands, codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs contains the substring `pub struct CheckpointCounts` and the struct has `pub manual: u32` and `pub auto: u32` fields; codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs contains the substring `async fn checkpoint_counts() -> CheckpointCounts`; codelet/napi/src/git.rs contains the function `pub fn count_checkpoints`

[13] RPC-013/014 invariants preserved: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/navigator.rs still does NOT contain `Constraint::Length(1)`; codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board.rs still contains `Action::EnterWorkUnit`, `Action::FocusNextColumn`, `Action::ReorderUp`, `← →`, `Work Agent`, `ESC`, `Back`, AND `Attachments` (details strip still painted)

rules.text: [0] A new shared type CheckpointCounts { manual: u32, auto: u32 } is added to codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs (gated on the `napi` feature for cross-binding parity), mirroring the TS interface `{ manual: number; auto: number }` from src/utils/checkpoint-index.ts

[1] A new helper `codelet_git::ghost_commit::count_checkpoints(dir: &Path) -> Result<CheckpointCounts>` iterates every git ref under `refs/fspec-checkpoints/` and classifies each by whether its last path segment (the checkpoint name) contains the substring `-auto-` — names containing `-auto-` are counted as auto, all others as manual. Mirrors the TS `isAutomaticCheckpoint` rule from src/utils/checkpoint-index.ts (AUTO_CHECKPOINT_PATTERN = '-auto-')

[2] The FspecService tarpc surface gains one new RPC `async fn checkpoint_counts() -> CheckpointCounts` implemented in `FspecServiceImpl` by delegating to `codelet_git::ghost_commit::count_checkpoints(cwd)`. The shared service is constructed with the workspace cwd it should count under; for tests that do not exercise checkpoint counting the cwd defaults to a path that yields zero counts (no `.git/`)

[3] The `FspecBackend` trait in codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs gains `async fn checkpoint_counts() -> Result<CheckpointCounts>`. Both `EmbeddedFspecBackend` and `WebSocketFspecBackend` implement it as one-line tarpc delegates (RPC-009 cross-transport parity)

[4] A new additive NAPI export `napi::count_checkpoints(cwd: String) -> CheckpointCounts` is exposed in codelet/napi/src/git.rs and re-exported through codelet/napi/index.d.ts. The existing TS pure-JS `countCheckpoints` in src/utils/checkpoint-index.ts is NOT changed — it can switch to the NAPI export at its own pace, and both converge on the same `codelet_git::ghost_commit::count_checkpoints` so they cannot drift

[5] BoardStore gains a `checkpoint_counts: CheckpointCounts` field and methods `checkpoint_counts(&self) -> CheckpointCounts` + `set_checkpoint_counts(&mut self, CheckpointCounts)`. The field defaults to `{ manual: 0, auto: 0 }` so the header paints `Checkpoints: None` until the bootstrap RPC returns

[6] A new Action variant `Action::CheckpointCountsLoaded(CheckpointCounts)` carries the counts from the bootstrap task to the App. `App::dispatch` handles it by calling `board_store.set_checkpoint_counts(counts)`. `App::bootstrap` fires off `backend.checkpoint_counts()` alongside `list_work_units()` and emits the new Action when it returns

[7] The BoardView render layout inserts a NEW 4-row header strip + 1-row separator BETWEEN the top border and the 5-row details strip. Layout becomes: top border (1) → header strip (4) → ├──┤ separator (1) → details strip (5) → ├┬┤ (1) → column header (1) → ├┼┤ (1) → content (Min) → ├┴┤ (1) → footer (1) → bottom border (1). The header strip is bordered on both sides by `│` glyphs matching the existing details strip pattern

[8] The header strip is painted by three new widget modules under codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board/: `logo.rs` paints the 4-row FSPEC ASCII art block (12 chars wide) glyph-for-glyph identical to src/tui/components/Logo.tsx; `checkpoint_status.rs` paints either `Checkpoints: None` (when both counts are 0) or `Checkpoints: {manual} Manual, {auto} Auto`; `keybinding_shortcuts.rs` paints `C Checkpoints ◆ F Changed Files ◆ D FOUNDATION.md ◆ / New Agent`

[9] Within the 4-row header strip: left column (12 chars wide) holds the FSPEC logo; right column holds (row 0) blank, (row 1) checkpoint status text, (row 2) a horizontal `─` divider line matching TS `borderTop`, (row 3) the keybinding shortcuts text. Logo and right column are separated by one space of padding

[10] The C / F / D / / keybindings are visible HINTS ONLY — they are NOT wired to actions in this card. Wiring lands in subsequent RPC-002 children (Checkpoint viewer, Changed Files viewer, FOUNDATION.md viewer, new Agent session)

[11] All RPC-012/013/014 invariants are preserved: BoardView still emits the same Actions on the same key events; the existing RPC-013 footer string + 5-row details strip + ├┬┤├┼┤├┴┤ junctions + work-type color coding stay intact; navigator.rs still has no `Constraint::Length(1)` footer reservation; no FooterView re-export; views still avoid `codelet_napi::`/`codelet_core::`/`tarpc::`/`tokio_tungstenite::` direct imports and never construct their own tokio runtime

[12] File-size discipline: every new module file (logo.rs / checkpoint_status.rs / keybinding_shortcuts.rs / extended board.rs / extended dispatch.rs / extended bootstrap.rs) stays under 300 LoC. The orchestrator board.rs continues to be < 300 LoC after the new layout split lands

architectureNotes.text: BoardStore gains `scroll_offsets: HashMap<String, usize>` + four mutation methods: scroll_offset_for, set_scroll_offset_for, move_selection(delta, viewport_height), scroll_focused_column(delta, viewport_height), select_first_in_focused, select_last_in_focused. All mutations remain single-task per RPC-009 invariants.

BoardView stashes the most recent viewport_height in a `last_viewport_height: Cell<u16>` field (computed at render time from `area.height - fixed_rows`) so handle_event can read it when emitting Action::ScrollFocusedColumnUp/Down / SelectFirstInFocused / SelectLastInFocused.

WorkUnitInfo.last_state_change_at is populated by codelet_core::work_units::WorkUnitRecord by reading `stateHistory[last].timestamp` during JSON deserialization. Legacy records without stateHistory yield None — preserving cross-transport parity and forward compatibility.

Indicator priority: when a unit is selected in the focused column the bg=Green/fg=Black/Bold style still wins; ⏩ and 🟢 prefixes are still rendered (as text inside the cell label) regardless of selection, matching the TS chalk behaviour.

Action enum gains four new variants: ScrollFocusedColumnUp(usize), ScrollFocusedColumnDown(usize), SelectFirstInFocused, SelectLastInFocused. App::dispatch routes Action::SelectNext/SelectPrev through BoardStore::move_selection(delta, viewport_height) (read from BoardView.last_viewport_height via a getter) so arrow keys also auto-scroll.

File layout: extract the new viewport math + auto-scroll helpers into `codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/board.rs` (still < 300 LoC) and a new `codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board/viewport.rs` module that owns the per-row painting + ↑/↓/⏩/🟢 cell-text building, keeping `views/board/columns.rs` thin or replaced. The `board.rs` orchestrator and every new module stay < 300 LoC.

RPC-016.description: Port the BoardView per-column scroll + auto-scroll + arrow indicators + last-changed (⏩) + session-attached (🟢) markers + keyboard nav (PageUp/PageDown/Home/End). Reference src/tui/components/UnifiedBoardLayout.tsx lines 95-103 (viewport_height), 149-234 (scroll state + auto-scroll), 169-183 (lastChangedWorkUnit), 251-352 (keyboard nav), 444-499 (cell render). Requires adding `last_state_change_at: Option<String>` field to WorkUnitInfo (rpc-types, additive — TS keeps using stateHistory[last].timestamp fallback). No new RPC methods (session-attachments + checkpoint counts already wired). See spec/attachments/RPC-016/typescript-reference.md.

examples.text: Given a column with 20 work units and viewport_height=10 and scroll_offset=0, rendering paints rows 0..9 showing units 0..8 with ↓ on row 9
Given a column with 20 work units, scroll_offset=5, viewport_height=10, rendering paints ↑ on row 0, units 6..13 on rows 1..8, ↓ on row 9
Given selected_index=8 with viewport_height=10 and scroll_offset=0, pressing Down moves selection to 9 and auto-scrolls so selection stays visible at the bottom of the viewport
Given a column with 30 units and viewport_height=10, pressing PageDown advances the focused column's selected_index by 10 rows and auto-scrolls accordingly
Pressing Home with focused column = `done` and selected_index=12 sets selected_index=0 and scroll_offset=0; pressing End sets selected_index=units.len()-1 with appropriate scroll

Given AUTH-001 has last_state_change_at = '2026-05-13T10:00:00Z' and AUTH-002 has last_state_change_at = '2026-05-14T10:00:00Z', the cell text for AUTH-002 renders as `⏩ AUTH-002 ⏩` while AUTH-001 renders plain
Given attach_session('AUTH-002', SessionId('s-1')) and AUTH-002 has estimate=5, the cell renders as `🟢 AUTH-002 [5]`
Given AUTH-002 is both the last-changed unit AND has an attached session, the cell renders as `⏩ 🟢 AUTH-002 ⏩`
Given a spec/work-units.json record with stateHistory ending at '2026-05-13T07:33:00.878Z', codelet_core::read_snapshot maps last_state_change_at = Some('2026-05-13T07:33:00.878Z')

Given a legacy spec/work-units.json record with no stateHistory field, codelet_core::read_snapshot maps last_state_change_at = None and the TS BoardView's existing stateHistory-based derivation continues to work unchanged

Given a BoardStore with 3 backlog units, focused column backlog, selected_index=2, scroll_offset=0; when move_selection(10, 10) is called the proposed index 12 wraps to 0 (selected_index_for("backlog") returns 0)

Given a BoardStore with 5 backlog units, focused column backlog, selected_index=0, scroll_offset=0; when move_selection(-1, 10) is called the proposed index -1 wraps to the last unit (selected_index_for("backlog") returns 4)

rules.text: Each kanban column tracks its own scroll_offset and renders at most viewport_height rows of work units
When scroll_offset > 0 the first viewport row of that column renders ↑ centered; when scroll_offset + viewport_height < units.len() the last viewport row renders ↓ centered
Moving the selection past the visible viewport auto-scrolls the focused column so the selection stays visible (account for ↑/↓ arrow rows consuming one viewport row each)
PageUp/PageDown scroll the focused column's selection by viewport_height rows; Home/End jump the focused column's selection to first/last unit
The most-recently-changed work unit (derived from WorkUnitInfo.last_state_change_at) renders as ⏩ {session_indicator}{id}{points} ⏩ in every column it appears
Work units whose id has an entry in BoardStore.session_attachments render with the 🟢  prefix before the id

WorkUnitInfo gains an additive Option<String> field `last_state_change_at` (ISO-8601 UTC) carrying the timestamp of the latest stateHistory entry; legacy work-units.json files without stateHistory yield None
No new RPC methods are introduced; the indicator data is delivered by the existing list_work_units payload (last_state_change_at) plus the existing BoardStore session_attachments map
No TypeScript source files in src/tui/ are modified; the TS BoardView continues to derive lastChangedWorkUnit from stateHistory[last].timestamp
All new source modules stay under the 300 LoC ceiling and tests/source_shape_* assertions stay green

move_selection wraps around: when the proposed index goes below 0 it wraps to the last unit, and when it goes past the last unit it wraps to index 0. Wrap-around happens unconditionally (even when the column is not scrollable). Mirrors TS BoardView.tsx onWorkUnitChange (src/tui/components/BoardView.tsx:535-540).

architectureNotes.text: The proper-lockfile-compatible mkdir-lock pattern currently inlined in codelet/napi/src/schedule_handler.rs is lifted into codelet/common/src/file_lock.rs as a reusable with_file_lock helper, and schedule_handler.rs is refactored to depend on it — single source of truth for inter-process locking

All store mutations happen synchronously inside App::dispatch on the App task — Action::ReorderUp / ReorderDown spawn a fire-and-forget tokio task that calls backend.move_work_unit_up/_down(id) and lets the watcher-driven Action::WorkUnitsLoaded path handle the re-seed (RPC-009 single-task tenere)

File-size discipline: codelet_core::work_units file is already at ~413 LoC — exceeds 300-line ceiling. The new move_work_unit helper goes into a sibling file codelet/core/src/work_units_write.rs so work_units.rs (read-side) stays focused

Cwd discovery on the RPC side: SharedFspecService::cwd() (added in RPC-015) returns the workspace root. FspecService::move_work_unit_up/_down delegates to codelet_core::work_units_write::move_work_unit(cwd, id, Direction). If no cwd is attached (in-process tests without with_cwd) the RPC returns an error so the TUI surfaces it via tracing rather than silently no-op'ing

This made move_work_unit_up/_down silently fail at runtime in BOTH combined and daemon modes (RPC handler returns Err which dispatch.rs swallows via tracing::debug!), and made checkpoint_counts silently return zero. Pressing ] mirrors with DOWN

Moving a unit at the bottom boundary on ] is a no-op

architectureNotes.text: SessionManagerHandle gains two new methods: `get_model_info(session_id) -> ModelInfo` and `get_thinking_level(session_id) -> ThinkingLevel`. The concrete impl in codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs resolves via the session's stored (provider_id, model_id) → codelet_providers models lookup. StubSessionManagerHandle returns default values. SharedFspecService::get_model_info / get_thinking_level delegate via the handle; when no handle is attached they return defaults.

`SharedFspecService::get_workspace_info()` uses the attached `cwd` (via `with_cwd`) plus `codelet_git::status::get_current_branch(cwd)` to build the WorkspaceInfo. When no cwd has been attached the method returns `WorkspaceInfo { cwd: std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_default().to_string_lossy().into_owned(), git_branch: None }`. The cwd is returned RAW (not yet `~`-shortened) — the SessionFooter widget does the home-directory replacement at render time using `home::home_dir()`.

Token state derivation: `AgentView::record_chunk` (called by App::dispatch on Action::ChunkReceived) gains a `token_state: &mut TokenState` parameter (or AgentView reaches into AgentViewStore via App::dispatch — TBD in implementation). On StreamChunk::TokenUpdate {tokens: TokenTracker} we update input_tokens/output_tokens; on StreamChunk::ContextFillUpdate {context_fill: ContextFillInfo} we update context_fill_pct from fill_percentage. All other variants leave the token state unchanged.

New Action variants: `ModelInfoLoaded(SessionId, ModelInfo)`, `ThinkingLevelLoaded(SessionId, ThinkingLevel)`, `WorkspaceInfoLoaded(WorkspaceInfo)`. App::dispatch matches each and writes to AgentViewStore. The bootstrap path fires get_workspace_info once. App::dispatch on Action::SessionCreated spawns two tasks per session — `backend.get_model_info(session)` and `backend.get_thinking_level(session)` — that dispatch their respective *Loaded actions on success.

SessionManagerHandle trait methods added with DEFAULT IMPLEMENTATIONS so the concrete SessionManager in codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs does not need a deep wiring change in this card — concrete override of `get_model_info`/`get_thinking_level` is deferred to RPC-022 (ModelSelector + ThinkingLevel modal dialogs). For RPC-018 the trait defaults return the safe `ModelInfo::default()` / `ThinkingLevel::Off`, the StubSessionManagerHandle inherits these defaults, and the RPC-018 tests assert default values from the dual-transport surface. The real values flow once RPC-022 lands.

Glyph: per the RPC-018 attachment the git-branch decoration in the SessionFooter uses the unicode '⌥' glyph (not the TS `⎇` glyph). The TS Ink SessionFooter is preserved unchanged — only the new Rust SessionFooter widget displays the `⌥` form.

RPC-018.description: Port the rich AgentView chrome from src/tui/components/SessionHeader.tsx (228 lines) and SessionFooter.tsx (74 lines). Header shows '#N: <model> [R] [V] [Nk] [T:<level>]  tokens: in↓ out↑ [N%]'. Footer shows input hints (left) and '~/projects/fspec [⌥ branch]' (right). Requires three new RPC methods: get_model_info, get_thinking_level, get_workspace_info. Adds shared types ModelInfo, ThinkingLevel, WorkspaceInfo to rpc-types (gated on napi feature). Token state derived from existing StreamChunk events. See spec/attachments/RPC-018/typescript-reference.md.

examples.text: An empty AgentViewStore (no session, no workspace, no model info) renders Header with placeholder text 'Agent' on the left + ' tokens: 0↓ 0↑ [0%]' on the right, and Footer with 'Enter=send  Ctrl+C=interrupt  ESC=back' on the left + '<cwd>' (no branch) on the right when not in a git repo

When session #1 exists with model info (Claude Opus 4.7, reasoning+vision, 192k context) and thinking level High, AgentView header renders '#1: Claude Opus 4.7 [R] [V] [192k] [T:High]' on the left and 'tokens: 0↓ 0↑ [0%]' on the right

When session #1 receives a `StreamChunk::TokenUpdate` carrying { input_tokens: 1234, output_tokens: 567 } followed by `StreamChunk::ContextFillUpdate` { fill_percentage: 45 }, the next render of AgentView header right-shows 'tokens: 1234↓ 567↑ [45%]'
When cwd is /Users/rquast/projects/fspec, $HOME is /Users/rquast, and the workspace is on git branch 'codelet-integration', AgentView footer right-shows '~/projects/fspec [⌥ codelet-integration]'
When cwd is /tmp/scratch and the directory is NOT a git repo, AgentView footer right-shows just '/tmp/scratch' with no '[⌥ ...]' branch segment

Calling backend.get_workspace_info() against an EmbeddedFspecBackend and a WebSocketFspecBackend wired to the SAME SharedFspecService (constructed with .with_cwd(tmp_path)) returns identical WorkspaceInfo on both transports

Calling backend.get_model_info(session_id) and backend.get_thinking_level(session_id) against an embedded backend whose SharedFspecService has NO session manager attached returns the safe defaults (empty display_name, all-false capabilities, ThinkingLevel::Off) without panicking

After App::bootstrap completes, the AgentViewStore has a workspace snapshot populated; if the user enters AgentView for the first time and Action::SessionCreated fires for session 's-1', within one App::dispatch turn the AgentViewStore has model_info_by_session['s-1'] and thinking_level_by_session['s-1'] populated

The TS Ink AgentView (src/tui/components/SessionHeader.tsx + SessionFooter.tsx + tokenStateUtils.ts + modelStore.ts) renders identically before and after RPC-018 lands — no diffs in those four files, no diffs in existing NAPI exports

Source-shape regression: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent.rs OR codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/mod.rs is under 300 LoC, and the new files codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/header.rs + footer.rs each exist and are under 300 LoC

rules.text: The SessionHeader renders a 1-row strip at the top of AgentView with `#N: <model display name> [R] [V] [Nk] [T:<level>]` on the LEFT and `tokens: <in>↓ <out>↑ [<fill>%]` on the RIGHT

The SessionFooter renders a 1-row strip at the bottom of AgentView with input hints on the LEFT and `<cwd> [⌥ <branch>]` on the RIGHT (cwd shortened with `~` when inside $HOME; no `[⌥ ...]` segment when the workspace is not a git repo)

Three new RPC methods exist on the shared FspecService trait — `get_model_info(session_id) -> ModelInfo`, `get_thinking_level(session_id) -> ThinkingLevel`, `get_workspace_info() -> WorkspaceInfo` — and BOTH FspecBackend impls (EmbeddedFspecBackend + WebSocketFspecBackend) implement them as one-line delegates
Three new shared types live in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs — `ModelInfo`, `ThinkingLevel`, `WorkspaceInfo` — gated on the `napi` feature so NAPI can re-export them with the same JS shape

AgentViewStore gains four new fields — `model_info_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, ModelInfo>`, `token_state_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, TokenState>`, `thinking_level_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, ThinkingLevel>`, and a single workspace snapshot `workspace: Option<WorkspaceInfo>` — all populated via App::dispatch, never directly

Token state for the current session is derived from `StreamChunk::TokenUpdate` (input/output token counts) and `StreamChunk::ContextFillUpdate` (context fill percentage) events as they arrive via `Action::ChunkReceived`; `record_chunk` updates `token_state_by_session` in addition to its existing scrollback append

AgentView render layout becomes a 4-row vertical split: Header(Length 1) / Scrollback(Min 0) / Input(Length 3) / Footer(Length 1); the existing single-line `tui_input::Input` from RPC-012 stays inside the Input row unchanged

App::bootstrap (and the post-Reconnected re-bootstrap path) calls `backend.get_workspace_info()` once and dispatches `Action::WorkspaceInfoLoaded(info)`; the AgentViewStore caches the result. Model info + thinking level are fetched per-session in App::dispatch on `Action::SessionCreated` (and on `EnterWorkUnit` when current_session is already set) via spawned tasks that emit `Action::ModelInfoLoaded(session_id, info)` and `Action::ThinkingLevelLoaded(session_id, level)`

Source-shape invariants from RPC-015/RPC-017 are preserved: every file under 300 LoC; views/ does NOT import codelet_napi / codelet_core / tarpc / tokio_tungstenite; no tokio::runtime::Builder; new widget files live under codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/ (header.rs + footer.rs); cross-transport parity tests exist in tests/ for each new RPC method

When the SessionManagerHandle / git helper returns no data (e.g. no session manager attached, no cwd attached, not a git repo, model unknown), the new RPC methods return safe defaults — `ModelInfo { display_name: '', supports_reasoning: false, supports_vision: false, context_window: 0 }`, `ThinkingLevel::Off`, `WorkspaceInfo { cwd: '<process cwd>', git_branch: None }` — never panic, never hang. The SessionHeader still renders, hiding empty badges so the UI degrades gracefully

NAPI surface remains additive: a new `napi::get_model_info(sessionId)` and `napi::get_workspace_info(cwd)` export are added that delegate to the SAME helpers the new RPC methods call. The existing `napi::get_thinking_config` / `JsThinkingLevel` exports stay untouched. No TypeScript code is modified.

RPC-018.title: AgentView SessionHeader + SessionFooter widgets

userStory.action: see a SessionHeader at the top of AgentView showing model badges + per-session token deltas, and a SessionFooter at the bottom showing input hints + cwd + git branch
userStory.benefit: the Rust ratatui AgentView matches the Ink TS AgentView chrome and exposes the same model/thinking/workspace state to both transports through three new RPC methods

architectureNotes.text: codelet/fspec-tui crate adds tui-textarea = "0.7" as a dep (workspace inherit)
New files: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/multiline_input.rs (< 300 lines) and codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/scrollback.rs (< 300 lines)

AgentView orchestrator (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent.rs) shrinks: input field becomes MultiLineInput, scrollback field becomes ScrollbackList; record_chunk delegates to ScrollbackList::push. Must stay under 300 LoC.

Action enum (codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs) gains four new variants: HistoryPrev, HistoryNext, SessionPrev, SessionNext. App::dispatch arms for these are deferred to RPC-021 — for RPC-019 they exist only so AgentView::handle_event can emit them.

InputEventOutcome { Submitted(String), Continued, Ignored } is an internal enum private to multiline_input.rs; AgentView translates it into EventResult + an Action. Submitted -> Action::InputSubmitted, Continued -> EventResult::consumed(), Ignored -> EventResult::ignored() so the compositor walks down.

ScrollbackList stores Vec<RenderedChunk> internally (lines pre-rendered just like before). render(area, buf) computes visible window from area.height + offset + stick_to_bottom; does NOT flatten all lines into a single Paragraph anymore.

Placeholder hint is owned by AgentView (NOT by MultiLineInput) so the prompt prefix '> ' renders in green and the hint in dim grey, mirroring TS ConversationInputArea layout. MultiLineInput just exposes is_empty() + cursor_position().

RPC-019.description: Replace the single-line tui_input::Input with a multi-line widget (recommend tui-textarea crate). Replace the flat Vec<RenderedChunk> scrollback with a windowed VirtualList-style widget that renders O(1) per frame regardless of scrollback length. References: src/tui/components/MultiLineInput.tsx (308 lines), src/tui/components/VirtualList.tsx (681 lines), src/tui/components/ConversationInputArea.tsx (input prompt + placeholder hint). Pure client-side widget work — no new RPC methods. Shift+arrow chords are forwarded as actions to caller because they trigger history/session navigation (RPC-021), not input editing. See spec/attachments/RPC-019/typescript-reference.md.

examples.text: User types `hello` then Shift+Enter then `world` then Enter — AgentView emits Action::InputSubmitted("hello\nworld") and the input resets to empty
User pastes 'line-a\nline-b\nline-c' into the empty input box — the input now shows 3 visual rows and the input box has grown to 3 rows of content (+2 border rows = Length(5))
User types 8 newlines in a row — the visible input box caps at 6 content rows (+2 border = Length(8)); the textarea internally retains all 8 lines and scrolls its own viewport
User opens AgentView with empty input — the input row shows '> Type a message... (\'Shift+↑/↓\' history | \'Shift+←/→\' sessions | \'Tab\' select turn)' in dim grey
User presses Shift+Up while typing — AgentView emits Action::HistoryPrev (the input text is NOT modified)
User presses Shift+Left — AgentView emits Action::SessionPrev
AgentView records 10_000 RenderedChunks via push (1 line each); render against an 80x20 TestBackend completes in <50ms because only ~16 chunks (viewport height) get laid out
User has 100 chunks, scrolls up with PageUp on an 80x20 viewport (12 scrollback rows) — offset decreases by exactly 12; PageDown returns to offset 88 and stick_to_bottom flips back to true
AgentView is in stick_to_bottom mode at offset 88 (showing chunks 88..99); a new chunk arrives via record_chunk — the ScrollbackList auto-bumps offset to 89 so chunks 89..100 remain visible
User presses ESC inside AgentView with a partially typed multi-line message — AgentView emits Action::BackToBoard (the typed buffer is preserved in the textarea for when the user comes back)

rules.text: Plain Enter submits the current input; Shift+Enter inserts a newline (so multi-line composition works)

The MultiLineInput auto-grows from 1 row to a configurable cap (default 6 rows) as the user types; the AgentView vertical layout reserves Length(N+2) for the input box where N is the current visible row count

Up/Down arrows move the cursor between visual lines when the input has multiple lines; when the cursor is on the first/last line, Up/Down events are forwarded as Ignored (no action emitted) so a future RPC can layer scrollback/overlay nav on top
Pasted text containing embedded newlines preserves those newlines verbatim in the input buffer (no \n -> space substitution)

Shift+Up/Down/Left/Right chords are forwarded to the AgentView as Action::HistoryPrev/HistoryNext/SessionPrev/SessionNext respectively — RPC-019 only emits the actions; RPC-021 will route them through App::dispatch
ESC always emits Action::BackToBoard from AgentView (preserved from RPC-012/RPC-013)

When the input buffer is empty AND the input area is focused, the input area paints a dim-style placeholder hint prefixed with '> ': "Type a message... ('Shift+↑/↓' history | 'Shift+←/→' sessions | 'Tab' select turn)"
The ScrollbackList renders in O(1) per frame regardless of total chunk count: only the slice of chunks that fits in the visible viewport (offset..offset+area.height) is laid out and painted
PageUp/PageDown move the scrollback offset by exactly viewport_height lines; pressing End jumps to bottom and re-enables stick_to_bottom

When stick_to_bottom is true, pushing a new chunk auto-scrolls so the latest chunk stays in view; PageUp disables stick_to_bottom; reaching the bottom (PageDown/End or pushing past total_lines-viewport) re-enables it
No new RPC methods, no NAPI exports, no TS file changes — purely client-side widget refactor inside codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/

RPC-019.title: Multi-line input + VirtualList-style scrollback in AgentView

userStory.action: replace the AgentView single-line tui_input with a tui-textarea-backed MultiLineInput and replace the flat scrollback Vec with an O(1) windowed ScrollbackList
userStory.benefit: long agent sessions remain responsive and multi-line composition (paste with newlines, Shift+Enter) works the same way the Ink TS AgentView does

architectureNotes.text: Architecture: AgentView OWNS the slash + file popups as Option<...> fields (rule [13]). Popup state is presentation-only; mutations flow through AgentView::sync_popups() after each MultiLineInput event. Critical modal dialogs (HelpDialog/DisconnectDialog) keep living on the Compositor and overlay these popups (Compositor renders AFTER AgentView in App::render order).

RPC method `search_files(prefix, limit) -> Vec<String>` lands on FspecService and FspecBackend. Shared service delegates to NEW helper `codelet_core::file_search::search(cwd, prefix, limit)` using ignore::WalkBuilder + globset::GlobBuilder (case-insensitive, pattern '**/*<prefix>*'). Sorted by mtime desc, capped at `limit`. Mirrors the existing codelet_tools::glob::GlobTool behaviour but lives in codelet_core so the dep boundary stays clean (no codelet_tools dep added to codelet_rpc).

Action enum gains: SlashCommandSelected(SlashCommandAction), SearchFiles(String), FileSearchResults(Vec<String>). App::dispatch routes (a) SlashCommandSelected{Help} → push HelpDialog onto compositor, {Clear} → reset scrollback + clear MultiLineInput, {Quit} → set should_quit, others → push '[notice] ...' line via navigator.agent.push_line; (b) SearchFiles(prefix) → spawn tokio task calling backend.search_files(prefix, 20) and emitting FileSearchResults; (c) FileSearchResults(matches) → forward into navigator.agent.set_file_search_results(matches). The SlashCommandAction enum is owned by views::agent::slash_commands and re-exported into the components/mod.rs Action enum.

RPC-020.description: Port the slash command palette (src/tui/components/SlashCommandPalette.tsx, 172 lines) and @file search popup (src/tui/components/FileSearchPopup.tsx, 170 lines). Triggered when input starts with / or contains @<filter>. Renders as a floating Compositor overlay above the input. Requires new RPC method search_files(prefix, limit) backed by codelet_core::file_search::search. This card delivers the PALETTE UX + handlers for /help, /clear, /quit only; richer handlers (/model /thinking /role land in RPC-022; /resume /search land in RPC-021). See spec/attachments/RPC-020/typescript-reference.md.

examples.text: User types '/' on an empty AgentView input → SlashCommandPopup appears centred above the input, showing all SLASH_COMMANDS with /help highlighted as the first match (no filter yet).
User types 'h' after '/' → popup filter is 'h', list filters to '/help' first (prefix match) then '/thinking' (substring match in description).
Slash palette is open; user presses Down twice then Enter on '/quit' → AgentView emits Action::Quit and the App exits cleanly.
Slash palette is open with /clear highlighted; user presses Enter → AgentView's scrollback is cleared (chunk_count returns 0) and the input box is empty.
Slash palette is open; user presses Enter on '/help' → HelpDialog modal appears at Priority::Critical above everything; ESC returns to the prior empty AgentView state.
Slash palette is open; user presses Enter on '/model' → a scrollback notice line appears reading '[notice] Not yet implemented (see RPC-022)' and the palette closes; the AgentView remains usable.
User types '/' then Esc → palette dismisses, input still contains '/'; user can keep typing or delete it.

User types 'hello @rea' → file search popup opens at the '@' anchor, shows 'README.md' (and others) sorted by mtime; arrow keys move selection; Enter on 'README.md' replaces '@rea' with '@README.md ' so the input reads 'hello @README.md ' with cursor at the end.
User types '@' then types a space → file search popup auto-dismisses (the space ends the file-reference token) and the input is unchanged ('@ ').

FspecBackend::search_files("README", 10) against a workspace where the project root is the codelet/ fixture returns at most 10 paths and includes 'README.md' as the first entry; identical lists are returned from both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend wrapping the same SharedFspecService.
User types '/' on an empty AgentView input, presses Down, then Tab → input fills with '/clear' (no execute), popup closes; user can edit further or press Enter to send '/clear' as ordinary text.
AgentView scrollback has 5 chunks of conversation; user types '/clear' then Enter from palette → scrollback is empty afterward and the input box is reset to empty.
User opens the slash command palette by typing '/' on an empty input; the palette renders all SLASH_COMMANDS entries; the only provider-related row is /provider — no /providers row anywhere
User types 'prov' after '/'; the palette filter matches exactly one entry (/provider) — the bogus /providers entry is no longer in the registry to match

questions.answer: Owned by AgentView as Option<SlashCommandPopup> and Option<FileSearchPopup> fields. Rationale: (a) tight coupling with MultiLineInput state for filter sync, (b) no need to add a Compositor accessor for borrowing layers by id, (c) matches the existing `pub scrollback: ScrollbackList` direct-ownership pattern. AgentView paints the popup on top of its own area (centered tui-popup) AFTER painting its base widgets. Critical-priority dialogs (HelpDialog/DisconnectDialog) still live on the Compositor at Priority::Critical and overlay everything including these popups, because Compositor renders AFTER AgentView in App::render's order.
questions.text: Slash command popup is open while user is in AgentView. The popup intercepts ↑/↓/Enter/Tab/Esc; pressing 'q' or Ctrl+C while the popup is on top is NOT routed as Quit/Interrupt — it propagates to AgentView's MultiLineInput which treats them as plain typed characters (so 'q' fills into the input).

questions.answer: AgentView owns the popups, so filter sync happens via direct mutator calls inside AgentView::sync_popups() after each MultiLineInput event. No new Action variant for filter changes is required — the popup's `filter` field is presentation state co-owned with the input buffer.
questions.text: How should the popup keep its filter in sync with MultiLineInput's buffer? Two options: (a) the popup snapshots filter text on each render by reading from a shared store, OR (b) AgentView re-emits Action::SlashFilterChanged(filter) / FileSearchFilterChanged(filter) after every keystroke that touches the input.

questions.answer: AgentView-owned (Option<SlashCommandPopup>, Option<FileSearchPopup>) — captured in rule [13].
questions.text: Are the slash + file popups owned by AgentView (as Option<...> fields) or pushed onto the Compositor as separate Components? Affects how filter-sync, event consumption, and rendering layering work.

rules.text: Slash command registry mirrors the TS SLASH_COMMANDS list (model, provider, debug, clear, compact, thinking, resume, detach, search, blocklist, role, merge-worktree, schedule, loop) plus a few from the dossier (help, quit, isolation, providers) — filter_commands uses three-tier matching (prefix → name substring → description substring), matching the TS filterCommands() helper.

The slash popup intercepts ↑/↓ (navigate, with wrap-around), Enter (select+execute), Tab (fill into input WITHOUT execute), Esc (dismiss). Other keys propagate so the user can keep typing into the input to refine the filter.

The file search popup intercepts ↑/↓ (navigate, with wrap-around), Enter (select+insert path + trailing space + dismiss), Tab (insert path without trailing space + dismiss), Esc (dismiss). Other keys propagate.

Selecting a file via Enter replaces the substring `@<filter>` in the input with `@<path> ` (literal selected path plus a single trailing space); Tab inserts `@<path>` without the trailing space. The anchor_offset captured at OpenFileSearch is used to locate the `@` to splice over.

FspecBackend gains async fn search_files(prefix, limit) -> Result<Vec<String>>; the shared service delegates to a NEW helper `codelet_core::file_search::search(cwd, prefix, limit)` that wraps `ignore::WalkBuilder` + `globset::GlobBuilder` (case-insensitive, **/*<prefix>* pattern) and returns at most `limit` paths sorted by modification time desc, mirroring the existing codelet_tools::glob::GlobTool behaviour.

Implemented slash handlers in this card: /help → pushes HelpDialog onto compositor; /clear → reset AgentView scrollback + next_seq; /quit → emit Action::Quit. ALL other commands (/resume, /search, /model, /thinking, /role, /isolation, /blocklist, /compact, /debug, /providers, /detach, /merge-worktree, /schedule, /loop, /provider) emit a [notice] line into the scrollback: 'Not yet implemented (see RPC-NNN)' or 'Not yet implemented in Rust TUI' — they do NOT crash, they DO consume the dispatch.

File search RPC method is additive — both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend implement it, and a cross-transport-parity test scenario asserts both backends return identical results for the same prefix against the same shared service cwd.

File-size discipline (RPC-002 rule [10]) is preserved: every new file under codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/ and any new file added by this card stays under 300 LoC; if the agent module risks crossing 300 LoC, split into submodules instead of mutating the orchestrator.

Decision: while a slash/file popup is open AND a key matches its registered chord (↑↓/Enter/Tab/Esc), it consumes. For OTHER keys including 'q' and Ctrl+C, the popup returns Ignored so the chord drops through to AgentView's normal dispatch (which is the desired behaviour — user can keep typing characters into the filter). Only Esc/Enter/Tab/↑/↓ are consumed; all other keys propagate to MultiLineInput.handle_key so the input itself keeps recording filter characters AND ESC always closes the popup (not BackToBoard).

Owned by AgentView as Option<SlashCommandPopup> and Option<FileSearchPopup> fields. Rationale: (a) tight coupling with MultiLineInput state for filter sync, (b) no need to add a Compositor accessor for borrowing layers by id, (c) matches the existing `pub scrollback: ScrollbackList` direct-ownership pattern. AgentView paints the popup on top of its own area (centered tui-popup) AFTER painting its base widgets. Critical-priority dialogs (HelpDialog/DisconnectDialog) still live on the Compositor at Priority::Critical and overlay everything including these popups, because Compositor renders AFTER AgentView in App::render's order.

App::dispatch routes Action::SlashCommandSelected(action) by case: Help → push HelpDialog onto compositor; Clear → reset navigator.agent's scrollback + next_seq + clear input buffer; Quit → set should_quit=true; All other variants → navigator.agent.push_line(format!('[notice] /{} not yet implemented (see RPC-NNN or future card)', name)). File search RPC is triggered by Action::SearchFiles(prefix) — App::dispatch spawns a tokio task calling backend.search_files(prefix, 20) and dispatches Action::FileSearchResults(Vec<String>) on success.

Three new Action variants land in components/mod.rs: SlashCommandSelected(SlashCommandAction), SearchFiles(String), FileSearchResults(Vec<String>). The SlashCommandAction enum is re-exported from views::agent::slash_commands so the Action enum can reference it. ClearScrollback semantics are folded into SlashCommandSelected(Clear) — no separate variant.

ScrollbackList gains a `reset()` method that drops all chunks AND resets the scroll_state to default (offset=0, stick_to_bottom=true). Called from App::dispatch on SlashCommandSelected(Clear). AgentView gains a sibling `reset_scrollback()` helper that also resets next_seq to 0.

After each MultiLineInput event, AgentView::sync_popups() inspects the joined buffer to decide whether to open/close/refilter the popups: a leading '/' on the first line opens slash popup (uses text after '/' as filter); a '@' followed by zero-or-more non-space chars opens file popup at the last '@' anchor (text after '@' as filter). Buffer state '/' followed by space, or '@' followed by space, closes the respective popup. Empty buffer closes both. This is presentation-only state owned by AgentView — no Action dispatch is required for filter sync.

The slash command registry mirrors the TypeScript Ink reference 1:1: src/tui/utils/slashCommands.ts contains exactly one provider-related entry (name: 'provider'). The Rust SLASH_COMMANDS registry MUST NOT contain a SlashCommandAction::Providers variant or a { action: Providers, description: 'Open provider settings' } entry — no alias has ever existed in the reference frontend

RPC-020.title: Slash command palette + @file search popup in AgentView

userStory.action: trigger a slash-command palette by typing '/' on a new line and a @file search popup by typing '@' inside the AgentView's MultiLineInput, with /help, /clear, /quit handlers wired live
userStory.benefit: I can pick a slash command or file path from a floating overlay instead of typing the full text manually, matching the Ink TS AgentView UX

architectureNotes.text: Lift HistoryStore from codelet/napi/src/persistence/history.rs into codelet/core/src/persistence/history.rs. Public surface (HistoryStore, HistoryEntry, add/get/search) re-exported from codelet_core::persistence. The existing data dir resolution (codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs::ensure_directories + get_data_dir) is co-lifted so the core helpers own the on-disk JSONL path.

Three NEW RPC methods land on FspecService in codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs and on the FspecBackend trait in codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs: persistence_add_history(session, text), persistence_get_history(session, limit) -> Vec<String>, persistence_search_history(query) -> Vec<HistoryMatch>. Both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend implement them as one-line delegates. The service impl in FspecServiceImpl calls codelet_core::persistence::history::{add, get, search}.

ONE new shared type lands in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs: HistoryMatch { session_id: SessionId, text: String, timestamp_iso: String } gated on the napi feature. Mirrors persistence::HistoryEntry but with a serialised ISO-8601 timestamp string for transport portability.

AgentViewStore restructure: the current `current_session: Option<SessionId>` single-slot field is REPLACED by `open_sessions: Vec<SessionContext>` + `current_session_index: usize`. SessionContext bundles { id, work_unit_id, scrollback: ScrollbackList (lifted from AgentView), input_draft: String }. AgentViewStore also gains `history_state_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, HistoryNavState>` where HistoryNavState { recall_index: Option<usize>, cached_draft: Option<String>, snapshot: Vec<String> }.

Action enum gains new variants in codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs: HistorySnapshotLoaded(SessionId, Vec<String>), HistorySearchResults(Vec<HistoryMatch>), OpenResumePicker, OpenSearchPalette, AttachToSession(SessionId), InsertIntoInput(String). Existing HistoryPrev/HistoryNext/SessionPrev/SessionNext variants from RPC-019 finally get App::dispatch wiring.

Two new popup widgets land under codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/: resume_picker.rs (sorted-by-last-used session list, Enter selects, Esc dismisses) and search_palette.rs (typeahead over history backed by Action::SearchHistory dispatch). Both follow the SlashCommandPopup/FileSearchPopup pattern from RPC-020 — owned by AgentView as Option<...> fields, rendered as centred floating overlay after base widgets paint. Each file < 300 LoC.

Slash command handlers /resume and /search are wired in App::dispatch::handle_slash_command (the existing match for SlashCommandSelected). /resume opens the resume_picker, /search opens the search_palette. Both currently emit `[notice] not yet implemented` lines — these arms get replaced by real popup-open dispatches once the popups exist.

RPC-021.description: Port multi-session AgentView state (TS: src/tui/store/sessionStore.ts + src/tui/hooks/useSessionStreamManager.ts) — Shift+←/→ cycles between concurrent sessions preserving each session's scrollback/input/scroll-offset. Shift+↑/↓ recalls submitted-input history via three new RPC methods (persistence_get_history, persistence_add_history, persistence_search_history) delegating to codelet_core::persistence (same backend as existing NAPI persistence* exports — TS keeps using them unchanged). /resume + /search slash command handlers also land here. **LARGE — likely needs split into RPC-021a (multi-session + cycling), 021b (history + recall), 021c (/resume + /search popups) during specifying.** See spec/attachments/RPC-021/typescript-reference.md.

rules.text: Parent epic decomposes into three child slices: RPC-021a (multi-session state + Shift+←/→ cycling, no history), RPC-021b (Shift+↑/↓ history recall + persistence_get/add/search_history RPC methods + HistoryStore lift to codelet_core), RPC-021c (/resume session picker + /search history search popups consuming 021a + 021b)

The HistoryStore module currently in codelet/napi/src/persistence/history.rs (and the helpers add_history_entry / get_history / search_history in codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs) is LIFTED into codelet/core/src/persistence/history.rs so codelet_rpc can delegate without re-introducing a rpc → napi dep. The existing #[napi] exports persistence_add_history / persistence_get_history / persistence_search_history become one-line delegates to the core helpers — their JS surface stays unchanged.

The slash command palette routes /model → push ModelSelectorDialog, /thinking → push ThinkingLevelDialog, /role <text> → emit Action::SetSessionRole(sid, Some(text)), /role clear → emit Action::SetSessionRole(sid, None). Every new code file (model_selector_dialog.rs, thinking_level_dialog.rs, role_banner.rs, plus the new dispatch helper file) is kept under 300 LoC; if any file approaches 300 LoC during implementation, split it into a sibling helper file (mirroring how dispatch_rpc020.rs / dispatch_rpc024.rs / dispatch_rpc026.rs were extracted from app/dispatch.rs)

RPC-023.description:
Port the TypeScript SGR-1006 mouse subsystem to the Rust ratatui frontend. Crossterm already delivers Event::Mouse via EnableMouseCapture (codelet/fspec-tui/src/terminal.rs lines 18-23, 66-76), but no component currently consumes those events — App::handle_event matches only Event::Key, so wheel scroll, click-to-focus, and native text-selection toggling are all no-ops.

Reference TypeScript implementation:
- src/tui/utils/mouseProtocol.ts (SGR_BUTTON constants, parseSgrMouse, MOUSE_ENABLE/DISABLE)
- src/tui/components/UnifiedBoardLayout.tsx lines 236-298 (per-column wheel scroll wired through onWorkUnitChange)
- src/tui/components/VirtualList.tsx lines 180-234, 504-572 (acceleration + TUI-078 native text-selection toggle)
- src/tui/components/BoardView.tsx lines 41, 118-126 (MOUSE_ENABLE on mount / MOUSE_DISABLE on unmount)
- src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx lines 197, 1388-1396, 4555-4573 (resume-mode wheel scroll)

The TypeScript implementation was low-level because Ink exposed mouse only as raw escape strings — crossterm gives us Event::Mouse(MouseEvent { kind, column, row, modifiers }) pre-parsed, so ~90% of mouseProtocol.ts evaporates. The Rust port follows ratatui best-practice as established across the RPC-002 research attachments (see spec/attachments/RPC-023/mouse-port-spec.md §'Prior research applied to this slice' for the full cross-reference table). Key decisions inherited: hit-testing is the app's job via last-rendered-Rect cells; TerminalGuard owns the global EnableMouseCapture lifecycle; Event::Key|Event::Mouse both fan through the Compositor; MouseTrackingToggle uses tokio timer + Action round-trip + Drop guard for TUI-078; rat-event/rat-salsa was rejected in favour of the existing custom Compositor.

RPC-016 already wired the per-column viewport math (BoardStore::move_selection / scroll_focused_column / select_first_in_focused / select_last_in_focused) and BoardView.last_viewport_height — this card only adds the mouse plumbing on top of that foundation.

This card's scope (post cross-reference review 2026-05-15) covers: BoardView wheel scroll (vertical → SelectPrev/Next, horizontal → FocusPrev/NextColumn), click-on-header → SetFocusedColumn, click-on-row → focus column + select row under cursor, the foundational rect_contains hit-test helper, the MouseTrackingToggle scaffolding (with W: Write + Send injection for testable escape-byte assertions), and source-shape invariants pinning dialog components to Event::Key-only. VirtualList wheel acceleration + TUI-078 wiring on the AgentView scrollback land in RPC-019; tui-popup drag-to-move lands in RPC-022.

Full port plan + crossterm/ratatui code examples + hit-test design + test plan + the 9 red-card items derived from the cross-reference review live in the attached spec/attachments/RPC-023/mouse-port-spec.md. See also spec/attachments/RPC-002/10-multilineinput-and-mouse-port-spec.md Part B for the original RPC-002 mouse-subsystem direction (this card supersedes that section's TODO into a concrete slice).

examples.text: BACKLOG has 20 units, viewport_height=10, focused column BACKLOG, selected_index=0; wheel-down inside content area emits Action::SelectNext and BoardStore.selected_index_for("backlog") becomes 1
Wheel-down at index=19 (last unit) with focused BACKLOG wraps the selection back to index 0 via RPC-016 move_selection
Wheel-up at row 0 (top border row) outside the content area returns Ignored, no Action is emitted
Wheel-right inside the BACKLOG content area emits Action::FocusNextColumn so the focus jumps to SPECIFYING
Wheel-left inside the IMPLEMENTING content area emits Action::FocusPrevColumn so the focus jumps to TESTING
Left-click on the SPECIFYING column header (focused column was BACKLOG) emits Action::SetFocusedColumn(1) and the focused column flips to SPECIFYING
Left-click on the third visible row (offset=0) of the DONE column emits Action::SetFocusedColumn(5) AND Action::SelectIndexInFocused(2)
Left-click on visible row 1 of a column whose scroll_offset is 5 emits SelectIndexInFocused(6) — the offset is added to the row index
MouseTrackingToggle::temporarily_disable with a Vec<u8> writer writes exactly the bytes "\x1b[?1006l\x1b[?1000l" (the crossterm DisableMouseCapture sequence) and sets disabled=true
MouseTrackingToggle::re_enable while disabled writes the EnableMouseCapture escape bytes and sets disabled=false; calling it again while already enabled is a no-op (no further bytes written)
MouseTrackingToggle::Drop with disabled=true writes the EnableMouseCapture escape bytes during Drop so the terminal isn't left in a broken state
Repeated temporarily_disable calls restart the debounce timer; only one Action::ReEnableMouseTracking is emitted after the FINAL 5-second window elapses
rect_contains: a Rect{x=5,y=5,w=10,h=10} returns true for (5,5), (14,14); false for (15,14), (14,15), (4,5)
An Event::Mouse(ScrollDown) sent into a running App via the action bus reaches BoardView::handle_event instead of being silently dropped by the run loop

rules.text: Wheel-up / wheel-down inside the column-content area scroll the FOCUSED column only — they delegate to Action::SelectPrev/SelectNext, inheriting RPC-016 wrap-around + auto-scroll
Wheel events outside the column-content area (e.g. on a header or border row) are Ignored — no Action emitted, dispatch propagates
Horizontal wheel (ScrollLeft / ScrollRight) inside the column-content area emits Action::FocusPrevColumn / Action::FocusNextColumn
Left-click on a column header emits Action::SetFocusedColumn(idx) for that column
Left-click on a content row emits Action::SetFocusedColumn(idx) AND Action::SelectIndexInFocused(row_under_cursor), accounting for scroll_offset
The App run loop forwards Event::Mouse(_) through App::handle_event → Compositor → Navigator instead of dropping it
rect_contains(rect, x, y) is half-open on the right/bottom edges, matching ratatui's Rect::intersects convention
MouseTrackingToggle is generic over W: Write + Send so tests can inject a Vec<u8> and assert the exact DisableMouseCapture / EnableMouseCapture escape bytes were written
MouseTrackingToggle::temporarily_disable writes DisableMouseCapture immediately and schedules a 5-second re-enable timer that fires Action::ReEnableMouseTracking(owner)
MouseTrackingToggle::re_enable cancels the pending timer and writes EnableMouseCapture immediately so the wheel works on the very next event
MouseTrackingToggle::Drop re-enables (writes EnableMouseCapture) if still disabled, restoring terminal state on panic/exit
Source-shape: no raw SGR mouse escape strings (\x1b[?1000h, \x1b[?1006h, \x1b[?1000l, \x1b[?1006l) appear anywhere in codelet/fspec-tui/src — crossterm owns the protocol
Source-shape: EnableMouseCapture / DisableMouseCapture appear only in src/terminal.rs and src/mouse/toggle.rs
Source-shape: Dialog-priority components (DisconnectDialog, HelpDialog) match Event::Key exclusively (no Event::Mouse arms)
Source-shape: src/mouse/*.rs files plus modifications to views/board.rs stay under 300 LoC each

architectureNotes.text: SessionContext struct lives in a new module `codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/session_context.rs` so agent_view.rs stays under 300 LoC. AgentViewStore re-exports SessionContext. The TokenState type stays in agent_view.rs.

AgentView shrinks: the per-AgentView `scrollback: ScrollbackList` and `next_seq: u64` fields move into SessionContext. AgentView now reaches into `store.current_session_context_mut()` for mutation (record_chunk, push_line, reset_scrollback) and `store.current_session_context()` for read (render_with_store, chunk_count, cursor_position). When there is no current session context, render paints an empty scrollback block and chunk_count returns 0.

App::dispatch on Action::SessionPrev/SessionNext: (1) snapshot current MultiLineInput.value() into AgentViewStore.open_sessions[current_session_index].input_draft, (2) call agent_view_store.cycle_session(±1), (3) load MultiLineInput.value() from the NEW open_sessions[current_session_index].input_draft, (4) emit Action::Redraw (already implicit via should_render = true). No backend RPC call required for RPC-024.

Action::ChunkReceived(id, chunk) routing: lookup the SessionContext whose id == id in open_sessions; if found, call ctx.record_chunk(chunk) (which appends to ctx.scrollback and increments ctx.scrollback_next_seq); also call agent_view_store.apply_chunk_to_token_state(id, chunk) (unchanged from RPC-018). If no SessionContext matches the id (race with session destruction), drop the chunk silently.

AgentViewStore.session_index() becomes a derived computation: `(current_session_index + 1, open_sessions.len())` when open_sessions is non-empty, else `(0, 0)`. The setter `set_session_index` from RPC-018 is REMOVED — it's no longer reachable. SessionHeader continues to read via `store.session_index()` unchanged.

RPC-024.description: First child slice of RPC-021. Adds multi-session support to AgentViewStore so the Rust TUI can hold N concurrent open sessions, cycle between them with Shift+←/→ (already emitted as Action::SessionPrev/SessionNext by RPC-019's MultiLineInput), and preserve each session's scrollback + input_draft + scroll offset when switching. No history (RPC-021b), no /resume picker (RPC-021c). Pure client-side refactor at the AgentViewStore / AgentView / App::dispatch layer — no new RPC methods, no new shared types, no NAPI changes. See parent RPC-021 architecture notes and spec/attachments/RPC-021/typescript-reference.md sections "Multi-session state" and "Session cycling".

examples.text: An empty AgentViewStore (no sessions) has open_sessions.is_empty() == true; session_index() returns (0, 0); current_session() returns None; cycle_session(±1) is a no-op (does not panic, does not change current_session_index).

App dispatches Action::SessionCreated(SessionId("s-1")); AgentViewStore.open_sessions now has length 1 with id == "s-1"; current_session_index == 0; session_index() returns (1, 1); current_session() returns Some("s-1").

After dispatching Action::SessionCreated(s-1) then SessionCreated(s-2) then SessionCreated(s-3), open_sessions has length 3 in creation order [s-1, s-2, s-3]; current_session_index == 2; session_index() returns (3, 3); current_session() returns Some("s-3").

Given open_sessions == [s-1, s-2, s-3] and current_session_index == 2: App dispatches Action::SessionPrev; current_session_index becomes 1; session_index() returns (2, 3); current_session() returns Some("s-2").

Given open_sessions == [s-1, s-2, s-3] and current_session_index == 0: App dispatches Action::SessionPrev; current_session_index wraps to 2; current_session() returns Some("s-3"). Dispatching Action::SessionNext afterwards wraps back to 0.
Given open_sessions has only s-1: dispatching Action::SessionPrev OR Action::SessionNext leaves current_session_index unchanged at 0 (single-session wrap is a self-loop, not a state change).

Given two sessions s-1 and s-2 (current = s-2) and the user has typed "hello world" into MultiLineInput, then presses Shift+←: open_sessions[1].input_draft == "hello world" (saved); MultiLineInput.value() == open_sessions[0].input_draft (restored, defaults to empty string on first switch). Pressing Shift+→ restores "hello world" into the MultiLineInput.

Given two sessions s-1 (with 3 chunks in its scrollback) and s-2 (with 5 chunks): switching from s-2 → s-1 via Shift+← causes the AgentView render to paint s-1's 3 chunks; switching back to s-2 paints s-2's 5 chunks. Neither scrollback is dropped or reset.

Given current = s-1 and the user is on s-1, a StreamChunk::Text arrives for s-2 (background) via Action::ChunkReceived("s-2", ...): open_sessions[idx_of_s_2].scrollback has one more entry afterwards; current_session_index stays at 0 (current still s-1); the user sees nothing change on screen; switching to s-2 reveals the new chunk in its scrollback.

Source-shape regression: `codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view.rs` stays under 300 LoC after the restructure; the new `codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/session_context.rs` (or similar split) stays under 300 LoC; no view file imports codelet_core / napi / tarpc / tokio_tungstenite.

rules.text: AgentViewStore replaces its single `current_session: Option<SessionId>` field with `open_sessions: Vec<SessionContext>` plus `current_session_index: usize`. `SessionContext { id: SessionId, work_unit_id: Option<String>, scrollback: ScrollbackList, scrollback_next_seq: u64, input_draft: String }`. The existing `current_session()` accessor remains and returns `open_sessions.get(current_session_index).map(|c| &c.id)` so call sites stay compatible.

Action::SessionCreated(session) appends a fresh SessionContext to open_sessions and sets current_session_index to the index of the newly-appended entry, so successive create_session calls accumulate (not overwrite) and `#N` increments naturally.

App::dispatch wires Action::SessionPrev / Action::SessionNext (already emitted by RPC-019's MultiLineInput on Shift+←/→) to mutate AgentViewStore.current_session_index with wrap-around: prev=(idx-1).rem_euclid(len), next=(idx+1).rem_euclid(len). No-op when open_sessions is empty or has length 1.

On every session switch, BEFORE mutating current_session_index, App::dispatch snapshots the current MultiLineInput buffer into the outgoing SessionContext.input_draft via `agent_view_store.set_input_draft(idx, view.input.value())`. AFTER mutating, the incoming session's saved draft is restored into the MultiLineInput via `view.input.set_value(&store.open_sessions[new_idx].input_draft)`.

ScrollbackList ownership moves from `AgentView.scrollback` to `SessionContext.scrollback`; `AgentView.next_seq` moves to `SessionContext.scrollback_next_seq`. AgentView's `record_chunk`, `push_line`, `chunk_count`, `reset_scrollback`, and `render_with_store` now operate on the SessionContext returned by `store.current_session_context_mut()` / `store.current_session_context()`. Empty open_sessions render an EMPTY scrollback box (no panic).

Action::ChunkReceived(id, chunk) routes the chunk into open_sessions[k] where k is the index of the SessionContext whose id == `id`, NOT necessarily current_session_index — background sessions keep accumulating scrollback in their own context. The existing `apply_chunk_to_token_state(id, chunk)` per-session HashMap update from RPC-018 already does the right thing; only the scrollback target needs the lookup.

The SessionHeader's `#N: <model>` derives from AgentViewStore.session_index() which is now computed as `(current_session_index + 1, open_sessions.len())` — the explicit setter `set_session_index(current, total)` from RPC-018 is REMOVED and the getter returns the derived pair. Empty open_sessions returns `(0, 0)` (placeholder mode).

Source-shape discipline: AgentViewStore stays under 300 LoC by splitting the new types into a sibling module `codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/session_context.rs`. The existing agent_view.rs continues to expose AgentViewStore + TokenState; the new file owns SessionContext (kept under 300 LoC).
