architectureNotes.text: Lifting: codelet_core::persistence re-exports HistoryStore, HistoryEntry, add(entry), get(project, limit), search(query, project) — all the public surface the NAPI bindings rely on. The existing codelet/napi/src/persistence/{history.rs, types.rs::HistoryEntry, mod.rs::add_history_entry/get_history/search_history} either become thin pub use re-exports of the core types or one-line delegate functions. No NAPI test changes; no TS test changes.

Shared type translation: codelet_core::persistence::history::HistoryEntry → codelet_rpc_types::HistoryMatch is a deliberate conversion at the FspecService boundary so HistoryEntry's chrono::DateTime<Utc> doesn't bleed into rpc-types (which is `no_std`-ish and gates `napi` features). The conversion `HistoryEntry::to_history_match()` formats the timestamp via `entry.timestamp.to_rfc3339()` and reuses `display` as `text`. `session_id` maps from Uuid to SessionId.

FspecServiceImpl in codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs delegates to codelet_core::persistence::history::{add, get, search} using the workspace's cwd as the project filter (the codelet_common::get_data_dir is global, but the `project` argument of HistoryStore::get/search filters per-cwd so each project's history is isolated). The shared service's existing `workspace_cwd: Option<PathBuf>` field provides the project path; if None, history is returned across all projects (same as passing None to HistoryStore::get).

AgentView side-effects: in App::dispatch's HistoryPrev arm, snapshot loading is synchronous via `backend.persistence_get_history(session, 100).await` from inside an async dispatch (the existing dispatch_rpc024.rs pattern already awaits backend calls — same shape here). After the snapshot is loaded into `cached_history_snapshot[session]`, subsequent HistoryPrev/Next presses re-use the cached snapshot without round-tripping; the cache is invalidated when the session is destroyed or when a new input is submitted (which resets recall_index + clears the cached snapshot for that session).

Fire-and-forget persistence_add_history: handle_input_submitted clones the backend Arc and `tokio::spawn(async move { let _ = backend.persistence_add_history(session, text).await; })` so a slow disk write never blocks input submission. The await on the spawned task is dropped — the test for persistence wait uses a oneshot channel injected only in tests to deterministically observe completion (the production path remains pure fire-and-forget).

Calling set_data_directory inside build_service is safe across all fspec binary modes: combined::run (TUI+server in one process) and daemon::run (headless server) both call build_service exactly once. client::run does NOT call build_service (it only constructs a WebSocketFspecBackend to a remote daemon), so client mode correctly inherits the daemon's data directory through tarpc round-trips.

RPC-025.description: Second child slice of RPC-021. Wires Shift+↑/↓ (Action::HistoryPrev/HistoryNext from RPC-019) through App::dispatch to walk per-session command history; submitting an input fires-and-forgets persistence_add_history(session, text). Three new FspecService RPC methods land: persistence_add_history, persistence_get_history(session, limit) -> Vec<String>, persistence_search_history(query) -> Vec<HistoryMatch>. ONE new shared type HistoryMatch lands in codelet/rpc-types. The HistoryStore module is LIFTED from codelet/napi/src/persistence/history.rs into codelet/core/src/persistence/history.rs; the existing #[napi] persistence_add/get/search_history exports become one-line delegates so the TS surface stays byte-identical. Both FspecBackend transports implement the three methods; cross-transport-parity tests cover both. Depends on RPC-021a for the per-session history-state map.

examples.text: codelet_core::persistence::history::add(entry) writes a JSONL line to codelet_common::get_data_dir().join("history.jsonl") and also inserts the entry at index 0 of the in-memory cache; codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs::add_history_entry(entry) is now a one-line delegate `codelet_core::persistence::history::add(entry)`; calling it from a Rust test reads back the entry via codelet_core::persistence::history::get(None, Some(1))[0].

FspecServiceImpl.persistence_add_history(session=Uuid("s-1"), text="hello") inserts a HistoryEntry { display: "hello", session_id: Uuid("s-1"), project: workspace_cwd, timestamp: now } into the lifted core store. A subsequent FspecServiceImpl.persistence_get_history(session=Uuid("s-1"), limit=10) returns Vec<String> == ["hello"].

FspecServiceImpl.persistence_search_history(query="foo") with history entries ["foobar", "baz", "FOOZ"] returns Vec<HistoryMatch> with text values ["foobar", "FOOZ"] in newest-first order; each HistoryMatch has session_id == the matching entry's session_id (Uuid stringified into SessionId) and timestamp_iso == entry.timestamp.to_rfc3339().

EmbeddedFspecBackend wraps codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs::FspecServiceImpl and `persistence_add_history` is a one-line delegate `self.service.persistence_add_history(ctx, session, text).await`. WebSocketFspecBackend's persistence_add_history routes through the same tarpc method over the WS transport. A cross-transport-parity test that calls both backends with `session=s-1, text="x"` then `persistence_get_history(s-1, 10)` returns `["x"]` for BOTH transports.

Given an AgentViewStore with open_sessions[0].id == s-1, history_state_by_session is empty, cached_history_snapshot is empty, and persistence_get_history(s-1, 100) returns ["third", "second", "first"]: When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryPrev for session s-1 with MultiLineInput == "live draft": Then history_state_by_session[s-1] == HistoryNavState { recall_index: Some(0), cached_draft: Some("live draft") }; cached_history_snapshot[s-1] == ["third", "second", "first"]; MultiLineInput.value() == "third".

Given history_state_by_session[s-1] == HistoryNavState { recall_index: Some(0), cached_draft: Some("live") } and cached_history_snapshot[s-1] == ["a", "b", "c"]: When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryPrev again: Then recall_index == Some(1); MultiLineInput.value() == "b". When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryPrev a third time: Then recall_index == Some(2); MultiLineInput.value() == "c". When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryPrev a fourth time (clamp at len-1): Then recall_index stays at Some(2); MultiLineInput.value() == "c".

Given history_state_by_session[s-1] == HistoryNavState { recall_index: Some(2), cached_draft: Some("live") } and cached_history_snapshot[s-1] == ["a", "b", "c"]: When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryNext: Then recall_index == Some(1); MultiLineInput.value() == "b". When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryNext: Then recall_index == Some(0); MultiLineInput.value() == "a". When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryNext (exit recall): Then recall_index == None; MultiLineInput.value() == "live" (restored cached_draft).

Given history_state_by_session[s-1].recall_index is None (live draft mode): When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryNext: Then it is a no-op — recall_index stays None and MultiLineInput is unchanged.

Given persistence_get_history(s-1, 100) returns an empty Vec []: When App::dispatch handles Action::HistoryPrev: Then history_state_by_session[s-1] stays at recall_index=None; cached_draft is not stored; MultiLineInput is unchanged (no-op when history is empty).

Given two open sessions s-1 and s-2 where s-1's history is ["a", "b"] and s-2's history is ["x", "y", "z"]: When the user is on s-1, presses Shift+↑ once (recall_index=Some(0), MultiLineInput="a"), then presses Shift+→ to switch to s-2 (RPC-024 cycling), then presses Shift+↑: Then history_state_by_session[s-1].recall_index stays Some(0); history_state_by_session[s-2].recall_index becomes Some(0); MultiLineInput.value() == "x". When the user presses Shift+← back to s-1: Then history_state_by_session[s-1].recall_index is still Some(0) (independent per-session); MultiLineInput.value() restores from RPC-024's input_draft (NOT from history) because the cycle_session path saves/restores `open_sessions[idx].input_draft` — the HistoryNavState's recall_index is preserved only so a subsequent Shift+↑ keeps walking from where it left off.

When App::dispatch handles Action::InputSubmitted("hello") for session s-1: Then backend.send_input(s-1, "hello") is invoked AND backend.persistence_add_history(s-1, "hello") is invoked via tokio::spawn (fire-and-forget); history_state_by_session[s-1] is reset to HistoryNavState { recall_index: None, cached_draft: None }; cached_history_snapshot[s-1] is cleared. Subsequent Action::HistoryPrev re-loads a fresh snapshot from persistence_get_history.

Source-shape regression: codelet/core/src/persistence/mod.rs is a new file under 100 LoC; codelet/core/src/persistence/history.rs after the lift is under 300 LoC; codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view.rs stays under 300 LoC after the new history_state_by_session and cached_history_snapshot fields are added; codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/history_state.rs is a new file under 100 LoC; no view file imports codelet_core / napi / tarpc / tokio_tungstenite.

Given the fspec combined binary has just bootstrapped against workspace W: When the user presses Shift+Up in the agent input field: Then dispatch_rpc025::handle_history_prev calls backend.persistence_get_history(session, 100), the EmbeddedFspecBackend delegates to FspecServiceImpl::persistence_get_history, codelet_core::persistence::history::get is called, codelet_common::get_data_dir() returns Ok(~/.fspec), HistoryStore::new() opens ~/.fspec/history.jsonl, the existing 11,171 entries are read back, and MultiLineInput.value() is replaced with the most-recent entry — NOT silently no-oped.

Source-shape regression: codelet/fspec/src/common.rs::build_service contains the literal call sequence `codelet_common::set_data_directory(home_fspec_dir()?)?` BEFORE the WorkUnitsWatcher::new call (mirrors codelet/cli/src/main.rs:15). A grep across codelet/fspec/src/ for 'set_data_directory' returns AT LEAST ONE hit. A unit test in codelet/fspec/src/common.rs::tests calls build_service against a tempdir, then asserts codelet_common::get_data_dir() returns Ok(~/.fspec) — proving the global mutex was set as a side-effect.

Production-binary smoke test: codelet/fspec/tests/combined_smoke.rs (or a new tests/persistence_bootstrap_rpc025.rs) spawns the real `fspec` binary against a tempdir HOME, sends a tarpc persistence_add_history call over the WS server, then a persistence_get_history call, and asserts the round-tripped Vec<String> is non-empty — exercising the actual binary bootstrap path that the unit tests miss.

rules.text: HistoryStore is LIFTED from codelet/napi/src/persistence/history.rs into codelet/core/src/persistence/history.rs along with HistoryEntry; codelet_core::persistence re-exports HistoryStore, HistoryEntry, and helpers add(entry), get(project, limit), search(query, project). The on-disk path is codelet_common::get_data_dir().join("history.jsonl") — the same JSONL file the existing NAPI HistoryStore already read/wrote.

The existing #[napi] exports persistence_add_history / persistence_get_history / persistence_search_history in codelet/napi/src/persistence/napi_bindings.rs and the helpers add_history_entry / get_history / search_history in codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs become one-line delegates to codelet_core::persistence::history. Their JS-facing signatures and behaviour stay byte-identical so all existing TypeScript callers keep working without changes.

Three NEW RPC methods land on FspecService in codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs and on the FspecBackend trait in codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs: `persistence_add_history(session: SessionId, text: String) -> Result<()>`, `persistence_get_history(session: SessionId, limit: u32) -> Result<Vec<String>>`, `persistence_search_history(query: String) -> Result<Vec<HistoryMatch>>`. EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend each implement them as one-line delegates over their respective transports.

ONE new shared type `HistoryMatch { session_id: SessionId, text: String, timestamp_iso: String }` lands in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs, gated on the existing `napi` feature alongside other shared types. timestamp_iso is the RFC3339/ISO-8601 string of the HistoryEntry.timestamp DateTime<Utc> — chosen for transport portability so non-Rust consumers don't need a chrono dep.

AgentViewStore gains `history_state_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, HistoryNavState>` plus a per-session `cached_history_snapshot: HashMap<SessionId, Vec<String>>`. HistoryNavState { recall_index: Option<usize>, cached_draft: Option<String> }: `recall_index = None` means the user is on the live input draft; `recall_index = Some(k)` means the user is on history entry k (0 = most recent). Switching sessions via cycle_session does NOT clear this map — each session keeps its independent recall position.

App::dispatch wires Action::HistoryPrev / Action::HistoryNext (already emitted by RPC-019's MultiLineInput on Shift+↑/↓). Sequence on HistoryPrev: (1) if `recall_index.is_none()`, cache the MultiLineInput.value() into `cached_draft` and snapshot history via persistence_get_history; (2) set `recall_index = Some(min(prev+1 or 0, history.len()-1))`; (3) replace MultiLineInput.value() with history[recall_index]. Sequence on HistoryNext: (1) if `recall_index.is_none()`, no-op; (2) else if `recall_index == Some(0)`, set `recall_index = None` and restore cached_draft into MultiLineInput; (3) else decrement recall_index and replace MultiLineInput.value() with history[recall_index].

App::dispatch::handle_input_submitted (or the dispatch arm that consumes Action::InputSubmitted) fires-and-forgets `backend.persistence_add_history(session, text)` after the existing backend.send_input call, BEFORE any await on the send_input result. The history is appended even if send_input later errors. After submission, the session's HistoryNavState is reset (recall_index=None, cached_draft=None) so the next Shift+↑ starts a fresh snapshot.

Source-shape discipline: every new file stays under 300 LoC; codelet_core/persistence/mod.rs and history.rs are new files; AgentViewStore's new state is added by SPLITTING a new sibling module codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/history_state.rs (HistoryNavState lives there) so agent_view.rs stays under 300 LoC; no view file imports codelet_core / napi / tarpc / tokio_tungstenite; the existing source_shape_*.rs scans still pass.

All RPC-002 invariants are preserved: every store mutation happens inside App::dispatch on the App task (no Mutex/RwLock/atomics on store types); only `tokio::spawn` (never Runtime::new) — the fire-and-forget persistence_add_history is `tokio::spawn(async move { let _ = backend.persistence_add_history(...).await; })`; loopback-only WS bind; codelet-napi is NOT a dep of codelet-fspec-tui; every new behaviour is exercised against BOTH EmbeddedFspecBackend AND WebSocketFspecBackend via cross-transport-parity tests.

The fspec binary MUST call codelet_common::set_data_directory(home_fspec_dir()) before any FspecService method that touches persistence can be invoked, so persistence_add_history / persistence_get_history / persistence_search_history reach the on-disk JSONL store instead of returning Err("Data directory not initialized").

set_data_directory must be invoked from common::build_service (or earlier in combined::run / daemon::run) so BOTH combined mode AND daemon mode initialize the global data directory before the WS server starts accepting persistence_*_history calls. Client mode does NOT need it because the remote daemon owns the FspecServiceImpl.

RPC-025.title: Shift+↑/↓ history recall + persistence_*_history RPCs (RPC-021b)

userStory.action: press Shift+↑/↓ to walk submitted-input history per session and have submitted inputs auto-persisted
userStory.benefit: I can recall earlier prompts without retyping, with the same JSONL store the TypeScript Ink TUI already uses
userStory.role: developer using the Rust ratatui TUI

architectureNotes.text: RPC-021c depends on RPC-024 (multi-session AgentViewStore — gives us open_sessions / append_session / cycle_session / session_index) and RPC-025 (persistence_search_history RPC method + HistoryMatch type). RPC-026 does NOT introduce new RPC methods or new shared types — only consumes them.

Render shape: ResumeSessionView::render(area, buf, store) and SearchHistoryView::render(area, buf, store) take the FULL area Rect. Their first statement is `Clear.render(area, buf)` so the underlying AgentView pixels are fully overwritten. They then split `area` vertically with Layout::default().constraints([Length(1), Length(1), Min(0), Length(1)]) for title row, separator, scrollable list, and footer hint — mirroring TS AgentView.tsx:5053-5191. Pattern reference inside this repo: see existing full-screen views like BoardView (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board.rs) — they paint directly into the supplied Rect, NOT into a sub-rect.

Mode-view ownership stays on AgentView (NOT Navigator) because: (a) they only make sense inside Agent mode (Navigator already ensures that); (b) they consume the SAME action_tx and backend the AgentView wires to its input; (c) the AgentView's existing input/popup state must survive the mode view (Esc returns to AgentView with input intact). The render gate is a simple `if let Some(v) = self.resume_view { v.render(area, buf, store); return; }` early-return at the TOP of AgentView::render_with_store, BEFORE the layout split.

Scroll machinery: both mode views compute `visible_rows = area.height.saturating_sub(chrome_rows)` where chrome_rows accounts for title + separator + footer (3 rows). Selection movement updates both selected_index AND scroll_offset using the standard formula: if selected_index < scroll_offset → scroll_offset = selected_index; if selected_index >= scroll_offset + visible_rows → scroll_offset = selected_index - visible_rows + 1. This mirrors the TS resume mode at AgentView.tsx:1347 (`resumeVisibleHeight = max(1, terminalHeight - 5)`).

ConfirmDialog: implemented as a centred floating overlay (this widget IS conceptually a popup — distinct from the mode views). It MAY use tui_popup or a manual centred Block. Layout: Block::default().borders(Borders::ALL).title(title) sized roughly width=max(40, body_width+4) × height=4-6 rows; bottom row hosts up to 3 inline button labels separated by `│`. Focus traversal uses Left/Right keys; Enter activates the focused button; Esc returns Cancel. The dialog does NOT own any backend state — it's a pure widget whose Outcome the resume_view (its parent) maps to Action::ConfirmDeleteSession or no-op.

Lifting delete_session: codelet/core/src/persistence/sessions.rs is a new file < 100 LoC that imports the SAME `~/.fspec/sessions.jsonl` reader/writer logic the existing NAPI module uses. It re-exports `delete_session(uuid)`, `list_sessions()` (for the FspecServiceImpl::list_sessions to also use), and any helper needed. codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs::delete_session becomes a one-line delegate to codelet_core::persistence::sessions::delete_session — preserving the byte-identical TS surface. NO #[napi] export signatures change.

Ctrl+R routing: views/agent/dispatch.rs::handle_event is amended with a guard `if event_is_ctrl_r(event) && self.search_view.is_none() && self.resume_view.is_none() && self.slash_popup.is_none() && self.file_popup.is_none() { return EventResult::Action(Action::OpenSearchView); }` placed BEFORE the existing slash_popup / file_popup routing. The chord is detected by both crossterm's parsed key (KeyModifiers::CONTROL + KeyCode::Char('r')) AND, for terminals that send a raw byte (^R = 0x12), the equivalent literal byte sequence — mirroring the dual-detection pattern RPC-019 uses for Shift+arrow chords.

RPC-026.description: Third child slice of RPC-021. Replaces the `[notice] not yet implemented` arms in App::dispatch::handle_slash_command for SlashCommandAction::Resume and ::Search with real popup overlays: ResumePicker (sorted-by-last-used session list, Enter attaches via Action::AttachToSession, Esc dismisses) and SearchPalette (typeahead over history matches backed by persistence_search_history, Enter inserts the matched text into the input via Action::InsertIntoInput). Both popups follow the SlashCommandPopup/FileSearchPopup pattern from RPC-020 — owned by AgentView as Option<...> fields, rendered as centred floating overlay. Depends on RPC-021a (for multi-session state to attach into) and RPC-021b (for history search RPC).

examples.text: Given an empty AgentViewStore and a backend with 3 known sessions: When the user types `/resume` + Enter in the input: Then the slash_popup is dropped, AgentView.resume_view becomes Some(default), and a tokio task is spawned to fetch backend.list_sessions(). When that task completes: Then Action::SessionListLoaded([s1, s2, s3]) is dispatched and resume_view.sessions == [s1, s2, s3] with selected_index == 0.

Given resume_view is open with 3 sessions and AgentView.render_with_store is called with area = Rect { x: 0, y: 0, width: 120, height: 24 }: Then the buffer contains a row reading `Resume Session (3 available)` near the top, a Clear-painted opaque background covers the whole 120×24 area, and NO `Agent —` scrollback title row appears (early-return — AgentView's normal layout did not paint). The footer row reads `Enter Select | ↑↓ Navigate | D Delete | Esc Cancel`.

Given resume_view has 40 sessions and the terminal area height is 24 (so the visible list is ~20 rows once chrome is subtracted): When the user presses ↓ 20 times: Then selected_index == 20 AND scroll_offset has advanced so row 20 is still on-screen (NOT clipped). The .take(10) cap from the previous popup-style impl MUST be gone — scrolling kicks in at row 20, not row 10.

Given resume_view is open with 3 sessions, current selection is row 0 with id `s-2`, and open_sessions == [SessionContext(s-9)]: When the user presses Enter: Then Action::AttachToSession(s-2) is dispatched, resume_view is dropped to None, open_sessions grows to [SessionContext(s-9), SessionContext(s-2)], current_session_index == 1, active_session_tx publishes Some(s-2), and refresh_session_chrome(s-2) runs.

Given resume_view is open with selection on session id `s-2` and open_sessions already contains [SessionContext(s-1), SessionContext(s-2), SessionContext(s-3)] with current_session_index == 0: When the user presses Enter: Then open_sessions length stays 3 (no duplicate), current_session_index moves to 1 (the existing slot), and Action::AttachToSession(s-2) still publishes to active_session_tx.

Given resume_view is open with 3 sessions selected on row 1 (id `s-2`): When the user presses D: Then Action::RequestDeleteSession(s-2) is dispatched, resume_view.delete_confirm becomes Some(ConfirmDialog { title: "Delete session?", primary_label: "Delete", ... }) overlaid on the resume view, AND no backend call has fired yet. When the user presses Enter on the delete-confirm dialog with Primary focused: Then Action::ConfirmDeleteSession(s-2) is dispatched; backend.persistence_delete_session(s-2) is spawned; on completion backend.list_sessions() is re-fetched and Action::SessionListLoaded is dispatched so resume_view.sessions becomes [s1, s3] without s-2; resume_view.delete_confirm is set back to None.

Given resume_view.delete_confirm is Some(...) with Primary focused: When the user presses Esc on the dialog OR cycles to Cancel and presses Enter: Then resume_view.delete_confirm becomes None, the resume_view stays open with its prior sessions unchanged, and NO backend call fires.

Given resume_view is open with 3 sessions: When the user presses Esc: Then Action::CloseResumeView is dispatched, resume_view becomes None, AgentViewStore.current_session_index is UNCHANGED, no AttachToSession dispatched, and AgentView's normal header/scrollback/input/footer layout paints on the next render.

Given backend.list_sessions() returns an empty Vec: When resume_view is open and receives Action::SessionListLoaded([]): Then resume_view.sessions is empty; render paints the centred placeholder `(no sessions to resume)`; Enter is a no-op; D is a no-op; Esc still dismisses.

Given AgentView is showing its normal layout with no popups/mode views open: When the user types `/search` + Enter: Then slash_popup is dropped, AgentView.search_view becomes Some(default with empty query), the input is reset, and NO backend call has fired yet. The next render shows the full-screen search view with header `(search): ` + inverse-space cursor + the placeholder `(type to search history)`.

Given AgentView is showing its normal layout with no popups/mode views open: When the user presses Ctrl+R: Then Action::OpenSearchView is dispatched (SAME action as /search + Enter), search_view becomes Some(default), and the same full-screen layout paints. Ctrl+R while search_view is ALREADY open is forwarded to the search_view (no-op — its handle_key returns Ignored).

Given search_view is open with empty query: When the user types `g`, `i`, `t`: Then each keystroke updates query (`g` → `gi` → `git`); each emits Action::SearchHistory; backend.persistence_search_history("git") returns 2 HistoryMatch values; Action::HistorySearchResults(matches) folds them in; search_view.matches has 2 entries; render shows the 2 rows with the first highlighted.

Given search_view is open with query `git` and 2 matches with `git status` highlighted: When the user presses Enter: Then Action::InsertIntoInput("git status") is dispatched, search_view becomes None, AgentView.input.value() == "git status", focus stays on the input, AND NO Action::InputSubmitted is auto-fired.

Given search_view is open with query `xyzzy` and backend returned zero matches: Then render shows the placeholder `(no history matches "xyzzy")`; Enter is ignored; Esc still dismisses via Action::CloseSearchView.

Given search_view has 40 matches and terminal height is 24: When the user presses ↓ 15 times: Then selected_index == 15 AND scroll_offset has advanced so row 15 is visible (no .take(10) cap). When the user keeps pressing ↓ past 39: Then selection wraps to 0 and scroll_offset resets.

codelet_core::persistence::delete_session(uuid) writes a tombstone (or removes the JSONL session entry, mirroring the existing NAPI implementation) at codelet_common::get_data_dir().join("sessions.jsonl"). The existing #[napi] persistence_delete_session in codelet/napi/src/persistence/napi_bindings.rs becomes a one-line delegate `codelet_core::persistence::delete_session(uuid)`. Calling it from a Rust test then calling codelet_core::persistence::sessions::list() does NOT include the deleted session.

FspecServiceImpl.persistence_delete_session(session=Uuid("s-1")) delegates to codelet_core::persistence::delete_session and returns Ok(()). EmbeddedFspecBackend.persistence_delete_session is a one-line delegate over the shared service; WebSocketFspecBackend routes through tarpc. A cross-transport parity test calls both backends and asserts both transports produce the same `list_sessions()` afterwards.

Source-shape regression: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/resume_session_view.rs and search_history_view.rs are new files each < 300 LoC; NEITHER imports `tui_popup` NOR `super::popup_body`; both `pub fn render(&self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, ...)` paint Clear(area) as their first statement and then paint within the FULL area (NOT an auto-sized sub-rect). codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/confirm_dialog.rs is a new file < 300 LoC. codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent.rs stays < 300 LoC after the mode-field additions. codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc026.rs stays < 300 LoC after the new helpers are added.

Source-shape regression: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/resume_picker.rs and search_palette.rs MUST be deleted (renamed/replaced by resume_session_view.rs and search_history_view.rs). A grep over codelet/fspec-tui/src/ for `ResumePicker` or `SearchPalette` returns ZERO hits. A grep over codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/{resume_session_view,search_history_view}.rs for `tui_popup` or `popup_body` returns ZERO hits.

rules.text: Two new FULL-SCREEN MODE VIEWS land under codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/: resume_session_view.rs (sorted-by-last-used session list with scrollbar, Enter attaches, Esc cancels, D opens a delete-confirm dialog) and search_history_view.rs (typeahead over history backed by backend.persistence_search_history). Both follow the BlocklistListView.tsx pattern (TS reference), NOT the SlashCommandPopup/FileSearchPopup pattern. NEITHER widget may import tui_popup nor super::popup_body — they render directly into the entire Rect with an opaque Clear-painted background. Each file < 300 LoC.

AgentView gains two Option<...> MODE fields: resume_view: Option<ResumeSessionView> and search_view: Option<SearchHistoryView>. AgentView.render_with_store EARLY-RETURNS when either is Some — it calls the mode view's render(area, buf, store) for the ENTIRE Rect and SKIPS its normal header/scrollback/input/footer layout. The mode view paints Clear over the full area first so AgentView is fully hidden behind it (matching the TS `position="absolute" width={terminalWidth} height={terminalHeight} backgroundColor="black"` pattern in AgentView.tsx:5002-5191).

App::dispatch::handle_slash_command in src/app/dispatch_rpc020.rs is amended so SlashCommandAction::Resume dispatches Action::OpenResumeView (which opens the resume_view AND spawns backend.list_sessions() → Action::SessionListLoaded on completion) and SlashCommandAction::Search dispatches Action::OpenSearchView (which opens an empty search_view — no initial backend call). The `[notice] /<name> not yet implemented` arm continues to fire for the OTHER unimplemented SlashCommandAction variants but Resume/Search are real wires now.

The Action enum gains TEN new variants (in codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs): OpenResumeView, OpenSearchView, CloseResumeView, CloseSearchView, SessionListLoaded(Vec<SessionInfo>), AttachToSession(SessionId), SearchHistory(String), HistorySearchResults(Vec<HistoryMatch>), InsertIntoInput(String), RequestDeleteSession(SessionId), ConfirmDeleteSession(SessionId). Each is dispatched by App::dispatch through helpers in dispatch_rpc026.rs.

ResumeSessionView behaviour: receives Vec<SessionInfo> via set_sessions(); displays them in the order delivered by the backend (no client-side sort — preserves RPC contract); maintains scroll_offset + selected_index; ↑/↓ navigate with wrap-around AND scroll-window updates so the selected row stays visible inside the terminal height; Enter emits ResumeSessionViewOutcome::Selected(SessionId) → Action::AttachToSession; D emits RequestDeleteSession(SessionId) → opens a ConfirmDialog overlay scoped to the resume view; Esc emits Dismiss → Action::CloseResumeView (no auto exit-confirmation). Empty session list renders the centred placeholder `(no sessions to resume)`. The .take(10) cap from the previous popup impl MUST be removed — scrolling is driven by available terminal rows.

SearchHistoryView behaviour: typeahead state holds query + matches: Vec<HistoryMatch> + selected_index. Typing chars/backspace updates query and the view emits Action::SearchHistory(query); App::dispatch spawns backend.persistence_search_history(query) and dispatches Action::HistorySearchResults(matches) back — folded via set_matches. ↑/↓ navigate; Enter emits Selected(text) → Action::InsertIntoInput(text); Esc emits Dismiss → Action::CloseSearchView. Header row shows `(search): {query}` with a block-cursor inverse-space after the query (matching TS AgentView.tsx:5021). Empty query renders `(type to search history)`; non-empty + zero matches renders `(no history matches "{query}")`. Scrolling matches terminal height — no .take(10) cap.

A new file codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/confirm_dialog.rs lands hosting ConfirmDialog (Rust equivalent of the TS ThreeButtonDialog). API: ConfirmDialog::new(title, body, primary_label, secondary_label, cancel_label); handle_key returns ConfirmDialogOutcome::{Primary, Secondary, Cancel, Continued, Ignored}. Left/Right cycle the focused button; Enter activates the focused button; Esc dismisses with Cancel. Rendered as a small centred floating overlay (THIS one is allowed to use tui_popup or a manual centred Block — the dialog IS conceptually a popup). File < 300 LoC. ResumeSessionView wraps it in `delete_confirm: Option<ConfirmDialog>` so the dialog paints on top of the resume view when D triggers it.

ONE new RPC method lands on FspecService in codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs and on the FspecBackend trait in codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs: `persistence_delete_session(id: SessionId) -> Result<(), String>`. EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend each implement it as a one-line delegate over their respective transports. ZERO new shared types are added in codelet/rpc-types (SessionId already exists).

`delete_session` is LIFTED from codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs into codelet/core/src/persistence/sessions.rs (new file) and re-exported via codelet_core::persistence::delete_session(Uuid) -> Result<(), String>. The existing NAPI export persistence_delete_session in codelet/napi/src/persistence/napi_bindings.rs becomes a one-line delegate so the TS surface stays byte-identical (same pattern RPC-025 used for history). FspecServiceImpl::persistence_delete_session converts the incoming SessionId → Uuid and calls codelet_core::persistence::delete_session.

Ctrl+R keybinding: when neither slash_popup, file_popup, resume_view nor search_view is open, pressing Ctrl+R in AgentView dispatches Action::OpenSearchView — providing a second trigger for the search history mode (mirrors TS AgentView.tsx handleSearchMode bound to /search command AND Ctrl+R). The binding lives in views/agent/dispatch.rs::handle_event BEFORE the existing key routing so it captures the chord with Modifiers::CONTROL + KeyCode::Char('r').

Action::AttachToSession(session_id) handling: if the session is already in AgentViewStore.open_sessions, set current_session_index to it; if NOT, append a fresh SessionContext::new(session_id) and set current_session_index to the new tail. Also publish to active_session_tx so the chunks subscriber re-points and refresh_session_chrome runs (RPC-018) so the new session gets its model + thinking + workspace state. The resume_view is dropped (set to None) as part of this action handler.

Action::InsertIntoInput(text) handling: replace AgentView.input's value with `text` AND drop the search_view (set to None). Submission is NOT auto-triggered — the user may edit before pressing Enter (mirrors TS /search behaviour). Action::CloseResumeView / Action::CloseSearchView simply null the corresponding Option field without other side-effects.

Action::ConfirmDeleteSession(id) handling: spawn `backend.persistence_delete_session(id)`; on success dispatch Action::SessionListLoaded with a refreshed list from backend.list_sessions() (the resume_view reads the new list via set_sessions); the resume_view's `delete_confirm` is set to None. If the session being deleted is currently focused in open_sessions, also remove it from open_sessions and clamp current_session_index. RequestDeleteSession(id) just opens the ConfirmDialog inside the resume_view without dispatching anything to the backend yet.

Both mode views MUST work against EmbeddedFspecBackend AND WebSocketFspecBackend (RPC-002 invariant). Cross-transport-parity tests live in tests/rpc026-*.rs and drive the SAME scripted scenarios (open /resume, list_sessions returns N, pick the 2nd, AttachToSession + index move; open /search, type query, persistence_search_history returns M, Enter on top match, InsertIntoInput; D + Enter confirms, persistence_delete_session round-trips, list re-renders without the deleted session) against both transports.

RPC-002 invariants preserved: every store mutation happens inside App::dispatch on the App task (no Mutex/RwLock/atomics on store types); only tokio::spawn (never Runtime::new); codelet-napi is NOT a dep of codelet-fspec-tui; every new file under 300 LoC; views/agent.rs stays under 300 LoC after the resume_view + search_view + Ctrl+R routing change; dispatch_rpc026.rs stays under 300 LoC after the 4 new helpers (handle_request_delete_session, handle_confirm_delete_session, handle_close_resume_view, handle_close_search_view) are added; source_shape_*.rs scans still pass.

RPC-026.title: /resume session picker + /search history palette (RPC-021c)

userStory.action: press /resume or /search (and Ctrl+R) to open full-screen mode views that mirror the TypeScript Ink TUI — listing resumable sessions or filtering submitted-input history with delete confirmation — rather than small floating popups
userStory.benefit: the Rust frontend's `/resume` and `/search` UX matches the existing TypeScript frontend pixel-for-pixel and feature-for-feature, so habits and integration tests carry across implementations unchanged
userStory.role: developer using the Rust ratatui TUI

architectureNotes.text: [0] Single source of truth: introduce codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/dialog_theme.rs exposing FspecDialog (renderer) + FspecDialogTheme (accent color, title, footer, optional selected row index) + render_dialog(area, buf, FspecDialog). All seven existing dialogs delegate to it; tui_popup::Popup is removed from every render() impl.

[1] Migration order (smallest blast radius first): (a) build dialog_theme.rs with full unit tests; (b) migrate HelpDialog (no selection, only title+body+footer); (c) migrate DisconnectDialog (no selection but dynamic title body); (d) migrate ThinkingLevelDialog (adds selection + D-key); (e) migrate ModelSelectorDialog (selection + non-selectable header rows); (f) migrate ConfirmDialog (button row variant); (g) replace popup_body.rs renderer for SlashCommandPopup + FileSearchPopup; (h) regenerate all insta snapshots.

[2] Cross-language style table (canonical reference):
  HelpDialog          accent=Cyan,    title='Help'
  DisconnectDialog    accent=Red,     title='Disconnected'
  ThinkingLevelDialog accent=Yellow,  title='Thinking Level'
  ModelSelectorDialog accent=Cyan,    title='Select Model'
  ConfirmDialog       accent=Yellow,  title=<caller>
  SlashCommandPopup   accent=Cyan,    title='Slash Commands'
  FileSearchPopup     accent=Cyan,    title='File Search'
All inverse highlights use bg=accent, fg=Color::Black, modifier=BOLD. All footer text uses Modifier::DIM. All separators in footer = │ (U+2502). All markers = '▸ ' / '  '. Border = BorderType::Rounded. Background = Color::Black via Clear.

[3] Existing tui_popup::Popup dependency stays in Cargo.toml (it remains as the fallback for any future ad-hoc popup) but the dialog modules listed in [1] stop importing it. The 'no centered_rect helper' invariant from the original RPC-022 scenarios remains valid because dialog_theme.rs replaces — not duplicates — the centering math.

[4] New Action variant: Action::SetThinkingLevelDefault(SessionId, ThinkingLevel) added to the Action enum and a corresponding handler in dispatch_rpc022.rs that calls backend.set_thinking_level_default (a new SessionManagerHandle trait method with a safe-default no-op impl, following the RPC-022 pattern). This unlocks the missing 'D Set Default' key in the Rust ThinkingLevelDialog without changing the TS side.

[5] Snapshots: every existing insta snapshot under codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/snapshots/ AND codelet/fspec-tui/tests/snapshots/ that captures a dialog rendering must be regenerated. The PR description must list every snapshot that changed and a maintainer reviews them visually before approving the merge.

RPC-027.description: All Rust ratatui dialogs in codelet/fspec-tui — HelpDialog, DisconnectDialog, ThinkingLevelDialog, ModelSelectorDialog, ConfirmDialog, SlashCommandPopup, FileSearchPopup — render as plain tui_popup::Popup widgets with raw uncolored text. They look nothing like the canonical TypeScript Ink dialogs (ThinkingLevelDialog.tsx, AttachmentDialog.tsx, ThreeButtonDialog, TurnContentModal, FileSearchPopup.tsx, SlashCommandPalette.tsx) which share a consistent visual language: rounded border, black background, padding=1, bold accent-colored inner title (NOT a border title), inverse-color selection highlight (accent bg + black fg), ▸ marker on selected rows, dimColor descriptions, dimColor footer hints with │ separators. Introduce a shared FspecDialog/FspecDialogTheme abstraction in codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/dialog_theme.rs, then refactor every existing dialog to use it. See spec/attachments/RPC-XXX/dialog-theme-refactor.md for the complete style guide, exact ANSI colors, characters, dimensions, and per-dialog migration steps.

examples.text: A user opens ThinkingLevelDialog: the dialog renders with a rounded yellow border, an opaque black background, and the bold yellow text 'Thinking Level' on the first content row (NOT inside the top border). One blank row separates the title from the four level rows. The current Off row is highlighted with a yellow background and black bold text, prefixed with '▸ '; the other three rows show plain white text prefixed with '  '. The footer row '↑↓ Navigate │ Enter Select │ D Set Default │ Esc Close' is centered and dimmed.

A user opens HelpDialog by pressing ?: the dialog renders with a rounded cyan border, opaque black background, and a bold cyan 'Help' header inside the body — not painted into the border. Each keybinding line ('j/k Navigate', 'Tab Switch pane', '? Toggle this help', 'q Quit fspec-tui', 'Enter Send', 'Ctrl+C Interrupt', 'ESC Dismiss this dialog') appears on its own row. The footer 'ESC to close' is dimmed and centered.

A user opens DisconnectDialog after a connection drop: rounded red border, opaque black background, bold red 'Disconnected' header on the first body row, three content lines ('daemon disconnected', blank row, 'q to quit', 'r to reconnect') with white text, dimmed centered footer. On Action::Reconnecting(3) the header body line changes inline to 'daemon disconnected — auto-reconnecting (attempt 3)…' while the red border, black background, and bold red title remain identical.

A user submits /model and arrow-navigates the ModelSelectorDialog: rounded cyan border, opaque black, bold cyan 'Select Model' title row, provider headers in plain text, selectable model rows prefixed with two-char marker ('▸ ' or '  '); the currently selected model row paints its full content width with cyan background + black bold foreground; non-selected model rows show white text and the capability badge segment '[R] [V] [Nk]' is dimmed. Dimmed centered footer reads '↑↓ Navigate │ Enter Select │ Esc Close'.

A user types / in AgentView: SlashCommandPopup renders above the input with a rounded cyan border, opaque black background, bold cyan 'Slash Commands' header inside the body, each command row aligned with a two-char prefix ('▸ ' selected / '  ' unselected) followed by '/<name>' padded to the widest name and a dimmed description; the selected row is highlighted with the full-width cyan/black inverse style. The centered dimmed footer reads '↑↓ Navigate │ Tab/Enter Select │ Esc Close'.

A user types @ to open FileSearchPopup: same cyan/black/rounded theme, bold cyan 'File Search' inner title, each match row uses the two-char marker prefix, selected match has full-row inverse highlight, and the dimmed centered footer reads '↑↓ Navigate │ Tab/Enter Select │ Esc Close'. The empty-state literals '(type to search files)' and '(no files match "<filter>")' render in plain (non-highlighted) text.

A user activates ConfirmDialog from ResumeSessionView to delete a session: rounded yellow border, opaque black background, bold yellow title 'Delete Session' on the first body row, body text in plain white, button row at the bottom with three labels separated by ' │ ' — the focused button is rendered with yellow background + black bold foreground, the other two as plain text. Left/Right cycles focus; Enter on focused 'Delete' emits Primary, focused 'Cancel' emits Cancel, Esc emits Cancel from anywhere.

After the refactor a developer screenshots ThinkingLevelDialog from the Rust TUI and the screenshot is visually indistinguishable (same border, same colors, same indicator, same footer text, same dimmed style, same centered position) from a screenshot of the TS Ink ThinkingLevelDialog rendered against the same terminal dimensions.

Insta snapshot regression tests for each refactored dialog (help_dialog, disconnect_dialog, thinking_level_dialog, model_selector_dialog) capture an 80x24 cell-grid rendering. Updated snapshots show: the inner title row at the top of the body, the inverse-highlight row, the dim footer row — and any subsequent code change that breaks the theme contract fails the snapshot.

rules.text: Introduce a single shared dialog renderer module at codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/dialog_theme.rs that owns the canonical look: rounded border, accent-colored bold inner title (not a border title), black opaque background, padding 1, dim footer hints, ▸ row marker, inverse selection highlight (accent bg + black fg)

All dialogs MUST stop using tui_popup::Popup .title() (which paints the title as part of the top border). The title is rendered INSIDE the dialog body as a bold accent-colored Text on its own row with one blank row below it — matching ThinkingLevelDialog.tsx lines 120–124.

Each dialog declares ONE accent color: HelpDialog=Cyan, DisconnectDialog=Red, ThinkingLevelDialog=Yellow, ModelSelectorDialog=Cyan, ConfirmDialog=Yellow, SlashCommandPopup=Cyan, FileSearchPopup=Cyan. The same accent is used for the border AND the inner title AND the selection-row background.

Selection-row highlight is INVERSE: the selected row's full width is painted Style::default().bg(accent).fg(Color::Black).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD). Unselected rows use Style::default().fg(Color::White) and ANY description text after the primary label uses Modifier::DIM.

Row markers are ▸  (U+25B8 + space) when selected and two spaces when not — exact byte-equal alignment must be preserved. The current single-space variant in slash_command_popup.rs / file_search_popup.rs build_body must be replaced with the two-character variant.

Footer hint rows are rendered with Modifier::DIM and centered (horizontally) using ratatui's Alignment::Center. The separator character is │ (U+2502 BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT VERTICAL) — NOT the ASCII pipe | — and a one-row top margin separates the footer from the body.

Dialog body has padding 1 on all sides between the border and the content. Border style is rounded (ratatui BorderType::Rounded — characters ╭─╮ │ ╰─╯). Background is Color::Black (Style::default().bg(Color::Black)) painted over the entire dialog rect via ratatui::widgets::Clear so underlying content is hidden.

Dialog dimensions: width = max(longest line in body, 45) + 4 (padding+border), clamped to area.width. Height = body line count + 2 (padding) + 2 (border), clamped to area.height. Centered with (area.width - width)/2 and (area.height - height)/2 — matching the existing tui_popup centering math.

ThinkingLevelDialog MUST gain the missing 'D Set Default' key binding that the TS reference has (ThinkingLevelDialog.tsx lines 93–96 and 151). The footer becomes ↑↓ Navigate │ Enter Select │ D Set Default │ Esc Close and pressing 'd' or 'D' emits Action::SetThinkingLevelDefault(level) without closing the dialog.

ConfirmDialog button row is themed the same way: focused button = inverse highlight (accent bg + Color::Black fg + Modifier::BOLD), unfocused = plain. Separator between buttons is │ (U+2502) wrapped in single spaces. Buttons are wrapped in a Padding-padded Block — no longer rendered with the raw Block::default().borders(Borders::ALL) used today.

popup_body.rs (PopupBody adapter used by slash + file search popups) MUST be replaced with the shared dialog_theme renderer. Inverse highlight changes from current Color::White on Color::Blue to the accent-color scheme (Color::Black on Color::Cyan). The matching insta snapshots for HelpDialog (help_dialog__centered_popup_80x24.snap) must be regenerated.

Every dialog .rs file MUST stay under the existing 300-LoC ceiling. dialog_theme.rs is a new shared module — extracting per-dialog code into it should REDUCE total LoC across the dialogs (we are removing duplicated render math, not adding it). If dialog_theme.rs itself approaches 300 LoC during implementation, split into dialog_theme.rs (renderer) + dialog_theme_rows.rs (row/highlight helpers) following the model_selector_dialog_rows.rs precedent.

The TypeScript Ink dialog files (src/tui/components/ThinkingLevelDialog.tsx, AttachmentDialog.tsx, ThreeButtonDialog, TurnContentModal.tsx, FileSearchPopup.tsx, SlashCommandPalette.tsx and the base src/components/Dialog.tsx) are the spec — they MUST NOT be modified. The Rust side is the consumer that must conform.

RPC-027.title: Refactor all Rust RPC dialogs to match TypeScript Ink dialog theming

userStory.action: have every dialog and popup render with the exact same visual language as the canonical TypeScript Ink dialogs
userStory.benefit: users moving between the TS Ink TUI and the new Rust ratatui TUI see a single consistent product instead of two visually unrelated apps
userStory.role: developer maintaining the codelet/fspec-tui Rust ratatui frontend

architectureNotes.text: [0] Introduce codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/scroll_viewport.rs with three primitives: wrap_index(current, delta, total) using rem_euclid (mirrors store/board_viewport.rs:42-44), ensure_visible(scroll_offset, selected, visible_rows, total) (popup-flavour of board_viewport::adjust_scroll_offset without the two-pass arrow correction), and WheelVelocity with last/vel Cells and a step(direction) method that mirrors TS AgentView.tsx:4435-4458.

[1] Each migrated view adds scroll_offset: usize and last_visible_rows: Cell<usize> fields, replaces iter().take(10) with iter().skip(scroll_offset).take(visible_rows), and wires Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End + ScrollUp/ScrollDown through wrap_index + ensure_visible. The dialog frame in components/dialog_theme.rs already provides the body height — exposing it via dialog_rect is enough; visible_rows = body.height - title - gap - footer.

[2] Mouse events route through the existing Compositor (no parallel pipeline). Each view exposes handle_mouse(&mut self, ev: MouseEvent, rect: Rect, vr: usize) called by AgentView's mouse branch after hit-testing the popup_rect. Events that fall outside the popup_rect return EventResult::Ignored so they bubble to AgentView's scrollback/board. The TUI-078 MouseTrackingToggle (5-second tokio re-enable timer) remains the responsibility of the App shell — popups do not own it.

[3] Migration order (smallest blast radius first): (a) scroll_viewport.rs + unit tests; (b) SlashCommandPopup (the reported defect); (c) FileSearchPopup (copy-paste-adapt); (d) ModelSelectorDialog (windowing + Pg keys + mouse, snapshot regen); (e) ResumeSessionView (replace bespoke wrap math with wrap_index + ensure_visible, add mouse + Pg keys); (f) SearchHistoryView (same as e); (g) ThinkingLevelDialog (mouse-wheel only); (h) regenerate every touched insta snapshot.

[4] TS Ink parity invariants (DO NOT modify TS sources): wrap-around behaviour matches src/tui/hooks/useSlashCommandInput.ts:156-174 + useFileSearchInput.ts:167-185 + ThinkingLevelDialog.tsx:98-110; mouse-wheel acceleration matches AgentView.tsx:4435-4458 (1×–5× ramp at <150ms intervals). The Rust port goes beyond the TS source by adding mouse-wheel to popups (TS only wires it for the Resume picker) — this is mandated by RPC-002 + RPC-023 master plan.

RPC-028.description: RPC-027 introduced themed dialogs but the SlashCommandPopup (and likely other selectable popups + the /resume picker + /search palette) do NOT scroll when the selection goes past the visible region. They also lack mouse wheel scroll support and wrap-around behavior. BoardView (RPC-016, RPC-023) already implements per-column viewport scrolling, mouse-wheel scroll, and wrap-around. Every selectable list view (HelpDialog body lines, ModelSelectorDialog rows, ThinkingLevelDialog rows, ConfirmDialog buttons, SlashCommandPopup, FileSearchPopup, ResumeSessionView, SearchPaletteView, plus any other) must follow the same patterns. This card audits every Rust scrolling view, documents the parity gaps versus the TS Ink source and the BoardView precedent, and ships the fixes.

examples.text: User opens SlashCommandPopup with 14 matching commands, presses Down 10 times: the 11th match is selected AND visible — scroll_offset advanced to 4 (visible_rows=10), and ↑ glyph appears on the top body row.
User in SlashCommandPopup at the last match presses Down: selection wraps to the first match and the popup re-scrolls to show row 0.
User scrolls the trackpad wheel up while hovering inside FileSearchPopup: the selection moves up one row; if at the first row, it wraps to the last match.

User in ModelSelectorDialog with 30 models presses PageDown: selection jumps forward by visible_rows skipping non-selectable provider headers, and the dialog body scrolls so the new selection is visible.
User in /resume session picker presses Home: selection jumps to the first session and the list scrolls to the top.
User in /search history palette presses End: selection jumps to the last match and the list scrolls so it is visible on the bottom row.
User clicks (left-button) on a row in /resume picker: the click row becomes the selected session and Enter immediately resumes it.
User in ThinkingLevelDialog scrolls the trackpad wheel down: selection advances to the next level (wrapping to Off at the bottom).

User scrolls the trackpad wheel over the underlying AgentView region OUTSIDE the open SlashCommandPopup rect: the popup ignores the event so the scrollback scrolls normally (popup hit-tests its last-rendered rect).

rules.text: SlashCommandPopup, FileSearchPopup, ModelSelectorDialog, ResumeSessionView, and SearchHistoryView MUST maintain a scroll_offset and window the visible rows via items[scroll_offset..scroll_offset+visible_rows] — the `.take(10)` hard cap in slash/file popups is removed.

Up/Down navigation in every selectable view wraps around the ends using rem_euclid (matching BoardStore::move_selection) and always calls adjust_scroll afterward so the post-wrap selection is visible.
Every selectable view handles MouseEventKind::ScrollUp/ScrollDown by emitting move_by(±1) and hit-tests the event against its last-rendered Rect (events outside the rect are Ignored).
PageUp/PageDown jump by exactly visible_rows; Home selects index 0 with scroll_offset 0; End selects len-1 with scroll_offset adjusted so the last row is visible.
↑ glyph is painted on the top body row when scroll_offset > 0; ↓ glyph on the bottom body row when scroll_offset + visible_rows < total — same idiom as views/board/viewport.rs:95-101.

A new shared module codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/scroll_viewport.rs owns wrap_index(current, delta, total), ensure_visible(scroll_offset, selected, visible_rows, total), and a WheelVelocity helper — every refactored view consumes it instead of duplicating math.
Mouse-wheel acceleration follows TS AgentView.tsx:4435-4458 — ≥5 wheel events within 150 ms cap velocity at 5; gap ≥150 ms resets to 1 — and is shared via WheelVelocity in scroll_viewport.rs.
No refactored view file exceeds 300 LoC; helpers move into scroll_viewport.rs (or per-view _rows.rs siblings) as needed.

RPC-028.title: Add proper scrolling, mouse wheel support, and wrap-around to all Rust dialog/popup/picker views

userStory.action: navigate every selectable dialog/popup/picker with scroll, mouse-wheel, and wrap-around just like BoardView does
userStory.benefit: no list view silently hides rows past index 9 and trackpad scroll works everywhere

RPC-029.description: The Rust ratatui AgentView (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent.rs) renders with a visibly different structure from the canonical TS Ink AgentView (src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx). KEY FINDING: TS AgentView does NOT use ConversationInputArea — it inlines its own input area with NO border at all (just paddingX={1} + green '> ' prefix + InputTransition). Major structural issues in the Rust port: (1) Scrollback wrapped in Block::ALL with title 'Agent — <session-id>' — TS has no border; (2) Input wrapped in 4-sided Block::ALL — TS has no border whatsoever; (3) SessionFooter rendered BELOW input — TS renders it ABOVE input. Major semantic issues: (4) Header missing work-unit prefix '(RPC-029: implementing)' between session # and model name; (5) Header missing dark grey #333333 row background; (6) Header colors are flat (white/darkgray) — TS uses cyan.bold prefix+model, magenta [R], blue [V], dim [Nk], red.bold [DEBUG], cyan [SELECT], yellow [T:*], green [ISOLATED]; (7) Header missing badges [ISOLATED], [DEBUG], [SELECT], tokens-per-second (magenta), reasoning tokens (🧠), COMPACTED N% suffix; (8) Header missing paddingX=1; (9) Footer missing #333333 background + paddingX=1; (10) Footer has left-side hint strings (Enter=send Ctrl+C=interrupt ESC=back) — TS footer left is EMPTY (right-aligned only); (11) Footer uses wrong branch glyph ⌥ (U+2325) — TS uses ⎇ (U+2387); (12) Footer paints full path cyan — TS dims cwd and only cyan-colors the [⎇ branch] suffix. Refactor the Rust AgentView render path in three phases — A) structural (reorder layout slots, drop both Blocks, pad input area), B) theming (dark grey row bg + paddingX, split footer color spans), C) header semantics (extend SessionHeader struct with work_unit_id/status + is_isolated + is_debug_enabled + tokens_per_second + reasoning_tokens + compaction_reduction + is_loading, rewrite build_left_text → multi-span Line, wire data from AgentViewStore). See spec/attachments/RPC-029/agentview-structure-alignment.md for the full side-by-side analysis with verbatim JSX excerpts from TS, the current Rust render path verbatim, the 17 prioritized issues, the step-by-step migration plan, and 10 acceptance criteria.

examples.text: Rendered scrollback area contains no border glyphs (┌, └, ─, │) and the literal ' Agent — ' title does not appear in buffer
Rendered input area has no border glyphs around it; the green '> ' prompt appears at column area.x+1
Footer row appears strictly above the input prompt row when scanning the buffer top to bottom
When current work unit is RPC-029 in status implementing, header left contains '(RPC-029: implementing)' between #N and model name
Every cell in the header row and footer row has background color RGB(0x33, 0x33, 0x33)
Footer right side shows '~/projects/fspec [⎇ main]' with the cwd dim and the bracketed branch suffix cyan
Footer left half (columns 1 through workspace text start) contains only background cells - no Enter=send / Ctrl+C / ESC=back glyphs
First column (x=area.x) and last column (x=area.x+area.width-1) of header_area and footer_area have no glyph content
When is_debug_enabled is true, the header left text contains '[DEBUG]' painted red-bold
When is_isolated is true, the header left text contains '[ISOLATED]' painted green

rules.text: AgentView outer Box has NO border, NO background, NO padding - only flexDirection column and flexGrow=1
Scrollback area has NO border and NO title - render ScrollbackList directly into the area
Input area has NO border whatsoever - only horizontal paddingX=1 around the bare input
Layout order top-to-bottom must be: Header, RoleBanner, Scrollback (flex), Footer, Input
Header row has #333333 dark grey background painted on every cell of the row
Footer row has #333333 dark grey background painted on every cell of the row

architectureNotes.text: Final layout: codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs becomes a ~15-line file containing exactly: a 5-line doc comment naming this as the NAPI persistence facade, a single `pub use codelet_core::persistence::*;` (the flat re-export that preserves every historical `crate::persistence::Foo` import in codelet-napi), and the `#[cfg(not(feature = "noop"))] mod napi_bindings;` + `#[cfg(not(feature = "noop"))] pub use napi_bindings::*;` declarations. The `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` and `#[cfg(test)] mod lazy_init_tests;` declarations are deleted (those test files no longer exist in codelet-napi). No pub fn declarations remain in mod.rs.

napi_bindings.rs imports header: the file opens with two `use` groups — first `use codelet_core::persistence::{ create_session, create_session_with_provider, load_session, resume_last_session, list_sessions, delete_session, rename_session, fork_session, merge_messages, cherry_pick, append_message, append_message_with_metadata, get_message, get_session_messages, get_session_messages_full, update_session_tokens, set_session_tokens, set_compaction_state, clear_compaction_state, cleanup_orphaned_messages, store_blob, get_blob, blob_exists, process_envelope_for_blob_storage, rehydrate_envelope_blobs, MessageEnvelope, MessagePayload, UserContent, AssistantContent, SessionManifest, ForkPoint, MergeRecord, CompactionState, TokenUsage, StoredMessage, HistoryEntry, history, };` (the explicit acknowledgement that codelet-napi consumes these from codelet-core), then `use napi::bindgen_prelude::*;` + `use std::collections::HashMap;` + `use std::path::PathBuf;`. No `use super::*;` line appears. The two history-aliasing wrappers are replaced by direct calls to `history::add`, `history::get`, `history::search` inside the `persistence_add_history`, `persistence_get_history`, `persistence_search_history` bodies.

set_data_directory inlining: the `#[napi] pub fn persistence_set_data_directory(dir: String) -> Result<()>` body becomes (in pseudo-code) `let path = PathBuf::from(dir); codelet_common::set_data_directory(path).map_err(Error::from_reason)?; codelet_core::persistence::reset_stores_for_tests(); crate::credentials::reset_credential_store(); crate::graph::reset_graph_db(); Ok(())` — i.e. the current mod.rs `set_data_directory` body is inlined verbatim. The matching `persistence_get_data_directory` body becomes `codelet_common::get_data_dir().map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().to_string()).map_err(Error::from_reason)`.

Test relocation mechanics: (1) `git mv codelet/napi/src/persistence/tests.rs codelet/core/src/persistence/tests.rs` and `git mv codelet/napi/src/persistence/lazy_init_tests.rs codelet/core/src/persistence/lazy_init_tests.rs` preserves git blame. (2) Add `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` + `#[cfg(test)] mod lazy_init_tests;` to codelet/core/src/persistence/mod.rs. (3) Replace `use super::*;` at the top of each file with `use crate::persistence::*;` (codelet-core canonical path). (4) Replace the body of `setup_test_env()` (currently `crate::persistence::set_data_directory(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()).expect(...)`) with the codelet-core-only sequence: `codelet_common::set_data_directory(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()).expect(...); reset_stores_for_tests();`. (5) Add `tempfile = { workspace = true }` and `lazy_static = { workspace = true }` to codelet/core/Cargo.toml under [dev-dependencies] if not already present. (6) Delete the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests; #[cfg(test)] mod lazy_init_tests;` lines from codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs.

Caller audit and ripple effects: a final `rg --hidden -t rust 'use super::\*' codelet/napi/src/persistence/` returns zero matches. `rg -t rust 'crate::persistence::set_data_directory' codelet/napi/src/` returns only test_support.rs:21 which is rewritten per rule [7]. `rg -t rust 'crate::persistence::ensure_directories' codelet/napi/src/` returns zero matches. `rg -t rust 'crate::persistence::add_history_entry|crate::persistence::get_history|crate::persistence::search_history' codelet/napi/src/` returns only the calls inside napi_bindings.rs (which now use `history::add`/`history::get`/`history::search` directly). The `#[cfg(test)] mod tests; #[cfg(test)] mod lazy_init_tests;` declarations are removed from codelet/napi/src/persistence/mod.rs.

Test coverage strategy and verification: matches the precedent set by RPC-031/032/033/034 lift cards. (a) Write `codelet/core/tests/persistence_shim_layout_test.rs` — a new build-time test that assert-greps the on-disk layout of codelet/napi/src/persistence/ to contain only `mod.rs` and `napi_bindings.rs` (using std::fs::read_dir). (b) Capture the SHA-256 of codelet/napi/index.d.ts BEFORE the card runs and assert byte-identity AFTER via a shell-driven CI step (or attach the pre-card hash as a fixture and verify it matches). (c) Run all 80+ persistence tests under their NEW codelet-core home and confirm the count is preserved (48 + 9). (d) Confirm `cargo build -p codelet-napi --features napi` AND `cargo build -p codelet-napi --features noop` BOTH succeed (the noop build must continue to compile because the `#[cfg(not(feature = "noop"))]` gate on `mod napi_bindings` is preserved). (e) Confirm `cargo test -p codelet-napi --test session_persistence_test` and `cargo test -p codelet-napi --test subordinate_session_persistence_test` still pass.

Clippy compliance and lint scope: the relocated test files are compiled under codelet-core's lint configuration (workspace-shared lints enforce `clippy::redundant_closure_for_method_calls`, `clippy::needless_collect`, etc. — stricter than codelet-napi). The existing `#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]` allow at the top of each test file is preserved. Any test that fails the stricter lints under codelet-core gets the minimum `#[allow(...)]` added to its `#[test] fn` rather than relaxing the file-wide attribute. Expect zero or one tests to need additional allows.

Forbidden-arrow regression intact: the existing `codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/rpc_006_source_shape.rs` test continues to pass — proving the `rpc → napi` forbidden arrow is not re-introduced by this card. A downstream consumer (codelet-rpc-embedded, which depends on codelet-core but never on codelet-napi) writes `use codelet_core::persistence::{create_session, load_session, append_message_with_metadata, fork_session, store_blob, get_blob, blob_exists, process_envelope_for_blob_storage, rehydrate_envelope_blobs, history};` and links cleanly — and ALSO writes `use codelet_core::persistence::ensure_directories;` cleanly (proving the ensure_directories shim's deletion from codelet-napi does not regress codelet-core's surface).

codelet/napi/index.d.ts is byte-identical before and after this card — verified by a build artifact snapshot diff. The 48-test suite from codelet/napi/src/persistence/tests.rs (89,620 bytes) and the 9-test suite from codelet/napi/src/persistence/lazy_init_tests.rs (14,680 bytes) are relocated to codelet/core/src/persistence/tests.rs and codelet/core/src/persistence/lazy_init_tests.rs respectively. The `Napi*` wire structs (NapiSessionManifest, NapiForkPoint, NapiMergeRecord, NapiCompactionState, NapiTokenUsage, NapiStoredMessage, NapiHistoryEntry, NapiAppendResult, NapiCherryPickResult) and their `From<…>` impls stay co-located with the bindings inside napi_bindings.rs. architectureNotes.text: Field-naming/napi-rename rule: types whose Rust field names already match the desired TS camelCase (e.g. SessionTokens.input_tokens → inputTokens) rely on napi-derive's automatic snake-to-camel conversion — no explicit `#[napi(js_name = ...)]` is needed. Fields with non-trivial renames (none in this card) would use explicit js_name. This matches the precedent set by WorkUnitInfo, SessionInfo, and TokenTracker in the same file.

ThinkingConfig.config_json field rationale: codelet-rpc-types currently has zero serde_json dependency (only serde + optional napi). Using `serde_json::Value` in a `#[napi(object)]` struct is not natively supported by napi-derive v3 and would require either an extra dependency on serde_json plus a custom NAPI-to-JsObject conversion shim, or `#[napi(ts_type = "any")]` hacks. Following the existing FspecRequest::args_json precedent, we store the provider-specific config as a JSON-encoded String — callers parse via `serde_json::from_str` on the consumer side (codelet-sessions / codelet-fspec-tui already have serde_json as a dependency). This keeps codelet-rpc-types dependency-light and the TS side gets a simple `configJson: string` field that JSON.parses cleanly.

PauseKind/PauseResponse/ApprovalChoice wire shape vs internal codelet_tools shape: the existing codelet_tools::tool_pause module owns PauseKind { Continue, Confirm, Triple } and PauseResponse { Resumed, Approved, Denied, Interrupted, AllowOnce, AllowSession } for the session-internal pause loop. The wire-portable shapes added here are deliberately distinct — they model only the AgentView-facing states (pause kinds the user can choose between in the UI and the responses the user can send back). Phase 4 (extract codelet-sessions) will map between the internal codelet_tools types and the wire types at the SessionManager boundary. Keeping the two type families separate avoids polluting codelet-rpc-types with internal session-loop concerns (Continue/Resumed/Interrupted are loop control signals, not user-facing choices).

IsolationStateChange backward-compat: the existing StreamChunk::IsolationStateChange variant has { is_isolated, worktree_path: Option<String> } today (see codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs:622-627). Adding `base_commit: Option<String>` as a new field is forward-compatible for serde JSON deserialization (Option fields default to None when missing) but the StreamChunk::isolation_state_change constructor at lib.rs:821 must be updated to accept and pass through the new field. Existing call sites that pass two args will need to be updated — search via `Grep('StreamChunk::isolation_state_change|isolation_state_change(', '*.rs')` before merging to ensure no caller is left compiling against the 2-arg signature.

Test placement: round-trip tests live in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs under a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; use serde_json; ... }` block at the bottom of the file. `serde_json` is added to `[dev-dependencies]` in codelet/rpc-types/Cargo.toml (not [dependencies]) to keep the default release build free of serde_json. This matches the codelet-core/codelet-common dev-dep pattern.

rules.text: Every new struct/enum lives in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs with #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] and (where it crosses the JS boundary) #[cfg_attr(feature = "napi", napi_derive::napi(object))] for structs or #[cfg_attr(feature = "napi", napi_derive::napi(string_enum))] for enums — matching the established pattern set by WorkUnitInfo, SessionStatus, and ThinkingLevel in the same file

The only modification is that the IsolationStateChange variant gains an additional field `base_commit: Option<String>` (camelCase `baseCommit` on the napi side) so the Rust AgentView can render isolation diff baselines against the worktree origin commit — additive, no removals, no renames

rules.text: Every new method declared on the SessionManagerHandle trait MUST carry a default body so existing handles (StubSessionManagerHandle pre-override, any future NAPI/test handles) compile unchanged — defaults return safe sentinels: empty collections, None, Ok(()), SessionTokens::default(), SessionModel::default()-style instances, etc.

send_input on SessionManagerHandle keeps its existing 2-arg signature for backward compatibility; a sibling send_input_with_thinking(session_id, text, thinking: Option<ThinkingConfig>) is added. The existing send_input default delegates to send_input_with_thinking(.., None) so implementers only override one method.

Every trait method added to SessionManagerHandle MUST have a peer async method on FspecService (codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs). FspecServiceImpl delegates each call through self.inner.session_manager() returning the same safe defaults when no handle is attached. The pre-existing set_thinking_level_default gap on the tarpc trait is closed in this card.

Every new tarpc method is mirrored on the FspecBackend trait (codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs) and implemented on BOTH EmbeddedFspecBackend (one-line delegate through self.client) and WebSocketFspecBackend (read-lock the client slot, fail with BackendError::Disconnected when None, otherwise one-line delegate).

StubSessionManagerHandle MUST override every new trait method with a deterministic, idempotent stub: get_session_tokens returns seeded SessionTokens, clear_history emits a UserNotification chunk + Ok(()), compact_session returns canned CompactionResult, pause_* / send_hitl_response set internal flags + emit SessionStateChange, status_changes_tx/rx expose a new internal broadcast::Sender<(SessionId, SessionStatus)>. The stub MUST be deterministic so cross-transport parity tests produce identical output across both transports.

A push-driven status_changes broadcast channel of (SessionId, SessionStatus) is introduced on SessionManagerHandle. status_changes_rx() returns a broadcast::Receiver; status_changes_tx() exposes the Sender for the host/co-listener. The Stub owns a real channel; default implementations on the trait return a fresh local channel whose sender is dropped immediately so subscribers observe Closed (safe degenerate behaviour for handles that haven't wired status push yet).

Cross-transport parity tests live in codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/ and codelet/rpc-server/tests/. A scenario runs the same call sequence through EmbeddedFspecBackend AND WebSocketFspecBackend constructed against the same StubSessionManagerHandle, and asserts every method's return value is byte-identical (modulo timestamps and any source-of-truth ID minted inside the stub).

No existing test in codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/ or codelet/rpc-server/tests/ is broken by the additions — every new method has a default impl on the trait so any pre-existing call site keeps compiling. cargo build of codelet-core, codelet-rpc, codelet-rpc-types, codelet-rpc-embedded, codelet-rpc-server, codelet-fspec-tui all pass. cargo clippy -p codelet-core -- -D warnings is clean.

userStory.action: move the entire BackgroundSession struct and impl into the NAPI-free codelet-sessions crate with import-path rewrites only

architectureNotes.text: Architecture: This card lifts FOUR things into codelet-sessions: (1) SessionManager struct + impl + Default, (2) ChainOfCommand struct + impl + Default, (3) the entire `crate::navigation` module (~285 lines, no napi deps once its only `use crate::session_manager::{BackgroundSession, ChainOfCommand};` is rewritten to point at codelet_sessions::), (4) the NAPI-free portion of `crate::credentials` (mod.rs / resolver.rs / store.rs / types.rs; only napi_bindings.rs stays in napi as a thin shim). All four lifts collectively eliminate every `crate::*` reference inside the moved SessionManager methods that the attachment names as a problem

Architecture: The napi-specific subsystems that SessionManager methods reach for (agent_loop, scheduler engine, footer poller, GLOBAL_CHUNK_CALLBACK, LoopStore) STAY napi-side and are injected via a new `SessionManagerHooks` trait stored as `hooks: ArcSwap<Arc<dyn SessionManagerHooks>>` on SessionManager. The default hooks (NoopSessionManagerHooks) are no-ops so the fspec binary in RPC-044 gets a fully-default SessionManager with no behaviour. The napi side at startup calls `SessionManager::instance().set_hooks(Arc::new(NapiSessionManagerHooks))` to install the JS-bridge behaviour. Trait methods needed for this card: spawn_agent_loop, spawn_scheduler, ensure_scheduler_running_for_loop, spawn_footer_poller, stop_footer_poller, cleanup_session_loops, emit_isolation_state_change

Architecture: The attachment cites SessionManager at lines 3141-4025 but the actual span is 2135-3013 (confirmed by grep of `^pub struct SessionManager` and the matching closing `}`). Methods documented in the attachment exist at slightly shifted lines: instance() at 2246 (not 3250), create_session_with_id at 2264 (not 3268), create_isolated_session_with_id at 2538 (not 3542), list_sessions at 2798 (not 3802), destroy_session at 2939 (not 3943), supervisor delegation at 2989-3011 (not 3993-4013). The ~1100-line offset is consistent — the napi file accumulated ~1100 LOC of additional code (tests, helpers) between the attachment authoring date (2026-05-19) and today (2026-05-21). All implementation work uses the actual current line numbers

Architecture: IsolatedSessionResult conversion strategy — the `#[napi(object)] pub struct IsolatedSessionResult` at codelet/napi/src/session_manager.rs:5258-5267 STAYS in napi (it carries the JS-bridge shape). The moved SessionManager::create_isolated_session_with_id returns `codelet_rpc_types::IsolatedSessionInfo` (already lifted by RPC-036). NAPI provides `impl From<codelet_rpc_types::IsolatedSessionInfo> for IsolatedSessionResult` so the #[napi] free function `session_manager_create_isolated` just maps the result. The TS surface is byte-stable

Architecture: Following the RPC-039 review-findings pattern, this card adds new dependency-rule tests at codelet/sessions/tests/session_manager_shape.rs that mirror background_session_shape.rs — each Gherkin scenario gets one `#[test] fn scenario_*()` with `@step` comments matching every Gherkin step verbatim. We do NOT add new clippy passes here (the same `#![allow(clippy::expect_used, ...)]` carry-overs from napi will need re-tightening — explicitly out of scope, tracked by RPC-042). The new shape test file MUST be added to coverage with accurate line ranges to avoid the line-drift class of bug found in the RPC-039 review (every scenario's testLines must point at the actual #[test] fn span, not a guesstimate)
