Given the same session s-1 with backend.get_thinking_level returning ThinkingLevel::High, after the spawned task completes, AgentViewStore.thinking_level_for(s-1) folds to Some(ThinkingLevel::High) via Action::ThinkingLevelLoaded

Given an App with one open session s-1, when input "/thinking gibberish" is submitted, then s-1's scrollback contains the line "[error] unknown thinking level: gibberish" AND backend.set_thinking_level is NOT called AND no dialog is pushed
Given an App with one open session s-1, when input "/thinking" (bare) is submitted, then the ThinkingLevelDialog is pushed onto the Compositor (RPC-022 parity, no regression)

rules.text: parse_slash_command MUST recognise `/thinking <arg>` where <arg> is off|low|med|medium|high (case-insensitive) and return SlashCommandParse::SetThinkingLevel(ThinkingLevel) without opening the ThinkingLevelDialog

parse_slash_command MUST recognise `/thinking <unknown>` (anything other than off|low|med|medium|high) and return SlashCommandParse::InvalidThinkingLevel(other) so the dispatcher can emit `[error] unknown thinking level: {other}` into the focused session's scrollback
Bare `/thinking` (no arg, with or without trailing whitespace-only suffix) MUST continue to return SlashCommandParse::OpenThinkingDialog (RPC-022 behaviour is preserved)

On SetThinkingLevel(level), handle_input_submitted MUST route through handle_thinking_level_selected so backend.set_thinking_level + backend.get_thinking_level fire AND AgentViewStore.thinking_level_for(session_id) is refreshed via Action::ThinkingLevelLoaded — the text is NOT forwarded to backend.send_input and NO dialog is pushed

On InvalidThinkingLevel(other), handle_input_submitted MUST push `[error] unknown thinking level: {other}` into the focused session's scrollback via navigator.agent.push_line — the text is NOT forwarded to backend.send_input and NO backend.set_thinking_level call fires

architectureNotes.text: Wire shape: new `resume_session` trait method on SessionManagerHandle with a default impl that performs: (1) Uuid::parse_str(session_id), (2) codelet_core::persistence::load_session(uuid), (3) codelet_core::persistence::get_session_message_envelopes(uuid), (4) build TokenRestoreState from manifest.token_usage, (5) self.restore_session_messages(session_id, envelopes), (6) self.restore_session_token_state(session_id, state). Errors at any step propagate as Result<(), String>.

Lift target: `get_session_message_envelopes(uuid: Uuid) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>` becomes a public free function in `codelet/core/src/persistence/manifest.rs` mirroring the existing `get_session_messages` function above it. The implementation ports the body of `persistence_get_session_message_envelopes` from `codelet/napi/src/persistence/napi_bindings.rs:729` minus the napi::Error wrapping (use plain String errors). The NAPI binding becomes a one-line delegate `codelet_core::persistence::get_session_message_envelopes(uuid).map_err(Error::from_reason)`.

Action plumbing: extend the components::Action enum with one new variant: `SessionResumeComplete(SessionId)`. The error path re-uses the existing `EmitSessionNotice(SessionId, String)` variant (RPC-046) so the failure notice arrives via the standard scrollback-routing path.

Dispatch wiring: extend `app/dispatch_rpc026.rs::handle_attach_to_session` to spawn a tokio task that awaits `backend.resume_session(session_id)` and dispatches either `Action::SessionResumeComplete(id)` (Ok) or `Action::EmitSessionNotice(id, format!("[error] /resume failed: {e}"))` (Err). A NEW `handle_session_resume_complete` helper in the same file spawns a second task that calls `backend.get_buffered_output(id, 1000)` and replays each returned chunk as `Action::ChunkReceived(id, chunk)`. App::dispatch gains one match arm `Action::SessionResumeComplete(id) => self.handle_session_resume_complete(id.clone())`. dispatch_rpc026.rs stays under 300 LoC because the additions are ~30 LoC.

RPC surface: `FspecService::resume_session(self, ctx, session_id: SessionId) -> Result<(), String>` is added in `codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs`; `FspecServiceImpl::resume_session` delegates through `self.inner.session_manager()?.resume_session(&session_id)`; default-when-no-handle returns Ok(()). Both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend gain `async fn resume_session(&self, session_id: SessionId) -> Result<()>` as one-line delegates following the same shape as their existing `clear_history` / `compact_session` impls. The StubSessionManagerHandle override increments an AtomicU64 call counter so cross-transport parity tests can assert call counts.

RPC-049.description: Phase 6.4: Extend ResumeSessionView (RPC-026) to perform durable restore on selection: backend.restore_session_messages(session_id, envelopes) + backend.restore_session_token_state(session_id, state). Then re-subscribe and seed scrollback from persistence. Mirrors TS handleResumeMode flow triggered by triggerResumeModeInit (AgentView.tsx line 2736).

examples.text: Given an App wired to a MockBackend with sessions ['s-1', 's-2'] and ResumeSessionView open with row 0 (s-1) selected, when the user presses Enter, then backend.resume_session(s-1) is called exactly once within 1 second AND open_sessions contains s-1 (append-or-focus semantics from RPC-026 preserved).

Given a MockBackend whose resume_session(s-1) returns Ok(()) and whose buffered_output for s-1 is [StreamChunk::text("hello"), StreamChunk::text("world")], when AttachToSession(s-1) is dispatched, then within 1 second the SessionContext for s-1 contains two scrollback chunks whose text is 'hello' and 'world'.

Given a MockBackend whose resume_session(s-1) returns Err("corrupt manifest"), when AttachToSession(s-1) is dispatched, then within 1 second the SessionContext for s-1 contains a scrollback line whose text equals '[error] /resume failed: corrupt manifest' AND get_buffered_output is NEVER called.

Given a MockBackend with a scripted sequence of envelopes for session s-1 ([{type:'user',text:'hi'},{type:'assistant',text:'hello'}]) loaded into buffered_output, when the user picks s-1 from /resume, then the scrollback (after the full async chain completes) shows BOTH the user and assistant lines in order.

Cross-transport parity: build a SharedFspecService with the StubSessionManagerHandle; construct EmbeddedFspecBackend AND WebSocketFspecBackend over the same service; call backend.resume_session(SessionId("stub-1")) through each; assert both return Ok(()) and the StubSessionManagerHandle's internal resume_session call counter increments to 2 (once per transport).

codelet_core::persistence::get_session_message_envelopes(uuid) for a non-existent session returns Err("..."); for an existing manifest with N messages returns Ok(Vec<String>) with N JSON envelopes (each parseable via serde_json::from_str into a serde_json::Value with a 'message' field). The lifted free function produces byte-identical output to the previous NAPI binding for the same input manifest.

Source-shape regression: a grep over `codelet/fspec-tui/src/` finds zero matches for `codelet_napi`; every file under `codelet/fspec-tui/src/` (including the new dispatch_rpc049.rs if introduced) is < 300 LoC; `codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch.rs` is < 300 LoC after the new AttachToSession + SessionResumeComplete arms are wired.

rules.text: A new `resume_session(session_id) -> Result<(), String>` method MUST exist on SessionManagerHandle (with a default impl that orchestrates load_session + get_session_message_envelopes + restore_session_messages + restore_session_token_state), on FspecService (tarpc), and on the FspecBackend trait — implemented as a one-line delegate on both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend.

`get_session_message_envelopes(session_id: Uuid) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>` MUST be lifted from `codelet/napi/src/persistence/napi_bindings.rs` into `codelet_core::persistence::manifest` (or messages) as a public free function; the NAPI binding `persistence_get_session_message_envelopes` becomes a thin one-line delegate that preserves the byte-identical TS surface (synthetic compaction summaries + blob rehydration behaviour included).

The ResumeSessionView's `Selected(SessionId)` outcome (already dispatched as `Action::AttachToSession`) MUST be extended so that AFTER the synchronous open_sessions move/append, a tokio task is spawned that awaits `backend.resume_session(session_id)` and routes the outcome via two new actions: `Action::SessionResumeComplete(SessionId)` on success and `Action::EmitSessionNotice(session_id, "[error] /resume failed: {reason}")` on failure.

On `Action::SessionResumeComplete(session_id)`, App::dispatch MUST spawn a tokio task that calls `backend.get_buffered_output(session_id, 1000).await` and re-emits each returned chunk into the action bus as `Action::ChunkReceived(session_id, chunk)` — so the resumed session's scrollback is seeded from the backend's replay buffer.

When `Action::AttachToSession` fires for a session already present in open_sessions, the existing focus-move semantics from RPC-026 are preserved AND `backend.resume_session` is STILL called (idempotent re-restore is acceptable parity with the TS handleResumeMode). The resumed-chunk re-seed is NOT deduplicated against existing scrollback entries — replay buffer arrival follows the same path as fresh streaming chunks.

MockBackend in `codelet/fspec-tui/tests/common/mod.rs` MUST gain (a) `resume_session_calls()` counter + `last_resume_session()` accessor, (b) `set_resume_session_error(message)` to script the Err branch, (c) `set_buffered_output(chunks)` to script the get_buffered_output replay set used by SessionResumeComplete, and (d) full `async fn resume_session(&self, id: SessionId) -> Result<()>` impl.

Cross-transport parity: `resume_session(id)` round-trips identically across EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend against the SAME StubSessionManagerHandle (the StubSessionManagerHandle override returns Ok(()) deterministically); the RPC-037 cross-transport parity test suite is extended with a scenario asserting parity for the new method.

Source-shape regression: no new file under `codelet/fspec-tui/src/` exceeds 300 LoC; `dispatch.rs` stays under the 300-LoC ceiling — the new AttachToSession / SessionResumeComplete arms are factored into a new `app/dispatch_rpc049.rs` helper file (or, if minimal, an addition to `dispatch_rpc026.rs` that keeps it under 300 LoC). codelet-fspec-tui MUST NOT depend on codelet-napi (RPC-002 invariant).

architectureNotes.text: Wire shape: Add two new Actions to `components::Action`: `AttachWorkUnitToSession(String)` (board → app), `WorkUnitAttached(SessionId, WorkUnitContext)` (spawned-task → app), `WorkUnitDetached(SessionId)` (spawned-task → app). Update `app/dispatch.rs` to route the new variants through new helpers in `app/dispatch_rpc050.rs` (mirrors the dispatch_rpc026/dispatch_rpc046 factoring pattern).

Store extension: `AgentViewStore` gains a `work_unit_context_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, WorkUnitContext>` field with accessors `work_unit_context_for(&SessionId) -> Option<&WorkUnitContext>`, `set_work_unit_context(SessionId, WorkUnitContext)`, `clear_work_unit_context(&SessionId)`. Also gain `reset_token_state(&SessionId)` that wipes the entry in `token_state_by_session`. Both blocks added in `store/agent_view.rs` to keep new files under the 300 LoC ceiling.

BoardView Enter trigger: BoardView.handle_event already emits Action::EnterWorkUnit on Enter. To preserve the existing lazy-session-creation flow AND add the attach-to-session semantics, App::dispatch's EnterWorkUnit arm gains a follow-up step that spawns backend.set_work_unit_context(session, Some(ctx)) — fired immediately when current_session is Some, or deferred to the SessionCreated arm when current_session is None (lazy-created). The new Action::AttachWorkUnitToSession variant remains the explicit path used by Slot 4 dialog/UI test paths; it dispatches the same backend round-trip without altering navigation.

SessionHeader read path: `views/agent.rs::render_with_store` currently passes `store.current_work_unit_id()` / `current_work_unit_status()` to SessionHeader. Replace with per-session lookup: when `store.work_unit_context_for(sid)` returns Some(ctx), use ctx.id + ctx.status; otherwise fall back to the legacy `current_work_unit_id` / `current_work_unit_status` so RPC-029 chrome-parity tests keep passing. The fallback is also what powers the initial chrome on bootstrap before the backend round-trip lands.

/detach handler shape: replace the current `other => [notice] not yet implemented` fallthrough for `SlashCommandAction::Detach` with a concrete arm in `dispatch_rpc020.rs::handle_slash_command`. The arm delegates to a new `handle_slash_detach` helper in `dispatch_rpc050.rs` to keep `dispatch_rpc020.rs` under 300 LoC. The helper: (1) returns silently if `current_session()` is None, (2) emits `Action::EmitSessionNotice(s, '[notice] /detach: no work unit attached')` when no binding exists, (3) otherwise spawns backend.set_work_unit_context(s, None) and routes Ok→`Action::WorkUnitDetached(s)` / Err→`Action::EmitSessionNotice(s, '[error] /detach failed: {e}')`. The WorkUnitDetached arm in App::dispatch clears the binding, resets scrollback via `navigator.agent.reset_scrollback`, and calls the new `agent_view_store.reset_token_state(&s)`.

MockBackend extensions: add `work_unit_context_calls()` counter + `last_set_work_unit_context() -> Option<(SessionId, Option<WorkUnitContext>)>` + `set_work_unit_context_error(msg)` to script the Err branch + internal HashMap mapping session→ctx so `get_work_unit_context` reads back what `set_work_unit_context` wrote (round-trip parity with the production stub). Implement the trait methods over those state slots.

RPC-050.description: Phase 6.4 + 6.6: BoardView click/keypress on a work unit dispatches AttachSessionToWorkUnit(work_unit_id). Dispatcher calls backend.set_work_unit_context(session_id, Some(ctx)). SessionHeader renders the work-unit chip from backend.get_work_unit_context(session_id). SlashCommandAction::Detach calls backend.set_work_unit_context(session_id, None) + cleanup (clear conversation/tokenUsage). Mirrors TS AgentView.tsx line 2764 detachFromWorkUnit + prepareForNewSession.

examples.text: Given an App with open session s-1 (current) and BoardStore containing AUTH-001(implementing), when Action::AttachWorkUnitToSession("AUTH-001") is dispatched, then within 1s backend.set_work_unit_context is called exactly once with (s-1, Some(WorkUnitContext{id:"AUTH-001", title:"AUTH-001", status:"implementing"})) AND Navigator.active_view == Agent AND AgentViewStore.work_unit_context_for(s-1) returns Some(ctx)

Given an App with open session s-1 bound to work unit AUTH-001, when the AgentView is rendered against an 80x10 TestBackend, then the rendered top row contains the substring `(AUTH-001: implementing)` so the SessionHeader chip is visible to the user

Given an App with open session s-1 bound to AUTH-001 and a MockBackend whose set_work_unit_context returns Ok, when the user submits `/detach` then within 1s backend.set_work_unit_context is called with (s-1, None) AND AgentViewStore.work_unit_context_for(s-1) returns None AND s-1's scrollback chunk_count becomes 0 AND s-1's TokenState equals TokenState::default()

Given an App with NO open session, when SlashCommandSelected(Detach) is dispatched, then backend.set_work_unit_context is NEVER called AND no session's scrollback is mutated (the no-session notice goes to the no-op path that maps to the action bus only)

Given an App with open session s-1 NOT bound to any work unit, when SlashCommandSelected(Detach) is dispatched, then within 1s s-1's scrollback contains a chunk whose text equals `[notice] /detach: no work unit attached` AND backend.set_work_unit_context is NEVER called

Given an App with open session s-1 bound to AUTH-001 and a MockBackend whose set_work_unit_context returns Err("corrupt manifest"), when /detach is submitted, then within 1s s-1's scrollback contains a chunk whose text equals `[error] /detach failed: corrupt manifest` AND AgentViewStore.work_unit_context_for(s-1) STILL returns Some(ctx)

Cross-transport: build SharedFspecService with StubSessionManagerHandle; build EmbeddedFspecBackend AND WebSocketFspecBackend over the same service; call set_work_unit_context(Some(ctx)) then get_work_unit_context() then set_work_unit_context(None) through each backend; assert StubSessionManagerHandle's set_work_unit_context counter increments by 4 (twice per transport) and get returns the previously-stored ctx for each transport

Source-shape: a grep over `codelet/fspec-tui/src/` finds zero matches for `codelet_napi`; every file under `codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/`, `codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/`, and `codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/` (including the new `dispatch_rpc050.rs`) is < 300 LoC; `app/dispatch.rs` and `app/dispatch_rpc020.rs` remain < 300 LoC after the new Attach/Detach arms are wired
Given an App with NO open session and BoardStore containing AUTH-001, when Action::AttachWorkUnitToSession("AUTH-001") is dispatched, then backend.set_work_unit_context is NEVER called (silent no-op)

rules.text: BoardView Enter on a work unit dispatches Action::AttachWorkUnitToSession(work_unit_id), which calls backend.set_work_unit_context(session_id, Some(ctx)) and navigates to AgentView

On success of backend.set_work_unit_context(Some), the dispatcher emits Action::WorkUnitAttached(SessionId, WorkUnitContext) which folds the context into AgentViewStore.work_unit_context_by_session[session_id]

SessionHeader renders the work-unit chip (id + status) from AgentViewStore.work_unit_context_for(session_id) when Some, falling back to the legacy current_work_unit_id/current_work_unit_status fields when None (so RPC-029 chrome tests keep passing)

SlashCommandAction::Detach with an active session AND a bound work unit calls backend.set_work_unit_context(session, None), then on Ok dispatches Action::WorkUnitDetached(session) which clears the per-session work-unit binding, resets the focused session's scrollback (parity with TS prepareForNewSession), and resets the per-session TokenState
/detach with NO active session emits `[notice] /detach: no active session` and DOES NOT call the backend
/detach with an active session but NO work unit attached emits `[notice] /detach: no work unit attached` and DOES NOT call the backend
On Err from backend.set_work_unit_context(None), the dispatcher emits `[error] /detach failed: {reason}` into the originating session's scrollback and does NOT reset the local binding or scrollback

Cross-transport parity: set_work_unit_context(Some) and set_work_unit_context(None) round-trip identically across EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend against the same StubSessionManagerHandle
Source-shape regression: no new file under codelet/fspec-tui/src/ exceeds 300 LoC; new dispatch arms factored into app/dispatch_rpc050.rs; codelet-fspec-tui MUST NOT depend on codelet-napi
AttachWorkUnitToSession with NO current session is a silent no-op (no backend call, no scrollback mutation — there is no session to push a notice into)

architectureNotes.text: The Esc cascade is implemented in three layers: (a) App::handle_event runs compositor.handle_event FIRST so HelpDialog/ModelSelectorDialog/ThinkingLevelDialog/ConfirmDialog consume Esc themselves before AgentView::handle_event runs (level 2); (b) AgentView::handle_event runs handle_mode_view_key (resume/search dismiss — level 3) then handle_popup_key (slash/file dismiss — level 1) — order doesn't matter for Esc because mode-views and popups are mutually exclusive; (c) The default Esc branch in AgentView::handle_event is extended with the interrupt check: if AgentViewStore.session_status_for(current_session) is Running or Compacting, spawn backend.interrupt(session_id) and return Consumed without emitting BackToBoard

Wire shape: Add Action::AgentEscPressed (no payload). AgentView's Esc branch in views/agent/dispatch.rs replaces the unconditional `self.emit(Action::BackToBoard)` with `self.emit(Action::AgentEscPressed)`. App::dispatch routes the new variant through a new file `app/dispatch_rpc051.rs::handle_agent_esc_pressed`. The helper reads `agent_view_store.current_session().cloned()` then `agent_view_store.session_status_for(&id)`. If status is Running or Compacting, spawn `backend.interrupt(id)` and do NOT change navigator state. Otherwise dispatch Action::BackToBoard. With no current session, dispatch Action::BackToBoard.

Tests live in codelet/fspec-tui/tests/keyboard_cascade_rpc051.rs. They drive AgentView via crossterm Esc/Ctrl+R/Shift+Up/Shift+Down KeyEvents through App::handle_event (so the compositor → AgentView routing is real). The MockBackend already exposes interrupt_calls() / last_interrupt() — no new helper needed. SessionStatus seeding uses `agent_view_store_mut().set_session_status(sid, status)` (RPC-045).

RPC-051.description: Phase 6.5: Shift+up/down history already wired in RPC-025. Ctrl+R already wired to OpenSearchView in dispatch.rs (line 195). Extend Esc priority cascade: when session is running, call backend.interrupt(session_id) before falling through to BackToBoard. Add tests for cascade priority: popup > mode-view > dialog > interrupt > navigate-back.

examples.text: Esc level 1 — popup dismiss: Given an AgentView with the slash command popup open AND session s-1 in Running status, when Esc is pressed, then the slash popup closes AND backend.interrupt is NEVER called AND no BackToBoard action is emitted

Esc level 2 — dialog dismiss: Given the compositor has a HelpDialog pushed on top AND session s-1 in Running status, when Esc is pressed, then the HelpDialog is removed by the compositor BEFORE the AgentView sees the key AND backend.interrupt is NEVER called AND no BackToBoard action is emitted

Esc level 3 — mode-view dismiss: Given an AgentView with resume_view open AND session s-1 in Running status, when Esc is pressed, then Action::CloseResumeView is emitted AND resume_view becomes None AND backend.interrupt is NEVER called AND no BackToBoard action is emitted

Esc level 4 — interrupt running session: Given an AgentView with NO popup, NO dialog, NO mode-view AND current session s-1 has SessionStatus::Running, when Esc is pressed, then within 1 second backend.interrupt is called exactly once with s-1 AND no Action::BackToBoard is emitted AND Navigator.active_view stays at ViewMode::Agent

Esc level 4 — interrupt compacting session: Given an AgentView with NO popup/dialog/mode-view AND current session s-1 has SessionStatus::Compacting, when Esc is pressed, then within 1 second backend.interrupt is called exactly once with s-1 AND Navigator.active_view stays at ViewMode::Agent

Esc level 5 — idle session navigates back: Given an AgentView with NO popup/dialog/mode-view AND current session s-1 has SessionStatus::Idle, when Esc is pressed, then Action::BackToBoard is emitted AND backend.interrupt is NEVER called AND Navigator.active_view becomes ViewMode::Board

Esc level 5 — no session navigates back: Given an AgentView with NO popup/dialog/mode-view AND NO current session, when Esc is pressed, then Action::BackToBoard is emitted AND backend.interrupt is NEVER called

Ctrl+R focuses search input on mount: Given an AgentView with NO popup/dialog/mode-view, when Ctrl+R is pressed and then the character 'h' is typed, then SearchHistoryView is open with query=='h' AND Action::SearchHistory("h") was dispatched

Shift+↑/↓ snapshot+walk+restore parity: Given session s-1 with persistence_get_history scripted to ['first', 'second', 'third'] AND the live input contains 'draft-text', when Shift+↑ is pressed once, then the input becomes 'first' AND cached_draft=='draft-text'; when Shift+↑ is pressed again, the input becomes 'second'; when Shift+↓ is pressed, the input becomes 'first'; when Shift+↓ is pressed again, the input becomes 'draft-text' AND recall_index becomes None

rules.text: When Esc is pressed in the AgentView the dispatch path follows a 5-level priority cascade: (1) slash/file popup dismiss > (2) compositor dialog dismiss > (3) resume/search mode-view dismiss > (4) interrupt running session > (5) BackToBoard navigation

When Esc reaches AgentView::handle_event with no popup and no mode view active AND the current session's SessionStatus is Running or Compacting, the dispatcher spawns backend.interrupt(session_id) and consumes the event WITHOUT emitting Action::BackToBoard

When Esc reaches AgentView::handle_event with no popup and no mode view active AND the current session's SessionStatus is Idle/Paused/Interrupted/Cleared (or unknown), the dispatcher emits Action::BackToBoard and does NOT call backend.interrupt
When Esc reaches AgentView::handle_event with NO active session (current_session() returns None), the dispatcher emits Action::BackToBoard (silent no-op for interrupt)

Ctrl+R while no popup/dialog/mode-view is active opens SearchHistoryView; the view's text input field is focused on mount so typing immediately filters history (already wired by RPC-026 — verified by test)

Shift+↑ first press snapshots the live MultiLineInput draft into cached_draft and asynchronously fetches history; subsequent Shift+↑ walk back through the cached snapshot and clamp at the tail (already wired by RPC-025 — verified by test)
Shift+↓ in recall mode at index 0 restores the cached_draft and clears recall_index; Shift+↓ in live-draft mode (recall_index=None) is a no-op (already wired by RPC-025 — verified by test)
Source-shape: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/dispatch.rs (after the interrupt cascade is wired) stays under the 300-LoC ceiling; codelet-fspec-tui MUST NOT depend on codelet-napi

RPC-051.title: Keyboard shortcut parity (Shift+up/down history, Ctrl+R search, Esc interrupt cascade)

Emit Action::PendingInputChanged from views/agent/dispatch.rs after input.handle_event when buffer text changed (compare before/after value).

Create codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc052.rs hosting handle_pending_input_changed (debounce + spawn) and handle_seed_pending_input + spawn_hydrate_pending_input. Register pub mod in app/mod.rs.

Add field pending_input_save_handle: Option<JoinHandle<()>> to App in src/app/state.rs. Abort previous handle on each PendingInputChanged then spawn task that sleeps 300ms and calls backend.set_pending_input.
Wire hydration into Action::SessionCreated arm in app/dispatch.rs and into handle_attach_to_session in app/dispatch_rpc026.rs (spawn_hydrate_pending_input).

Extend MockBackend in tests/common/mod.rs with: pending_input scripted Option<String>, pending_input_calls counter, last_set_pending_input slot, get_pending_input_error / set_pending_input_error scripting. Implement FspecBackend get/set_pending_input on MockBackend.
Add backend.set_pending_input(session, None) clear after InputSubmitted in app/dispatch_rpc020.rs::handle_input_submitted (spawn after send_input + persistence).
Integration test file: codelet/fspec-tui/tests/pending_input_durability_rpc052.rs with @step comments mapped 1:1 to feature scenarios.

RPC-052.description: Phase 6.7: MultiLineInput calls backend.set_pending_input(session_id, text) on every change (debounced). Already partially implemented via SessionContext.input_draft + handle_session_cycle (dispatch_rpc024.rs). This card upgrades it to durable backend-backed storage so drafts survive session reload. App::dispatch calls backend.get_pending_input(session_id) on session activation and seeds the input.

examples.text: User types 'hello' over 250ms then waits 350ms; backend.set_pending_input(s, Some("hello")) is called exactly once
User types 'h', 'i' in two rapid edits within 100ms; only one debounced backend save fires after 300ms idle with the final value 'hi'
User types a draft on session A, kills fspec, restarts, attaches to session A — the live input is restored to the draft text
User submits the input via Enter — the durable draft is cleared (backend.set_pending_input(session, None) is called) and the next session activation does not restore old draft
User switches via Shift+Right to a session whose backend pending_input is Some('partial sentence') — the live MultiLineInput shows 'partial sentence'
User switches to a session whose backend pending_input is None — the live MultiLineInput shows an empty buffer
Backend.set_pending_input returns Err — UI remains responsive and no scrollback notice is emitted
Rapid Shift+Left/Right cycling between two sessions immediately reflects each session's last typed draft (mirrors RPC-024 behaviour preserved by SessionContext.input_draft)
Hydration completes 100ms after the user has already switched away to a different session — the late result is dropped and the now-focused session's input is NOT overwritten

rules.text: Typing into MultiLineInput triggers Action::PendingInputChanged on every edit
Action::PendingInputChanged is debounced by 300ms before calling backend.set_pending_input(session, Some(text))
A second PendingInputChanged within the debounce window cancels the previous pending save
On session activation (SessionCreated/AttachToSession/SessionPrev/SessionNext) the App spawns backend.get_pending_input(session) and seeds the live MultiLineInput when the result is Some(text)
Successful Action::InputSubmitted spawns backend.set_pending_input(session, None) to clear the durable draft
SessionContext.input_draft mirrors the live MultiLineInput buffer so handle_session_cycle still works without a backend round-trip on every keystroke
Errors from set_pending_input or get_pending_input are silently dropped (logged via tracing); they never panic the UI or emit notice/scrollback
Hydration on session activation only seeds the live input when the activated session is still the focused session at the moment the result arrives

RPC-052.title: Pending-input draft persistence on session switch

architectureNotes.text: New Action variants in components/mod.rs: Action::OpenPauseDialog{session_id, state}, Action::OpenHitlDialog{session_id, request}, Action::PauseConfirmed{session_id, accept: bool}, Action::PauseTriple{session_id, choice: ApprovalChoice}, Action::PauseResumed{session_id}, Action::HitlSubmitted{session_id, response: HitlResponse}, Action::PauseCleared{session_id} (sent by chunk dispatcher on Running/Idle to pop any mounted dialog)

Create codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/pause_dialog.rs hosting PauseDialog (priority Critical, uses Accent::Yellow via dialog_theme::render_dialog, 2-row layout for Confirm and 3-row layout for Triple). PauseDialog::new(session_id, state, action_tx) emits Action::PauseConfirmed/Action::PauseTriple/Action::PauseResumed when Enter/Esc fires; pop callback removes itself from Compositor via PAUSE_DIALOG_ID constant.

Create codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/hitl_dialog.rs hosting HitlDialog (priority Critical, uses Accent::Cyan via dialog_theme::render_dialog). Renders question as title, header as first body row, options as labelled rows (hotkey letter prefix), and an optional free-text input row when allow_text_input. Tab/Down advances selection (looping through options + free-text row when present), Enter submits, hotkey letters (a..z, case-insensitive) jump directly to the matching option AND submit, Esc dismisses without submit. HITL_DIALOG_ID constant for idempotent push and self-pop.

Create codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc053.rs hosting impl App methods: handle_pause_chunk(session_id) — fired from dispatch_rpc045 SessionStateChange{Paused} arm, spawns parallel backend.get_pause_state + get_hitl_request and dispatches OpenPauseDialog OR OpenHitlDialog (HITL wins on tie); handle_open_pause_dialog(session, state) — idempotent compositor push; handle_open_hitl_dialog(session, request) — idempotent compositor push; handle_pause_confirmed/handle_pause_triple/handle_pause_resumed — fire-and-forget backend writes, pop dialog before await (best-effort UX); handle_hitl_submitted — fire-and-forget backend.send_hitl_response, pop dialog before await; handle_pause_cleared — pop any mounted PauseDialog/HitlDialog for the session.

Wire into dispatch_rpc045::handle_stream_chunk_state_updates: branch SessionStateChange{state} on Running/Idle to dispatch Action::PauseCleared (so any mounted dialog is popped on resume), AND on Paused to dispatch a NEW Action::PauseChunkReceived(session_id) which routes through handle_pause_chunk (the parallel get_pause_state/get_hitl_request fetcher). Route both new actions in app/dispatch.rs (or via try_dispatch_rpc053 catch-all helper).

Extend MockBackend in tests/common/mod.rs with: pause_state scripted Mutex<Option<PauseState>>, hitl_request scripted Mutex<Option<HitlRequest>>, per-call counters + last-call captures for pause_resume, pause_confirm, pause_triple, send_hitl_response, get_pause_state, get_hitl_request. Helpers: script_pause_state, script_hitl_request, set_get_pause_state_error, set_get_hitl_request_error, set_pause_confirm_error, set_pause_triple_error, set_pause_resume_error, set_send_hitl_response_error. Implement FspecBackend overrides on MockBackend (they currently use the trait defaults).

Integration test file: codelet/fspec-tui/tests/pause_hitl_rpc053.rs with @step comments mapped 1:1 to feature scenarios. Use #[tokio::test(flavor='current_thread')] consistent with rpc049/rpc050 tests. Drive Action::ChunkReceived(s, SessionStateChange{Paused}) to fire the chunk path; assert compositor.contains(PAUSE_DIALOG_ID) or HITL_DIALOG_ID after the fetcher tasks drain (use tokio::task::yield_now or short sleep).

Source-shape regression test asserting source-shape invariants is merged into codelet/fspec-tui/tests/pause_hitl_rpc053.rs (test `dispatch_rpc053_hosts_pause_hitl_helpers` at the bottom of the file) to keep the 1:1 feature ↔ test-file mapping enforced by fspec coverage. The test asserts: dispatch_rpc053.rs exists; pub mod dispatch_rpc053 declared in app/mod.rs; pub mod pause_dialog and pub mod hitl_dialog declared in components/mod.rs (file existence is transitively required for these declarations to compile); app/dispatch.rs stays under 300 logical lines.

RPC-053.description: Phase 6.8: ConfirmDialog reads backend.get_pause_state(session_id). Two-choice: backend.pause_confirm(session_id, accept). Three-choice: backend.pause_triple(session_id, choice). Resume: backend.pause_resume(session_id). New HitlDialog reads backend.get_hitl_request(session_id) → on submit calls backend.send_hitl_response(session_id, response). Currently in BackgroundSession: pause_state (line 539), pause_response_tx/rx (542-543), hitl_response_tx/rx (550-551), hitl_request (555).

examples.text: User types 'rm -rf /' which triggers a Confirm pause; the agent emits SessionStateChange{Paused}; the dispatcher polls and opens a 2-button PauseDialog showing the prompt; user presses Enter on 'Accept' → backend.pause_confirm(session, true) is called exactly once and the dialog is removed

User types a sensitive command that triggers a Triple pause (Approve/Approve-Session/Deny); user presses Right twice and Enter to select 'Deny' → backend.pause_triple(session, ApprovalChoice::Deny) is called exactly once and the dialog is removed
PauseDialog is open with focus on 'Accept'; user presses Esc → backend.pause_resume(session) is called exactly once and the dialog is removed; backend.pause_confirm is NEVER called

Agent loop's request_user_input handler sets hitl_request and emits SessionStateChange{Paused}; the dispatcher polls and opens HitlDialog with 2 options 'Yes' and 'No'; user presses 'a' (hotkey for 'Yes') → backend.send_hitl_response(session, HitlResponse{id:req.id, value:'Yes'}) is called exactly once and the dialog is removed

HitlDialog with allow_text_input=true is open; user presses Tab until the free-text row is focused, types 'maybe later', and presses Enter → backend.send_hitl_response(session, HitlResponse{id:req.id, value:'maybe later'}) is called exactly once and the dialog is removed

HitlDialog is open; user presses Esc → the dialog is removed; backend.send_hitl_response is NEVER called (the agent loop stays blocked until either a new HITL request arrives OR a follow-up user submit fires)
SessionStateChange{Paused} arrives but BOTH backend.get_pause_state and backend.get_hitl_request return None (race/stale chunk) → no dialog is pushed and no further backend call is made
SessionStateChange{Paused} arrives twice in rapid succession (e.g. agent toggles status) → only ONE PauseDialog is mounted on the Compositor (idempotent push)

PauseDialog is open and SessionStateChange{Running} arrives (agent loop received its response and resumed) → the dialog is popped automatically; subsequent Pause dialogs for the next pause cycle work cleanly

Backend.pause_confirm returns Err('network blip') after the user clicks Accept → the dialog is still popped (best-effort), no scrollback notice is emitted, no panic, and the error is logged via tracing
Backend.get_hitl_request returns Err('decode failed') after SessionStateChange{Paused} arrives → no HitlDialog is mounted; the App must not panic and no scrollback notice fires

Two sessions are open (s-1, s-2); s-1 is focused; backend.push_status_change(s-2, Paused) fires AND the SessionStateChange chunk for s-2 routes a polled pause dialog targeting s-2 — the dialog is mounted on the Compositor but the user is free to stay on s-1; the dialog dispatches its actions targeting s-2 (the bound session id) regardless of currently-focused session

rules.text: When the chunk dispatcher receives StreamChunk::SessionStateChange { state: Paused }, the App spawns backend.get_pause_state(session) AND backend.get_hitl_request(session) in parallel and dispatches Action::OpenPauseDialog when get_pause_state returns Some, Action::OpenHitlDialog when get_hitl_request returns Some, or nothing when both return None

Action::OpenPauseDialog{session_id, state} pushes a fresh PauseDialog at Priority::Critical onto the Compositor, idempotent on dialog-id collision (no duplicate push when the dialog is already mounted)

PauseDialog of kind PauseKind::Confirm renders a 2-button layout (Accept / Deny) with Tab/Left/Right cycling focus, Enter committing the focused choice via backend.pause_confirm(session, accept: bool)

PauseDialog of kind PauseKind::Triple renders a 3-button layout (Approve / Approve Session / Deny) with Tab/Left/Right cycling focus, Enter committing the focused choice via backend.pause_triple(session, choice: ApprovalChoice)
Esc on PauseDialog calls backend.pause_resume(session) and pops the dialog from the Compositor (treated as dismiss-without-choosing per the attachment)
Action::OpenHitlDialog{session_id, request} pushes a fresh HitlDialog at Priority::Critical onto the Compositor, idempotent on dialog-id collision
HitlDialog renders the request.question as title, request.header as body text, and one row per HitlOption labelled with a hotkey letter (a, b, c, ...) plus the option label and description
When request.allow_text_input is true HitlDialog renders an additional free-text input row below the options that gains focus on Tab cycling and accepts text edit keystrokes

Pressing the hotkey letter for an option directly submits HitlResponse{ id: request.id, value: option.label } via backend.send_hitl_response and pops the dialog; Enter on the highlighted option does the same
Enter while the free-text row is focused submits HitlResponse{ id: request.id, value: <typed text> } via backend.send_hitl_response and pops the dialog
Esc on HitlDialog pops the dialog but does NOT submit a response (the agent loop stays blocked on wait_for_hitl_response until the user submits OR a new HITL request supersedes)

Errors from backend.get_pause_state, backend.get_hitl_request, backend.pause_confirm, backend.pause_triple, backend.pause_resume, and backend.send_hitl_response are silently logged via tracing — no scrollback notice and no panic

PauseDialog and HitlDialog are mutually exclusive — at most one is mounted at a time per session. When SessionStateChange{Paused} arrives and BOTH backend.get_pause_state and backend.get_hitl_request return Some, the HitlDialog wins (the HITL handler in the agent loop sets hitl_request AND set_status(Paused); pause_state is only set by the tool-pause path)

When SessionStateChange{Running} or SessionStateChange{Idle} arrives, any mounted PauseDialog or HitlDialog for that session is popped from the Compositor (agent loop has resumed or cleared the request server-side; UI should not strand a stale dialog)

userStory.benefit: I can approve or deny tool calls and answer agent questions without leaving the TUI or stalling the agent loop

architectureNotes.text: Architecture: ProviderSettingsView ports the full-screen mode-view pattern from RPC-026's ResumeSessionView. Crate layout: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/{mod.rs (orchestrator: ProviderSettingsView struct, key dispatcher, render outer shell, ProviderSettingsMode enum), list.rs (render_list), detail.rs (render_detail), status_text.rs (DetailStatus → coloured text)}. Each file < 300 LoC per RPC-002 rule [10]

Render shape: render(area, buf) first calls Clear.render(area, buf), then splits the FULL area with Layout::default().direction(Vertical).constraints([Length(1) /* title */, Length(1) /* separator */, Min(0) /* body */, Length(1) /* footer */]).split(area); title row paints via render_title_with_count('Provider Settings', configured_count); footer row paints via render_footer_hint(mode_aware_hint). Body content branches on ProviderSettingsMode (List vs Detail). ConfirmDialog renders LAST as an overlay on top of the body when delete_confirm is Some — same pattern as ResumeSessionView

Slash command registry surgery: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/slash_commands.rs MUST (a) remove the SlashCommandAction::Providers variant from the enum; (b) remove the corresponding name() match arm; (c) remove the SLASH_COMMANDS entry { action: Providers, description: 'Open provider settings' }; (d) leave the SlashCommandAction::Provider variant and { action: Provider, description: 'Configure API providers' } entry intact. Dispatch: codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc020.rs changes the `SlashCommandAction::Provider | SlashCommandAction::Providers =>` arm to `SlashCommandAction::Provider =>` and updates the comment to drop the alias reference

Action enum additions in components/mod.rs: existing variants (OpenProviderSettingsView, CloseProviderSettingsView, ProviderCredentialsLoaded, SaveProviderCredentials { provider_id, api_key }, TestProviderConnection(provider_id), ProviderTestComplete { provider_id, result }, RefreshProviderModels(provider_id), ProviderModelsRefreshed { provider_id, model_count }, DeleteProviderCredentials(provider_id), ProviderSettingsStatus(status)) all stay — they map to the same backend RPCs. New action: Action::ConfirmDeleteProviderCredentials(provider_id) — emitted when the user accepts the ConfirmDialog Primary, replaces the previous direct backend call from list view's 'd' handler

Reuse contract: ConfirmDialog from codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/confirm_dialog.rs (the same component RPC-026 uses for delete-session) is reused verbatim — no new dialog component. Dialog id constant DELETE_PROVIDER_CREDS_DIALOG_ID for idempotent push. ConfirmDialogOutcome::Primary → emit Action::ConfirmDeleteProviderCredentials(provider_id); ConfirmDialogOutcome::Secondary | Cancel → close dialog with no action emitted

Test surgery: (a) codelet/fspec-tui/tests/provider_settings_view_rpc054.rs — rewrite assertions to target ProviderSettingsMode (List vs Detail) instead of the old ProviderSettingsMode { List, EditApiKey }; assert ConfirmDialog flow for 'd' key; (b) codelet/fspec-tui/tests/provider_settings_dispatch_rpc054.rs — keep Action::Open/Close flow; (c) codelet/fspec-tui/tests/source_shape_rpc054.rs — update import-list assertion to require Clear/ensure_visible/wrap_index/ConfirmDialog/render_title_with_count/render_footer_hint and FORBID Borders/Block; (d) tests/rpc054_cross_transport_parity.rs — UNCHANGED (backend surface didn't change); (e) tests/behaviour_parity_rpc065.rs — delete slash_providers_alias_activates_provider_settings_view; (f) tests/slash_debug_rpc055.rs — audit for any /providers references

Filter mode lives as a sub-state on the List variant: ProviderSettingsView holds `filter: String` and `filter_mode: bool` fields. The list mode key dispatcher checks `filter_mode` first — when true, it routes keys to a filter sub-handler (printable→push, Backspace→pop, Enter→exit filter_mode keeping filter, Esc→clear filter + exit filter_mode). When `filter_mode` is false, list mode runs normally but Esc still has a precedence: non-empty filter → clear filter; empty filter → emit Close. This matches TS hooks/useProviderSettingsState.ts (isFilterMode, filter) + inputHandlers/filterModeHandler.ts + listModeHandler.ts:47-67.

RPC-054.description: Phase 7.1: New child view ProviderSettingsView in codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/ mirroring TS src/tui/components/ProviderSettingsScreen.tsx. New RPC methods on FspecService + FspecBackend: list_provider_credentials, set_provider_credentials, test_provider_connection (existing #[napi] at line 7975 of session_manager.rs), refresh_models_cache. Trait additions on SessionManagerHandle. Implementation in codelet-sessions delegates to codelet-providers (already NAPI-free).

Cross-transport parity: a test exercises set_provider_credentials + test_provider_connection through both the embedded transport and the WebSocket transport against StubSessionManagerHandle; both transports increment the same per-stub call counters identically — the view-layer rewrite did not regress the backend RPC surface
User filters providers by typing "an" — list narrows to anthropic only, then Esc clears filter and Esc again closes the view (two-step cascade).
Pressing "/" in filter-capable list mode enters filter mode (does NOT insert the slash anywhere) — matches TS listModeHandler.ts:63-67.
Backspace inside the filter input removes the last typed character; Enter exits filter mode while keeping the filter applied to the visible provider list.

rules.text: The non-existent slash command /providers MUST be removed: delete SlashCommandAction::Providers variant, its name() arm, its SLASH_COMMANDS registry entry, and the | SlashCommandAction::Providers arm in dispatch_rpc020.rs — the TypeScript reference src/tui/utils/slashCommands.ts defines exactly one entry (name: 'provider'), so the Rust enum mirrors it 1:1 with no alias

/blocklist wiring lives in a new app/dispatch_rpc056.rs file (mirrors dispatch_rpc054 pattern), exposing try_dispatch_rpc056 + handle_open_blocklist_view + handle_close_blocklist_view + handle_blocklist_rules_loaded. The orchestrator dispatch_rpc020.rs's handle_slash_command match arm for Blocklist sends Action::OpenBlocklistView via self.action_tx instead of using the catch-all notice fallback.

Category derivation lives as a free function on BlocklistView (or a helper module) so unit tests can pin the heuristic deterministically. Function signature: fn derive_category(pattern: &str) -> &'static str returning "file_path" or "bash".

BlocklistView struct shape is { rules: Vec<BlocklistRuleInfo>, selected_index: usize } — the per-session disabled set is NOT a field on the view. The disabled HashSet<String> lives on AgentViewStore.blocklist_disabled_by_session (HashMap<SessionId, HashSet<String>>) and is passed by reference into BlocklistView::render() and the Navigator's key-handling path, so it persists across view open/close cycles — TS parity with useState<Set<string>> lifted to the AgentView component scope. Toggling emits Action::ToggleBlocklistRule, which dispatch_rpc056::handle_toggle_blocklist_rule folds into the store.

codelet-sessions handle_impl.rs::blocklist_list re-loads system + project configs separately via codelet_tools::blocklist::system_config_path() and codelet_tools::blocklist::project_config_path(cwd) so the source tag (system/project) can be attached per-rule. The function NEVER calls load_blocklist_config (which merges and loses provenance). The cwd is resolved at call time via std::env::current_dir() — mirroring TS's blocklistLoad(cwd) which is also called with the process's current working directory; SessionManager itself does not capture a workspace path at construction time.

architectureNotes.text: MergeConfirmDialog and ConfirmDialog (RPC-026 generic dialog) share the dialog_theme renderer but live in separate modules — MergeConfirmDialog is purpose-built for the merge flow because it carries a SessionChangesSummary payload and emits typed actions (MergeConfirmed, DiscardConfirmed, CancelMergeDialog) rather than the generic Primary/Secondary/Cancel outcomes. The dialog has a stable id 'merge-confirm-dialog' for compositor idempotency.

MergeStrategy is on the wire trait surface for future evolution but the codelet-git crate currently has a single merge algorithm (codelet_git::merge_session). The handle_impl ignores the strategy argument (consumes it via `let _ = strategy;`). The UI passes MergeStrategy::FastForward as a placeholder — when future cards add Squash/ThreeWay support, the wire shape does not need to change.

The conflict-context message format mirrors the TS buildConflictLlmContext helper conceptually: it starts with 'Merge produced conflicts in the following files:' followed by a bullet list of file paths and an 'Effective worktree: <path>' footer when the SessionWorktreeInfo for the session is known. This payload is delivered via Action::SeedPendingInput so it replaces the current input draft and the user can submit it directly — TS parity with pendingAutoSubmitRef. No automatic submit fires in the Rust port (matching the explicit-Enter UX the rest of RPC-030 settled on).

Mapping codelet-git results to the new wire types: MergeResult (files_modified+files_added+files_deleted → conflicts: Vec::new(), status: Success, merge_commit: None) — codelet_git::merge_session does not currently return the commit SHA, so merge_commit is None until codelet-git surfaces it. Conflict detection: codelet_git::apply_session_changes returns GitError::ConflictError { files } — this is mapped to MergeOutcome { status: Conflict, conflicts: files, merge_commit: None }. DiscardResult is mapped to unit-result for the wire (the caller only needs success/failure). list_session_worktrees combines list_worktrees + derive_session_status + a dirty flag derived from get_session_diff non-empty. inspect_session_changes maps SessionResult to SessionChangesSummary by counting files_changed+files_added+files_deleted and listing the commit short SHAs from session_log (or Vec::new() when no commits exist yet).

/merge-worktree slash command wiring lives in a new dispatch_rpc057.rs file (mirrors dispatch_rpc056 pattern). The App.dispatch orchestrator's catch-all already routes through try_dispatch_rpc022 → try_dispatch_rpc053 → try_dispatch_rpc054 → try_dispatch_rpc056 — we extend the chain to also try_dispatch_rpc057 so the orchestrator file stays under the 300-LoC ceiling.

RPC-057 retro (2026-05-27): MergeStrategy and MergeStatus enums were authored with manual `impl Default { fn default() -> Self { Self::<Variant> } }` blocks. The codelet workspace's clippy lint level is `-D warnings` which includes `clippy::derivable_impls` — this lint flags any manual Default impl that COULD be expressed as `#[derive(Default)]` + `#[default]`. The fix is purely mechanical: add `#[derive(Default)]` to the enum declaration, add `#[default]` attribute to the same variant the manual impl returned, delete the manual `impl Default` block. No serialisation behaviour, no public-API surface change, no runtime semantics change — the Default trait implementation is byte-identical via derive vs manual. This regression was discovered during RPC-043 retro followup (2026-05-27) when the codelet-sessions skeleton_invariants test scenario_workspace_lints_are_inherited_and_clippy_passes became runnable for the first time after the RPC-039/040/041 shape-test path regressions were unblocked.

RPC-057.description: Phase 7.4: New RPC methods: merge_session_worktree, discard_session_worktree, prune_orphaned_worktrees, list_session_worktrees, inspect_session_changes. Trait additions on SessionManagerHandle. Implementation in codelet-sessions delegates to codelet-git (already NAPI-free). Confirm dialog UI in codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/ for the merge/discard prompt. On conflicts, equivalent to TS pendingAutoSubmitRef pattern: seed input with conflict context.

MergeStrategy ... MergeStatus`)

rules.text: SessionManagerHandle MUST expose default-impl methods merge_session_worktree, discard_session_worktree, prune_orphaned_worktrees, list_session_worktrees, inspect_session_changes so existing handles compile unchanged. Defaults return safe values (Vec::new, Ok(()), Ok(MergeOutcome::default with NoChanges status)).

StubSessionManagerHandle overrides each of the five methods with deterministic in-memory snapshots and per-call counters (merge_session_worktree_calls, discard_session_worktree_calls, prune_orphaned_worktrees_calls, list_session_worktrees_calls, inspect_session_changes_calls) for cross-transport parity tests.

FspecService (tarpc) declares async fns merge_session_worktree, discard_session_worktree, prune_orphaned_worktrees, list_session_worktrees, inspect_session_changes; FspecServiceImpl routes each through self.inner.session_manager() with safe defaults when no handle is attached.
FspecBackend trait exposes async variants of all five methods returning Result<…>; EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend each forward to the tarpc client.

Five new wire types live in codelet-rpc-types: MergeStrategy enum (FastForward|Squash|ThreeWay, serde tag 'snake_case'), MergeStatus enum (Success|Conflict|NoChanges, serde tag 'snake_case'), MergeOutcome { status, conflicts: Vec<String>, merge_commit: Option<String> }, SessionWorktreeInfo { session_id, worktree_path, base_commit, head_commit, dirty }, SessionChangesSummary { files_changed: u32, insertions: u32, deletions: u32, commits: Vec<String> }. All structs are flat with String/primitive fields so napi(object) compatibility is preserved; enums serialise as strings for napi compatibility.

codelet-sessions handle_impl delegates each method to codelet-git: merge_session_worktree → codelet_git::merge_session, discard_session_worktree → codelet_git::discard_session, prune_orphaned_worktrees → codelet_git::prune_orphaned with the SessionManager's active set, list_session_worktrees → codelet_git::list_worktrees + per-row derive_session_status + dirty heuristic, inspect_session_changes → codelet_git::inspect_session. The MergeStrategy argument is accepted on the trait surface for future evolution but the underlying codelet-git layer uses a single fast-forward-style algorithm (parity with the current TS sessionMergeChanges). The repo_path is resolved at call time via std::env::current_dir() (matching the blocklist_list pattern in RPC-056).

SlashCommandAction::MergeWorktree dispatches Action::OpenMergeConfirmDialog after spawning backend.inspect_session_changes(session_id). With no current session the slash handler is a silent no-op (mirrors /clear, /compact, /debug). When inspect returns Ok with zero files_changed+insertions+deletions+commits the handler emits a 'Nothing to merge' notice via Action::EmitSessionNotice (TS parity).

MergeConfirmDialog is a centred compositor dialog (Priority::Foreground) built on the shared dialog_theme renderer (rounded yellow border, bold yellow inner title, opaque black background, inverse highlight on focused button). It paints the SessionChangesSummary (files_changed, insertions, deletions, commits count) and offers four buttons in left-to-right order: 'Merge' (Primary, default focus), 'Discard', 'Cancel', and Esc dismisses with Cancel semantics. The dialog has a stable id 'merge-confirm-dialog' so the compositor's idempotent push semantics apply.

On Action::MergeConfirmed { session_id }, dispatch_rpc057 spawns backend.merge_session_worktree(session_id, MergeStrategy::FastForward) and routes the response: (a) MergeStatus::Success → Action::EmitSessionNotice with '[merge] success — N files merged' + commit SHA when present; (b) MergeStatus::NoChanges → Action::EmitSessionNotice with '[merge] nothing to merge'; (c) MergeStatus::Conflict → Action::SeedPendingInput with a conflict-context message listing the conflicting file paths and worktree path so the LLM can see and resolve them (TS pendingAutoSubmitRef parity); (d) Err(e) → Action::EmitSessionNotice with '[error] /merge-worktree: {e}'. The dialog is popped from the compositor BEFORE the backend round-trip completes (best-effort UX, matches the pause-dialog pattern in RPC-053).

On Action::DiscardConfirmed { session_id }, dispatch_rpc057 spawns backend.discard_session_worktree(session_id) and routes the response: Ok → Action::EmitSessionNotice with '[discard] worktree discarded'; Err(e) → Action::EmitSessionNotice with '[error] /merge-worktree discard: {e}'. The dialog is popped before the round-trip completes.

Cross-transport parity: invoking each of the five new RPC methods through both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend MUST land on the same StubSessionManagerHandle with identical per-call counter increments and return the same payload.

All slash-command wiring for /merge-worktree lives in a new dispatch_rpc057.rs file (mirrors dispatch_rpc056 pattern), exposing try_dispatch_rpc057 + handle_slash_merge_worktree + handle_inspect_changes_loaded + handle_merge_confirmed + handle_discard_confirmed + handle_cancel_merge_dialog. The orchestrator dispatch_rpc020.rs's MergeWorktree arm calls self.handle_slash_merge_worktree() instead of the catch-all notice fallback.

The MergeStrategy and MergeStatus enums in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs MUST use #[derive(Default)] with a #[default] variant attribute instead of manual `impl Default { fn default() -> Self { Self::<Variant> } }` blocks — the manual form triggers clippy::derivable_impls under -D warnings, which RPC-038's skeleton_invariants test runs as `cargo clippy -p codelet-sessions -- -D warnings` and which therefore blocks codelet-sessions test runs

architectureNotes.text: The lift maps cleanly: codelet/core/src/scheduler/{mod,engine,state,cron_utils,types,trigger,agent_job,shell_job,catch_up,job_log}.rs receive the engine modules. codelet/napi/src/scheduler/mod.rs collapses to `pub use codelet_core::scheduler::{engine, state, cron_utils, types, trigger, agent_job, shell_job, catch_up, job_log};` plus the still-NAPI-resident `pub mod loop_store;`. The two SessionManager-instance references in engine.rs (get_session_count/get_live_session_ids) and one in agent_job.rs (spawn_scheduled_session) are replaced with the new SchedulerHooks trait: codelet-core declares `pub trait SchedulerHooks { async fn get_session_count(&self) -> usize; async fn get_live_session_ids(&self) -> Vec<Uuid>; async fn spawn_scheduled_session(&self, ScheduleTrigger) -> Result<(), String>; fn default_model(&self) -> String; }`. NAPI provides one impl wrapping crate::session_bindings::SessionManager::instance(); codelet-sessions::SessionManager provides another. The engine API gains `pub fn spawn_scheduler(project_path, handle, hooks: Arc<dyn SchedulerHooks>) -> JoinHandle<()>`.

The CRUD RPC surface (schedule_add/list/pause/resume/remove) reuses the file-lock + atomic write + cron/timezone validation logic that already lives in codelet/napi/src/schedule_handler.rs. That handler stays where it is (it is the ScheduleTool handler called by the LLM tool call). The new RPC implementations in codelet-sessions::handle_impl re-use the same helpers via a thin reorganisation: the pure validation + JSON I/O helpers (validate_cron, validate_timezone, validate_add_request, with_schedules_lock, read_schedules_file, write_schedules_file, handle_add/list/pause/resume/remove) move out of codelet/napi/src/schedule_handler.rs into a new codelet/core/src/scheduler/crud.rs (NAPI-free). The existing ScheduleHandler in NAPI then becomes a thin shim that adapts ScheduleRequest/ScheduleResult to/from the new codelet-core CRUD. The codelet-sessions handle_impl calls the same crud module with std::env::current_dir() as the project root.

Mapping codelet-tools::schedule::types::ScheduleResult to the new wire types: handle_add maps the Value::Object returned to a ScheduledJob with name from the request, cron/timezone/job_type/status from the response, plus role+prompt OR command from the request. handle_list maps each Value in schedules to a ScheduledJob with all wire fields populated. handle_pause/resume return the updated ScheduledJob with status flipped. handle_remove returns Ok(()) — the wire layer doesn't need to echo the name back since the caller already knows it. Errors bubble up as Result<*, String> per RPC-057 convention.

Notice formatters in dispatch_rpc058.rs: format_schedule_added(job) -> '[schedule] added "NAME" (TYPE, CRON, TZ)'; format_schedule_paused(name)/resumed/removed -> '[schedule] STATE "NAME"'; format_schedule_list(rows) -> multi-line with header '[schedule] N schedule(s)' + one '  NAME    CRON    TZ    TYPE    STATUS    LAST RUN' line per row, or '[schedule] No schedules configured.' when empty; format_schedule_error(sub, e) -> '[error] /schedule SUB: {e}'; format_schedule_help() -> static multi-line usage block matching TS USAGE_TEXT. All emitted via Action::EmitSessionNotice so the line lands on the right SessionContext even if the user switched tabs while the RPC was in flight (RPC-046 / RPC-057 pattern).

Action enum additions: Action::ScheduleSubcommandParsed(ScheduleSubcommand) is dispatched from handle_input_submitted when parse_slash_command resolves a /schedule … submit-line input. try_dispatch_rpc058 routes it to handle_schedule_subcommand which fans out to handle_schedule_add/list/pause/resume/remove. Each handler spawns a tokio task awaiting the backend round-trip and routes the response via Action::EmitSessionNotice. With no Tokio runtime (sync unit tests), the helpers are a graceful no-op (matches the RPC-057 pattern). With no current session, the helpers emit no notice at all.

RPC-058 retro (2026-05-27): the lift of the scheduler engine + cron_utils into codelet-core preserved the original SCHED-002/SCHED-003 era format!/anyhow! call sites which use the trailing-argument syntax `format!("foo {}", x)`. The codelet workspace's `-D warnings` clippy level (inherited by codelet-sessions's skeleton_invariants test) now flags these under `clippy::uninlined_format_args`. The fix is mechanical: rewrite each `"... {} ...", name` to `"... {name} ..."`. Affected sites: engine.rs:284 + engine.rs:299 (parse_cron error context) and cron_utils.rs:41 + cron_utils.rs:49 (cron-expression error messages). Behaviour byte-identical — both syntaxes produce the same formatted string. This regression was masked by the RPC-039/040 shape-test file-path panics until the RPC-043 retro fix unblocked clippy execution.

architectureNotes.text: The lift maps cleanly: codelet/core/src/loops/mod.rs receives the full loop_store module (LoopEntry, LoopStore, IdleCheckFn, Inner, register_with_task, register_with_task_and_idle_check, try_register_with_task, try_register_with_task_and_idle_check, cancel, list_for_session, remove_for_session, has_active_task, is_empty, new_local, instance). The static `LOOP_STORE: OnceLock<LoopStore>` becomes the codelet-core::loops singleton; both NAPI and codelet-sessions share the same process-global instance. codelet/napi/src/scheduler/mod.rs collapses its `pub mod loop_store; pub use loop_store::LoopStore;` into `pub use codelet_core::loops::{LoopEntry, LoopStore, IdleCheckFn};` plus a `pub mod loop_store { pub use codelet_core::loops::*; }` shim so existing absolute paths `crate::scheduler::loop_store::LoopEntry` etc. in session_bindings.rs continue to resolve.

Wire type mapping: LoopEntry (chrono::DateTime<Utc> fields, Uuid session_id) → RegisteredLoop (RFC-3339 String timestamps, SessionId wrapper from codelet-rpc-types). The conversion `From<&LoopEntry> for RegisteredLoop` lives in codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs (entry_to_wire helper) and produces id, session_id (Uuid::to_string wrapped in SessionId::new), prompt, interval_seconds, created_at (DateTime::to_rfc3339()), expires_at (same), last_run_at (Option<String> via .map(|t| t.to_rfc3339())).

codelet-sessions handle_impl loop_add: resolves the session via self.get_session(session_id.value.as_str()) (returns Err(String) if not found). Builds an `on_fire` closure capturing the session Arc that calls `session_clone.send_input(prompt_text, None)` on each tick. Builds an `idle_check` closure that returns `session_clone.get_status() == SessionStatus::Idle`. Generates the 4-byte hex id via `let mut bytes = [0u8; 4]; rand::thread_rng().fill_bytes(&mut bytes); hex::encode(bytes)` (or equivalent uuid-based fallback if `rand` isn't already in workspace deps). Sets `expires_at = created_at + Duration::days(3)` matching NAPI. Calls `LoopStore::instance().try_register_with_task_and_idle_check(entry, on_fire, idle_check).await` and maps the Result. Returns RegisteredLoop on success. NOTE: loop_add is sync at the trait level but spawns into the current tokio runtime via tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(...) (matching the sync→async pattern used by create_session in handle_impl.rs).

Interval-to-display formatter (format_interval) in dispatch_rpc059.rs mirrors TS formatInterval: <60s → 'N second[s]'; integer minutes <60 → 'N minute[s]'; sub-3600s non-integer-minute → 'N seconds'; <24h integer hours → 'N hour[s]'; integer days → 'N day[s]'; integer-minutes fallback → 'N minutes'; else 'N seconds'. format_loop_added(entry) → '[loop] scheduled every <intervalStr> [job: ID]'. format_loop_cancelled(id) → '[loop] cancelled ID'. format_loop_cancel_missing(id) → '[error] /loop cancel: Loop "ID" not found'. format_loop_list(entries) → 'Active loops:' + table header 'ID(10)Prompt(30)Interval(15)' + separator '-'*55 + one truncated-prompt row per entry, OR '[loop] No active loops.' when empty. format_loop_error(sub, e) → '[error] /loop SUB: {e}'. format_loop_help() → static multi-line USAGE_TEXT matching TS handleLoopCommand.

Action enum additions: Action::LoopSubcommandParsed(LoopSubcommand) is dispatched from handle_input_submitted when parse_slash_command resolves a `/loop …` submit-line input. try_dispatch_rpc059 routes it to handle_loop_subcommand which fans out to handle_loop_add / handle_loop_list / handle_loop_cancel. Each handler spawns a tokio task awaiting the backend round-trip and routes the response via Action::EmitSessionNotice. With no Tokio runtime (sync unit tests), the helpers are graceful no-ops. With no current session, the helpers emit no notice at all.

Parser implementation in codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/loop_parser.rs: LEADING_INTERVAL_RE matches `^(\d+)([smhd])$` against the first whitespace-split token; TRAILING_INTERVAL_RE matches `\s+every\s+(\d+)\s*(s|sec|seconds?|m|min|minutes?|h|hrs?|hours?|d|days?)$` (case-insensitive) against the body. unit_to_seconds maps s/sec/second[s]→Math.max(1,n), m/min/minute[s]→n*60, h/hr[s]/hour[s]→n*3600, d/day[s]→n*86400. parse_loop_command strips the leading `/loop` prefix, returns Help on empty body, List on body=='list', Cancel(id) on body.starts_with('cancel '), LEADING match (use first token's interval + remaining tokens as prompt), TRAILING match (use full body minus the trailing-`every N <unit>` as prompt), else default 600s with the whole body as the prompt.

Loop id generation: a fresh 8-char lowercase-hex id per loop. The TS uses crypto.randomBytes(4).toString('hex'); the Rust equivalent uses `Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string()[..8]` to avoid adding a `rand` dependency (uuid is already in workspace deps). Single helper `fn generate_loop_id() -> String` lives next to the loop_add impl.

/loop slash-command dispatch lives in codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc059.rs (mirrors dispatch_rpc058.rs) and exposes try_dispatch_rpc059 + handle_slash_loop_help + handle_loop_subcommand + handle_loop_add + handle_loop_list + handle_loop_cancel. Each subcommand spawns the backend RPC and routes the response into the focused session's scrollback via Action::EmitSessionNotice. Notice formatters live in dispatch_rpc059.rs so format strings are single-sourced. add success → `[loop] scheduled every <intervalStr> [job: ID]`; list success with N>0 → `[loop] Active loops:` followed by aligned table rows; list success with N==0 → `[loop] No active loops.`; cancel success (true) → `[loop] cancelled ID`; cancel success (false) → `[error] /loop cancel: Loop "ID" not found`; any other Err(e) → `[error] /loop SUB: {e}`.

Cross-transport parity: invoking each of loop_add/loop_cancel/loop_list through both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend MUST land on the same StubSessionManagerHandle with identical per-call counter increments and byte-identical return payloads.

With no current session, every /loop subcommand (including bare /loop help via the slash-popup pick) is a silent no-op — no backend call, no notice. Matches the /schedule no-op pattern. /loop submit-line input with no current session is silently dropped at handle_input_submitted.

Loops auto-cancel on session destroy: codelet-sessions::SessionManager::destroy_session continues to call self.hooks().cleanup_session_loops(uuid). The Rust binary's hooks impl MUST call codelet_core::loops::LoopStore::instance().remove_for_session(uuid) so loops registered by the new code path are also cleaned up (parity with NAPI's existing cleanup_session_loops which calls the same LoopStore singleton via the re-export shim).

Note: get_supervisors already exists from RPC-037.
