FspecServiceImpl routes each through self.inner.session_manager() with safe defaults when no handle is attached, matching the established RPC-037 pattern.

Backend forwarders in codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/embedded.rs and websocket.rs and trait method defaults in transport/mod.rs FspecBackend trait: async fn add_supervisor / remove_supervisor / get_subordinate / get_subordinates / receive_incoming_message. Defaults on the trait return safe values (Ok / None / Vec::new) so mock backends and existing call sites compile unchanged.

Production handle impl in codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs: add_supervisor delegates to self.chain_of_command.add_supervisor(uuid_from(sub), uuid_from(sup)) — surfaces the 'circular supervision not allowed' / 'subordinate already registered' errors verbatim. remove_supervisor delegates. get_subordinate/get_subordinates delegate. receive_incoming_message looks up the BackgroundSession via self.get_session(subordinate_id) and calls session.receive_incoming_message(IncomingMessage::with_images(...)), translating Err to String.

StubSessionManagerHandle additions in codelet/core/src/session_manager_handle.rs: internal sub_to_sup: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Vec<SessionId>>>>, sup_to_subs: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Vec<SessionId>>>>, plus AtomicU64 counters add_supervisor_calls, remove_supervisor_calls, get_supervisors_calls, get_subordinate_calls, get_subordinates_calls, receive_incoming_message_calls, and Mutex<Vec<(SessionId, IncomingMessageInput)>> recorded_incoming_messages. add_supervisor implements BFS cycle detection mirroring ChainOfCommand.

Action variants in codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs: SupervisorsLoaded(SessionId, Vec<SessionId>), SendToSubordinate { subordinate_id: SessionId, message: IncomingMessageInput }. The first is the result of an async get_supervisors snapshot; the second is the dispatch the supervisor's UI emits when sending a message into a subordinate.

AgentViewStore additions in codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view.rs (and possibly a new module agent_view/supervisor_state.rs to keep agent_view.rs near 300 lines): supervisors_for(&SessionId) -> &[SessionId]; supervisor_pending_count_for(&SessionId) -> usize; set_supervisors(SessionId, Vec<SessionId>); set_supervisor_pending_count(SessionId, usize); apply_supervisor_pending_injection(&SessionId) — bumps count by 1 (current TS semantics). Reset on chunk with explicit count or session destroy.

Dispatch wiring in codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc061.rs (new file, mirrors dispatch_rpc060 pattern): handle_supervisors_loaded(session_id, supervisors) — write into store; handle_send_to_subordinate(subordinate_id, message) — spawn backend.receive_incoming_message, emit EmitSessionNotice on Err; spawn_load_supervisors(session_id) — async backend.get_supervisors -> Action::SupervisorsLoaded; try_dispatch_rpc061 — match SupervisorsLoaded / SendToSubordinate. app/dispatch.rs catch-all threads try_dispatch_rpc061 after try_dispatch_rpc060. App::dispatch on Action::SessionCreated and on SessionContext activation calls spawn_load_supervisors.

Stream chunk handling: codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc045.rs (handle_stream_chunk_state_updates) extends the StreamChunk::SupervisorPendingInjection arm to bump store.set_supervisor_pending_count(session_id, current + 1). The TS BackgroundSession emits this chunk on receive_incoming_message — so seeing it = a real pending message just landed.

SessionHeader badge in codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/header_build.rs build_left_line: takes an optional `subordinate_of: Option<&str>` parameter. When Some, appends ` [Subordinate of: <s>]` (cyan, no modifier) directly after the model/badges block. The format-string helper `format_subordinate_label(supervisors: &[SessionId]) -> Option<String>` returns None for empty, `Some("first8")` for one, `Some("first8+N")` for N+1. SessionHeader gains a subordinate_label: Option<&'a str> field; orchestrator computes from store.supervisors_for(current_session).

SessionFooter pending chip in codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/footer.rs: SessionFooter struct gains supervisor_pending_count: usize. When > 0, the left-aligned slot paints `[N pending from supervisor]` (yellow) instead of the compaction chip (supervisor wins). Helper build_left_supervisor_line(count) returns the styled Line.

MockBackend additions in codelet/fspec-tui/tests/common/mod.rs: supervisors_results: Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Vec<SessionId>>>, add_supervisor_result: Mutex<Result<(), String>>, receive_incoming_message_result: Mutex<Result<(), String>>, plus per-method call counters add_supervisor_calls, remove_supervisor_calls, get_supervisors_calls, get_subordinate_calls, get_subordinates_calls, receive_incoming_message_calls, and last_received_incoming_message: Mutex<Option<(SessionId, IncomingMessageInput)>>. impl FspecBackend gets one-line forwarders that read/write these slots.

Tests: tests/source_shape_rpc061.rs (pins file locations: dispatch_rpc061.rs, IncomingMessageInput in rpc-types, Action variants, app/dispatch.rs catch-all routing, sessions/handle_impl.rs supervisor methods, < 300 lines per file). tests/rpc061_cross_transport_parity.rs (exercises every method through both transports against StubSessionManagerHandle). tests/supervisor_links_rpc061.rs (App + MockBackend integration: SupervisorsLoaded → badge rendered; SupervisorPendingInjection chunk → pending chip rendered; SendToSubordinate Ok / Err paths).

RPC-061.description: Phase 7.8: Port supervisor surface from BackgroundSession (WATCH-003/006/008/011/019/020). Trait additions on SessionManagerHandle: add_supervisor, remove_supervisor, get_supervisors, get_subordinates, receive_incoming_message. Backed by existing methods in session_manager.rs lines 3993-4013 (add_supervisor, remove_supervisor, get_supervisors, get_subordinate, get_subordinates) and BackgroundSession::receive_incoming_message (line 1206). AgentView surfaces a 'this is a subordinate' badge based on backend.get_supervisors.

examples.text: App boots with session s-sub wired to a MockBackend whose get_supervisors(s-sub) returns vec![s-sup]. App::dispatch spawns get_supervisors on SessionCreated; within 1 s Action::SupervisorsLoaded(s-sub, [s-sup]) lands on the action bus. The next render shows `[Subordinate of: <s-sup-short>]` in the SessionHeader.
App boots with session s-sub which has NO supervisor. The SessionHeader renders normally with no subordinate badge present.

A subordinate session s-sub receives a StreamChunk::SupervisorPendingInjection with content="check the build". The next render shows `[1 pending from supervisor]` in the SessionFooter left-aligned slot. After the subordinate consumes the message via the agent loop, a fresh chunk lowers the count to 0 and the chip disappears.

A supervisor calls add_supervisor(s-sub, s-sup) — succeeds. Then attempts add_supervisor(s-sup, s-sub) — backend returns Err("circular supervision not allowed"). The supervisor session scrollback shows the error notice.

From the supervisor's AgentView, Action::SendToSubordinate { subordinate_id: s-sub, message: IncomingMessageInput { source_session_id: "s-sup", role_name: "reviewer", message: "please fix lint", images: None } } is dispatched. Within 1 s backend.receive_incoming_message lands exactly one call with the matching payload. The subordinate's session footer eventually shows `[1 pending from supervisor]` after the matching SupervisorPendingInjection chunk arrives.

Action::SendToSubordinate is dispatched but backend.receive_incoming_message returns Err("Failed to queue supervisor input: channel closed"). Within 1 s an Action::EmitSessionNotice for the originating supervisor session lands with text `[error] send to subordinate: Failed to queue supervisor input: channel closed`, and the next render shows that notice in the supervisor's scrollback.

Cross-transport parity test exercises add_supervisor + get_supervisors + get_subordinates + receive_incoming_message + remove_supervisor through both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend against the same StubSessionManagerHandle. Both transports return identical observable state (same supervisor list, same subordinate list, identical error from the loop attempt) and the stub records exactly one call per method per transport.

A subordinate session has three supervisors (s-sup-aaa, s-sup-bbb, s-sup-ccc). The SessionHeader renders `[Subordinate of: s-sup-aa+2]` — first 8 chars of the first supervisor id plus `+<count of remaining supervisors>` so multi-supervisor configurations stay readable on narrow terminals.

Both the supervisor and compaction chips would be visible at once on a session: the supervisor pending chip is rendered (left slot) and the compaction chip is suppressed for that frame (the supervisor signal is more urgent).

rules.text: SessionManagerHandle gains five trait methods with no-op safe defaults: add_supervisor(subordinate_id, supervisor_id) -> Result<(), String>, remove_supervisor(supervisor_id) -> Result<(), String>, get_subordinate(supervisor_id) -> Option<SessionId>, get_subordinates(supervisor_id) -> Vec<SessionId>, receive_incoming_message(subordinate_id, msg: IncomingMessageInput) -> Result<(), String>. get_supervisors already exists from RPC-037 and is reused.

codelet-rpc-types gains a new wire-portable struct IncomingMessageInput { source_session_id: String, role_name: String, message: String, images: Option<Vec<IncomingMessageImage>> } that carries the exact same fields as codelet_sessions::IncomingMessage. IncomingMessageImage is reused (already exists).

FspecService gains four new tarpc methods (add_supervisor, remove_supervisor, get_subordinate, get_subordinates, receive_incoming_message). get_supervisors is already on FspecService from RPC-037. FspecServiceImpl routes each through self.inner.session_manager() with safe defaults when no handle is attached.

Both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend gain async methods for each of the five trait methods; embedded delegates to its in-process tarpc client (no extra plumbing) and websocket follows the existing client.read().await + BackendError::Disconnected guard pattern.

Loops in the supervisor graph are rejected: add_supervisor(A, B) followed by add_supervisor(B, A) returns Err("circular supervision not allowed") at the ChainOfCommand layer. Both the Stub and the production SessionManager surface this error verbatim.

StubSessionManagerHandle gains an internal ChainOfCommand-equivalent map (Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Vec<SessionId>>> for both directions) plus per-method call counters so cross-transport parity tests can assert each transport lands exactly one call on the underlying handle and observes identical state.

AgentViewStore gains two read accessors: supervisors_for(&SessionId) -> &[SessionId] and supervisor_pending_count_for(&SessionId) -> usize. State is updated by App::dispatch on Action::SupervisorsLoaded (push from a backend.get_supervisors snapshot) and on StreamChunk::SupervisorPendingInjection (increments count, resets when a fresh count chunk arrives).

SessionHeader renders a cyan `[Subordinate of: <short-id>]` badge directly after the model/badge block when supervisors_for(current_session) is non-empty. The short-id is the first 8 chars of the supervisor SessionId. Multiple supervisors render as `[Subordinate of: <id1>+<n>]` where <n> is the count of additional supervisors.

SessionFooter renders a left-aligned `[N pending from supervisor]` chip (yellow) when supervisor_pending_count_for(current_session) > 0. The chip sits in the same left-aligned slot as the compaction chip; when both are present, the supervisor chip wins (it is more urgent). Hidden when count is 0.

On Action::SessionCreated and on session activation (Action::AttachToSession or session cycle), App::dispatch spawns a backend.get_supervisors task that emits Action::SupervisorsLoaded(session_id, supervisors). The AgentViewStore caches the result so subsequent renders read from memory.

Action::SendToSubordinate { subordinate_id: SessionId, message: IncomingMessageInput } spawns backend.receive_incoming_message(subordinate_id, message). On Err, an Action::EmitSessionNotice for the originating session is emitted with text `[error] send to subordinate: <e>`. On Ok the dispatch is silent — the chunk stream from the subordinate's BackgroundSession already broadcasts visible progress through the existing chunks_rx path.

App::dispatch routes SupervisorsLoaded / SendToSubordinate through a new dispatch_rpc061.rs helper module (try_dispatch_rpc061), keeping app/dispatch.rs under its 300-LoC ceiling. The catch-all arm threads the call after try_dispatch_rpc060.

Cross-transport parity test rpc061_cross_transport_parity.rs (in codelet/fspec-tui/tests/) exercises add_supervisor + get_supervisors + get_subordinates + receive_incoming_message + remove_supervisor through both EmbeddedFspecBackend and WebSocketFspecBackend against a fresh StubSessionManagerHandle and asserts identical observable state and per-method call counts.

Integration test supervisor_links_rpc061.rs drives an App with a MockBackend that scripts: two sessions s-sup and s-sub, add_supervisor(s-sub, s-sup), get_supervisors(s-sub) returns [s-sup], a SupervisorPendingInjection chunk on s-sub, an Action::SendToSubordinate { subordinate_id: s-sub, message } — and asserts the SessionHeader paints the subordinate badge, the SessionFooter paints the pending chip, backend.receive_incoming_message is called exactly once with the expected payload, and the error path emits EmitSessionNotice.

architectureNotes.text: [A] Test file layout (mirrors RPC-061 pattern): two new test files in codelet/sessions/tests/: (1) `mcp_injection_lifecycle.rs` — runtime tests against codelet_tools::{init_mcp_session, cleanup_mcp_session, get_mcp_connections} verifying init→Some, cleanup→None, idempotent re-init, and unknown-uuid no-op. (2) `mcp_injection_source_shape.rs` — substring/AST-grep scans over codelet/sessions/src/session_manager.rs (and codelet/napi/src/agent_loop.rs for the consumer side) pinning the import, the two init call sites, the one cleanup call site, and the spawn_agent_loop signature.

[B] Test isolation: every lifecycle test generates a fresh `uuid::Uuid::new_v4()` so the process-global MCP_SESSIONS registry can be tested in parallel without cross-test interference. Tests call `cleanup_mcp_session` at the end (or rely on the Drop semantics on the connections map) so they don't leak entries between runs.

[C] Source-shape test helpers: reuse the existing `strip_rust_comments` / `read` / `sessions_src_dir` style helpers from codelet/sessions/tests/handle_impl.rs (or copy the same pattern) to scan session_manager.rs after stripping comments. Count occurrences with `src.matches(needle).count()` and use exact substring assertions like in RPC-042/RPC-061 source-shape tests.

[D] Negative grep for new RPC surface: in the source-shape test, after stripping comments, assert that scanning codelet/core/src/session_manager_handle.rs, codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs, and codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs finds ZERO occurrences of the substrings `init_mcp`, `cleanup_mcp`, `mcp_session`, and `mcp_injection` (these would all indicate a leaking MCP RPC method). Use one assertion per file × substring pair for actionable error messages.

[E] Feature file layout: two feature files mirroring the RPC-061 pattern — `spec/features/rpc062-mcp-injection-lifecycle.feature` (lifecycle scenarios) and `spec/features/rpc062-mcp-injection-source-shape.feature` (source-shape scenarios). Both tagged `@RPC-062 @rust @mcp @session-management`.

[F] No new public API: the SessionManager API surface, SessionManagerHandle trait, FspecService trait, FspecBackend trait, and StubSessionManagerHandle are all UNCHANGED. RPC-062 is a pure audit + test landing — zero production-code edits expected unless source-shape tests reveal a missing call site (in which case minimal repair is in scope).

[G] AST research findings (verified before specifying): `use codelet_tools::McpInjection;` already at session_manager.rs:58; two `codelet_tools::init_mcp_session(uuid)` calls at session_manager.rs:600 and 846; one `codelet_tools::cleanup_mcp_session(uuid)` at session_manager.rs:935; `spawn_agent_loop` trait signature at session_manager.rs:83 with `mcp_injection_rx: mpsc::Receiver<McpInjection>`; consumer-side `agent_loop.rs:307` takes `mut mcp_injection_rx: mpsc::Receiver<McpInjection>` and selects on `mcp_injection_rx.recv()` at line 424.

RPC-062.description: Phase 7.9: McpInjection types already in codelet-tools (NAPI-free, imported at session_manager.rs line 41). Port the mcp_injection_rx plumbing into the new SessionManager (Phase 4.3 / RPC-040 already moves it implicitly). No new RPC surface needed — purely internal to the agent loop. Includes init_mcp_session (3760) and cleanup_mcp_session (3971) call sites.

examples.text: Lifecycle test: calling codelet_tools::init_mcp_session(uuid) for a fresh uuid returns a receiver and a connection map; immediately after, codelet_tools::get_mcp_connections(uuid) returns Some(<same map>). Subsequent codelet_tools::cleanup_mcp_session(uuid) makes get_mcp_connections(uuid) return None.

Idempotent re-init: calling init_mcp_session(uuid) twice for the same uuid (without cleanup in between) replaces the entry — the second call returns a fresh injection_rx, and get_mcp_connections(uuid) still returns Some after both calls. cleanup_mcp_session(uuid) then drops the entry.

Cleanup on unknown uuid: codelet_tools::cleanup_mcp_session(<random-uuid-never-registered>) does NOT panic and is a silent no-op — proven by the fact that get_mcp_connections(<other-uuid>) still returns the existing entry.
Source-shape — McpInjection import: codelet/sessions/src/session_manager.rs contains exactly one `use codelet_tools::McpInjection;` line and zero local redefinitions of the McpInjection enum.

Source-shape — init call sites: codelet/sessions/src/session_manager.rs contains exactly two occurrences of `codelet_tools::init_mcp_session(uuid)` — one inside `pub async fn create_session_with_id` and one inside `pub async fn create_isolated_session_with_id`.
Source-shape — cleanup call site: codelet/sessions/src/session_manager.rs contains exactly one occurrence of `codelet_tools::cleanup_mcp_session(uuid)` and it sits inside `pub fn destroy_session`.

Source-shape — spawn_agent_loop signature: the SessionManagerHooks trait declares spawn_agent_loop with the third parameter typed `mcp_injection_rx: mpsc::Receiver<McpInjection>` so the receiver is handed across to the NAPI-side agent_loop.

Source-shape — agent_loop consumes the receiver: codelet/napi/src/agent_loop.rs `agent_loop` function signature takes `mut mcp_injection_rx: mpsc::Receiver<McpInjection>` and contains a `mcp_injection_rx.recv()` arm inside its tokio::select! loop.

No new RPC surface — negative grep: scanning codelet/core/src/session_manager_handle.rs, codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs, and codelet/fspec-tui/src/transport/mod.rs finds ZERO method names matching /init_mcp|cleanup_mcp|mcp_session|mcp_injection/.

NAPI-free dependency invariant: the existing codelet/sessions/tests/no_napi_dependency.rs continues to pass — codelet-sessions still has no transitive napi dependency and no `codelet_napi` import even after the MCP injection audit landings.

rules.text: codelet-sessions imports the NAPI-free McpInjection type from codelet-tools (no McpInjection redefinition inside codelet-sessions)

SessionManager::create_session_with_id calls codelet_tools::init_mcp_session(uuid) exactly once and forwards the returned mcp_injection_rx to self.hooks().spawn_agent_loop(session, input_rx, mcp_injection_rx)
SessionManager::create_isolated_session_with_id also calls codelet_tools::init_mcp_session(uuid) exactly once and forwards the returned mcp_injection_rx via self.hooks().spawn_agent_loop
SessionManager::destroy_session calls codelet_tools::cleanup_mcp_session(uuid) exactly once after the session is removed from the sessions map

The SessionManagerHooks trait's spawn_agent_loop method has the exact signature spawn_agent_loop(&self, session: Arc<BackgroundSession>, input_rx: mpsc::Receiver<PromptInput>, mcp_injection_rx: mpsc::Receiver<McpInjection>) so the NAPI-side NapiSessionManagerHooks adapter can hand the receiver to crate::agent_loop::agent_loop where it is consumed

codelet_tools::init_mcp_session(uuid) is a public NAPI-free function: it registers per-session MCP state in the global MCP_SESSIONS map, returns (mpsc::Receiver<McpInjection>, McpConnectionMap), and codelet_tools::get_mcp_connections(uuid) returns Some after init

codelet_tools::cleanup_mcp_session(uuid) removes the per-session entry from MCP_SESSIONS, cancels every active MCP connection's cancellation_token, and codelet_tools::get_mcp_connections(uuid) returns None after cleanup

MCP handler registration is singleton-per-session: constructing a fresh SessionManager and then init_mcp_session(uuid) for the same uuid replaces the previous entry without leaking the old connections (idempotent re-init returns a fresh injection_rx)
No new RPC surface is added: SessionManagerHandle, FspecService, FspecBackend trait, and StubSessionManagerHandle gain ZERO MCP-related methods — MCP injection stays internal to the agent loop

Source-shape regression tests pin the four call sites: (a) `use codelet_tools::McpInjection;` import in session_manager.rs, (b) two `codelet_tools::init_mcp_session(uuid)` call sites inside create_session_with_id and create_isolated_session_with_id, (c) one `codelet_tools::cleanup_mcp_session(uuid)` call site inside destroy_session, (d) one `spawn_agent_loop(session.clone(), input_rx, mcp_injection_rx)` invocation per create path

architectureNotes.text: [A] RoleDialog component location: codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/role_dialog.rs (flat in components/, matching existing dialog convention — model_selector_dialog.rs, thinking_level_dialog.rs, etc.). The attachment suggests components/dialogs/role_dialog.rs but we follow the existing flat layout.

[B] RoleDialog uses tui-textarea (single-line mode is fine — out of scope per attachment: 'TS uses textarea but content rarely exceeds one line'). Pattern follows MultiLineInput's TextArea wrapping. Constant ROLE_DIALOG_ID = 'role-dialog'.

[C] Action wiring: Reuse existing Action::SetSessionRole(SessionId, Option<String>) for both save (Some(text)) and Ctrl+D clear (None). NO new Action variant is required — handle_set_session_role in dispatch_rpc022.rs already updates the store AND fires backend.set_session_role. RoleDialog stashes pending action and exposes take_pending_action() for tests, mirroring ThinkingLevelDialog.

[D] Slash parser changes (codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/slash_parser.rs): bare '/role' switches from SlashCommandParse::ClearRole → new variant SlashCommandParse::OpenRoleDialog (dispatched as handle_open_role_dialog). '/role <text>' stays SetRole(text). '/role clear' (case-insensitive, after the prefix '/role ') stays ClearRole. '/role ' with empty trailing arg also OpenRoleDialog (no longer ClearRole) — explicit 'clear' arg now required to clear from submit-line.

[E] Dispatch wiring (codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc020.rs): SlashCommandAction::Role arm replaces the existing 'bare /role clears' shortcut with self.handle_open_role_dialog(). Submit-line OpenRoleDialog SlashCommandParse arm also routes to handle_open_role_dialog. The helper handle_open_role_dialog (new in dispatch_rpc020.rs, OR a new dispatch_rpc063.rs file if dispatch_rpc020.rs grows past 300 LoC) reads the current role from AgentViewStore::role_for(current_session), constructs a RoleDialog seeded with that text, and pushes it to the compositor at Priority::Foreground. No backend.get_session_role round-trip is required (store is already synced).

[F] Test file layout: codelet/fspec-tui/tests/role_dialog_rpc063.rs (component-level: priority, render, handle_event paths, footer text, take_pending_action). The existing slash_parser tests in app/slash_parser.rs will be updated to assert the new OpenRoleDialog parse outcome for bare '/role' and '/role '. A second integration file codelet/fspec-tui/tests/slash_role_rpc063.rs covers the App dispatch path: bare /role from palette opens the dialog; '/role text' from submit-line sets the role directly; '/role clear' from submit-line clears without dialog.

[G] Public exports: codelet/fspec-tui/src/lib.rs adds 'pub use components::role_dialog::{RoleDialog, ROLE_DIALOG_ID};'. components/mod.rs adds 'pub mod role_dialog;'. Followed across the existing dialog precedent (ThinkingLevelDialog, ModelSelectorDialog, etc.).

[H] Backwards-compat impact: This card CHANGES the default semantics of bare '/role' from 'clear role' to 'open dialog'. Users wanting to clear must now explicitly type '/role clear' or open the dialog and press Ctrl+D. The previous SlashCommandParse::ClearRole arm in dispatch_rpc020.rs (handle_input_submitted match) MUST keep handling '/role clear' (case-insensitive). The palette-pick path in handle_slash_command must NO LONGER call handle_set_session_role(sid, None); it must call handle_open_role_dialog(sid).

[I] Existing app_dispatch_rpc022.rs and slash_command_wiring_rpc022.rs tests that assert 'bare /role clears role' MUST be UPDATED to assert 'bare /role opens the dialog' instead. Tests asserting '/role clear' explicitly clearing must continue to pass.

architectureNotes.text: [A] Debounce strategy: emit `FilterChanged(query)` immediately from the widget on every keystroke (preserve existing RPC-026 behaviour and tests). The DEBOUNCE lives in `App::handle_search_history` — when called, schedule a tokio sleep(150ms) task that, after the wait, fires `backend.persistence_search_history(query)`. A new keystroke aborts the prior in-flight tokio JoinHandle (stored on `App` or on a new `SearchDebounceState` field) so only the final query reaches the backend within a fast burst. Synchronous test-runtime path (`Handle::try_current().is_err()`) skips the debounce and silently no-ops, matching existing dispatch_rpc026.rs pattern.

[B] Stale result discarding: widen `Action::HistorySearchResults` from `Vec<HistoryMatch>` to a struct-style variant `{ query: String, matches: Vec<HistoryMatch> }`. The spawned task captures the query it sent and emits it back with the matches. `handle_history_search_results` compares the response query to `search_view.query()` and only folds when they match. Update existing rpc026 tests that construct `Action::HistorySearchResults(...)` to use the new variant form. The `SearchHistoryView` gains a `set_matches_for(query: &str, matches: Vec<HistoryMatch>)` helper OR the dispatcher does the equality check before calling `set_matches`.

[C] Result highlighting: `SearchHistoryView::render_body` switches from `Paragraph::new(Line::from(Span::styled(label, style)))` to building a `Vec<Span>` where each case-insensitive occurrence of `self.query` inside `m.text` is split into BOLD vs plain spans. A small helper `highlight_query(text: &str, query: &str, row_style: Style)` returns the `Vec<Span<'static>>` (or `Vec<Span<'_>>`). Selected-row inversion (REVERSED) is applied on top of the per-span BOLD so the highlighted-row visual still indicates selection. Empty query takes the existing no-highlight path.

[D] j/k navigation: `SearchHistoryView::handle_key` adds `KeyCode::Char('j')` → move_by(+1) and `KeyCode::Char('k')` → move_by(-1) BEFORE the generic `KeyCode::Char(c)` branch that appends to the query. Both must be no-modifier (Ctrl/Alt rejected at the top of handle_key). This means uppercase J/K typed into the search query still works because `KeyModifiers::SHIFT` will be set for capital letters and the j/k branch checks for empty modifiers. Update the existing rpc026_search_history_view test `typing_characters_emits_filter_changed` confirmation that lowercase j/k now navigate instead of filter (alternative: pick different test chars to keep filter test intact). Resolution: the existing test types `g`, `i`, `t` — none of which are j/k — so it's unaffected.

[E] File layout: changes confined to (1) `codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/search_history_view.rs` — add j/k branch, add `highlight_query` helper, extend handle_key tests; (2) `codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc026.rs` — add debounce + stale-discard logic; (3) `codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs` — widen `Action::HistorySearchResults` variant; (4) new integration test file `codelet/fspec-tui/tests/search_view_rpc064.rs` covering debounce + stale + insert + dismiss + j/k + highlight. NO new dispatch_rpc064.rs file expected (logic fits in existing dispatch_rpc026.rs). All affected files must stay under 300 lines — search_history_view.rs is at 297 lines currently, so the j/k + highlight changes will push it past the budget; extract the renderer body to a new sibling file `search_history_view_render.rs` if needed.

[F] Backwards-compat impact: widening `Action::HistorySearchResults` from a tuple variant `(Vec<HistoryMatch>)` to a struct variant breaks every test that constructed it. Affected tests today: `rpc026_app_dispatch.rs` does NOT construct it directly (the spawned task does). Only the dispatcher path constructs it via `action_tx.send(Action::HistorySearchResults(matches))` in `dispatch_rpc026.rs` line 158. So the impact is limited to one production-code line plus the new test file. Confirmed by `Grep HistorySearchResults` — only 2 hits.

[G] App state for debounce: add `last_search_debounce: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` to `App` (in `src/app/state.rs`). Each `handle_search_history` call aborts the previous handle (if any), then spawns a new tokio task that does `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150)).await` then calls `backend.persistence_search_history(query)` and dispatches `Action::HistorySearchResults { query, matches }`. The spawn ALSO pushes the new handle into `App::pending_tasks` so the existing test harness drains it. The 150ms constant lives as `const SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS: u64 = 150;` in `dispatch_rpc026.rs`.

RPC-064.description: Phase 6.4: /search trait already wired (persistence_search_history on FspecService/FspecBackend) and SearchHistoryView exists (RPC-026). This card polishes the slash command path: SlashCommandAction::Search → OpenSearchView already works; ensure full TS parity (search-as-you-type, result highlighting, Enter to insert). examples.text: User picks /search from the palette while no popup or mode-view is open — AgentView.search_view becomes Some(SearchHistoryView with empty query) and AgentView.slash_popup is reset to None; no backend call has fired yet
User presses Ctrl+R while no popup or mode-view is open — `Action::OpenSearchView` is dispatched and SearchHistoryView appears empty, same as the palette path

User types `g`, `i`, `t` within 150ms of each other — only one `backend.persistence_search_history("git")` call fires (the previous timer is cancelled on each keystroke); the view's `query` reflects the latest typed text
User types `g`, waits 200ms (longer than the debounce window), then types `i`, waits 200ms, then types `t` — three separate backend round-trips fire with queries `g`, `gi`, `git`

Backend returns the result list for query `g` 250ms after the user has already typed up to `git` — the stale `g` response is discarded and the view continues to show the prior matches (or empty placeholder) until the `git` response lands
Result row text is `git status now` and the current query is `git` — the substring `git` is rendered with `Modifier::BOLD`, the trailing ` status now` is rendered plain
Result row text is `GIT add then git push` and the current query is `git` (lowercase) — both `GIT` and `git` are rendered with `Modifier::BOLD` (case-insensitive match, original casing preserved)
User presses `j` with two results loaded — `selected_index` advances from 0 to 1; pressing `k` moves back to 0; pressing `j` again wraps from 1 to 0 (matching the existing arrow-key wrap semantics)

User presses Enter on the highlighted match `git status` — `Action::InsertIntoInput("git status")` is dispatched, the input's value becomes `git status`, the search_view is removed, and the input is NOT auto-submitted

User presses Esc with `git` typed and a match highlighted — `Action::CloseSearchView` is dispatched, the search_view is removed, and the input remains unchanged (whatever it was before /search opened)
User opens /search with an empty query — the placeholder `(type to search history)` is rendered in the body and zero backend calls have fired; pressing Esc immediately closes without RPC traffic

rules.text: Both `/search` (picked from the slash palette) and `Ctrl+R` (chord) open the SearchHistoryView via `Action::OpenSearchView` with no backend call until the user types

Typing into the open SearchHistoryView debounces keystrokes by ~150ms before dispatching `backend.persistence_search_history(query)` (rapid typing fires at most one RPC per debounce window with the latest text)
Each rendered result row highlights every case-insensitive occurrence of the current query inside the result text using `Modifier::BOLD` (rest of the text renders plain)
Selection navigation accepts both arrow keys (↑/↓) AND vim-style j/k (lowercase, no modifiers) so the result list matches the TS frontend's keybindings

Enter on a highlighted result dispatches `Action::InsertIntoInput(text)` and `Action::CloseSearchView`, leaving the input pre-filled (but not auto-submitted) so the user can edit before pressing Enter again
Esc closes the view via `Action::CloseSearchView` without inserting anything into the input

Stale results from an in-flight RPC whose query no longer matches the view's current query are discarded — the dispatcher folds `HistorySearchResults` only when the response's query equals the view's current query
Empty query state renders the existing `(type to search history)` placeholder and never fires a backend call (no implicit recent-history fetch — matches the TS behaviour)

architectureNotes.text: [A] File layout: (1) new module `codelet/fspec-tui/tests/common/harness.rs` declared from `tests/common/mod.rs` via `pub mod harness;`. The harness wraps `App` + `Arc<MockBackend>` (the existing 2876-LoC double already exports every counter we need). (2) new integration test file `codelet/fspec-tui/tests/behaviour_parity_rpc065.rs` declaring `mod common;` to pull in the harness module.

[B] AppTestHarness API surface (private to tests/common/harness.rs): `pub struct AppTestHarness { pub app: App, pub mock: Arc<MockBackend> }`. Constructors: `pub fn new() -> Self` (seeds session s-1 + focuses it), `pub fn empty() -> Self` (no sessions). Helpers: `add_session(SessionId)`, `seed_chunks(&SessionId, usize)`, `submit_input(&str)` (synchronous: drives `Action::InputSubmitted` through dispatch), `press_key(KeyEvent)` (drives navigator.handle_event → emit → dispatch), `dispatch_slash(SlashCommandAction)` (sugar over Action::SlashCommandSelected), `current_session() -> Option<&SessionId>`, `compositor_contains(id: &str) -> bool`, `active_view() -> ViewMode`, `should_quit() -> bool`, `scrollback_chunk_count(&SessionId) -> usize`, `drain_pending() -> async` (loops until pending_tasks all settle and action_rx is drained — bounded by 1s), `wait_until(predicate, label) -> async`.

[C] drain_pending implementation: re-uses the well-tested pattern from `slash_clear_rpc046.rs::drain_pending` — repeatedly `tokio::select!` over (action_rx.recv(), tokio::time::sleep(1ms)) and on each received Action call `app.dispatch(action)`; bail out when both action_rx is empty AND pending_tasks is empty AND no new actions appeared after a 10ms quiescence window. Wrap in `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), …)` to fail fast on stuck tests.

[D] Test file structure: `behaviour_parity_rpc065.rs` organises tests by SECTION using `mod` blocks (slash_help, slash_clear, slash_quit, slash_model, slash_thinking, slash_role, slash_resume, slash_search, slash_provider, slash_providers_alias, slash_debug, slash_compact, slash_isolation, slash_blocklist, slash_detach, slash_merge_worktree, slash_schedule, slash_loop, key_shift_arrows, key_history_recall, key_tab_turn_selection, key_ctrl_r, key_esc_cascade, key_enter_submit, key_ctrl_c_interrupt, key_pagedown_end). One `#[tokio::test]` per matrix row, each ~10-20 LoC of harness sugar.

[E] Per-test TS-REF/DEEP-REF convention: each test has a triple-slash doc comment block of the form `/// TS-REF: src/tui/views/AgentView.tsx line 2721 (handleSearchSlash) /// DEEP-REF: tests/search_view_rpc064.rs::picking_search_from_palette_opens_empty_view`. These doubles as searchable breadcrumbs when the TS frontend changes and we need to update parity.

[F] Backward compatibility: MockBackend currently lives at tests/common/mod.rs and is imported by every test as `use common::MockBackend;`. Adding `pub mod harness;` to tests/common/mod.rs does NOT break any existing test (only adds a new sub-module). The harness IMPORTS MockBackend via `super::MockBackend` so the existing file stays untouched.

[G] No source code production changes required. Everything in this card lives in `tests/` — including the harness — so the dependency-rule regression tests (no_napi_dependency.rs etc.) remain unaffected. `cargo build -p codelet-fspec-tui` behaviour is unchanged.

[H] Runtime flavour: every parity test uses `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]` because nine of the matrix rows require draining spawned tasks (clear/compact/debug/detach/role-set/thinking-set/schedule/loop/ctrl-c). Synthetic-key smoke tests (help/quit/model-dialog/thinking-dialog/role-dialog/resume/search/blocklist/provider) could use current_thread but uniformity outweighs the minor scheduler overhead — total wall-clock cost <30s per attachment AC #4.

[I] /merge-worktree quirk: the slash command does NOT push the MergeConfirmDialog directly — it first spawns `backend.inspect_session_changes(session)` and only on a non-zero summary dispatches `Action::OpenMergeConfirmDialog`. So the matrix smoke assertion is `mock.inspect_session_changes_calls() == 1` (NOT compositor.contains(MERGE_CONFIRM_DIALOG_ID)). The dialog-push half of the flow is the canonical merge_worktree_rpc057.rs test.

[J] /isolation quirk: SlashCommandSelected(Isolation) dispatches `Action::OpenCreateSessionDialog { preselect: Some(CreateSessionOption::Isolated) }` (NOT a separate isolation dialog). Matrix assertion: `compositor_contains(CREATE_SESSION_DIALOG_ID)` after draining the action bus (the dispatch goes through action_tx, not direct compositor push).

[K] /provider vs /providers alias verification: both branches share the `Provider | Providers` match arm in dispatch_rpc020.rs::handle_slash_command (line 103). The parity test fires Provider and Providers from two fresh harnesses and asserts both produce `navigator.active_view == ViewMode::ProviderSettings` after draining (the OpenProviderSettingsView action is delivered via action_tx → navigator.apply_action).

[L] Ctrl+C requires the session to be in a state where the dispatch path emits `Action::Interrupt` (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/dispatch.rs line 240). The harness press_key helper synthesises the KeyEvent and routes it through `app.handle_event(Event::Key(_))`. Status gating: the App::dispatch handler for Interrupt only spawns backend.interrupt when the focused session's status is Running/Compacting (per dispatch_rpc051.rs). The parity test seeds `SessionStatus::Running` via `mock.push_status_change(s-1, Running)` then drains, then presses Ctrl+C.

architectureNotes.text: [A] File layout: (1) NEW codelet/fspec/tests/cross_frontend_parity.rs — the integration test binary. (2) NEW codelet/fspec/tests/fixtures/cross_frontend_run.jsonl — Rust-pinned golden chunk stream. (3) NEW codelet/fspec/tests/README.md — regeneration + future-TS-fixture docs. (4) WIDENED codelet/providers/src/stub_provider.rs — adds `impl LlmProvider for StubProvider`. (5) NEW codelet/providers/src/stub_provider_registration.rs (or inline in stub_provider.rs) — `pub fn register_stub_provider()` that inserts a synthetic ProviderConfig into the custom provider registry so ProviderType::Custom("stub") routes to it. (6) NEW codelet/fspec/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies] entry `codelet-providers = { workspace = true, features = ["test-support"] }`.

[B] StubProvider LlmProvider impl: name() = "stub"; model() = "canned"; context_window() = 200_000; max_output_tokens() = 4096; supports_caching() = false; supports_streaming() = true; complete(_) returns Ok("hi back".to_string()); complete_with_tools depends on the scripted run — for inputs containing "trigger-tool" it emits a CompletionResponse with content=MessageContent::ToolUse{...} so the SessionManager's tool dispatcher exercises the ToolCall + ToolResult chunk path; otherwise it emits content=MessageContent::Text("hi back") + StopReason::EndTurn. The tool call is for a sandboxed tool slug `noop_tool` that codelet_tools resolves to a no-op result.

[C] Custom-provider registration without disk JSON: rather than authoring a `.fspec/providers/stub.json` file (which would force a Rhai-script round-trip), the test calls a NEW helper `codelet_providers::stub_provider::register_stub_provider()` (gated by `test-support`) that synthesises a `codelet_providers::custom::ProviderConfig` and inserts it directly into the custom provider registry. Verify via codelet_providers::custom_provider_registered("stub") == true after registration. This sidesteps Rhai entirely and keeps the test deterministic.

[D] Daemon boot helper: re-use common::spawn_fspec_daemon (in codelet/fspec/tests/common/mod.rs) — same pattern as daemon_mode.rs:37. The test's `mod common;` import gives us spawn_fspec_daemon, make_workspace, ChildGuard, scan_for_port_equals for free. Cross_frontend_parity.rs adds a NEW `setup_stub_workspace(env_vars: &[(&str, &str)]) -> (TempDir, ChildGuard, u16)` helper that (a) calls make_workspace, (b) calls register_stub_provider() in the spawned binary's environment (via FSPEC_RPC_066_FORCE_STUB=1 env var that triggers a one-time registration call inside `codelet_providers::manager::ProviderManager::with_model_support` — only compiled when `test-support` feature is on).

[E] Subprocess problem: the fspec daemon subprocess is built by `cargo build --bin fspec` which compiles codelet-fspec and its transitive deps WITHOUT the providers/test-support feature (cargo features don't propagate across `[dev-dependencies]` to the binary). Solution: a NEW `[features]` table entry in codelet/fspec/Cargo.toml — `test-stub-provider = ["codelet-providers/test-support"]` — and the test invocation becomes `cargo test --features test-stub-provider -p codelet-fspec --test cross_frontend_parity`. The fspec binary built under that feature flag includes the stub provider registration call gated by `#[cfg(feature = "test-stub-provider")]` in src/common.rs (one-time `register_stub_provider()` call inside build_service). Without the feature flag the test compiles into a no-op that prints SKIP and returns Ok (so the default `cargo test` invocation isn't broken).

[F] Normalisation pipeline: a new module-private `mod normalise` inside cross_frontend_parity.rs exposes `fn normalise_chunk_stream(chunks: &[(SessionId, StreamChunk)]) -> Vec<serde_json::Value>`. For each chunk: (1) serialise to serde_json::Value via serde_json::to_value, (2) recursively walk the Value substituting (a) any string field named `tool_call_id` with "<tc>", (b) any string field named `correlation_id` / `id` matching the UUID regex with "<uuid>", (c) any string field named `timestamp` / `created_at` matching the RFC-3339 regex with "<ts>". Uses regex-once-compiled-via-Lazy. The output Vec<Value> is then serialised line-by-line as JSONL via serde_json::to_string and compared byte-by-byte to the golden file.

[G] Status-settling discipline: after every backend RPC call that triggers an agent-loop turn (send_input, compact_session), the test calls `wait_for_status(&mut status_rx, SessionStatus::Idle, Duration::from_secs(5))` BEFORE issuing the next RPC. This prevents racey chunk-stream interleaving. The helper subscribes to backend.status_changes_rx() and drains until it sees the target status for the active session.

[H] Test runtime gating: top-level test fn is annotated `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]`. The whole test body is wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(45), …)` to enforce AC #5 (< 60s). The fixture-regeneration codepath is also wrapped in the same timeout.

[I] Risk acknowledgement: this is the FIRST card that exercises the real SessionManager + BackgroundSession against a real provider end-to-end through a WS client. Earlier cards (RPC-037, RPC-049, etc.) use StubSessionManagerHandle, which bypasses the agent loop entirely. Expect to discover small bugs in the agent-loop wiring (compaction, interrupt, status-change broadcast on tool calls) during the implementing phase. If the test surfaces blocking bugs, split them into sibling cards rather than fixing inline.

[J] AST research finding: custom_provider_registered (codelet/providers/src/manager.rs:131) consults ONLY discover_provider_configs() which scans disk-resident JSON. The original architecture note [C] ("insert a synthetic ProviderConfig into the custom provider registry") does not match the current code shape — there is no in-memory registry slot. RESOLUTION: register_stub_provider() (in codelet/providers/src/stub_provider.rs behind test-support) adds a NEW process-global OnceLock<HashMap<String, Arc<dyn LlmProvider>>> and custom_provider_registered() is extended to consult BOTH the disk discovery AND the in-memory map. The ProviderManager's match arm for ProviderType::Custom is also extended to look up the in-memory map first, falling back to the existing RhaiCustomProvider path. This keeps the stub registration entirely RAM-only, deterministic, and out of the Rhai code path.

[K] AST research finding: FspecBackend::create_session(role: Option<String>) does NOT accept a model string — it routes to SessionManagerHandle::create_session which reads SessionManager::get_default_model() (codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs:75). RESOLUTION: build_service() under #[cfg(feature = "test-stub-provider")] must (a) call codelet_providers::stub_provider::register_stub_provider() FIRST, then (b) call manager.set_default_model("stub/canned") BEFORE the SessionManager is wrapped in Arc<dyn SessionManagerHandle>. The test then drives create_session(None) over the WS backend and gets a session bound to the stub provider automatically.

[L] AST research finding: the stub provider's complete_with_tools ToolUse branch will route the SessionManager into codelet_tools to dispatch a tool slug. RESOLUTION: register a stub tool slug `noop_tool` in codelet/providers/src/stub_provider.rs (or a sibling module) behind test-support that takes empty input and returns a static `"ok"` ToolResult. Wired alongside register_stub_provider(). Without this the agent loop will error out trying to find an unregistered tool.

RPC-066.description: Phase 8.2: Boot the fspec binary in combined mode against a stub provider. Drive every slash command end-to-end. Capture chunks. Assert the chunk stream matches the equivalent TS-frontend run against the same stub provider, modulo cosmetic differences (timestamps, UUIDs). Test lives in codelet/fspec/tests/ or codelet/fspec-tui/tests/.

examples.text: When the test seeds a workspace under tempdir with no spec/work-units.json and spawns `fspec daemon --workspace <tmp>`, scan_for_port_equals on stdout returns a u16 in 1024..=65535 within 5s (mirrors daemon_mode.rs:31 contract)

When the workspace contains `.fspec/providers/stub.json` whose `name` is `stub` (handled by codelet_providers::custom::discover_provider_configs), and the test enables the providers crate `test-support` feature so the new StubProvider LlmProvider impl is compiled in, then ProviderType::from_str("stub") returns Ok(ProviderType::Custom("stub")) and SessionManager::create_session("stub/canned", workspace) succeeds without HTTP I/O

When the test connects a WebSocketFspecBackend to the daemon, calls backend.create_session("stub/canned"), subscribes to backend.chunks_rx() into a Vec<(SessionId, StreamChunk)>, and calls backend.send_input(session, "hello"), then within 5 seconds the captured vec contains EXACTLY the sequence [Text { text: "hi back", .. }, Done] (matches the existing StubProvider::canned_chunks() contract from RPC-007)

When the scripted run sends the sequence [send_input("hello"), clear_history(), set_thinking_level(High), send_input("trigger-tool"), compact_session(), interrupt()] against the daemon, and each step waits for the SessionStatus to settle back to Idle via backend.status_changes_rx(), then the captured chunk stream — after normalisation — is byte-identical to the golden file at codelet/fspec/tests/fixtures/cross_frontend_run.jsonl

When normalise_chunk_stream(&chunks) is invoked, every Text chunk's text field passes through unchanged, but ToolCall.tool_call_id becomes "<tc>", any UUID matching the regex `[0-9a-f]{8}-([0-9a-f]{4}-){3}[0-9a-f]{12}` becomes "<uuid>", any RFC-3339 timestamp becomes "<ts>", and any correlation_id field becomes "<corr>"

When the codelet/fspec/tests/fixtures/cross_frontend_run.jsonl file is missing AND the env var FSPEC_RPC_066_REGENERATE=1 is set, the test re-records the captured-and-normalised stream to that file and skips assertion (exit success); without the env var, a missing fixture fails the test with a clear message pointing at the regeneration command

When a regression is injected by editing background_session.rs to emit StreamChunk::text("oops") instead of forwarding the provider chunk, then `cargo test -p codelet-fspec --test cross_frontend_parity` fails with a diff that points at the changed chunk (proves the test catches regressions — AC #4)
When `cargo test -p codelet-fspec --test cross_frontend_parity --features codelet-providers/test-support` runs end-to-end, total wall-clock time is under 60s on a stock dev laptop (AC #5)

When the test boots the daemon with HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1 and HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1 (a dead proxy), the stub provider's send_input still resolves to the canned chunk stream within 5s — proving no network egress occurs during the scripted run (deny-network guard)

When the new codelet/fspec/tests/README.md is read, it contains a section titled `## Regenerating cross_frontend_run.jsonl` describing the FSPEC_RPC_066_REGENERATE=1 step AND a section titled `## Future: TS-recorded reference fixture` documenting the (deferred) follow-up procedure for re-recording chunks from the TS Ink frontend

Should this card (a) ship with a TS reference fixture you regenerate as part of this card (requires booting the TS frontend against the same stub provider — significant scope), OR (b) ship with a Rust-side golden file as the initial pinned reference (so the test guards against regressions in the Rust-only chunk stream and the TS-side fixture is added in a follow-up RPC card)? rules.text: Test file lives at codelet/fspec/tests/cross_frontend_parity.rs and exercises the real fspec binary, NOT a MockBackend (that is RPC-065's surface)

The test uses daemon mode (fspec daemon --workspace <tmp>) NOT combined mode — combined-mode tests grab /dev/tty via ratatui::init and the existing combined_smoke.rs tests are all #[ignore]'d for that reason; daemon mode exercises the exact same SessionManager + RPC surface (codelet/fspec/src/common.rs::build_service is shared) with zero TTY contention

The stub provider is a NEW LlmProvider impl in codelet/providers/src/stub_provider.rs, gated by the existing `test-support` cargo feature, that returns deterministic responses with NO network I/O — the existing minimal StubProvider struct only exposes canned_chunks() and does not implement LlmProvider; this card widens it

The stub provider is registered as a ProviderType::Custom variant via the existing codelet_providers::manager::register_custom_provider mechanism so that SessionManager::create_session_with_id("stub/canned", ...) routes through it without any HTTP requests

The scripted run drives every USER-FACING slash command equivalent (/help, plain text, /clear, /thinking high, tool-call-trigger prompt, /compact, /quit) via the WebSocketFspecBackend RPC methods that the AgentView's dispatch path already wires to (NOT by faking keystrokes into the TUI — the TUI is not booted in daemon mode)

Captured chunks pass through a normalisation pipeline that substitutes timestamps → <ts>, UUIDs → <uuid>, correlation IDs → <corr>, tool-call IDs → <tc> BEFORE assertions; the normalised stream is byte-identical to spec/attachments/RPC-066/fixtures/ts_reference_run.jsonl (or a pinned Rust-side golden if the TS fixture is deferred — see questions)

Total test runtime is under 60 seconds wall-clock; tool calls invoke ONLY sandboxed paths (the stub provider's tool-call response carries a pre-shaped JSON envelope with NO real Bash / file I/O) — the SessionManager's tool dispatcher must never reach codelet_tools::bash or codelet_tools::edit during the scripted run

The test fails fast if the stub provider attempts ANY network access (reqwest::get / HTTP / WebSocket leak detection via a deny-network harness wrapper or a tracing assertion that no `eventsource-stream` / `reqwest::Client` paths fire during the scripted run)
Regeneration procedure for the TS reference fixture is documented in codelet/fspec/tests/README.md (new file) so the team can re-record after a TS frontend change without spelunking the test source

Use daemon mode (`fspec daemon --workspace <tmp>`) for headless CI parity — combined and daemon share build_service() so the SessionManager + chunk surface is identical. Combined-mode coverage stays the responsibility of the existing #[ignore]'d combined_smoke.rs tests.

Ship a Rust-pinned golden file at codelet/fspec/tests/fixtures/cross_frontend_run.jsonl as the initial regression baseline. TS-side fixture regeneration is a follow-up RPC card once the TS stub-provider boot recipe is documented.

Widen codelet/providers/src/stub_provider.rs to implement the LlmProvider trait behind the existing `test-support` feature; register under slug `stub` via the existing custom-provider mechanism so SessionManager::create_session("stub/canned", ...) reaches it via ProviderType::Custom. This keeps the agent loop in the test path.

Omit /thinking from the chunk-stream comparison for this card. Side-effect coverage (set_thinking_level, get_session_model, etc.) lives in the per-method cross-transport parity tests already (rpc037_cross_transport_parity.rs, rpc049_cross_transport_parity.rs, etc.).

architectureNotes.text: The new codelet/test-helpers/ crate is added to the workspace `members` list AND exposed as `codelet-test-helpers = { path = "test-helpers" }` in [workspace.dependencies] — so consuming crates declare it via `codelet-test-helpers.workspace = true` in [dev-dependencies]

The helper API has two functions: `assert_no_codelet_napi_in_dependency_graph(crate_name: &str)` (cargo metadata BFS — fails if codelet-napi appears in the transitive set) and `assert_no_codelet_napi_imports_in_sources(crate_dir: &str)` (walks codelet/<crate_dir>/src/*.rs, strips comments, fails on `use codelet_napi` or `codelet_napi::` substrings)

Helpers do not hardcode `codelet-napi` — they take it as `forbidden: &str` so the same scaffolding can later forbid other arrows (e.g. `core → napi`-third-party, `rpc-types → tokio`). The first wave passes `"codelet-napi"` and `"codelet_napi"` explicitly.

Refined helper API: `assert_no_transitive_dependency(from_crate: &str, forbidden_pkg: &str)` and `assert_no_import_in_sources(crate_dir_name: &str, forbidden_module: &str)`. The crate_dir_name is the directory name under codelet/ (e.g. "fspec", "fspec-tui", "sessions", "core", "rpc-types").

codelet/test-helpers/Cargo.toml depends on serde_json (workspace) ONLY — no other deps. It is a library crate with [lib] (default) plus the workspace lints inherited. The `[lints] workspace = true` block applies.

examples.text: Sabotage scenario (manually verified): temporarily adding `codelet-napi = { workspace = true }` to codelet/core/Cargo.toml makes codelet-core's no_napi_dependency.rs FAIL with a clear message naming codelet-napi
When the codelet workspace is in its current state, `cargo test -p codelet-core --test no_napi_dependency` exits 0 and reports the transitive package set excludes `codelet-napi`

When `cargo test -p codelet-rpc-types --test no_napi_dependency` runs with the default feature set (no `napi` feature), the transitive package walk completes without finding `codelet-napi`, and the source scan of codelet/rpc-types/src/ finds no `use codelet_napi` import

After migration, the file codelet/fspec/tests/no_napi_dependency.rs is under 30 lines and contains only `use codelet_test_helpers::dependency_rules::*` plus two #[test] fns that call assert_no_codelet_napi_in_dependency_graph("codelet-fspec") and assert_no_codelet_napi_imports_in_sources("fspec")

If a developer adds `codelet-napi = { workspace = true }` to codelet/core/Cargo.toml and re-runs `cargo test -p codelet-core --test no_napi_dependency`, the test FAILS with an error message containing both `codelet-core` and `codelet-napi` and pointing at the forbidden-arrow rule

When the source-scan helper walks a crate root that contains a doc comment with the literal text `// codelet_napi was here`, it does NOT flag the file because comments are stripped before substring matching (mirrors strip_rust_comments in the existing tests)

When `cargo test --workspace` runs from a clean target dir, every no_napi_dependency.rs test binary (core, rpc-types, fspec, fspec-tui, sessions) completes within 10 seconds each — the cargo metadata invocation dominates runtime and is shared across all binaries

rules.text: A new workspace crate codelet-test-helpers exposes assert_no_dependency(from, to) and assert_no_imports_in_sources(crate_root, forbidden_module) helpers that any tests/*.rs binary can call

The helpers use the same cargo metadata JSON-walk strategy already used by codelet/fspec/tests/no_napi_dependency.rs (NOT cargo tree text grep) so behaviour is consistent with the existing RPC-044 tests
codelet-test-helpers itself MUST NOT depend on codelet-napi (it must be safe to consume from any forbidden-arrow test) — only dev-quality helpers like serde_json

New regression test file codelet/core/tests/no_napi_dependency.rs asserts (a) no codelet-napi in codelet-core's transitive cargo-metadata dependency graph and (b) no `codelet_napi::` / `use codelet_napi` substring under codelet/core/src/

New regression test file codelet/rpc-types/tests/no_napi_dependency.rs asserts (a) no codelet-napi in codelet-rpc-types' transitive dependency graph (the optional `napi` feature pulls the third-party `napi` crate, NOT `codelet-napi`) and (b) no `codelet_napi::` / `use codelet_napi` substring under codelet/rpc-types/src/

The three existing no_napi_dependency.rs files under codelet/fspec/tests, codelet/fspec-tui/tests, codelet/sessions/tests are migrated to delegate to the shared helpers — each file remains a thin wrapper of two #[test] fns that call the helper with the appropriate crate name + source root

codelet/rpc-embedded/tests/rpc_006_source_shape.rs is left untouched — it asserts wider invariants (default_fixture cfg-gating, host-runtime handle, loopback-only bind, WorkUnitInfo deduplication, no-bincode push path) that go beyond the no-napi rule and would be lost if collapsed into the helper

RPC-070.description:
End-to-end reproduction via @microsoft/tui-test (e2e/rpc-068-work-agent-panic-repro.test.ts) confirms the Rust `fspec` binary panics the moment a user presses Enter on a work unit to open the Work Agent. The board renders fine (control test passes); the crash is isolated to the create_session path.

ROOT CAUSE
----------
In codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs, several SessionManagerHandle trait methods are SYNCHRONOUS but bridge to ASYNC SessionManager methods using `tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(...)`. The tarpc handler at codelet/rpc/src/lib.rs:761 is itself an `async` closure already running on a multi-thread tokio worker, so `Handle::current().block_on()` panics with:

    'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at sessions/src/handle_impl.rs:79:14:
    Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime.

The doc comment at lines 11–18 conflates 'thread has a runtime handle' with 'thread isn't already being driven by that runtime' — the latter is what `block_on` actually requires.

SIX AFFECTED CALL SITES
-----------------------
  • handle_impl.rs:78–80   create_session            (Handle::current().block_on)
  • handle_impl.rs:620–623 create_isolated_session   (Handle::current().block_on)
  • handle_impl.rs:877–879 test_provider_connection  (owns runtime, but called from tarpc context)
  • handle_impl.rs:1251    loop_add        (via loop_block_on)
  • handle_impl.rs:1262    loop_cancel     (via loop_block_on)
  • handle_impl.rs:1275    loop_list       (via loop_block_on)
  • handle_impl.rs:1288–1294 loop_block_on() helper itself

WHY RPC-068 MISSED IT
---------------------
RPC-068's audit ran `cargo test --workspace` + the no_napi_dependency boundary test. Unit tests for these bridge methods all use `#[tokio::test]` which spins up its OWN runtime — `Handle::current().block_on()` only panics when invoked from inside an already-running async future, which only the live tarpc dispatch path produces. The cross_frontend_parity tests exercise the WS transport but four of them are `#[ignore]`'d pending RPC-069.

FIX OPTIONS
-----------
A. Refactor SessionManagerHandle trait methods to `async fn` and `.await` them in the tarpc handler. Cleanest, but ripples through every impl (NAPI, stub) and every caller.

B. Wrap each bridge call in `tokio::task::block_in_place(|| Handle::current().block_on(...))`. Only works on a multi-thread runtime — both the fspec binary and codelet-napi tokio_main use multi-thread, so this is safe. Minimal surface change.

C. Inline async work into a fresh `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()` per call (already what test_provider_connection does at line 875). Heavyweight; allocates a dedicated runtime for every RPC call.

Recommend OPTION B for the production fix — matches the pattern codelet/tools/src/schedule/handler.rs:21 already uses, requires no trait surface changes, and unblocks tarpc dispatch immediately. Option A can be a follow-up cleanup card if desired.

ACCEPTANCE
----------
• `e2e/rpc-068-work-agent-panic-repro.test.ts` MUST pass (no 'Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime' in the rendered buffer after pressing Enter).
• Existing `cargo test --workspace -p codelet-sessions` MUST still pass.
• Add a new integration test that calls `create_session` via the live tarpc WebSocket transport (not `#[tokio::test]`) to prevent regression — RPC-068's boundary audit would have caught this with such a test.

RPC-071.description:
AgentView's per-session scrollback renderer falls through `format!("{other:?}")` for every StreamChunk variant it doesn't explicitly handle, leaking raw Rust Debug output into the user-visible scrollback.

User-visible symptom (reproduced 2026-05-27 via fspec binary, codelet-integration branch):

    user> please review this card
    UserInput { text: "please review this card" }
    SessionStateChange { state: Running }
    SessionStateChange { state: Idle }

The last three lines should NOT appear. The TypeScript Ink frontend (src/tui/utils/chunkProcessor.ts:227-232 and src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx:291,3501) treats UserInput as a friendly `user> {text}` scrollback line, and treats SessionStateChange / IsolationStateChange / DebugStateChange / FooterStateUpdate / FspecCommandRequest / SupervisorPendingInjection / CompactionComplete as PURE state-mutation chunks that drive footer / status-pill / dialog state but NEVER land in scrollback.

ROOT CAUSE
----------
codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/session_context.rs:101-111 — chunk_to_lines has a catch-all `other => format!("{other:?}")` arm that unconditionally Debug-prints every unhandled variant into scrollback.

Additionally, dispatch_rpc045.rs::handle_stream_chunk_state_updates already correctly mutates store state for the seven RPC-045 state variants, but record_chunk runs BEFORE that helper inside the Action::ChunkReceived arm and pushes a rendered line regardless. So the state variants are double-handled: state mutation (correct) PLUS a Debug-dumped scrollback line (wrong).

CONTRACT THE FIX MUST ESTABLISH
-------------------------------
chunk_to_lines must return Option<Vec<Line>>:
  • Some(formatted line) for human-visible chunks: Text, Thinking, UserInput, UserNotification, Error, Done
  • None for pure state-mutation chunks: SessionStateChange, IsolationStateChange, DebugStateChange, FooterStateUpdate, FspecCommandRequest, SupervisorPendingInjection, CompactionComplete, FspecCommandResult, WorkUnitsUpdate, IncomingMessage (handled separately), TokenUpdate, ContextFillUpdate, Interrupted, ToolCall (handled separately), ToolResult (handled separately), ToolProgress (handled separately)
  • Catch-all arm replaced with `debug_assert!(false, "unhandled StreamChunk variant: {other:?}")` so any future enum addition fails loud in debug builds

record_chunk skips the scrollback push when chunk_to_lines returns None.

This card is the RPC-045 follow-up the original acceptance promised but didn't deliver ("handle every new StreamChunk variant").

See spec/attachments/RPC-071/ for full root-cause analysis, TS parity reference, fix plan, and test plan.

12. Lifecycle hooks — session_start/user_prompt_submit/post_tool_use/session_end never invoked.
13. Persistence (REFAC-007) — zero persist calls; /resume finds nothing to restore.

RPC-073.description:
Three distinct regressions discovered after RPC-072 landed and the fspec Rust binary started accepting input:

1. **/clear panics the binary** — typing `/clear` in a Work Agent session crashes the tokio worker with `thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at sessions/src/background_session.rs:1156:36: Cannot block the current thread from within a runtime`. Root cause: `BackgroundSession::clear_history` uses `self.inner.blocking_lock()` and is invoked synchronously from `handle_impl.rs::clear_history` which runs inside an async tarpc dispatcher. RPC-070's enforcement only guards `Handle::current().block_on(` — `blocking_lock` slipped through.

2. **`?` and `q` are trapped globally even while typing in AgentView input** — `App::handle_event` calls `handle_app_shortcut` BEFORE the compositor and navigator (see codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/events.rs:46-54). Pressing `?` always opens the HelpDialog regardless of whether the user is composing a message. `q` quits the app. The dispatch order is inverted from what the AgentView needs.

3. **Model selector dialog is empty / doesn't reflect ~/.fspec/fspec-config.json** — `SessionManager::list_providers` in codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs:709-715 returns hardcoded `Vec::new()` with a comment deferring the wiring to RPC-054. RPC-054 actually wired `list_provider_credentials` (the /provider settings view), NOT `list_providers` (the model selector dialog populated by RPC-022). The path from `ProviderManager` / `codelet_providers::custom::management::list_providers_info` into the trait override never landed.

User repro (codelet-integration branch, 2026-05-27 11:38–11:39):
- Build: `cd codelet && cargo build --release`
- Run: `./codelet/target/release/fspec`
- Open a Work Agent on RPC-071 (any done card).
- Type `is this card done` → provider does respond (claude 429 — RPC-072 wiring works), but the user can't type `?` while composing.
- Open model dialog → list is empty (no providers).
- Type `/clear` → tarpc deadline error, then panic backtrace from background_session.rs:1156.

See spec/attachments/RPC-073/ for full root-cause analysis, screenshot evidence, and proposed fixes per bug.

RPC-074.description:
The Rust /clear slash command pushes a synthetic '[notice] /clear: history cleared' line into the focused session's scrollback on Ok and '[error] /clear failed: <e>' on Err. The TypeScript reference (src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx:1554-1564, handleClearCommand) does NOT do this — it only blanks the input and calls sessionClearHistory(currentSessionId). Errors go to logger.error, never to scrollback.

The scrollback reset must happen as a side effect of the SessionStateChange { state: Cleared } chunk arriving (TUI-066 contract in TS), not synchronously from the dispatcher pushing a notice string.

The divergence exists in TWO places:
1. codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc046.rs:59 — synthesises the notice text and pushes via Action::EmitSessionNotice
2. codelet/core/src/session_manager_handle.rs:1509 — broadcasts a StreamChunk::UserNotification { message: 'history cleared' } chunk that the TS path never emits

RPC-046 codified this divergence on 2026-05-22 (before TS parity was a stated requirement). RPC-037 cross-transport-parity tests then ASSERT the divergence exists in both transports — those assertions must be retired.

User directive (verbatim, 2026-05-27): '"message history cleared" with /clear IS NOT THE FUNCTIONALITY OF TYPESCRIPT IMPLEMENTATION! YOU MUST COPY THE EXACT WAY IT WORKS - NOT MAKE SHIT UP!!!'

See spec/attachments/RPC-074/ for full root-cause analysis, TS reference evidence, fix plan, and the screenshot the user captured.

Given a subscriber on backend.chunks_rx(), when backend.clear_history(sid).await is called on either transport against the StubSessionManagerHandle, then within 1 second a StreamChunk::SessionStateChange { state: Cleared } arrives for sid — and NO StreamChunk::UserNotification with message 'history cleared' is observed

Given the real fspec binary running under tui-test, when the user opens a Work Agent and types '/clear' followed by Enter, then the rendered scrollback after the keystroke does NOT contain '[notice] /clear:' or '[error] /clear failed:' anywhere
Source-shape check: a grep for 'history cleared' in codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc046.rs and codelet/core/src/session_manager_handle.rs returns zero matches

The StubSessionManagerHandle MUST emit the same SessionStateChange { state: Cleared } chunk on clear_history so cross-transport parity tests can observe identical behaviour on both transports

The import was added in uncommitted WIP — see `git diff codelet/core/src/session_manager_handle.rs` which shows `+ NotificationSeverity, PauseState, ProviderInfo,` but no consuming use site inside the file.

Fix options:

  B) Add a use site (if the WIP that added the import is incomplete and was supposed to call it).

  - cargo test -p codelet-sessions --test skeleton_invariants -- scenario_workspace_lints_are_inherited_and_clippy_passes → passes

RPC-077.description:
codelet/sessions/tests/skeleton_invariants.rs::scenario_workspace_lints_are_inherited_and_clippy_passes still fails after RPC-076 (which fixed the NotificationSeverity unused_imports in codelet-core/src/session_manager_handle.rs) because `cargo clippy -p codelet-sessions --all-targets -- -D warnings` now surfaces two `clippy::redundant_clone` diagnostics in codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs:

  - line 1321:    `id: id.clone(),`            -- this value is dropped without further use
  - line 1323:    `prompt: prompt.clone(),`     -- this value is dropped without further use

This is the third in a chain of sibling bugs filed against `scenario_workspace_lints_are_inherited_and_clippy_passes`:
  - RPC-075 (done): fixed `clippy::uninlined_format_args` in codelet-core/src/scheduler/
  - RPC-076 (in progress at filing time): fixed `clippy::unused_imports` for NotificationSeverity in codelet-core/src/session_manager_handle.rs
  - RPC-077 (this card): fix `clippy::redundant_clone` in codelet-sessions/src/handle_impl.rs

Fix is a pure mechanical refactor — drop the `.clone()` calls because both `id` and `prompt` are owned values dropped at the end of the struct literal anyway.

Verification:

  - cargo test -p codelet-sessions --test skeleton_invariants -- scenario_workspace_lints_are_inherited_and_clippy_passes  → passes (this is the third sibling card needed to take skeleton_invariants fully green)

If any FURTHER clippy violations are surfaced after this fix, file an RPC-078 sibling. The pattern of one-bug-one-card prevents scope creep and keeps each fix mechanically obvious.
