RPC-078.description:
The Rust ratatui port of AgentView in codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/session_context.rs::chunk_to_lines uses literal prefixes that DO NOT EXIST anywhere in the TypeScript Ink reference (src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx + src/tui/utils/chunkProcessor.ts + src/tui/utils/conversationUtils.ts):

WRONG (current Rust port):
  UserInput      → "user> {text}"
  Text           → "assistant> {text}"
  Thinking       → "(thinking) {text}"
  Error          → "[error] {error}"
  Done           → "[done]"
  Interrupted    → "[interrupted] N queued"
  UserNotification → "[notice] {message}"
  IncomingMessage → "supervisor> {text}"

CORRECT (TS Ink reference — grep proves "user>" and "assistant>" literals do NOT exist anywhere in src/tui/):
  UserInput      → prefix "You: " (conversationUtils.ts:67-68), rendered GREEN (AgentView.tsx:5379)
  Text           → prefix "● " (U+25CF, conversationUtils.ts:69-71), rendered WHITE, while streaming "..." is appended (line 88-90)
  Thinking       → prefix "[Thinking]\n" + body (thinkingBlockManager.ts:36), rendered YELLOW (AgentView.tsx:5366-5372)
  Error          → "API Error: {error}" as a 'status' message (chunkProcessor.ts:355-358, 570-573), rendered WHITE
  Done           → NO scrollback line at all — finalises streaming by stripping the trailing "..." from the assistant message
  Interrupted    → "⚠ Interrupted" as a 'status' message (AgentView.tsx:465-468) — OR appends "\nL ⚠ Interrupted" to the in-flight tool-call when a tool is active (chunkProcessor.ts:374-378)
  UserNotification → use chunk.message verbatim (no [notice] prefix) — used for "⟳ Reconnecting...", "✓ Reconnected", "✗ Reconnection failed" (AgentView.tsx:469-487)
  IncomingMessage → reformat "[SUPERVISOR: {role} | Session: {id}]\n{body}" as "[W] {role}> {body}" (chunkProcessor.ts:99; AgentView.tsx:301), rendered MAGENTA (AgentView.tsx:5380)

DUPLICATE USER INPUT BUG (visible in 2026-05-28 screenshot):
  app/dispatch_rpc020.rs::handle_input_submitted at line 251-253 unconditionally pushes a synchronous "user> {text}" line into the focused session's scrollback. THEN sessions/src/background_session.rs::send_input at line 1089 broadcasts StreamChunk::user_input back through the chunk subscriber, which chunk_to_lines also renders. Two pushes per Enter — every user message appears twice.

  TS Ink reference does NOT duplicate: AgentView.tsx::handleSubmit synchronously appends ONE { type: 'user-input', content: userMessage } to local conversation state (line 1870-1873), and the rust-side BackgroundSession::send_input UserInput broadcast is the buffered replay channel that ONLY fires when the conversation is rehydrated via /resume — NOT during live input. The Rust SessionManager broadcasts UserInput on EVERY send_input which is the root-cause divergence from TS.

WRAPPING / TRUNCATION BUG (visible in 2026-05-28 screenshot — long rig 429 error clipped at right edge):
  views/agent/scrollback.rs::render_count_visited paints each Line into a 1-row tall Rect with Paragraph::new(line).render(row, buf) and NO wrap(Wrap{trim:false}). ratatui Paragraph truncates at width by default. max_offset_for_viewport assumes 1 row per chunk.

  TS Ink reference: wrapping happens BEFORE the items hit VirtualList. conversationUtils.ts::messagesToLines calls wrapText(content, {maxWidth}) for each message, producing one ConversationLine per visual row. VirtualList's "1 item = 1 visual row" invariant is upheld by pre-splitting (textWrap.ts lines 7-19). NO Ink wrap=\"wrap\" attribute is used.

FIX (exact parity port):
  1) Rewrite session_context.rs::chunk_to_lines to produce the EXACT TS prefixes ("You: ", "● ", "[Thinking]\n", "API Error: ", "⚠ Interrupted", supervisor reformatting, no [done] line). Drop Done/UserNotification/Interrupted Debug-style brackets.
  2) Add a ratatui Style per line variant (green for user, yellow for thinking, magenta for supervisor, white default, red for tool-error). chunk_to_lines returns Vec<Line<'static>> where each Line carries the appropriate Color::Green/Yellow/Magenta/White Span style.
  3) Delete the synchronous push_line("user> {text}") at dispatch_rpc020.rs:251-253. The visible user input line comes ONLY from the UserInput chunk broadcast.
  4) Port the TS wrapText algorithm to Rust (or use ratatui Paragraph::line_count with the unstable-rendered-line-info feature) so each chunk's body is pre-split into one Line per visual row before it lands in ScrollbackList. Then render each Line into a 1-row Rect as today (no wrapping needed at render time because the wrapping is already baked in).
  5) Fix max_offset_for_viewport to count actual rendered Lines per chunk (not chunks).

Regression coverage:
  - chunk_rendering_parity_rpc078.rs unit test: UserInput renders "You: hi" GREEN; Text renders "● hi" WHITE; Thinking renders "[Thinking]\n..." YELLOW; Error renders "API Error: ..." WHITE; Done renders no line; UserNotification renders verbatim; Interrupted renders "⚠ Interrupted".
  - duplicate_user_input_rpc078.rs unit test: dispatch(InputSubmitted("hi")) followed by dispatch(ChunkReceived(s-1, UserInput("hi"))) yields exactly ONE "You: hi" line.
  - scrollback_wrap_rpc078.rs unit test: a 300-char chunk body pre-wraps into ceil(308/80)=4 ConversationLine items inside a fresh 80-column viewport.
  - e2e/rpc-078-scrollback-wrap-and-no-duplicate.test.ts driving the real binary: types "is this card done?", presses Enter, asserts "You: is this card done?" appears EXACTLY ONCE (regex with negative double-match assertion). Types "is this card done?" again, asserts a SECOND "You: is this card done?" appears (so total count is 2, not 4). Forces a synthetic long error line and asserts it wraps without leaving stranded fragments.

examples.text: User types "hi" and presses Enter — the scrollback shows exactly one green line reading `You: hi`, never `user> hi` and never duplicated
The assistant replies — the scrollback shows a white line that starts with `● ` followed by the reply text, never `assistant> `
The provider returns a 429 — the user sees `API Error: ...` in white, NOT `[error] ...`
Streaming finishes — the trailing `...` on the assistant line is removed and no `[done]` line ever appears
User presses Ctrl+C while streaming — the user sees `⚠ Interrupted` in white, NOT `[interrupted] 0 queued`
The reasoning model emits thinking — the user sees a YELLOW block starting with `[Thinking]` on its own row, followed by the thinking body — not `(thinking) ...`
A supervisor session sends `[SUPERVISOR: reviewer | Session: s-2]\nplease check this` — the user sees `[W] reviewer> please check this` in MAGENTA — never `supervisor> ...`
WebSocket reconnects — the user sees `⟳ Reconnecting...` then `✓ Reconnected` rendered verbatim (the chunk message is the visible text, no `[notice]` prefix)
User types a 300-char message in a 80-column terminal — the green `You: ...` line wraps across multiple visual rows, every character is visible, nothing is clipped at the right edge
After a long wrapped API Error spanning 4 visual rows, the user can still see the lines that follow it — none of them are stranded as the only visible row while earlier content is clipped

On a fresh session with only a 'You: what is this card about?' line and an 'API Error: ...' line, the rendered buffer shows those two lines at the TOP of the scrollback viewport, NOT at the bottom with empty space above. The empty rows fall below the most recent message (or are absorbed by the flex layout), never above the first message.

End-to-end App.render: user submits 'what is this card about?', provider returns Error chunk; the rendered 80x24 buffer shows 'You: ...' at scrollback row 0 (y=1), 'API Error: ...' at row 1 (y=2), and NO blank rows above 'You: ...' (no empty rows between header at y=0 and 'You: ...' at y=1)

rules.text: Scrollback lines wider than the viewport MUST wrap onto multiple visual rows using ratatui Paragraph word-wrap and MUST NOT be truncated
Stick-to-bottom mode keeps the latest chunk fully visible, accounting for wrapped row counts of every chunk between the new offset and the tail
UserInput chunks render as one line prefixed with "You: " in GREEN — never as "user> "
Text (assistant) chunks render prefixed with "● " (U+25CF) in WHITE — never as "assistant> "
Thinking chunks render prefixed with "[Thinking]\n" in YELLOW — never as "(thinking) "
Error chunks render as "API Error: {error}" in WHITE — never as "[error] {error}"
Done chunks produce NO scrollback line at all — never "[done]"
Interrupted chunks render as "⚠ Interrupted" in WHITE — never as "[interrupted] N queued"
UserNotification chunks render the message text verbatim — never wrapped in "[notice] "
IncomingMessage chunks parse "[SUPERVISOR: role | Session: id]\nbody" and render as "[W] role> body" in MAGENTA — never as "supervisor> "
Each Enter press produces EXACTLY ONE "You: {text}" line in scrollback — the local synchronous push at handle_input_submitted must be removed so the UserInput chunk broadcast is the single source

Scrollback lines wider than the viewport are pre-wrapped into one Line per visual row before being pushed (mirrors TS wrapText + messagesToLines) so the existing one-Line-per-row render path produces no truncation
Stick-to-bottom math counts actual rendered Lines (visual rows) per chunk — not chunk count — so the tail-most visible content stays in view when chunks wrap

Scrollback content fills from the TOP of the viewport when total visual rows are fewer than the viewport height; bottom-anchored stick-to-bottom only applies when content overflows the viewport. A short conversation must NEVER leave blank rows above the first message.

Scrollback content top-fills through the FULL App.render path (Navigator → AgentView::render_with_store → ScrollbackList::render_count_visited), not just when rendering ScrollbackList directly — the AgentView layout (Header + RoleBanner + Scrollback(Min(0)) + Footer + Input) must place 'You: hi' at the FIRST row of the scrollback area (y=1 when header height=1 and role_height=0), never at the bottom row of the scrollback area

Rust port targets: codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/error_dialog.rs, notification_dialog.rs, status_dialog.rs (new). Register in codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/mod.rs.
Canonical primitive: codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/dialog_theme.rs::render_dialog. Reuse Accent enum, FspecDialog struct, MARKER_SELECTED/MARKER_UNSELECTED/FOOTER_SEPARATOR constants.

RPC-079.description: The Rust TUI side has dialog_theme::render_dialog as the canonical overlay primitive (the Accent/FspecDialog system created in RPC-027), and 8 concrete dialogs delegate to it. But it lacks generic reusable wrappers for the three TS Ink dialog semantics: ErrorDialog (red, sticky, ESC-only), NotificationDialog (green/cyan/yellow by type, auto-dismiss with countdown), and StatusDialog (cyan→green/red state machine for progress→complete/error). Today every consumer of these semantics rolls a one-off FspecDialog struct inline. This work unit ports the three TS components from src/components/{ErrorDialog,NotificationDialog,StatusDialog}.tsx to codelet/fspec-tui/src/components/{error_dialog,notification_dialog,status_dialog}.rs. Each must: (1) delegate to render_dialog (no hand-rendering), (2) match the TS API surface (message, type/severity, auto_dismiss_ms, onClose semantics via Callback), (3) implement Component with Priority::Critical, (4) live alongside the other dialogs in components/, and (5) ship with insta snapshot tests + behaviour tests verifying ESC dismissal, auto-dismiss timing (where applicable), and state transitions (StatusDialog). Then refactor every existing inline-FspecDialog error/notification/progress consumer to use the new wrappers.

examples.text: ErrorDialog::new('Disk full') rendered into an 80x24 TestBackend produces a centered red rounded border, bold red 'Error' title, red 'Disk full' body row, dim centered 'Press ESC to dismiss' footer

NotificationDialog::success('Saved') with default auto_dismiss_ms=2000 shows green title 'Success', cyan border, 'Closing in 2s... (ESC to dismiss)' footer; after 2s the dialog emits a dismissal Callback
NotificationDialog::warning('Slow connection') with auto_dismiss_ms=0 shows yellow title 'Warning', yellow border, static 'Press ESC to dismiss' footer (no countdown)
StatusDialog in Restoring state with current='file3.txt' idx=3 total=10 shows cyan border, cyan 'Restoring Files' title, 'file3.txt' body, '(3/10)' counter; ESC is ignored (no Callback emitted)
StatusDialog transitions Restoring→Complete: cyan border with green title 'Restore Complete!', auto-closes after 3s with 'Closing in Ns...' countdown, ESC skips the wait
StatusDialog transitions Restoring→Error: red border, bold red 'Error' title, red error_message body, ESC dismisses the dialog
Every new dialog test fixture that grep-asserts the rendered buffer NEVER finds inline FspecDialog struct usage in non-test code (verified by clippy lint or repo grep)

User asks Claude a question; provider returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests; the user sees an ErrorDialog modal centered on screen with red 'Error' title and the full rate-limit message body, and can press ESC to dismiss — while the same text also appears as 'API Error: ...' in scrollback

End-to-end App.render after Action::ChunkReceived(s-1, StreamChunk::Error{error: '...429...'}): the Compositor's ErrorDialog overlay is painted ON TOP of the scrollback at Priority::Critical (i.e., its rounded red border and 'Error' title are visible in the rendered buffer at centre), AND the scrollback still shows 'API Error: ...' beneath the modal per RPC-078

rules.text: ErrorDialog renders Accent::Red, title 'Error', single message body row, footer 'Press ESC to dismiss', sticky (no auto-dismiss)
NotificationDialog supports three severities: Success→Accent::Cyan border with green title text, Info→Accent::Cyan border with cyan title text, Warning→Accent::Yellow border with yellow title text
NotificationDialog auto-dismisses after auto_dismiss_ms (default 2000ms, 0 disables) and shows live 'Closing in Ns... (ESC to dismiss)' countdown in the footer

StatusDialog is a state machine: Restoring (Accent::Cyan, current item + 'idx/total' counter, no dismissal), Complete (Accent::Cyan with green title, auto-closes after 3s with countdown, ESC skips), Error (Accent::Red, error_message body, ESC dismisses)
Every new dialog struct must delegate rendering to dialog_theme::render_dialog(area, buf, &FspecDialog{..}); hand-rendering with Block/Paragraph is rejected

Every new dialog implements Component with Priority::Critical, exposes a const ID (e.g. ERROR_DIALOG_ID, NOTIFICATION_DIALOG_ID, STATUS_DIALOG_ID), and emits a Callback that calls compositor.remove(&id) on dismissal
ESC key handling: ErrorDialog dismisses; NotificationDialog dismisses (cancels auto-dismiss timer); StatusDialog ESC only active in Complete and Error states, ignored during Restoring
All three dialogs ship with insta snapshot tests on an 80x24 buffer + behaviour tests asserting Component::priority(), id(), handle_event(ESC), and state transitions

Every existing inline-FspecDialog consumer in codelet/fspec-tui/ that displays an error / notification / progress modal is refactored to use the new wrappers; no inline FspecDialog struct literals remain for these three semantics after this work unit

When the LLM provider/Rig backend returns an Error chunk (StreamChunk::Error), the App pushes an ErrorDialog modal onto the Compositor at Priority::Critical containing the error message so the user is alerted to the failure with the same prominence as a disconnect — in addition to rendering the 'API Error: ...' line in scrollback per RPC-078

ErrorDialog overlay must be rendered through App::render (which calls compositor.render AFTER navigator.render_with_stores) so the modal appears on top of the AgentView. App-level integration tests must verify the rounded red border appears centred in the App's render buffer when a StreamChunk::Error has been dispatched

RPC-080.description: Gap class 12 of RPC-072 parity. Port persist_user_message / persist_assistant_message_internal / persist_tool_result_internal / persist_token_state / persist_compaction_marker from codelet/napi/src/persist.rs into codelet/core/src/persistence/agent_loop_persist.rs (already NAPI-free Rust calling append_message_with_metadata). Invoke them at the same call sites as the canonical loop: persist_user_message BEFORE LLM call (agent_loop.rs:529); persist_assistant_message on Done (agent_loop.rs:1666-1690); persist_tool_result on each ToolResult (agent_loop.rs:1558-1572); persist_token_state on Done. ACCEPTANCE: kill+restart fspec binary, /resume restores prior turn via session_restore_messages with UserInput+Text+ToolCall+ToolResult chunks replayed. See spec/attachments/RPC-072/agent-loop-parity-gap.md §12.

examples.text: User sends 'hello' as the first prompt of a session; before any LLM stream chunk arrives, the session manifest on disk gains exactly one MessageEnvelope { message_type: "user", payload: User { content: [Text("hello")] } }

Stub provider streams Text("reading") → ToolCall(Read /tmp/x) → ToolResult("contents") → Text("done") → Done(stop_reason="end_turn"); disk order after the turn is: user("hello") → assistant[Text("reading")+ToolUse] → tool_result("contents") → assistant[Text("done")] (with stop_reason="end_turn" on the final assistant envelope)

Stub provider returns Tokens{input:100, output:50} then Done(stop_reason="end_turn"); after the turn session.get_tokens() returns (100, 50, ...) AND the session manifest's token_state on disk has input=100, output=50
Stub provider returns Done with stop_reason=None (e.g. Gemini before stop_reason was implemented); on disk the final assistant envelope has stop_reason="unknown" — NOT the legacy "end_turn" sentinel

User completes one Text/ToolCall/ToolResult/Done turn; fspec binary is killed and restarted; opening the same session via /resume calls session_restore_messages which replays StreamChunk::UserInput → StreamChunk::Text → StreamChunk::ToolCall → StreamChunk::ToolResult in that original order

Stream emits Text("partial") then provider errors (e.g. 429); the accumulated assistant content "partial" is persisted to disk via persist_assistant_message BEFORE StreamChunk::Error reaches the TUI — so a subsequent restart/resume shows the partial assistant reply

Stream emits Text("thinking aloud…") then user hits Esc → StreamEvent::Interrupted; the accumulated assistant content is persisted to disk via persist_assistant_message before StreamChunk::Interrupted is emitted — verified by reading the manifest after the interrupt

load_session() fails inside persist_user_message (e.g. corrupted manifest); the function returns Err(String), tracing::error! logs the failure, the agent loop body proceeds to invoke the LLM stream — the stream's chunks still reach the TUI broadcast

rules.text: persist_user_message MUST be invoked BEFORE the LLM stream begins for the turn — at the same call site as canonical NAPI agent_loop.rs:529 — with the user's plain text input

persist_assistant_message_internal MUST flush the accumulated assistant content BEFORE persist_tool_result_internal on every StreamEvent::ToolResult so on-disk order is user → assistant(text+tool_use) → tool_result → assistant(final) (canonical site NAPI agent_loop.rs:1436-1446)

persist_assistant_message_with_stop_reason MUST be invoked on StreamEvent::Done passing the provider's real stop_reason — same call site as canonical NAPI agent_loop.rs:1542 (PROV-039); None becomes the literal string "unknown" on disk

persist_tool_result_internal MUST be invoked on every StreamEvent::ToolResult with (tool_call_id, content, is_error) — after the accumulated assistant message is flushed (canonical site NAPI agent_loop.rs:1439-1446)
persist_token_state MUST be invoked on StreamEvent::Done using session.get_tokens() (input + output) — same call site as canonical NAPI agent_loop.rs:1545-1548 (REFAC-007 Rule [31])

Persistence failures MUST be logged via tracing::error! and MUST NOT panic, MUST NOT short-circuit the stream, MUST NOT abort the turn — the stream continues so the user still sees text/tool output even when on-disk writes fail

persist_assistant_message (no stop_reason) MUST also be invoked on StreamEvent::Error and StreamEvent::Interrupted so partial assistant content from an aborted turn is preserved (canonical sites NAPI agent_loop.rs:1532, 1537)

All four persist functions live in codelet/agent-loop/src/persist.rs (the NAPI-free lift from RPC-072 Phase A) — the agent loop body and BackgroundOutput in codelet-agent-loop MUST call THIS module, not codelet/napi/src/persist.rs, to preserve the no_napi_dependency boundary

architectureNotes.text: Implementation home for restoration: port the body of codelet/napi/src/session_bindings.rs:2401-2567 (session_restore_messages) into codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs::restore_session_messages, replacing the current 5-line stub. The handler walks each envelope's message.content blocks, builds parallel rig::message::Message + StreamChunk vectors, then pushes rig messages into session.inner.lock().await.messages and dispatches StreamChunks via session.handle_output. Skip-rule for system-reminder envelopes (joined text contains both '<system-reminder>' and '<!-- type:') is preserved verbatim from the NAPI source.

Test strategy: the agent-loop round-trip uses an extended stub provider that (a) records the rig::completion::Message slice it receives on each complete_with_tools/prompt invocation and (b) optionally returns a programmable response sequence. Two turns are sent through SessionManager via session.send_input — assertions are made against (1) the stub's recorded second-turn history length+content, (2) session.inner.lock().await.messages.len() after each turn, and (3) a grep regression that the agent_loop body source contains zero literal 'vec![Message { role: MessageRole::User' single-element constructions. Restoration tests live in codelet/sessions/tests/rpc081_restore_session_messages.rs and exercise the SessionManagerHandle impl directly with hand-crafted envelope JSON strings (no NAPI dependency).

Call-site contract: agent loop body already passes &mut inner_session into run_with_provider! and into run_agent_stream_with_images (codelet/agent-loop/src/agent_loop.rs:867-1019 + codelet/agent-loop/src/dispatch.rs:38-105). The new RPC-081 coverage pins this with structural tests + a behavioural multi-turn round-trip. For restoration, the canonical NAPI source is codelet/napi/src/session_bindings.rs:2401-2567; the NAPI-free target lives in the existing trait impl at codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs:274 which currently returns Ok(()) without touching messages.

RPC-081.description: Gap class 2 of RPC-072 parity. The canonical loop reads + appends rig::message::Message values to session.inner.messages every turn (CLI-008). prompt_streaming_with_history_and_hook clones it for the LLM, then we push the new user message for the next turn. RPC-072 stub rebuilds vec![only the new user text] each turn — LLM has no chat history. Port the read/append cycle from codelet/cli/src/interactive/stream_loop.rs:461-471. ACCEPTANCE: 'remember 42' then 'what number did I just give you' → LLM answers '42'. See gap-analysis §2.

examples.text: Session sends 'remember 42' (turn 1); stub provider records the rig history it received as []. Stub replies 'noted, 42'. Session sends 'what number' (turn 2); stub records the rig history it received as [User('remember 42'), Assistant('noted, 42')]
After turn 1 above, session.inner.lock().await.messages.len() == 2 — one rig::message::Message::User('remember 42') and one rig::message::Message::Assistant containing 'noted, 42'

After two turns, the agent loop body in codelet/agent-loop/src/agent_loop.rs never constructs a 'vec![Message { role: User, content: Text(input) }]' single-element history — source-shape regression test grep-asserts the literal is absent

restore_session_messages(session_id, vec![envelope_json_user, envelope_json_assistant]) pushes 2 rig::message::Message values onto session.inner.messages and dispatches StreamChunk::UserInput → StreamChunk::Text → StreamChunk::Done to session.handle_output

Assistant envelope with content blocks [{type:'thinking', thinking:'..._'}, {type:'text', text:'reading'}, {type:'tool_use', id:'t1', name:'Read', input:{path:'/tmp/x'}}] yields StreamChunk::Thinking → StreamChunk::Text('reading') → StreamChunk::ToolCall{id:'t1', name:'Read', input:'{\"path\":\"/tmp/x\"}'} → StreamChunk::Done
User envelope containing the literal text '<system-reminder>\n<!-- type:fspecWorkflow -->\n...' is silently skipped — neither pushed into inner.messages nor emitted to output_buffer
restore_session_messages('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', vec![]) returns Err('Session not found: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000') without panicking
restore_session_messages(valid_id, vec!['{ not json'.to_string()]) returns Err('Failed to parse envelope: ...') without panicking and without mutating session.inner.messages
Boundary test asserts codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs contains no 'codelet_napi' import after the restoration port — the no_napi_dependency rule on codelet-sessions continues to hold

rules.text: Each turn passes session.inner.messages by &mut to run_agent_stream_with_images so the LLM sees the accumulated chat history before producing the new assistant turn (canonical site stream_loop.rs:461-471)
After rig clones the history for the LLM call, the new user prompt MUST be pushed onto session.inner.messages as rig::message::Message::User so subsequent turns see it

session.inner.messages is the single source of truth for in-memory chat history — the agent loop body MUST NOT rebuild a one-shot vec![only the new user text] per turn (BRIDGE-007 / CLI-008 regression guard)

restore_session_messages MUST parse each envelope JSON's message.role + content blocks and produce both (a) Vec<rig::message::Message> pushed into session.inner.messages and (b) Vec<StreamChunk> dispatched via session.handle_output (canonical site session_bindings.rs:2401-2567)

User-message restoration recognises content-block types 'text' (replayed as StreamChunk::UserInput + accumulated into rig::message::Message::User) and 'tool_result' (replayed as StreamChunk::ToolResult with tool_use_id/content/is_error)

Assistant-message restoration recognises content-block types 'thinking' (StreamChunk::Thinking), 'text' (StreamChunk::Text + accumulated into rig::message::Message::Assistant), and 'tool_use' (StreamChunk::ToolCall with id/name/JSON-stringified input), then emits a terminating StreamChunk::Done per assistant turn

Restoration MUST skip persisted system-reminder envelopes (joined text contains both '<system-reminder>' AND '<!-- type:') so fresh reminders are re-injected post-restore — no replay of stale reminders into either inner.messages or output buffer

restore_session_messages MUST return Err(String) with 'Session not found: <id>' when the SessionManager has no session with that id, and MUST return Err on envelope JSON parse failures — without panicking

Restoration lives in codelet/sessions/src/handle_impl.rs (the NAPI-free SessionManagerHandle impl) — the codelet-agent-loop / codelet-fspec binary path MUST call THIS impl, not codelet/napi/src/session_bindings.rs, to preserve the no_napi_dependency boundary

architectureNotes.text: Test approach: structural verification of source files (codelet/agent-loop/src/dispatch.rs and codelet/agent-loop/src/agent_loop.rs) plus unit tests on BackgroundSession.{get_role,set_role,clear_role}. Pattern: read source, extract relevant region (macro body / match arm), assert key tokens present. Mirrors the pattern used by copilot_create_rig_agent_signature_matches_dispatch_macro_contract in dispatch.rs:198-214.

Provider create_rig_agent signature unification: every provider (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, ZAI, Codex, Copilot, CustomProvider) exposes `create_rig_agent(session_id: uuid::Uuid, preamble: Option<&str>, thinking: Option<serde_json::Value>) -> ...`. Compile-time closure assertions prove this. NAPI parity reference: codelet/napi/src/agent_loop.rs:91-96.

Out of scope: live behavioral test through `/role` slash command. The slash-command path (TUI -> RPC -> set_role) is covered by RPC-063 ("/role slash command end-to-end (UI dialog)") which is already DONE. RPC-082 only verifies the agent loop reads the stored role.

RPC-082.description: Gap class 3 of RPC-072 parity. Canonical loop reads session.get_role() per turn and passes Option<&str> as preamble to provider.create_rig_agent (agent_loop.rs:91-96). SystemPromptFacade transforms it into the on-wire system field (claude.rs:507-595). RPC-072 stub does neither. /role slash command (RPC-063) sets the role but nothing reads it. ACCEPTANCE: /role 'You are a pirate' then 'hello' → stub provider receives the preamble in additional_params['system']. See gap-analysis §3.

examples.text: claude arm: macro expansion calls provider.create_rig_agent(session.id, role_preamble.as_deref(), thinking_config_value.clone())

openai inlined arm: between `match inner_session.provider_manager_mut().get_openai(session.id)` and `provider.create_rig_agent(...)` there is a `let role_preamble = session.get_role();` and the call uses `role_preamble.as_deref()`

BackgroundSession round-trip: new session.get_role() == None; after set_role("You are a pirate"), get_role() == Some("You are a pirate"); after clear_role(), get_role() == None

Signature contract closures: a `let _ = |provider: &P, session_id, preamble: Option<&str>, thinking| provider.create_rig_agent(session_id, preamble, thinking)` compiles for each of Claude/OpenAI/Gemini/Zai/Codex/Copilot/Custom providers — proving every provider accepts a preamble

rules.text: Every per-turn agent dispatch must read session.get_role() and pass it as the second positional argument to provider.create_rig_agent
The run_with_provider! macro in dispatch.rs is the canonical site for role-preamble plumbing for the macro-driven provider arms (claude, gemini, zai, codex, github-copilot, copilot)

architectureNotes.text: RigAgent::with_default_depth wraps the rig agent in the inner agentic loop — wrapping is what makes Read/Write/Edit/Bash actually executable; without it the provider would return raw ToolUse stop reasons

Three dispatch paths exist (macro, OpenAI inlined, CustomProvider fallthrough). They must stay in lock-step. Drift between them is the same defect class as RPC-072's premature 'done' marking, so tests must lock structural calls in all three paths.

MCP wrapper gather happens at turn start (try_read, non-blocking). Tools that connect mid-turn become visible via ConnectMcpTool which uses the ToolServerHandle stored by set_mcp_tool_server_handle. So set_mcp_tool_server_handle is the second half of MCP-002 — without it mid-turn dynamic tools never appear.

RPC-083.description: Gap class 4 of RPC-072 parity. complete_with_tools(messages, &[]) is called with an empty tool slice — the agent cannot Read/Write/Edit/Bash. Port the create_rig_agent call (which registers ~21 tools) + RigAgent::with_default_depth wrap (which installs the inner agentic loop) + codelet_tools::gather_mcp_tool_wrappers + set_mcp_tool_server_handle from run_with_provider! macro body (agent_loop.rs:79-97). ACCEPTANCE: 'read /tmp/test.txt' → ToolCall(Read) → ToolResult → final Text chunk with contents. See gap-analysis §4.

examples.text: End-to-end: stub provider that emits ToolCall(Read,/tmp/x.txt) -> agent loop dispatches via with_default_depth -> ToolResult arrives with file contents -> final assistant Text -> Done

Structural: dispatch.rs run_with_provider! macro body contains the five calls in order — gather_mcp_tool_wrappers, create_rig_agent, add_tool loop guarded by !is_empty, set_mcp_tool_server_handle, RigAgent::with_default_depth
Structural: agent_loop.rs OpenAI inlined arm at lines 869-914 contains the same five calls because get_openai takes session.id

Structural: agent_loop.rs custom-provider fallthrough arm at lines 953-1020 contains gather_mcp_tool_wrappers, add_tool loop, set_mcp_tool_server_handle, RigAgent::with_default_depth around CustomProvider::create_rig_agent
Signature: every provider's create_rig_agent accepts (session_id: Uuid, preamble: Option<&str>, thinking: Option<Value>) so the macro is interchangeable across providers
Signature: codelet_core::RigAgent::with_default_depth(agent: Agent<M>) -> RigAgent<M> is callable on the output of every create_rig_agent — closure type-check
Signature: codelet_tools::gather_mcp_tool_wrappers(session.id: Uuid) -> Vec<McpToolWrapper> and set_mcp_tool_server_handle(session.id: Uuid, handle: ToolServerHandle) — closure type-check

run_with_provider! macro must call provider.create_rig_agent(session.id, role_preamble.as_deref(), thinking.clone()) to register the full tool slate
run_with_provider! macro must install each gathered MCP wrapper via agent.tool_server_handle.add_tool(wrapper).await
run_with_provider! macro must call set_mcp_tool_server_handle(session.id, agent.tool_server_handle.clone()) so ConnectMcpTool can register mid-turn tools
run_with_provider! macro must wrap the rig agent with codelet_core::RigAgent::with_default_depth(agent) before streaming so the inner agentic loop is installed

architectureNotes.text: Streaming dispatch is structural: parity is enforced by source-string assertions against the three dispatch arms in agent_loop.rs + dispatch.rs (macro body, OpenAI inlined arm, custom-provider fallthrough). Drift between them is the same defect class as RPC-072's premature 'done' marking, so all three must be locked simultaneously.

StreamChunk variant census: codelet_rpc_types::StreamChunk currently has 22 variants in lib.rs. The gap analysis requires ≥19. We assert ≥19 (not ==N) so adding new variants doesn't break the parity test.

BackgroundOutput is the rig→StreamChunk translator. It lives in codelet/agent-loop/src/background_output.rs and impls StreamOutput. Locking the 11 canonical StreamEvent→StreamChunk translations here means run_agent_stream_with_images will emit the right shapes regardless of provider.

RPC-084.description: Gap class 5 of RPC-072 parity. Stub uses non-streaming complete_with_tools and emits only Text+Done. Port the streaming path: each provider arm calls codelet_cli::interactive::run_agent_stream_with_images which opens agent.prompt_streaming_with_history_and_hook and translates rig StreamEvent → StreamChunk via BackgroundOutput (agent_loop.rs:1463-1700). Emit Text/Thinking/ToolCall/ToolResult/ToolProgress/TokenUpdate/ContextFillUpdate/UserNotification/Interrupted/Done/Error + all state variants. AgentView's RPC-045 dispatch path is dead code until this lands. ACCEPTANCE: one turn against a streaming stub yields >1 StreamChunk::Text before Done. See gap-analysis §5,§13.

examples.text: Structural: dispatch.rs run_with_provider! macro body contains the call codelet_cli::interactive::run_agent_stream_with_images(agent, $input, $images, $inner, ...) with the 8 positional args in canonical order
Structural: agent_loop.rs OpenAI inlined arm at ~869-914 contains exactly one direct codelet_cli::interactive::run_agent_stream_with_images call
Structural: agent_loop.rs custom-provider fallthrough at ~953-1020 contains exactly one codelet_cli::interactive::run_agent_stream_with_images call after RigAgent::with_default_depth
Structural: agent_loop.rs body contains zero occurrences of `.complete_with_tools(` outside test/comment blocks (search excludes lines starting with // or inside #[cfg(test)] modules)

Variant census: codelet_rpc_types::StreamChunk has ≥19 declared variants (Text, Thinking, ToolCall, ToolResult, ToolProgress, SessionStateChange, UserNotification, Interrupted, TokenUpdate, ContextFillUpdate, Done, Error, UserInput, IncomingMessage, SupervisorPendingInjection, CompactionComplete, FspecCommandRequest, FspecCommandResult, WorkUnitsUpdate)

Structural: background_output.rs handle_stream_event match arms produce the 11 canonical StreamChunk constructors — StreamChunk::text, ::thinking, ::tool_call, ::tool_result, ::tool_progress, ::user_notification, ::token_update, ::context_fill_update, ::error, ::interrupted, ::done

Signature: a closure reference to codelet_cli::interactive::run_agent_stream_with_images compiles against the canonical 8-argument signature — proving the public API the dispatch arms depend on is stable

architectureNotes.text: Implementation already lives in `codelet/agent-loop/src/background_output.rs` (StreamEvent::Tokens arm @ 226-243, StreamEvent::ContextFill arm @ 244-249) — lifted as part of RPC-072/RPC-080/RPC-081. RPC-086 is a coverage-only card mirroring the RPC-082/083/084 pattern.

Tests at `codelet/agent-loop/tests/rpc086_token_tracking.rs` use structural source-string assertions (read background_output.rs / rpc-types/lib.rs / cli/output.rs and assert canonical substrings) plus a small integration test against a real BackgroundSession built via test helpers — same shape as `rpc082_role_injection.rs` and `rpc084_streaming.rs`.

BackgroundOutput::emit must NOT regress: dropping the `update_tokens`/`update_reasoning_tokens` calls would freeze the TUI tokens widget at 0↓ 0↑; dropping the StreamChunk::token_update emission would freeze the agent-view ledger. Both are pinned by source-string assertions.

TokenInfo carries u64 input/output, ContextFillInfo carries u32 fill_percentage + u64 effective_tokens/threshold/context_window. BackgroundOutput casts to u32 for session storage (cached_*_tokens are AtomicU32) and to f64 for ContextFillInfo fields in StreamChunk.

RPC-086.description: Gap class 8 of RPC-072 parity. BackgroundOutput::emit on StreamEvent::Tokens calls session.update_tokens(input, output) + update_reasoning_tokens(reasoning) + emits StreamChunk::TokenUpdate + ContextFillUpdate. RPC-072 stub does none of this — TUI header tokens widget is stuck at 0↓ 0↑ [0%] which is exactly the 2026-05-28 screenshot. ACCEPTANCE: one turn against stub returning Usage{input:100, output:50} → session.get_tokens() returns (100,50,...) AND TUI header displays tokens: 100↓ 50↑. See gap-analysis §7.

examples.text: BackgroundOutput::emit receives StreamEvent::Tokens with input_tokens=100, output_tokens=50, reasoning_tokens=None and session.get_tokens() then returns (100, 50, None)
BackgroundOutput::emit receives StreamEvent::Tokens with reasoning_tokens=Some(25) and session.get_tokens() returns reasoning=Some(25)
agent_loop.rs and background_output.rs source contain the eight-field TokenTracker construction inside the StreamEvent::Tokens arm

rules.text: The canonical `agent_loop` function in `codelet/agent-loop/src/agent_loop.rs` MUST declare a parameter `mut mcp_injection_rx: mpsc::Receiver<McpInjection>` so MCP server messages can flow into the per-session loop

The body of `agent_loop` MUST declare a `let mut mcp_channel_open = true;` flag so the tokio::select! arm can be disabled once the channel closes (preventing CPU busy-loop on a permanently-ready closed receiver)

The `tokio::select!` body inside `agent_loop` MUST contain an arm matching the substring `result = mcp_injection_rx.recv(), if mcp_channel_open =>` — the `if mcp_channel_open` guard MUST appear inline on the same arm so polling stops the moment the flag is flipped

The `mcp_injection_rx.recv()` arm body MUST contain a `Some(McpInjection::Notification(text)) =>` match arm that converts the notification into an `InputWithImages` containing the notification text (so MCP notifications are routed as a normal LLM turn)

The `mcp_injection_rx.recv()` arm body MUST contain a `Some(McpInjection::SamplingRequest { params, response_tx }) =>` match arm — even when the V1 implementation rejects sampling, the SamplingRequest variant MUST be acknowledged at this call site so the channel does not leak the request
The `mcp_injection_rx.recv()` arm body MUST contain a `None =>` match arm that assigns `mcp_channel_open = false;` so the closed channel cannot busy-loop the select

The `mcp_injection_rx` parameter MUST NOT be prefixed with an underscore (e.g. `_mcp_injection_rx`) — an underscore prefix signals the RPC-072 stub state where the channel was held open but never drained

RPC-092.description:
PREREQUISITE for RPC-072 Phase B (agent loop body port).

## Why this card exists

The canonical NAPI agent_loop body (codelet/napi/src/agent_loop.rs:299-1456) invokes:
  - graph_search_handler::create_handler()
  - register_deep_search_handler(...)

Both handlers transitively depend on codelet/napi/src/graph/ — **52 .rs files, ~15,013 LOC** (16 root files + 33 ast_pipeline/ files + 3 ast_call_chain/ files), plus 4 bundled schemas under codelet/napi/schemas/. None of these are currently exposed outside the codelet-napi crate.

Adding `codelet-napi` to codelet-agent-loop's [dependencies] is FORBIDDEN by the RPC-067 boundary guard (codelet/agent-loop/tests/no_napi_dependency.rs). A stub-handler / BridgeHandlers / NoopBridgeHandlers approach was considered and rejected — it would silently swallow GraphSearch + DeepSearch tool calls, violating RPC-072 Rule [5] (zero functional cut-downs).

## Scope

1. Create new peer crate codelet/graph/ (codelet-graph) with zero napi-derive dependency.
2. Lift all 52 .rs files verbatim from codelet/napi/src/graph/ to codelet/graph/src/ using `git mv` (preserves blame).
3. Move 4 bundled schemas (ast-code.pg, ast-queries.gq, learnings.pg, learnings-queries.gq) from codelet/napi/schemas/ to codelet/graph/schemas/.
4. Apply ONLY mechanical path rewrites: `crate::graph::*` → `crate::*` and `include_str!("../../schemas/...")` → `include_str!("../schemas/...")`.

Architecture: prefix moves render-side (parity with RPC-091 '● ' decision); source.text stays as raw opaque model output; in_flight_thinking is the Option<usize> equivalent of TS findActiveThinkingBlock's 'last streaming thinking with no UserInput after it'

No batching/throttling layer needed: TS PERF-003 deliberately removed useDeferredValue because Ink uses LegacyRoot (synchronous). Rust ratatui has its own draw loop; rewrap_at(idx) per chunk mutation is sufficient — the renderer coalesces frames

OUT of scope (separate cards if needed): streaming '...' indicator parity (deferred per RPC-091 note), appendThinkingBulk hydration (Rust doesn't rehydrate yet), markdown formatting inside thinking blocks (TS also doesn't)

The current implementation has three regressions vs TS Ink parity: (A) spinner not smooth — Rust render loop is event-driven (should_render flag set only by events/actions); spinner elapsed_ms comes from Instant::now() but no timer triggers redraws so the spinner only advances when stream chunks arrive, making it look 'tied to scrollback'. (B) No finish animation when busy→idle — TS InputTransition.tsx runs a phase machine (loading→hiding→showing→complete): hiding sweeps the spinner text out 5 chars/frame at ~17ms (INK_FRAME_TIME_MS), then a 34ms gap, then showing sweeps the placeholder in 5 chars/frame; total ~450ms. Rust currently swaps spinner↔input atomically. (C) Terminal cursor visible during spinner — events.rs:184/222 unconditionally calls frame.set_cursor_position when ViewMode::Agent. Should be suppressed when session is Running/Compacting OR when finish animation is in hiding/showing phase.

Rust touch points to fix: app/events.rs (gate set_cursor_position on session_status), app/state.rs (add render-trigger timer for spinner ticks while busy, or repaint each tick frame at 60fps), views/agent/input_transition.rs (add hiding/showing state machine + paint), views/agent.rs (cache last spinner text for capture-on-finish, drive transition state).

<delta>' scrollback row (see attached screenshot transcript). …' chunk; ToolCall/Done/Error/UserInput/Interrupted finalise the in-flight thinking block so the next Thinking delta starts a fresh '[Thinking]

questions.answer: Two-layer: ScrollbackList::insert(idx, RenderedChunk) is a Vec-shaped primitive (mirrors push, re-wraps on insert, recomputes stick-to-bottom — same encapsulation as push). SessionContext::insert_source_at(idx, ChunkSource) is the wrapper that allocates seq from scrollback_next_seq, does initial wrap_source, and delegates. Matches the matched-primitive convention RPC-091 established (push/push_source, chunks_mut().remove + handle_done, rewrap_at + in-place mutate). Keeps both files under the RPC-024 300-LoC ceiling. chunk_processor::append_thinking calls ctx.insert_source_at(idx, source) and bumps in_flight_assistant by one.
questions.text: @human: Should ScrollbackList::insert_chunk_at(idx, source) live on ScrollbackList itself (mirrors Vec::insert) or on SessionContext (auto-handles scrollback_next_seq + rewrap_at)? Lean: ScrollbackList for the primitive + SessionContext::insert_source_at wrapper.

rules.text: Consecutive StreamChunk::Thinking deltas for the same logical thought MUST accumulate into a single RenderedChunk (parity with TS appendThinking)
The '[Thinking]\n' prefix MUST live in the render layer (ChunkKind::Thinking) — NOT baked into source.text per delta
SessionContext.in_flight_thinking: Option<usize> tracks the currently-streaming thinking chunk index (analogue of TS findActiveThinkingBlock)
Only handle_tool_call calls finalize_in_flight_thinking (sets is_streaming=false). Done/Error/UserInput/Interrupted only CLEAR the slot — they never mutate the existing thinking chunk

When a new thinking block is created while in_flight_assistant is Some, the new chunk MUST be inserted BEFORE the in-flight assistant (mirrors TS splice-before-streaming-assistant); in_flight_assistant index is bumped by 1
No throttling, batching, or debouncing at the conversation layer — one chunk → one mutation → rewrap_at(idx), matching TS PERF-003 (useDeferredValue was deliberately removed)

The Thinking spinner braille frame must advance at 80ms cadence INDEPENDENTLY of stream chunk arrivals — a render trigger fires at least every 80ms while the session is Running or Compacting, so the spinner visually ticks even when no chunks are arriving

When a session transitions from Running/Compacting to Idle, the input row plays a finish animation matching TS InputTransition.tsx: phase 'hiding' subtracts CHARS_PER_FRAME=5 chars per ~17ms frame from the captured 'Thinking... (Esc to stop)' string until visibleChars==0, then a 34ms gap, then phase 'showing' adds 5 chars per ~17ms frame to reveal the placeholder, then phase 'complete' mounts MultiLineInput with cursor

The terminal cursor (frame.set_cursor_position) MUST NOT be called when the input row is in any non-Idle InputTransitionState — specifically when SessionStatus is Running or Compacting, OR when the finish animation is in phase 'hiding' or 'showing'. The cursor is only set when MultiLineInput is actually painted (phase 'complete' / idle)

If a new Running state begins while a finish animation is in progress, the animation MUST abort and the spinner MUST resume on the next frame (mirrors TS InputTransition useEffect that resets phase to 'loading' when isLoading becomes true mid-transition)

If the user types a printable key during the 'hiding' or 'showing' phase, the animation MUST short-circuit to 'complete' and the keystroke MUST be inserted into the now-mounted MultiLineInput (mirrors TS InputTransition useInputCompat MEDIUM-priority handler at InputTransition.tsx)

The render loop MUST also tick during Hiding/Showing finish animation phases — not just while Running/Compacting. Without this, the Loading→Hiding transition state freezes at full captured text and the spinner row never sweeps out.

RPC-097.description:
User reports Shift+Right does not create a new session in the Rust port. DeepSearch of the TS source confirmed the expected contract: when Shift+Right fires past the last session (or with no sessions), `useSessionNavigation.handleShiftRight` calls `openCreateSessionDialog` which mounts <CreateSessionDialog> as a CRITICAL-priority modal showing three options (Yes / Yes - Isolated / Cancel), context-aware title ('Start New Agent?' vs 'Work on <id>?'), and the user picks an option to call createSession({...}) or createIsolatedSession({...}) on the Rust backend.

RPC-096 was previously marked done but ships a wiring bug: `handle_session_cycle` (codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc024.rs:43) calls `agent_view_store.request_create_session_dialog_no_auto()` for NavTarget::CreateDialog. That method only sets the store flag `show_create_session_dialog = true` — NOTHING in the render pipeline ever reads that flag to push the dialog onto the Compositor. The actual dialog mount path is `App::handle_open_create_session_dialog` (dispatch_rpc060.rs) which is only triggered by `Action::OpenCreateSessionDialog`. The result: Shift+Right at the end of the session list silently does nothing — no dialog ever appears.

Additionally, the existing Rust CreateSessionDialog visual styling drifts from the TS Ink original which the user requires to be copied EXACTLY:
  * TS selected option = backgroundColor='blue', color='white', bold, label padded with spaces (e.g. ' Yes ').
  * TS unselected option = color='gray', no background, label padded with spaces.
  * TS option rendering is three side-by-side <Box marginX={1}> buttons centered (justifyContent='center').
  * TS footer separator is '|' (ASCII pipe), not '│' (U+2502 box-drawing).
  * Rust currently uses ▸/○ markers + raw spans + '│' separators.

This bug card fixes BOTH defects so Shift+Right opens an EXACT visual+behavioural copy of the TS CreateSessionDialog (the existing CreateSessionDialog Rust component is refactored to match TS rendering), AND the dispatch wires Shift+Right → Action::OpenCreateSessionDialog so the dialog actually mounts.

BUG (observed 2026-05-31): pressing Shift+Right on the same work unit after Close Session navigated back to the destroyed session. Root cause: dispatch_rpc098.rs ExitChoice::CloseSession only invoked backend.destroy_session — it never called board_store.detach_session(work_unit_id). The TS reference destroySession() in src/tui/services/sessionService.ts:620-647 performs FOUR cleanup steps; the original RPC-098 port implemented only step 1. The Rust-side BoardStore.session_attachments registry (mirrors TS fspecStore.sessionAttachments, defined at codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/board.rs:50) retained the stale work-unit → session entry, and Shift+Right from BoardView consults that registry via selected_session (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/board.rs:182-185). Fix: capture agent_view_store.current_work_unit_id() before spawning destroy_session, then call self.board_store.detach_session(&wu_id) synchronously in handle_agent_exit_choice. (TS unsubscribe + setCurrentWorkUnit(null,null) are orthogonal — tracked separately if shown to be observable.)

BUG REGRESSION (observed 2026-05-31 after first fix): the prior patch cleared board_store.session_attachments but the user still saw the destroyed session when cycling sessions in AgentView. Root cause #2: agent_view_store.open_sessions retained the destroyed SessionContext. AgentView Shift+Left/Right uses AgentViewStore::navigate_next/navigate_prev (codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/navigation.rs:41-69) which iterates open_sessions; and AgentView re-entry from BoardView consults first_open_session_id (same file, line 78). Fix #2: in dispatch_rpc098.rs handle_agent_exit_choice ExitChoice::CloseSession, BEFORE spawning backend.destroy_session, ALSO call self.agent_view_store.remove_session_if_open(&session). This mirrors the canonical pattern at codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc026.rs:249 (handle_confirm_delete_session) which already does the same step before persistence_delete_session. Order of cleanup in handle_agent_exit_choice CloseSession arm: 1. snapshot session_id and work_unit_id, 2. board_store.detach_session(wu_id), 3. agent_view_store.remove_session_if_open(&session), 4. tokio::spawn(backend.destroy_session(session)), 5. dispatch Action::BackToBoard.

RPC-098.description: When the user presses ESC in the Rust AgentView and L1-L6 of the Esc-cascade do not consume it (no popup, no mode view, no compacting/running session, empty input buffer), the current Rust port falls through to Action::BackToBoard and exits immediately. The TypeScript reference (src/tui/components/AgentView.tsx:4731-4773 + 5502-5515) instead opens a three-button confirmation modal (ThreeButtonDialog at src/components/ThreeButtonDialog.tsx) with options ['Detach', 'Close Session', 'Cancel']. Detach calls cleanupCurrentSessionHandler(); onExit() so the session keeps running in background via GlobalSessionStreamManager. Close Session calls cleanupCurrentSessionHandler(); await destroySession(currentSessionId); onExit() which terminates the backend session via the transport's destroy_session RPC. Cancel just closes the dialog and stays on AgentView. This work unit ports that behaviour: a new ExitConfirmationDialog component delegating to dialog_theme::render_dialog (Accent::Yellow per TS borderColor='yellow'), a new Action::AgentExitChoice { choice: ExitChoice } variant with Detach|CloseSession|Cancel, replacement of the dispatch_rpc051.rs L7 fall-through with compositor.push(ExitConfirmationDialog::new(...)), and a dispatcher that on Detach emits BackToBoard while on CloseSession spawns backend.destroy_session(id) then emits BackToBoard. The dialog description is conditional on session status: 'The agent is currently running. Choose how to exit.' when Running/Compacting else 'Choose how to exit the session.'. Cyclic Left/Right navigation, defaultSelectedIndex=0 (Detach), ESC dismisses (== Cancel), Enter commits.

rules.text: When ESC reaches Esc-cascade level 7 (no popup, no mode view, no running stream, empty input) and a session exists, the App pushes an ExitConfirmationDialog onto the compositor instead of dispatching Action::BackToBoard directly
When ESC reaches Esc-cascade level 7 and NO session exists (current_session() is None), the App still dispatches Action::BackToBoard directly with no dialog (matches TS 'if (currentSessionId)' guard)
ExitConfirmationDialog delegates rendering to dialog_theme::render_dialog with Accent::Yellow, title 'Exit Session?' (bold), Priority::Critical, and the canonical id 'exit-confirmation-dialog'
Description text is conditional on session status: 'The agent is currently running. Choose how to exit.' when the session status is Running or Compacting, else 'Choose how to exit the session.'

The dialog renders three flat buttons in order [Detach, Close Session, Cancel], selected button styled bg=Blue/fg=White/Bold with label padded ' <label> ', unselected fg=Gray, footer '← → Navigate | Enter Select | Esc Cancel', default selection Detach (index 0)
Left/Right arrow keys cyclically navigate selection: Left from Detach wraps to Cancel; Right from Cancel wraps to Detach
Enter emits Action::AgentExitChoice { choice } with the currently selected option (Detach | CloseSession | Cancel) and removes the dialog from the compositor via Callback
ESC inside the dialog is equivalent to Cancel: emits Action::AgentExitChoice { choice: Cancel } and removes the dialog

Dispatcher: AgentExitChoice::Cancel is a no-op (dialog already removed, AgentView remains active); AgentExitChoice::Detach dispatches Action::BackToBoard without calling backend.destroy_session; AgentExitChoice::CloseSession spawns backend.destroy_session(current_session_id) as a pending task THEN dispatches Action::BackToBoard
Pressing ESC again while the dialog is already on the compositor does NOT push a second dialog (App L7 checks compositor.contains(EXIT_CONFIRMATION_DIALOG_ID) before pushing)

On Action::AgentExitChoice { choice: CloseSession }, the App MUST also clear the work-unit→session attachment via board_store.detach_session(work_unit_id) — mirroring TS destroySession step 2 (fspecState.detachSession(workUnitId) at src/tui/services/sessionService.ts:637). Without this, BoardView::selected_session (views/board.rs:184) keeps returning the destroyed SessionId, so Shift+Right on the same work unit routes to a dead session instead of falling back to first_open_session_id / Create Session dialog.

AgentViewStore::open_sessions must also be cleared on Close Session — call agent_view_store.remove_session_if_open(&session) BEFORE spawning backend.destroy_session. Without this, the destroyed SessionContext stays in open_sessions and Shift+Left/Right cycle via navigate_prev/navigate_next/first_open_session_id (codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/navigation.rs) keeps surfacing the dead session. Mirrors the existing handle_confirm_delete_session pattern (dispatch_rpc026.rs:249) which already calls remove_session_if_open before backend.persistence_delete_session.

architectureNotes.text: TS REFERENCE (DeepSearch confirmed): src/tui/components/SessionHeader.tsx:104-206 is the renderer. It receives `tokenUsage` (local React state from current session's stream) and `rustTokens` (per-session SessionTokens via useSyncExternalStore on currentSessionId) as props and calls getMaxTokens(tokenUsage, rustTokens) at line 127. The display at lines 196-197 is `tokens: {input}↓ {output}↑ {reasoningTokens > 0 ? ` ${reasoningTokens}🧠` : ''}`. The Zustand sessionStore does NOT hold tokens — Rust SessionManager (per-session, NAPI sessionGetTokens) is the authoritative source.

TS PARALLEL state: AgentView.tsx:836-839 holds local `tokenUsage` (TokenTracker) state. updateTokenStateFromChunk (1110-1125) calls setTokenUsage(chunk.tokens) on every TokenUpdate for the CURRENT session. On session switch via resumeSessionById (3532+), setTokenUsage is called again with restored tokens (3549) or extractTokenStateFromChunks (3609) for background sessions. Rust port can skip the parallel local-state mirror since token_state_by_session HashMap is already the single source per-session.

RUST CURRENT GAP (verified by AST read):  TokenState in store/agent_view.rs:40-45 only has {input_tokens, output_tokens, context_fill_pct}. apply_token_tracker (lines 59-62) only copies input+output, drops cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, reasoning_tokens, tokens_per_second. chrome_paint.rs:58-60 HARDCODES tokens_per_second:None, reasoning_tokens:0, compaction_reduction:None — they never read from the per-session map. header.rs:66-71 declares fields tokens_per_second/reasoning_tokens/compaction_reduction but they always arrive as defaults at the render site.

ROUTING IS ALREADY CORRECT: app/dispatch.rs:32 `apply_chunk_to_token_state(id, chunk)` uses the chunk's source id (NOT current_session). RPC-045 lifted the active-session filter in bootstrap.rs:92 so background chunks reach the App. Thus the fix is purely about (a) extending TokenState fields and (b) wiring chrome_paint.rs to read them per-session — no routing changes needed.

TokenTracker shape (codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs:766-788): {input_tokens: i32, output_tokens: i32, cache_read_input_tokens: Option<u32>, cache_creation_input_tokens: Option<u32>, tokens_per_second: Option<f64>, reasoning_tokens: Option<u32>}. Rust TokenState should mirror these with appropriate widened types (u64 for counts, Option<f32 or f64> for tps).

RPC-099.description: The Rust TUI SessionHeader does not keep track of each individual session's full token metrics when switching between sessions with Shift+Left/Right. While `TokenState::{input_tokens, output_tokens, context_fill_pct}` are correctly per-session, the richer TokenTracker fields (reasoning_tokens, tokens_per_second, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens) and compaction_reduction are HARDCODED in chrome_paint::paint_header_and_role (tokens_per_second: None, reasoning_tokens: 0, compaction_reduction: None at lines 58-60). The TS reference (src/tui/components/SessionHeader.tsx + AgentView.tsx) reads ALL token fields via getMaxTokens(tokenUsage, rustTokens) where rustTokens comes from useRustSessionState(currentSessionId) — a per-session useSyncExternalStore subscription. Per-session storage must extend to all TokenTracker fields and the header build site must read them from the per-session map (keyed by current SessionId). Restoring on session switch (resumeSessionById equivalent) must also restore all fields.

examples.text: Two sessions s-1 and s-2 are open in AgentView. Action::ChunkReceived(s-1, TokenUpdate{input:100, output:50, reasoning_tokens:Some(20), tokens_per_second:Some(8.5)}) is dispatched. Action::ChunkReceived(s-2, TokenUpdate{input:200, output:75, reasoning_tokens:Some(60), tokens_per_second:Some(12.0)}) is dispatched. Render frame with s-1 focused shows `tokens: 100↓ 50↑ 20🧠` and tok/sec=8.5. Render frame after Action::SessionNext (now s-2 focused) shows `tokens: 200↓ 75↑ 60🧠` and tok/sec=12.0. Action::SessionPrev shows s-1 values again.

Background session accumulation: s-1 is focused, s-2 is open but background. Action::ChunkReceived(s-2, TokenUpdate{input:200, output:75, reasoning_tokens:Some(60)}) is dispatched (user never visits s-2 between updates). User does Shift+Right to focus s-2. Header IMMEDIATELY displays 200↓ 75↑ 60🧠 — proving the background session's TokenState was being maintained while not visible.

Cache token fields: Action::ChunkReceived(s-1, TokenUpdate{input:100, output:50, cache_read_input_tokens:Some(5000), cache_creation_input_tokens:Some(800)}) is dispatched. token_state_for(s-1) returns TokenState with cache_read = 5000 and cache_creation = 800 — these survive a switch to s-2 and a switch back.

Empty-state on switch to never-updated session: s-1 has tokens 1234↓ 567↑. User opens fresh s-2 (no TokenUpdate dispatched yet) and does Shift+Right. Header shows `tokens: 0↓ 0↑` for s-2 (NOT 1234↓ 567↑ carry-over from s-1) because token_state_for(s-2) returns None and unwrap_or_default() yields zeros.

Reasoning suffix toggling: s-1 has reasoning_tokens=0 (Default), s-2 has reasoning_tokens=Some(45). When focused on s-1, header text contains `tokens: in↓ out↑` (no 🧠 suffix). When focused on s-2, header text contains `tokens: in↓ out↑ 45🧠`.

rules.text: TokenState in AgentViewStore (codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view.rs:40-67) MUST be extended to track all TokenTracker fields: input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, reasoning_tokens, tokens_per_second, AND context_fill_pct — all persisted per SessionId in token_state_by_session HashMap

TokenState::apply_token_tracker (agent_view.rs:59-62) MUST copy ALL TokenTracker fields from the incoming chunk — currently it only copies input_tokens and output_tokens and silently drops cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, reasoning_tokens, tokens_per_second

chrome_paint::paint_header_and_role (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/chrome_paint.rs:25-71) MUST source tokens_per_second, reasoning_tokens, and compaction_reduction from store.token_state_for(sid) — currently these are hardcoded None/0/None at lines 58-60

When the user does Shift+Left/Right (Action::SessionPrev / Action::SessionNext → handle_session_cycle → switch_to_session_index → focus_session_index), the next render frame's SessionHeader MUST display the NEW focused session's tokens — not the previous session's tokens and not zeros (unless the new session genuinely has no token state yet)

Background sessions (those not currently focused) MUST continue to accumulate per-session TokenState as their TokenUpdate chunks arrive via Action::ChunkReceived(id, chunk) — apply_chunk_to_token_state already routes by source id (RPC-045 lifted the active-session filter), so background updates must NOT be filtered

Per TS parity (src/tui/components/SessionHeader.tsx lines 196-197) the displayed header text MUST format as `tokens: {input}↓ {output}↑ {reasoning}🧠` when reasoning_tokens > 0, omitting the reasoning suffix otherwise — and when tokens_per_second is Some, it MUST drive the existing tok/sec indicator in build_right_line
