architectureNotes.text:
TS REFERENCE (DeepSearch confirmed):
• Renderer: src/tui/components/SessionHeader.tsx:129-132 — `percentText = compactionReduction !== null ? `[${fp}%: COMPACTED ${Math.abs(reduction)}%]` : `[${fp}%]``
• fillPercentage origin: live `StreamChunk::ContextFillUpdate{contextFill.fillPercentage}` → setContextFillPercentage; fallback `calculateContextFillPercentage(currentContextTokens, contextWindow, maxOutput)` = round((inputTokens / (contextWindow - min(maxOutput, 32_000))) * 100) on restore
• compactionReduction origin: AgentView.tsx:959-979 — handleCompactionComplete → setCompactionReductionRef.current?.(Math.round(result.compressionRatio)) (TS bug: should be (1-ratio)*100; Rust will use the correct formula)
• Reset on cleared: AgentView.tsx:992-1006 — SessionStateChange→Cleared resets contextFillPercentage and tokenUsage to 0
• Color: src/tui/utils/sessionHeaderUtils.ts:37-42 — <50 green, <70 yellow, <85 magenta, >=85 red

RUST CURRENT GAPS (verified by AST read):
• codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/token_state.rs:63 — `self.context_fill_pct = info.fill_percentage.min(100) as u8;` ← CLAMP BUG, also drops u32→u8 range
• codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/chrome_paint.rs:65 — `compaction_reduction: None,` ← HARDCODED, never read from store
• codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc045.rs:120-133 — CompactionComplete branch only formats scrollback notice, never persists per-session reduction
• codelet/fspec-tui/src/app/dispatch_rpc045.rs:57-75 — SessionStateChange branch handles state→pause/resume but does NOT reset TokenState or compaction_reduction on `Cleared`
• codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/work_unit_state.rs:48 — `reset_token_state(session)` already exists; reuse it
• codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/header.rs:71 + header_build.rs:134 + header_build.rs:158-164 — render path already supports compaction_reduction Option<i32>; just needs to receive non-None

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN:
1. token_state.rs: change `context_fill_pct: u8` → `context_fill_pct: u16`; change apply_context_fill to `self.context_fill_pct = info.fill_percentage.min(u16::MAX as u32) as u16;`. Update header_build.rs build_right_line + context_fill_color signature to take u16 (color thresholds 50/70/85 still work).
2. AgentViewStore (store/agent_view.rs): add field `compaction_reduction_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, i32>`. Add accessors `compaction_reduction_for(&SessionId) -> Option<i32>`, `set_compaction_reduction(SessionId, i32)`, `clear_compaction_reduction(&SessionId)`.
3. dispatch_rpc045.rs CompactionComplete branch: compute `reduction = ((1.0 - compaction_result.compression_ratio) * 100.0).round() as i32;` and call `self.agent_view_store.set_compaction_reduction(session_id.clone(), reduction);` BEFORE the existing notice emit.
4. dispatch_rpc045.rs SessionStateChange branch: on `SessionState::Cleared`, call `self.agent_view_store.reset_token_state(session_id);` and `self.agent_view_store.clear_compaction_reduction(session_id);` BEFORE the existing set_session_status call.
5. chrome_paint.rs: replace hardcoded `compaction_reduction: None` with `compaction_reduction: sid.and_then(|s| store.compaction_reduction_for(s))`.
6. Type changes propagate to header.rs SessionHeader.compaction_reduction field type stays Option<i32>; build_right_line ALREADY uses `r.abs()` so any i32 sign is safe.

INTEGRATION TEST FIXTURE PLAN: spec file → spec/features/agentview-session-header-compaction-percentage.feature, test → codelet/fspec-tui/tests/agentview_session_header_compaction_percentage_rpc100.rs.
Use the shared helpers in tests/common/mod.rs (sid, build_app, render_into 80x24 ratatui::TestBackend) — same pattern as agentview_session_header_per_session_tokens_rpc099.rs.
Four scenarios:
• (a) >100% fill renders raw value: dispatch ContextFillUpdate{105} on s-1, render, scrape header line, assert contains `[105%]` not `[100%]`, assert span style fg=Red.
• (b) COMPACTED suffix renders after CompactionComplete: dispatch ContextFillUpdate{80} then CompactionComplete{ratio:0.4}, assert header contains `[80%: COMPACTED 60%]`.
• (c) compaction_reduction does not leak across sessions: dispatch CompactionComplete on s-1, dispatch nothing on s-2, render s-1 (`COMPACTED N%` present), Action::SessionNext → render s-2 (no `COMPACTED`), Action::SessionPrev → render s-1 (`COMPACTED N%` present again).
• (d) SessionStateChange→Cleared resets both: seed s-1 with tokens+fill+compaction, dispatch SessionStateChange{state:Cleared}, render, assert `[0%]`, no COMPACTED suffix, `tokens: 0↓ 0↑`.

RPC-100.description:
The Rust port's SessionHeader top-right `[X%]` (and post-compaction `[X%: COMPACTED Y%]`) badge does not match the TypeScript original. Three concrete gaps identified by DeepSearch into src/tui/ (TS) vs codelet/fspec-tui/src/ (Rust):

(1) CLAMP BUG: TokenState::apply_context_fill at codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/token_state.rs:63 clamps the wire value with `info.fill_percentage.min(100) as u8`. ContextFillInfo.fill_percentage is u32 and the TS comment at SessionHeader.tsx:101 explicitly says `Fill percentage (0-100+, can exceed 100 near compaction threshold)`. Clamping hides the >100% pre-compaction signal the user relies on to know compaction is imminent.

(2) COMPACTED SUFFIX DEAD CODE: chrome_paint::paint_header_and_role at codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/chrome_paint.rs:65 hardcodes `compaction_reduction: None`. RPC-099 left this gap deliberately. The TS reference (AgentView.tsx:959-979) stores `compactionReduction` from StreamChunk::CompactionComplete via `setCompactionReductionRef.current?.(Math.round(result.compressionRatio))` and SessionHeader.tsx:129-132 widens the bracket to `[fp%: COMPACTED N%]` when non-null. Rust dispatch_rpc045.rs:120-133 only formats a scrollback notice (via format_compaction_notice in dispatch_rpc020.rs:289) — the reduction value is never stored per-session for the header to read back.

(3) NO CLEARED-STATE RESET: TS AgentView.tsx:992-1006 resets contextFillPercentage to 0 on SessionStateChange→cleared via setContextFillPercentageRef.current(0). Rust has no such reset — TokenState lives in AgentViewStore::token_state_by_session and is only reset on /detach (reset_token_state via dispatch_rpc050.rs:89). When a session reaches a cleared state, the header keeps showing the last percentage.

FIX SCOPE: (a) Widen TokenState.context_fill_pct from u8 (clamped) to u16 (raw value preserved) — color band still works since context_fill_color falls into the >=85 red bucket for any value above 85. (b) Add `compaction_reduction_by_session: HashMap<SessionId, i32>` to AgentViewStore + a setter populated by dispatch_rpc045.rs CompactionComplete branch + a getter wired into chrome_paint.rs. (c) Wire reset_token_state into SessionStateChange→Cleared in dispatch_rpc045.rs (alongside the existing match). Integration test must drive Action::ChunkReceived(s, ContextFillUpdate{105}) + Action::ChunkReceived(s, CompactionComplete{ratio:0.4}) and assert the rendered header line text contains `[105%]` then `[N%: COMPACTED 60%]` after compaction settles.

examples.text: ContextFillUpdate with fill_percentage=105 arrives for session s-1. Render frame: header right-side text contains `tokens: ...↑ [105%]` rendered in red (>=85 bucket). Currently it shows `[100%]` due to the .min(100) clamp.

Session s-1: ContextFillUpdate{fill_percentage=80} then CompactionComplete{original_tokens=10000, compacted_tokens=4000, compression_ratio=0.4, turns_summarized=12}. Header right-side text contains `[80%: COMPACTED 60%]` — the 60 comes from round((1 - 0.4) * 100). Currently the COMPACTED suffix never appears.

Two sessions: s-1 (CompactionComplete with ratio 0.3 → reduction 70%) and s-2 (no compaction yet). Header for s-1 shows `[X%: COMPACTED 70%]`. Shift+Right to focus s-2 → header for s-2 shows `[X%]` only (no COMPACTED suffix — s-1's value did NOT leak).

Session s-1 has accumulated TokenUpdate{input:5000, output:1200}, ContextFillUpdate{fill_percentage=45}, and CompactionComplete{ratio:0.3}. Then SessionStateChange{state: Cleared} arrives. Next render: header shows `tokens: 0↓ 0↑` and `[0%]` (no COMPACTED suffix) — both TokenState and compaction_reduction were reset for that session.
Color verification: ContextFillUpdate{fill_percentage=105} for session s-1. The rendered `[105%]` span MUST have foreground style Color::Red (matches context_fill_color band `pct >= 85`).

Formula coherence: CompactionComplete{original_tokens=10000, compacted_tokens=4000, compression_ratio=0.4} → scrollback notice contains `60.0% reduction` AND header badge contains `COMPACTED 60%` — both derive from `(1 - 0.4) * 100 = 60`.

rules.text: TokenState.context_fill_pct MUST preserve the raw u32 fill_percentage from ContextFillInfo (widened to u16) — values >100 are valid and MUST render as `[105%]` etc. so the user sees pre-compaction overshoot. Currently `.min(100) as u8` discards this signal.

AgentViewStore MUST hold a per-session compaction_reduction value (HashMap<SessionId, i32> keyed by session) populated when StreamChunk::CompactionComplete arrives — mirrors TS AgentView.tsx:959-979 `setCompactionReductionRef.current?.(Math.round(result.compressionRatio))` (with the TS formula bug fixed: real formula is round((1.0 - compression_ratio) * 100)).

chrome_paint::paint_header_and_role MUST read the per-session compaction_reduction from the store and pass it as `Some(value)` into SessionHeader so build_right_line renders `[X%: COMPACTED Y%]` form — not hardcoded `None` as it is today at chrome_paint.rs:65.

The compaction_reduction value MUST be computed as `((1.0 - compaction_result.compression_ratio) * 100.0).round() as i32` — same formula as format_compaction_notice in dispatch_rpc020.rs:290, keeping notice text and badge suffix coherent.

When SessionStateChange { state: Cleared } arrives via dispatch_rpc045.rs, the per-session TokenState AND compaction_reduction entry MUST be reset (TokenState back to Default, compaction_reduction removed) so the header shows `[0%]` for a freshly-cleared session — mirrors TS AgentView.tsx:992-1006.
compaction_reduction is PER-SESSION: setting it on s-1 MUST NOT leak into s-2's header when the user cycles with Shift+Right (same per-session-storage invariant RPC-099 established for tokens).

Color band selection (context_fill_color) MUST continue to honour the 50/70/85 thresholds for the now-u16 percentage value — values >=85 (including 100+, e.g. 105%) MUST land in the red bucket; no separate band for >100%.

RPC-100.title: Session header compaction percentage not calculating/updating properly — clamp >100, missing COMPACTED suffix, no reset on session_state cleared

userStory.action: see the SessionHeader top-right [X%] badge accurately reflect the live context-fill percentage AND show the [X%: COMPACTED Y%] suffix immediately after a CompactionComplete event
userStory.benefit: I know when my session is approaching compaction (>=85% red) AND I get the same visual COMPACTED feedback the TypeScript original provides — without losing values >100% that signal pre-compaction state

architectureNotes.text: Rust impl: TokenState.context_threshold_tokens (u64), apply_context_fill caches threshold only when finite & >0, apply_token_tracker recomputes pct = round((input - floor(cache_read * 0.9)) / threshold * 100) and clamps to u16::MAX (not 100). See codelet/fspec-tui/src/store/agent_view/token_state.rs:26-125.

TS impl: AgentView.tsx uses `cachedContextThresholdRef = useRef<number>(0)` (line 1122). updateTokenStateFromChunk (1132-1175) recomputes on TokenUpdate when threshold>0 (lines 1142-1161) and caches threshold from ContextFillUpdate when incoming>0 (lines 1164-1173). Both session-restore sites (~3664 and ~4290) seed cachedContextThresholdRef.current from extractTokenStateFromChunks.contextThreshold.

ExtractedTokenState (src/tui/utils/tokenStateUtils.ts:38-53) gained `contextThreshold: number | null` field. extractTokenStateFromChunks (lines 66-105) surfaces last-ContextFillUpdate.threshold if finite & >0, else null. Used by AgentView restore paths to prime the recompute cache.

Wire format (codelet/napi/index.d.ts:2952-2957): ContextFillInfo { fillPercentage, effectiveTokens, threshold, contextWindow }. TS StreamChunk interface in AgentView.tsx:207-219 widened to expose threshold; TokenStateChunk interface in tokenStateUtils.ts:20-33 widened similarly. Older fixtures that only set fillPercentage remain backward compatible (threshold defaults to undefined → cache untouched).

Tests: 6 Rust unit tests in codelet/fspec-tui/tests/token_state_realtime_recompute_rpc101.rs (no-threshold guard, recompute-with-threshold, cache discount, backend override, overshoot, zero-threshold safety). 3 TS utility tests in src/tui/utils/__tests__/tokenStateUtils.test.ts:138-194. 4 TS integration tests in src/tui/__tests__/context-window-fill-percentage.test.tsx:536-671 (real-time recompute, no-threshold no-op, cache discount, backend override). All 13 RPC-101 tests pass.

Formula authority: emit_context_fill_from_usage in codelet/cli/src/interactive/stream_loop.rs:108-126 is the canonical source. TokenTracker::effective_tokens in codelet/core/src/compaction/model.rs:90-96 defines the 90% cache discount. Local recompute MUST match both — backend ContextFillUpdate always wins when it arrives.

RPC-101.description: The SessionHeader [X%] badge only updates on ContextFillUpdate StreamChunks. Both TS (src/tui/) and Rust (codelet/fspec-tui/) ignore context-fill on TokenUpdate chunks, even though TokenUpdate arrives at high cadence during streaming and carries the live input_tokens needed to compute the percentage. Two user-visible bugs: (1) badge appears frozen during streaming because backend emits TokenUpdate frequently but ContextFillUpdate only at end-of-turn; (2) ESC interrupt skips the final ContextFillUpdate, leaving stale percentage. ROOT CAUSE: TS AgentView.tsx:1112-1125 updateTokenStateFromChunk only calls setContextFillPercentage on ContextFillUpdate. Rust token_state.rs:42-50 apply_chunk routes TokenUpdate to apply_token_tracker which writes input/output/cache/reasoning/tps but not context_fill_pct. FIX: derive percentage on every TokenUpdate using threshold = contextWindow - min(maxOutput, 32000); fillPercentage = round((inputTokens / threshold) * 100). Same formula as calculateContextFillPercentage and the existing restore-path at AgentView.tsx:4253. Real ContextFillUpdate must still override derived value (backend authoritative). One card, two parallel fixes.

examples.text: After ContextFillUpdate{fill_percentage=10, threshold=100000}, two consecutive TokenUpdate{input_tokens=45000} then {input_tokens=90000} (no intervening ContextFillUpdate) update the badge to [45%] then [90%].
On a fresh session with no ContextFillUpdate yet received, a TokenUpdate{input_tokens=50000} MUST leave the badge at [0%] (no threshold to divide by).

After ContextFillUpdate{threshold=100000}, a TokenUpdate{input_tokens=50000, cache_read=20000} sets the badge to [32%] (effective=50000-(20000*0.9)=32000; 32000/100000=32%) — matches TokenTracker::effective_tokens.

After a locally-recomputed [50%], an authoritative ContextFillUpdate{fill_percentage=62} from the backend MUST overwrite the badge to [62%] while the cached threshold remains at 100000 for future TokenUpdates.
TokenUpdate{input_tokens=110000} against cached threshold=100000 sets badge to [110%] — overshoot preserved (NOT clamped to 100, matches RPC-100 invariant).

After ContextFillUpdate{threshold=100000}, a fixture-style ContextFillUpdate{fill_percentage=60, threshold=0.0} updates the badge to [60%] but MUST keep the cached threshold at 100000; a subsequent TokenUpdate{input_tokens=75000} correctly recomputes to [75%].

rules.text: TokenState (Rust) and AgentView (TS) MUST cache the context-fill threshold (in tokens) from every ContextFillUpdate; non-positive or non-finite thresholds MUST NOT wipe a previously-cached good value.

Every StreamChunk::TokenUpdate MUST recompute context_fill_pct locally using the cached threshold; when threshold == 0 the recompute MUST be skipped (no divide-by-zero, badge stays at last known value).

Local recompute MUST apply the 90% cache discount to cache_read_input_tokens (effective = input_tokens - floor(cache_read * 0.9)) so it matches TokenTracker::effective_tokens and the backend's emit_context_fill_from_usage formula.
An authoritative ContextFillUpdate from the backend MUST overwrite any locally-recomputed value (backend knows reasoning_tokens and other adjustments the local recompute does not model).
Overshoot above 100% MUST be preserved (RPC-100 invariant — pre-compaction overshoot is a user signal). The recompute MUST NOT clamp to 100.

Session restore (resume / Shift+Left|Right) MUST seed the threshold cache from extractTokenStateFromChunks().contextThreshold so live TokenUpdates immediately move the badge — without this, the badge freezes again after every session swap.
TokenState.context_threshold_tokens is per-session (lives inside the per-SessionId TokenState struct established by RPC-099) — setting it on s-1 MUST NOT affect s-2's badge.

architectureNotes.text: Rust ProviderSettingsView replaces `ProviderSettingsMode::Detail { sub: DetailSub }` with a flat `Vec<NavItem>` where `NavItemKind` enum has six variants: Provider{expanded}, Profile{profile_name}, AddProfile, ApiKey, OAuthLogin{method,label}, OAuthStatus{label}. architectureNotes.text: Wire-type extension design: ProviderCredentialInfo in codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs:391-401 gains two new fields keeping Option<String> shape because napi(object) does not support discriminated enums (existing credential_type at L397-399 uses the same convention). Backwards-compatible: older clients ignore None fields, serde defaults Option to None on missing JSON keys. The masking helper lives in codelet/providers/src/credentials.rs as `pub fn mask_api_key(&str) -> String` — single source of truth across all transports, called by the codelet-providers credential-detection path before the data crosses the wire

Cross-transport parity contract: extend codelet/fspec-tui/tests/rpc054_cross_transport_parity.rs so the same env-seeded ANTHROPIC_API_KEY surfaces the same masked_key 'sk-ant-••••mnop' AND the same source 'env' through BOTH embedded and websocket transports. Masking happens server-side inside codelet-providers BEFORE the wire boundary — never on the client — so the bytes of the raw key never leave the manager process. The view layer (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/list.rs) just renders whatever masked_key + source comes off the wire

rules.text: Masking helper follows the TS contract at src/utils/credentials.ts:277-291: keys shorter than 12 chars return the literal '••••••••'; otherwise the helper matches one of 5 known prefixes (sk-ant-, sk-, gsk_, AIza, xai-) in that declaration order, falls back to first-6-chars when no prefix matches, then appends '••••••••' + last-4-chars

Prefix matching order is significant: 'sk-ant-' MUST be tested BEFORE 'sk-' because both would match an Anthropic key 'sk-ant-XXXX'; the Rust port iterates the prefix slice in TS regex declaration order [sk-ant-, sk-, gsk_, AIza, xai-] and stops at the first match

ProviderCredentialInfo (codelet/rpc-types/src/lib.rs:393-401) gains two new optional fields: masked_key: Option<String> populated via mask_api_key() when the credential is api-key+configured, None otherwise; source: Option<String> tagged with one of 'explicit' | 'file' | 'env' | 'dotenv' matching TS ProviderConfigResult.source at src/utils/credentials.ts:56-59

Source tag is determined by credential-detection order in codelet/providers/src/credentials.rs mirroring src/utils/credentials.ts getProviderConfig L219-266: 'file' when the credential came from ~/.fspec/credentials/credentials.json (TS L232); 'env' when from process.env (TS L243); 'dotenv' when parsed from .env in cwd (TS L260); 'explicit' when caller-supplied

OAuth-type providers (anthropic, codex, github-copilot) do NOT use mask_api_key — their masked_key field stays None and the TUI renders the literal 'OAuth' string from the view layer (mirrors TS useProviderSettingsState.ts:289, 302, 315). The wire ProviderCredentialInfo never carries OAuth token bytes — masking would not be reversible/safe

architectureNotes.text: Implementation: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/mod.rs — add `pub test_result: Option<ProviderTestResult>` field on `ProviderSettingsView` (default None in `new()`); add `pub fn set_test_result(&mut self, provider_id: impl Into<String>, status: ProviderTestStatus)` and `pub fn clear_test_result(&mut self)`. Define `ProviderTestResult { pub provider_id: String, pub status: ProviderTestStatus }` and `pub enum ProviderTestStatus { Testing, Ok { latency_ms: u32 }, Err { message: String } }` — derive Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq. Re-export both from `mod.rs`.

Render integration: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/list_nav_render.rs — `render_nav_items` checks `view.test_result` for each Provider row. If `test_result.provider_id == item.provider_id`, after the existing `render_row` call, paint the test-result span on top of the row's color band. Decoration column = end-of-label column returned from a refactored `render_row` (change render_row return type from `()` to `u16` representing the column AFTER the last painted label cell — 18 existing RPC-104 callers ignore return value, no test changes required). Decoration style: foreground from ProviderTestStatus::span_color (Cyan/Green/Red), background from the row's existing band style (selected ? tint : Reset). Use `buf.set_stringn(end_x, y, &decoration_text, remaining_width, decoration_style)`. Skip painting if `end_x >= row_area.x + row_area.width` (no space left).

Decoration text + color: introduce `ProviderTestStatus::decoration(&self) -> (String, Color)` returning ('Testing…', Cyan) | (format!('✓ ok ({n}ms)'), Green) | (format!('✗ {m}'), Red). Mirrors the existing `DetailStatus::to_span()` for the Testing/TestOk/TestErr variants (status_text.rs L28-37) bytes-for-bytes. Prefix the decoration with a single ASCII space when painting so the visible row reads 'Label ✓ ok (Nms)'.

TS reference: src/tui/components/ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx renders testResult inline as `<Text color={color}> {symbol} {text}</Text>` immediately after the provider row label inside the same `<Box>` row. testResult lives on the panel-level state (`useProviderSettingsState.ts` testResult field, set by handleTestProviderConnection). The TS implementation scopes testResult to the row that triggered the test via provider_id matching — the same contract this card ports.

Test plan: codelet/fspec-tui/tests/provider_settings_test_result_inline_rpc158.rs with one #[test] fn per scenario. Helpers: `view_with_two_providers()` builds a List-mode view containing OpenAI + Anthropic ProviderDisplayInfo; `render_to_buffer(view) -> Buffer` invokes `view.render(area, &mut buf)` against a fixed Rect. Buffer assertion helper `row_contains(buf, row_idx, needle) -> bool` walks one buffer row symbol-by-symbol and looks for substring. Color assertion helper `cell_fg(buf, x, y) -> Color`.

Downstream wiring (out of scope for RPC-158): the backend test_provider_connection round-trip plumbed in `dispatch.rs` already routes its result to `DetailStatus`. A follow-up card or thin patch under RPC-054 epic will switch that wiring to call `view.set_test_result(...)` instead. RPC-158's exclusive contract is the field + methods + render integration. The legacy Detail::Summary path (status_text.rs DetailStatus) remains untouched so any current callers continue to compile.

The current Rust impl shows testResult only inside Detail::Summary, which is being removed (RPC-103). Port the inline rendering: when a connection test completes, the result decoration appears on the focused row in list mode. References: src/tui/components/ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx (testResult prop, inline render around L600+); src/tui/hooks/useProviderSettingsState.ts (testResult state).

rules.text: ProviderSettingsView carries a public field test_result: Option<ProviderTestResult> with ProviderTestResult { provider_id: String, status: ProviderTestStatus }
ProviderTestStatus has exactly three variants: Testing, Ok { latency_ms: u32 }, Err { message: String } — mirroring the TS testResult discriminated union
ProviderSettingsView exposes set_test_result(provider_id, status) and clear_test_result() public methods so backend round-trips and RPC-159 navigation handlers can drive the field
test_result is None for newly-constructed (Default) views — no decoration is rendered until set_test_result is called

List-mode rendering injects the test result inline ONLY on the Provider header row (RowKind::Provider) whose provider_id matches test_result.provider_id — Profile, ApiKey, OAuthLogin, OAuthStatus and AddProfile rows never render the decoration

Inline decoration text follows the TS visual contract: Testing → 'Testing…' (U+2026 ellipsis) in cyan; Ok{latency_ms} → '✓ ok (Nms)' in green; Err{message} → '✗ <message>' in red — text bytes-for-bytes identical to status_text::DetailStatus rendering

Decoration foreground (cyan/green/red) is independent of the row's selection band — the selection band still extends across the full row width and the decoration text inherits the band's background while using its own foreground color
Decoration is appended after the row's label separated by a single ASCII space — final visible label is e.g. 'OpenAI API ✓ ok (42ms)'
If test_result.provider_id does not match any provider currently in the nav-item flat tree, no decoration is rendered anywhere — silent no-op, no panic
set_test_result is last-write-wins — a second call with the same or different provider_id overrides the prior status with no merging
Both set_test_result and clear_test_result are PURE state mutations — they never touch selected_index, scroll_offset, mode, filter, filter_mode, expanded, nav_items, or status

architectureNotes.text: Implementation: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/mod.rs adds a new variant `ProviderSettingsEvent::SwitchToModels` next to `Consumed`/`Ignored`/`Emit(Action)`/`Close`. list.rs::handle_list_key inserts a new arm `KeyCode::Tab => ProviderSettingsEvent::SwitchToModels` BEFORE the catch-all `_ => Consumed`. Filter-mode Tab continues to fall through handle_filter_key's catch-all (Consumed) because filter_mode is checked first.

Callers downstream of ProviderSettingsView::handle_key — currently the Navigator in codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/* — need a new match arm for `ProviderSettingsEvent::SwitchToModels`. For this card we add the variant and prove handle_key emits it; wiring into the actual model-settings view transition belongs to Navigator-layer follow-up if not already in place. Search call sites for `ProviderSettingsEvent::Close` to find equivalent handling locations.

TS reference: src/tui/inputHandlers/listModeHandler.ts lines 57-60 — `if (key.tab) { onSwitchToModels(); return; }`. The callback is invoked as a sibling of `onClose()` and returns immediately, so any subsequent navigation logic is skipped. Position the Rust Tab arm anywhere AFTER Esc and BEFORE the catch-all — order within the match is functionally irrelevant since Tab does not overlap any other arm's KeyCode.

Test file convention: `codelet/fspec-tui/tests/provider_settings_tab_switch_to_models_rpc160.rs` with one #[test] fn per scenario, helper `view_with_n_providers(n: usize)` to build deterministic List-mode state. Reuse helpers from `provider_settings_view_rpc054.rs` where possible. Each test maps to one Gherkin scenario via the @step comment convention.

Navigator wiring: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/navigator.rs::handle_provider_settings_event adds an arm `ProviderSettingsEvent::SwitchToModels => EventResult::consumed()` so the new variant compiles. The actual Navigator-to-models-view transition (Action::OpenModelSettingsView or similar) is deferred to a follow-up card — no such Action exists today, and creating one without a consumer view is dead code. RPC-160's contract is exclusively that handle_key returns SwitchToModels on Tab; downstream wiring is a separate concern.

RPC-160.description: TS provider settings binds Tab in list mode to switch the right-pane view to the models list (src/tui/inputHandlers/listModeHandler.ts — onSwitchToModels callback). The Rust port must bind Tab in list mode to a new ProviderSettingsEvent::SwitchToModels which Navigator translates to the equivalent model-settings view transition. Footer hint already advertises 'Tab: Switch to models' per RPC-106 — this card wires the actual binding.

Regression guard: pressing Up, then Tab, then Down — Up moves cursor to clamped position, Tab emits SwitchToModels without affecting cursor, Down moves cursor by 1. All three events return their expected variants in order.

rules.text: Pressing Tab in List mode emits a new ProviderSettingsEvent::SwitchToModels variant — distinct from Consumed/Close/Emit/Ignored — which the caller (Navigator) translates into the models-view transition. Adding this variant is part of the contract.

Tab MUST NOT emit any Action — SwitchToModels is a pure UI navigation event, not a backend command. The TS reference calls `onSwitchToModels()` as a sibling of `onClose()`, never dispatching a Redux action.
Tab in List mode MUST NOT mutate selected_index, scroll_offset, filter, filter_mode, mode, or any other view state — it is a pure event emission.

Tab is only bound in List mode. Tab in Detail mode (Summary / EditApiKey / OAuthNotice) and Tab while in delete-confirm dialog remain unbound and follow their pre-existing behaviour (e.g., focus cycling in ConfirmDialog). RPC-160 only changes List-mode Tab handling.

Tab in filter sub-mode (when filter_mode == true) MUST NOT trigger SwitchToModels — it continues to be consumed silently as a no-op via the catch-all arm so typing into the filter is not interrupted. TS parity: TS Tab is only checked at the top-level list mode, not within the filter input.

architectureNotes.text: Architecture: Add a private helper `fn is_printable_ascii(c: char) -> bool { (32u32..=126).contains(&(c as u32)) }` at the top of codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/detail.rs (or in a tiny sibling helper module if cleaner). Modify the `KeyCode::Char(c) =>` arm of `handle_edit_key` (currently lines 135-146) to wrap the `draft.push(c)` and the validation-clearing branch inside `if is_printable_ascii(c) { ... }`. If the char is dropped, still emit ProviderSettingsEvent::Consumed and re-enter the same Detail::EditApiKey { draft } mode unchanged (mirrors the existing `_ =>` fall-through pattern, but keeps the buffer unchanged). This isolates RPC-161 to ~10 lines under list.rs' 300 LoC ceiling cousin (detail.rs is currently 233 lines).

Test plan: New integration test file codelet/fspec-tui/tests/provider_settings_api_key_charset_rpc161.rs driving ProviderSettingsView::handle_key with KeyCode::Char(c) at the boundary and interior of the printable range (' ', 'A', '~') plus representative dropped chars ('\t', '\x1F', '\x7F', 'é', '✓', '🔑'). Inline rust unit test at the bottom of detail.rs covers is_printable_ascii() directly for branch coverage. All tests have @step comments matching the Gherkin scenarios. Total ~9 integration scenarios + 1 unit test = ~10 tests.

RPC-161.description: TS API-key edit form uses filterPrintableChars() (src/tui/utils/filterPrintableChars.ts) to allow ONLY ASCII 32-126 printable characters into the draft buffer — control chars, escape sequences, and non-ASCII bytes are dropped silently. The current Rust impl accepts any KeyEvent::Char which lets non-ASCII/control bytes leak into the API key string. Port filterPrintableChars to Rust: a helper `fn is_printable_ascii(c: char) -> bool { (32u32..=126).contains(&(c as u32)) }` filters every char-event before push.

is_printable_ascii() unit-tested directly: returns true for ' ' (32), 'A' (65), '~' (126); returns false for '\t' (9), 31, 127, 'é' (233), '🔑' (128017)

rules.text: A char event is appended to the EditApiKey draft IFF its char code lies in the inclusive range 32..=126 (TS filterPrintableChars at src/tui/utils/providerSettingsHelpers.ts:39-47); any char outside that range is silently dropped — no draft mutation, no status text, no event/Action emitted, ProviderSettingsEvent::Consumed is still returned so the key is swallowed

The filter is enforced at the KeyCode::Char(c) arm of handle_edit_key in codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/detail.rs — NOT at the list-mode filter arm, NOT at Backspace/Enter/Esc paths (those keep their existing behaviour unchanged)
Space (U+0020 / decimal 32) and tilde (U+007E / decimal 126) are the inclusive boundaries — both MUST be accepted as draft characters (regression guards against off-by-one)

Common dropped categories that must be regression-tested: ASCII control chars (0..=31, e.g. \t = 9, \n = 10, ESC = 27, US = 31), DEL (127), and any non-ASCII char with code > 127 (e.g. 'é' = U+00E9, '✓' = U+2713, emoji '🔑' = U+1F511)

Dropping a char never clears the 'API key cannot be empty' validation status — only an ACCEPTED printable char clears that status (preserves existing line 142-144 behaviour scoped to accepted characters only)

The filter is implemented as a free function `pub(super) fn is_printable_ascii(c: char) -> bool { let code = c as u32; (32..=126).contains(&code) }` in codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/provider_settings/detail.rs (or a sibling helper module) so it can be unit-tested in isolation

Esc arm now sets view.mode = ProviderSettingsMode::List (was Detail::Summary { last_status: None }). Enter arm with non-empty draft now sets view.mode = ProviderSettingsMode::List before emitting Action::SaveProviderCredentials (was Detail::Summary { SavingCredentials }). The DetailSub::Summary variant and DetailStatus enum remain untouched for legacy callers and existing tests.

TS reference: src/tui/components/ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx — the editApiKey form's Enter handler returns silently when draft is empty (no validation chip rendered). On successful save, the form closes and the panel returns to the provider list (Ink unmounts the form node and re-renders the list). No "summary" intermediate view exists in TS.

Test impact: codelet/fspec-tui/tests/provider_settings_view_rpc054.rs contains pre-existing tests that pin the OLD Esc→Summary and Enter→Summary { SavingCredentials } behavior (lines 285, 448). Those scenarios must be deleted from spec/features/rpc054-provider-settings-view.feature and their test bodies removed from provider_settings_view_rpc054.rs as part of this card — they are superseded by the new RPC-162 scenarios.

RPC-162.description: TS API-key edit form treats Enter with an empty draft as a silent cancel — it closes the form and returns to list view without dispatching a save action and without showing inline validation text (src/tui/components/ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx editApiKey form handler). The current Rust impl shows 'API key cannot be empty' inline and stays in EditApiKey mode (RPC-054 rule [9], example [15]). Drop the inline validation: empty-Enter cancels silently. NOTE: This card also removes the Detail::Summary view (replaced by inline list rendering per RPC-103/RPC-158) so the cancel returns to list mode, not Summary. The t (test connection) keybind that lived in Detail::Summary moves to list mode in a separate card (or is dropped if TS does not bind t in list mode — see RPC-157).

The current Rust impl binds only KeyCode::Backspace. Add KeyCode::Delete as a second binding mapping to the same pop-last-char action. Minor parity tweak.

architectureNotes.text: TS reference: src/tui/inputHandlers/deleteConfirmModeHandler.ts handleConfirmation() function — 'y' || 'Y' → onConfirm; 'n' || 'N' || Esc → onCancel. Visible UI hint: 'Press y to confirm, n or Esc to cancel' (ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx lines 198, 225, 251).

Rust implementation site: codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/confirm_dialog.rs ConfirmDialog::handle_key() (line 139-160). Insert two new match arms BEFORE the catch-all `_ => Ignored`: KeyCode::Char('y') | KeyCode::Char('Y') => self.outcome_for_index(0) which yields Primary; KeyCode::Char('n') | KeyCode::Char('N') => self.outcome_for_index(self.cancel_index()) which yields Cancel.
The existing modifier-guard at the top of handle_key (`if mods.contains(CONTROL) || mods.contains(ALT) → Ignored`) already covers y/Y/n/N with modifiers — no extra guard required for Rule 4.

ConfirmDialog is shared by two callers: ProviderSettingsView (delete provider credentials) and ResumeSessionView (delete session). Both benefit equally from this parity addition; no caller-side changes required since both already destructure Primary/Cancel outcomes.
MergeConfirmDialog (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/merge_confirm_dialog.rs) is a SEPARATE component with its own enum and is NOT covered by this work unit. Out of scope.

RPC-164.description: TS delete-confirm dialog binds 'n' / 'N' as a shortcut to the Cancel/Secondary action (src/tui/components/ProviderSettingsPanel.tsx ConfirmDialog handler — y/n binary). The current Rust ConfirmDialog (codelet/fspec-tui/src/views/agent/confirm_dialog.rs) accepts Esc and Tab+Enter on Secondary but does NOT bind n/N as a fast-path cancel. Add n/N → ConfirmDialogOutcome::Cancel so users can press n to close the delete-credentials dialog. Mirror y/Y → Primary if not already bound (audit confirm_dialog.rs first).

rules.text: Pressing 'y' or 'Y' (no Ctrl/Alt modifiers) in a ConfirmDialog emits ConfirmDialogOutcome::Primary — identical to Enter on the Primary button
Pressing 'n' or 'N' (no Ctrl/Alt modifiers) in a ConfirmDialog emits ConfirmDialogOutcome::Cancel — identical to Esc or to Enter on the Cancel button
y/Y/n/N shortcuts ignore the currently focused button — focus state is NOT consulted and NOT mutated by the shortcut
y/Y/n/N with CONTROL or ALT modifiers return ConfirmDialogOutcome::Ignored (same pre-existing guard already applied to all other keys)
On a 3-button dialog (Primary, Secondary, Cancel), 'n'/'N' still emits Cancel — never Secondary — because 'n' is wired to the cancel-index outcome path
All pre-existing keybinds (Esc → Cancel, Left/Right/Tab → focus navigation, Enter → focused outcome) remain unchanged
Other printable characters (e.g., 'q', 'a', 'd') continue to return ConfirmDialogOutcome::Ignored — only y/Y/n/N gain new meaning

RSPEC-001.description: Create new 'rspec' command that performs reverse ACDD by decomposing/reverse engineering existing applications. The command discovers user stories, personas, and acceptance criteria from existing code. Extends the /fspec slash command to tell Claude to read fspec.md and continue with reverse engineering workflow.

examples.text: Skeleton test file header includes: /** Feature: spec/features/[name].feature\n * This test validates acceptance criteria. Tests map to Gherkin scenarios.\n */
User runs /rspec in Claude Code → AI reads .claude/commands/rspec.md → First line says 'fully read fspec.md' (with link) → AI follows fspec workflow while reverse engineering
User story map created as Mermaid diagram in foundation.json architectureDiagrams array with section='User Story Map'

Reverse engineered Express.js app: creates epic 'api-management', prefix 'API', work units API-001 'User authentication', API-002 'Data validation', feature files with inferred scenarios, skeleton tests with describe/it blocks (no implementation)

rules.text: Must identify user personas who interact with the system
Must identify high-level activities or goals users achieve with the software
Must break down high-level activities into smaller specific tasks or interactions that code supports

Analysis involves: (1) analyzing functionality and mapping to user goals, (2) examining UI elements/features/workflows, (3) grouping related features into epics/journeys, (4) decomposing into individual user stories
Must produce user story map organized visually along user journey (broad activities at top, detailed interactions underneath)
User stories must be expressed as user-centric narratives (As a [persona], I want [goal], So that [benefit])
fspec init must install rspec.md slash command (similar to how it installs fspec.md)

rules.text: When a schedule triggers and its previous run is still active, the overlap_policy field determines behavior: 'skip' silently skips, 'queue' enqueues for later
Default overlap_policy is 'skip' when not specified in the schedule entry
Active run detection uses an in-memory HashMap<String, Uuid> mapping schedule_name to session_id, checked before each trigger
When MAX_SESSIONS (10) is reached, scheduled jobs are deferred to a FIFO queue and retried each 30-second tick
Overlap check happens BEFORE session limit check — skip policy prevents attempting to spawn at all
Only ONE deferred or queued job is spawned per tick to prevent burst-spawning
Completion detection uses poll-on-tick: each 30s tick checks if active_runs session IDs are still present in SessionManager
Queued jobs (overlap=queue) wait for the SAME schedule's previous run to complete; deferred jobs wait for ANY session slot to open
Shell jobs don't occupy session slots (they use tokio::process::Command, not BackgroundSession), so session limit only applies to agent jobs

rules.text: On scheduler startup, each active schedule is checked: if lastRunAt < previous cron trigger time, fire at most ONE catch-up run
At most one catch-up per schedule — never replay multiple missed triggers regardless of downtime duration
Schedules with lastRunAt=null that have a cron trigger due in the past get one catch-up fire
Paused schedules are skipped during catch-up — only active schedules are checked
Catch-up runs ONCE before the regular 30-second tick loop begins
Catch-up jobs respect overlap policy and MAX_SESSIONS — they use the same SchedulerState as regular jobs
lastRunAt is updated immediately when catch-up fires (prevents double-fire on the first regular tick)

SCHED-011.description: Add a /loop slash command as a natural-language shorthand for creating recurring schedules. The user types '/loop 5m check deployment status' and the system parses the interval + prompt, converts to a cron expression, and creates a recurring schedule with sensible defaults (auto-expiry after 3 days, overlap: skip). This is syntactic sugar over the /schedule add infrastructure (SCHED-008) and the Schedule AI tool (SCHED-009) — it doesn't add new scheduling capabilities, just a faster UX path for the most common case: 'run this prompt every N minutes/hours'.

examples.text: User types '/loop 5m check deployment status' → interval parsed as 5m, cron='*/5 * * * *', prompt='check deployment status' — TUI confirms 'Scheduled every 5 minutes [job: a1b2c3d4]'
User types '/loop check the build' (no interval) → defaults to 10m, cron='*/10 * * * *', prompt='check the build'
User types '/loop check build status every 2 hours' → trailing 'every 2h' parsed, cron='0 */2 * * *', prompt='check build status'
User types '/loop 30s run health check' → 30s rounds up to 1m, cron='*/1 * * * *', TUI confirms 'Scheduled every 1 minute (rounded from 30s)'
User types '/loop 20m /review-pr 1234' → slash command chaining, every 20 minutes the scheduler sends '/review-pr 1234' as the prompt to the subordinate session
User types '/loop cancel a1b2c3d4' → the session-scoped schedule with that ID is removed and TUI confirms 'Cancelled loop a1b2c3d4'
User types '/loop list' → sees table of all active session-scoped loops with ID, prompt, interval, next fire time, time remaining until expiry
User exits fspec and restarts → all /loop schedules are gone (session-scoped), while /schedule add entries persist and resume

rules.text: /loop creates session-scoped schedules — not persisted to spec/schedules.json, lost when fspec exits (matches Claude Code behavior)
Interval parsing is deterministic (no LLM round-trip) — supports leading token (5m, 2h), trailing 'every N unit' clause, and default 10m fallback
Supported time units: s (seconds, rounds up to nearest minute), m (minutes), h (hours), d (days)
Session-scoped schedules auto-expire after 3 days — prevents forgotten loops from running indefinitely
Default overlap policy is 'skip' — if previous run still active, skip this trigger
/loop jobs are agent sessions (not shell commands) — the prompt is sent to a subordinate agent session via AgentManager
/loop returns an 8-character job ID used for cancellation via '/loop cancel <id>'
The prompt in /loop can itself be a slash command (e.g., '/loop 20m /review-pr 1234') — chaining is supported
Session-scoped schedules count toward MAX_SESSIONS (10) — same limit as persistent schedules

SCHED-012.description: Add a persistent job log for scheduled task executions. Every time the scheduler triggers, completes, fails, skips, or defers a job, append a structured log entry to spec/schedule-log.jsonl. This gives visibility into what the scheduler has been doing without requiring a bridge connection. The log file should be added to .gitignore since it's local runtime state, not project specification. The log should use JSONL format (one JSON object per line) for easy tailing/grep and include fields like timestamp, event type (triggered/completed/failed/skipped/deferred), schedule name, job type (agent/shell), duration, exit code (shell), error message, and session ID (agent). Consider log rotation or max-size truncation to prevent unbounded growth.

examples.text: Scheduler triggers 'daily-sync' agent job → appends {"timestamp":"2026-03-18T10:00:00Z","event":"triggered","schedule":"daily-sync","jobType":"agent","sessionId":"abc-123"} to spec/schedule-log.jsonl
Agent job completes → appends entry with event='completed', duration_ms=3200, sessionId
Shell job fails with exit code 1 → appends entry with event='failed', exitCode=1, error='npm ERR! missing script: sync'
Overlap policy=skip causes a job to be skipped → appends entry with event='skipped', message='Previous run still active'
Session limit reached for agent job → appends entry with event='deferred', message='10/10 sessions active'
Log has 2001 entries → rotation kicks in, file is truncated to most recent 1000 entries
Log file write fails due to permissions → scheduler continues normally, tracing::warn emitted, no crash
Overlap policy=queue causes a job to be queued → appends entry with event='queued'

rules.text: Log file is spec/schedule-log.jsonl — JSONL format, one JSON object per line, append-only
spec/schedule-log.jsonl must be in .gitignore — it's local runtime state, not project specification
Every scheduler lifecycle event is logged: triggered, completed, failed, skipped, deferred, queued
Each log entry includes: timestamp (ISO 8601), event type, schedule name, job type (agent/shell), and optional fields: duration_ms, exit_code (shell), error message, session_id (agent)
Log rotation: truncate to most recent 1000 entries when file exceeds 2000 entries — prevents unbounded growth
Log writes must be non-blocking — append to file asynchronously, never delay the scheduler tick
If the log file cannot be written (permissions, disk full), log a warning via tracing but never crash the scheduler

SCHED-013.description: Replace the polling-based loop evaluation (tied to the 30s cron tick) with per-entry spawned tokio tasks. Each /loop entry gets its own task that sleeps for exactly its interval, checks session idle, and fires — giving true sub-second resolution without coupling to the cron engine.

examples.text: User runs `/loop 5s check status` → task spawns, prompt fires after exactly 5 seconds, then every 5 seconds thereafter
User runs `/loop 1s heartbeat` → prompt fires every 1 second (minimum allowed interval)
User cancels loop via `/loop cancel <id>` → task stops immediately, no further firings
Session is busy when loop interval elapses → loop skips that tick, tries again after the next interval
Session is destroyed while loop is active → loop task self-terminates, no orphaned tasks
Cron schedules at 30s tick continue working identically — no regression

rules.text: Each /loop entry spawns its own tokio task that sleeps for exactly the configured interval — no shared polling tick
Cancelling a loop aborts its spawned task (JoinHandle::abort) — no lingering timers
Loop tasks skip firing when the session is busy (not idle) — same skip policy as before, no queuing
Loop tasks auto-terminate when the session is destroyed or the entry expires
The cron engine tick (30s) is untouched — only /loop evaluation is decoupled from it
evaluate_and_fire_loops() is removed from the engine tick — loops are fully self-managed
LoopStore stores JoinHandle alongside LoopEntry — cancel/remove operations abort the handle
Minimum interval is 1 second (enforced at registration) — prevents accidental tight loops

SCHED-014.description: When multiple /loop entries target the same session, a high-frequency loop can starve lower-frequency loops because each loop task independently races to fire when the session becomes idle (TOCTOU race, first-to-wake wins, no coordination). Introduce a centralized per-session loop dispatcher that receives enqueued prompts from loop tasks and drains them fairly (round-robin or starvation-ratio priority) — modeled on the cron engine's proven queue/drain pattern.

architectureNotes.text: Current Implementation: src/utils/scenario-similarity.ts uses Levenshtein distance (character-level edit distance) with 70/30 weighted scoring (title vs steps). Has 7 critical bugs and achieves only 60% accuracy.

Proposed Hybrid Algorithm: Combine 5 algorithms with weighted scoring - Jaro-Winkler (30% - title matching), Token Set Ratio (25% - word reordering), Gherkin Structural (20% - Given/When/Then awareness), Trigram Similarity (15% - fuzzy matching), Jaccard Similarity (10% - keyword overlap). Expected 88% accuracy.

Bug Fixes Required: (1) Division by zero for empty strings/keywords, (2) Strip Gherkin keywords before comparison, (3) Include numbers in keyword regex for technical terms, (4) Fix keyword extraction for match objects, (5) Remove redundant lowercasing, (6) Handle step reordering, (7) Support partial step matching.

Performance: All Phase 1+2 algorithms have no external dependencies and run in O(n*m) time or better. For large codebases (100+ scenarios), consider two-stage matching: (1) Fast keyword filtering, (2) Full similarity only on candidates.

Test Coverage: Must cover empty strings, empty steps, empty keywords, special characters, numbers in terms (OAuth2/SHA256), short titles, reordered steps, partial matches, typos, and performance with 100+ scenarios. See src/commands/__tests__/scenario-deduplication.test.ts

References: (1) spec/attachments/SPEC-003/SIMILARITY_ANALYSIS.md - Bug analysis and test gaps, (2) spec/attachments/SPEC-003/ALGORITHM_ANALYSIS.md - Algorithm comparison and implementation guide, (3) Jaro-Winkler, Token Set Ratio, Trigram algorithms ~200 lines total with no dependencies

TOKEN-001.description:
When stream_loop/gemini_continuation/recovery_compaction build an ApiTokenUsage to pass into TokenTracker::update_from_usage, they hardcode 0 for the output_tokens argument of ApiTokenUsage::new. Because TokenTracker::update_from_usage accumulates billing as `cumulative_billed_output += usage.output_tokens`, this means cumulative_billed_output NEVER increments across the session. The cumulative display output (second arg) is correctly set on session.token_tracker.output_tokens, but the raw per-turn billing accumulator is broken.

Call sites (4):
- codelet/cli/src/interactive/stream_loop.rs:1808  (main turn finalization)
- codelet/cli/src/interactive/gemini_continuation.rs:324 (Gemini continuation normal completion)
- codelet/cli/src/interactive/gemini_continuation.rs:427 (update_token_tracker helper)
- codelet/cli/src/interactive/recovery_compaction.rs:189 (CMPCT-024 flush on cancel)

Fix: compute per-turn delta = current.output_tokens - session.token_tracker.output_tokens (saturating_sub) and pass that as the output_tokens arg to ApiTokenUsage::new. The second cumulative_output arg continues to carry the cumulative display value.

examples.text: A session with two sequential turns (turn1 emits 100 output, turn2 emits 120 output) ends with cumulative_billed_output = 220 rather than 0
All four call sites use the same centralized helper — grep for saturating_sub(…output_tokens) should find only one call site in production code
A stream that reports a lower cumulative output (display tick-back) does NOT cause cumulative_billed_output to decrease and does NOT panic on underflow

rules.text: All ApiTokenUsage::new() calls that feed TokenTracker::update_from_usage must pass a real per-turn output_tokens delta instead of literal 0
The per-turn delta is computed as saturating_sub(current_cumulative_output, session.token_tracker.output_tokens) so it is always non-negative even when the display ticks backwards
The delta computation is centralized in a single TokenTracker helper to satisfy DRY across all four call sites

TOKEN-001.title: Fix cumulative_billed_output never incrementing — all update_from_usage call sites pass output_tokens=0

userStory.action: have accurate cumulative output-token billing
userStory.benefit: I can monitor per-session token spend

TOKEN-002.description:
Review of TOKEN-001 surfaced a gap: the integration test only exercises ONE of the four call sites (flush_partial_state_before_compaction in recovery_compaction.rs). The other three sites are only protected by a static source-grep assertion that counts `compute_output_delta(` occurrences — a regression where a caller calls the helper but still passes 0 to ApiTokenUsage::new would silently pass.

Add focused tests that exercise each of the remaining three call sites:
- codelet/cli/src/interactive/stream_loop.rs — main turn finalization (~line 1806-1813)
- codelet/cli/src/interactive/gemini_continuation.rs — normal completion (~line 322-329)
- codelet/cli/src/interactive/gemini_continuation.rs — update_token_tracker helper (~line 430-437)

Construct each scenario: fresh tracker at output_tokens=X, simulate a turn reporting cumulative output X+N, assert cumulative_billed_output incremented by N.

Also: remove the redundant safety net in TokenTracker::update_from_usage (line 162: `self.output_tokens.max(cumulative_output)` clamp). The compute_output_delta helper already handles the tick-back case via saturating_sub — two layers mean a regression in either layer goes undetected. Pin compute_output_delta as the single source of truth.

Also update the feature file's architecture doc string to match the actual ApiTokenUsage::new signature (4 args, not 5 — the cumulative_output is passed to update_from_usage, not to ApiTokenUsage::new).

architectureNotes.text: Three-layer architecture: Provider Facades → Tool Adapter Layer → Base Implementation. ToolFacade trait with provider(), tool_name(), definition(), map_params(). ProviderToolRegistry for facade lookup. Located in codelet/tools/src/facade/. Integrates with existing provider implementations in codelet/providers/.

TOOL-001.description: Implement a facade pattern for tools that presents provider-specific interfaces while sharing a common implementation. Different LLM providers (Claude, Gemini, OpenAI) expect different tool schemas, names, and parameter formats. This story creates an abstraction layer that maps provider-specific tool calls to shared implementations.

examples.text: Claude web search: provider sends {action: {type: 'search', query: 'rust async'}} → facade maps to InternalParams::Search{query: 'rust async'} → base tool executes search
Gemini web search: provider sends {query: 'rust async'} to 'google_web_search' tool → facade maps to InternalParams::Search{query: 'rust async'} → same base tool executes
Gemini URL fetch: provider sends {prompt: 'https://example.com summarize'} to 'web_fetch' tool → facade extracts URL and maps to InternalParams::OpenPage{url: 'https://example.com'}
Registry lookup: tools_for_provider('gemini') returns [GeminiGoogleWebSearchFacade, GeminiWebFetchFacade, GeminiReadFileFacade, ...] but NOT Claude facades
Tool definition for Gemini: google_web_search sends schema {type: 'object', properties: {query: {type: 'string'}}, required: ['query']} - flat structure, no oneOf
Tool definition for Claude: web_search sends schema with oneOf containing search/open_page/find_in_page action variants - Claude handles complex schemas well

rules.text: Each tool facade MUST implement the ToolFacade trait with provider(), tool_name(), definition(), and map_params() methods
Provider-specific parameters MUST be mapped to internal parameters through the facade before tool execution
A single internal tool MAY have multiple facades for a provider (e.g., Gemini has google_web_search AND web_fetch for our web_search)
Tool definitions MUST use JSON Schema format that the target provider understands (no oneOf for Gemini)

Tool definitions sent to the provider API MUST use the provider's expected schema format, tool names, and parameter structures (e.g., Gemini gets 'google_web_search' with flat {query} schema, not 'web_search' with nested action objects)
Base tool implementations MUST remain unchanged - only facades adapt the interface
ProviderToolRegistry MUST return only facades registered for the requested provider

TOOL-012.description:
The Fspec and Bridge tools intermittently fail with 'handler not configured' because they rely on thread-local 'current session' state to look up handlers. This is fundamentally broken:

1. Thread-local state can be polluted by other sessions
2. The 'current' session concept doesn't survive async boundaries reliably
3. Claude Code CLI doesn't set up thread-local state at all

**Root Cause:**
Tools try to discover their session at call time via `get_current_fspec_session()` instead of knowing it at construction time.

**Solution:**
Tool wrappers should be constructed WITH their session ID. The session_id becomes a field on the wrapper struct, passed to registration functions like `claude_fspec_tool(session_id)`. At call time, the tool uses `self.session_id` directly instead of looking up thread-local state.

This eliminates all reliance on 'current session' thread-local storage and makes session association explicit and deterministic.

examples.text: Session manager creates claude_fspec_tool(session_id) → wrapper stores session_id → call() uses self.session_id → correct handler found
Tool call crosses async boundary → self.session_id still valid → handler lookup succeeds (thread-local would fail)
Two sessions A and B each create their own tool instances → A's tool uses A's handler, B's tool uses B's handler → no cross-contamination

Claude Code CLI scenario: Agent built once at startup → no session context at creation time → Current architecture fails. New architecture: CLI must create session_id UUID before building agent, pass to create_rig_agent().

Watcher session A monitors parent session B: A has its own Fspec tool (session_id=A), B has its own Fspec tool (session_id=B). When A's tool is called, handler for A is used. When B's tool is called, handler for B is used. No confusion possible.

TOOL-013.description:
The Bash tool currently inherits its working directory from the parent fspec process. When fspec manages multiple parallel sessions with different git worktrees, each session needs to run commands in its own worktree. Currently, agents must prefix every command with 'cd /path/to/worktree &&' which is error-prone and verbose.

Add an optional 'cwd' parameter to the Bash tool that uses Rust's std::process::Command::current_dir() to set the child process working directory before spawning.

examples.text: Agent calls Bash with cwd='/path/to/worktree' and command='pwd' → output shows '/path/to/worktree'
Agent calls Bash without cwd parameter → command runs in fspec's working directory (backward compatible)

rules.text: The cwd parameter is optional - if not provided, the tool behaves as before (inherits parent working directory)
When cwd is provided, use std::process::Command::current_dir() to set the child process working directory
If cwd path does not exist, return an error before executing the command

TOOL-014.description:
Currently only BashTool requires session_id. All other tools (ReadTool, WriteTool, EditTool, GrepTool, GlobTool, LsTool, AstGrepTool, AstGrepRefactorTool, WebSearchTool, FspecTool, BridgeTool) use parameterless new() constructors. This means file operations in isolated sessions may read/write from the wrong directory.

All tools must require session_id in their constructor so they can look up effective_cwd via get_effective_cwd(session_id) and operate in the correct worktree directory for isolated sessions.

TOOL-015.description:
The CodexProvider currently registers Claude-style tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Ls) but the GPT-5.1-codex model is trained on Codex CLI's native tool names and schemas (shell_command, read_file, list_dir, grep_files, apply_patch, view_image, update_plan). This causes suboptimal tool usage because the model doesn't recognize our tool names.

Create Codex-specific facade wrappers following the existing facade pattern (see Gemini/Z.AI facades) that present Codex-native tool interfaces while mapping to our shared internal implementations.

Tool mapping required:
- Bash → shell_command (command, workdir, timeout_ms params)
- Read → read_file (file_path, offset, limit, mode, indentation params)
- Ls → list_dir (dir_path, offset, limit, depth params)
- Grep → grep_files (pattern, include, path, limit params)
- Edit/Write → keep as-is initially, consider apply_patch later
- Glob → no Codex equivalent, keep our Glob tool
- AstGrep/AstGrepRefactor → no Codex equivalent, keep our tools
- WebSearch → use native web_search ToolSpec type (not a function tool)
- Fspec → already has OpenAIFspecFacade, reuse for Codex
- Bridge → already has OpenAIBridgeFacade, reuse for Codex

Reference: /tmp/codex-cli/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec.rs
Research: spec/attachments/TOOL-001/codex-tool-facade-research.md

examples.text: Codex model calls shell_command with {command: 'ls -la', workdir: '/tmp'} → CodexShellCommandFacade maps to InternalBashParams::Execute{command: 'ls -la'} with cwd='/tmp' → BashTool executes

Codex model calls read_file with {file_path: '/src/main.rs', offset: 10, limit: 50} → CodexReadFileFacade maps to InternalFileParams::Read{file_path: '/src/main.rs', offset: Some(10), limit: Some(50)} → ReadTool executes
Codex model calls list_dir with {dir_path: '/src', depth: 2} → CodexListDirFacade maps to InternalLsParams::List{path: Some('/src')} → LsTool executes
Codex model calls grep_files with {pattern: 'TODO', include: '*.rs', path: '/src'} → CodexGrepFilesFacade maps to InternalSearchParams::Grep{pattern: 'TODO', path: Some('/src')} → GrepTool executes

Tool names MUST match Codex CLI exactly: shell_command, read_file, list_dir, grep_files (not shell, readFile, ls, etc.)
Parameter schemas MUST match Codex CLI definitions from codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec.rs (e.g., read_file uses file_path not path, list_dir uses dir_path not path)
Tools without a Codex equivalent (Glob, AstGrep, AstGrepRefactor, Write, Edit) MUST be kept with current naming since Codex has no native equivalent
CodexProvider::create_rig_agent() MUST use FacadeToolWrapper for tools with Codex equivalents, replacing direct tool registration

The tool uses action-based dispatch: run spawns processes, write/poll interact with running sessions, list/close manage sessions. ProcessStore is a global static behind Arc<Mutex<>>. BashTool remains unchanged for direct Claude usage; providers that need session management use UnifiedExecTool via facades.

New facade trait ExecToolFacade in codelet/tools/src/facade/traits.rs with InternalExecParams enum (Run, Write, Poll, List, Close variants). ExecToolFacadeWrapper in wrapper.rs delegates to UnifiedExecTool. Codex facades (BUG-114, BUG-115) implement ExecToolFacade to map exec_command/write_stdin/shell to the internal params. Current BashToolFacade and BashToolFacadeWrapper remain untouched.

TOOL-016.description:
Create a provider-agnostic unified exec tool that supports PTY session management, following VTCode's architecture. Instead of separate tools per provider, build a single unified tool with action-based dispatch that all providers can use.

The unified exec tool consolidates:
- Shell command execution (run action)
- PTY session creation with yield-and-resume (run with tty=true)
- Interactive stdin writing to live sessions (write action)
- Output polling from running sessions (poll action)
- Session listing (list action)
- Session cleanup (close action)

This replaces the current BashTool's one-shot execution model with a session-aware architecture. Each execution either completes immediately (returning exit_code) or yields control back to the LLM with a session_id for follow-up interaction.

Key components:
- ProcessStore: HashMap of session_id → (child_process, stdin_sender, stdout_buffer) with LRU eviction
- Output buffering with configurable yield_time_ms and max_output_tokens
- Background exit watchers for cleanup
- PTY spawning for interactive sessions (tty=true)
- Pipe-mode for non-interactive commands (default)

Reference: VTCode vtcode-core/src/tools/registry/builtins.rs (unified_exec)
Reference: Codex codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs

examples.text: Agent runs 'ls -la' with default settings → process exits immediately → returns exit_code: 0, output: file listing, no session_id (backward compatible with BashTool)
Agent runs 'python3' with tty=true → process stays running → returns session_id: 'abc123', no exit_code, output: Python prompt text
Agent calls write action with session_id='abc123', input='print(42)\n' → returns output: '42\n', session_id still present (process alive)
Agent calls write with input='exit()\n' → Python exits → returns exit_code: 0, no session_id, output includes exit message
Agent calls poll on a running session → returns any new output since last read, session_id still present
Agent calls list action → returns array of active sessions with their session_ids and metadata
Agent calls close with session_id → process is killed, session removed from ProcessStore, returns confirmation
65th process spawned when store is full → LRU eviction kills least recently used session (not in top 8 recent), new process takes its slot
Agent runs ['ls', '-la'] as argv array → execvp-style execution without shell interpretation (no glob expansion)
Agent runs 'sleep 300' with yield_time_ms=2000 → after 2 seconds, returns session_id (process still running), output may be empty
Agent runs command with yield_time_ms=50 → clamped to 250ms minimum, process given at least 250ms to produce output

rules.text: The unified exec tool MUST support five actions: run, write, poll, list, close dispatched via an action parameter
The run action spawns a process (PTY if tty=true, pipe otherwise), collects output for yield_time_ms, and returns exit_code if exited or session_id if still running
The write action sends input bytes to a running session's stdin and polls for output, returning new output plus session status
The poll action checks for new output from a running session without sending input, with a higher minimum wait time (5000ms)
ProcessStore MUST enforce a max of 64 concurrent processes with LRU eviction protecting the 8 most recently used sessions
Yield time MUST be clamped: min 250ms, max 30000ms, default 10000ms; poll/empty-write uses min 5000ms
Output buffer per session MUST be capped at 1 MiB (UNIFIED_EXEC_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES)
When tty=false (default) and process exits within yield_time_ms, behavior MUST be identical to current BashTool one-shot execution for backward compatibility
Background reaper tasks MUST watch for process exit and clean up ProcessStore entries automatically
The command parameter MUST accept both string (shell command) and array of strings (argv for execvp-style) forms
The tool MUST respect session isolation via effective_cwd lookup (TOOL-014 pattern) for workdir resolution
The tool MUST check commands against the blocklist before execution (same as current BashTool)

TOOL-016.title: Unified Exec Tool with PTY Session Management

userStory.action: execute commands with session management including PTY support and yield-and-resume patterns
userStory.benefit: interactive long-running processes can be controlled across multiple tool calls

architectureNotes.text: Create codelet/tools/src/request_user_input.rs following the InjectSummaryTool pattern: HitlHandler type alias (Arc<dyn Fn(Uuid, HitlRequest) -> Result<HitlResponse, String> + Send + Sync>), global HITL_HANDLERS: RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, HitlHandler>>, pub fn set_hitl_handler/has_hitl_handler/execute_hitl/clear_all_hitl_handlers, and RequestUserInputTool implementing rig::tool::Tool

HitlRequest contains: questions: Vec<HitlQuestion>. HitlQuestion contains: id: String, header: String, question: String, options: Option<Vec<HitlOption>>. HitlOption contains: label: String, description: String. HitlResponse is an enum: Answered { answers: HashMap<String, HitlAnswer> } | Cancelled. HitlAnswer contains: selected: Vec<String>, other: Option<String>.

The tool schema presented to the LLM uses the exact JSON schema from the attachment (questions array with id/header/question/options). The tool is registered as 'request_user_input' for all providers. BUG-116 creates the Codex-specific facade wrapper separately.

TOOL-017.description:
Create a provider-agnostic human-in-the-loop (HITL) tool that allows any LLM to request structured user input mid-turn, following VTCode's architecture.

The tool pauses the agent loop, presents a structured question form to the user via the TUI, and resumes with the user's answers.

Schema:
- questions: Array of 1-3 questions
  - id: String (snake_case) - stable answer identifier
  - header: String (≤12 chars) - short UI label
  - question: String - single-sentence prompt
  - options: Optional array of 2-3 mutually exclusive choices
    - label: String - user-facing label (1-5 words)
    - description: String - one sentence explaining impact

Implementation uses the block-on-oneshot pattern:
1. Handler creates a oneshot channel
2. Sends a pause/input-request event to the TUI
3. Awaits the response (agent loop is suspended)
4. TUI renders a modal/wizard with options + freeform text
5. User responds, oneshot resolves, handler returns answers to LLM

Integrates with existing PauseHandler infrastructure in codelet/tools/src/tool_pause.rs.

Mode-gated: only available when TUI is present and interactive. Returns error in headless/non-interactive mode.

Reference: VTCode vtcode-core/src/tools/request_user_input.rs (declaration)
Reference: VTCode src/agent/runloop/unified/request_user_input/modal.rs (TUI execution)
Reference: Codex codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input.rs

examples.text: Agent calls request_user_input with two questions (each with options) → handler blocks → TUI renders modal → user selects options and adds freeform text → tool returns answers with selected labels and other text
Agent calls request_user_input in headless mode (no handler registered) → tool immediately returns error message about unavailable session mode
Agent sends question with header 'This Is Too Long' (15 chars) → validation rejects with error about header length exceeding 12 characters
Agent sends question with id 'camelCase' → validation rejects because id must be snake_case
User cancels the modal without answering → tool returns {cancelled: true}
Agent sends 4 questions → validation rejects because maxItems is 3
Agent sends question with 1 option → validation rejects because minItems for options is 2
Agent sends question without options (just freeform) → tool accepts it, TUI shows only freeform input for that question, response has empty selected array and populated other field
set_hitl_handler registers handler for session → has_hitl_handler returns true → clear_all_hitl_handlers removes all → has_hitl_handler returns false

rules.text: The tool MUST accept a questions array (1-3 items) where each question has id (snake_case), header (≤12 chars), question (single sentence), and optional options (2-3 mutually exclusive choices with label and description)
The tool MUST use the per-session handler pattern (like InjectSummaryHandler, SessionSearchHandler, FspecHandler) with a global RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, Handler>> registry
The handler MUST block the tool call (synchronously) until the TUI sends back the user's answers, following the same blocking pattern as pause_for_user
Mode-gated: when no HITL handler is registered for the session (headless/non-interactive), return error 'request_user_input is unavailable in the current session mode'
Response MUST return JSON with answers keyed by question id, each containing selected (array of chosen labels) and optional other (freeform text)
Cancellation MUST return JSON with cancelled: true instead of answers

Validation MUST reject: empty questions array, questions with empty id/header/question, header longer than 12 chars, id not in snake_case, fewer than 2 or more than 3 options per question, more than 3 questions
The tool module MUST live in codelet/tools/src/request_user_input.rs following the established single-file handler pattern (like inject_summary.rs)
The tool MUST NOT depend on PauseHandler - it uses its own separate handler type (HitlHandler) to avoid mixing structured question/answer data with the simple continue/confirm pause semantics
The tool MUST be registered in lib.rs with pub use exports and in facade/mod.rs for facade support

userStory.benefit: make informed decisions based on user preferences without guessing

architectureNotes.text: Changes are entirely in the TUI layer — InputTransition rendering and useHitlInput hook. No changes to the Rust request_user_input.rs tool definition, HitlRequest/HitlResponse types, NAPI bindings, or tool schema. The 'Other...' is a virtual UI-only option.

useHitlInput hook needs a new state: isOtherActive (boolean). When true, the current question renders MultiLineInput instead of the option list. Escape while isOtherActive sets it back to false (returns to option list). Enter on the 'Other...' option index sets isOtherActive to true.

InputTransition rendering: when hasOptions is true, map options to display items and append { label: 'Other...', description: '' } as the last entry. The 'Other...' entry uses dim/italic chalk styling. The selectedOption index wraps around length+1 (options count + 1 for Other).

TOOL-018.description: When request_user_input presents a question with predefined options (2-3 choices), the user currently MUST pick one — there is no way to provide a different answer. Add an 'Other' option that, when selected, opens a freeform text input so the user can type a custom response when none of the predefined choices are appropriate.

examples.text: AI asks 'Which approach?' with options [A, B, C] — TUI renders: ○ A, ○ B, ○ C, ○ Other... (dim) — user navigates to 'Other...', presses Enter, types 'I want approach D which combines A and C', presses Enter — answer returned as { selected: [], other: 'I want approach D which combines A and C' }

AI asks 'Which approach?' with options [A, B] — user navigates to 'Other...', presses Enter, sees freeform input — then presses Escape — returns to the option list with ○ A, ○ B, ○ Other... — selects 'A' instead and presses Enter — answer returned as { selected: ['A'] }

User selects 'Other...' on question 1 of 2, types a response, presses Enter — advances to question 2 which also has options — user picks a predefined option on question 2 — both answers submitted together, question 1 has { selected: [], other: 'custom text' } and question 2 has { selected: ['Option B'] }

User selects 'Other...', presses Enter, sees freeform input, presses Enter with empty text — sees inline hint 'Please type a response or press Esc to go back' — cursor stays in freeform input, not advanced
Question has no options (freeform-only) — no 'Other...' is appended because the entire question is already freeform — behavior unchanged from current implementation

rules.text: When a question has predefined options, the TUI MUST append an 'Other...' entry at the bottom of the option list that the user can select with ↑/↓ like any other option

Selecting 'Other...' and pressing Enter MUST transition the current question from option-selection mode to freeform text input mode — reusing the same MultiLineInput component already used for freeform-only questions
When the user submits via 'Other...', the answer shape MUST be { selected: [], other: "user typed text" } — same shape as a freeform-only question, so the LLM receives a consistent response format
Pressing Escape while in the freeform text input (after selecting 'Other...') MUST go back to the option list for that question — NOT cancel the entire HITL flow
The 'Other...' option is TUI-only — no schema changes to the tool definition or Rust types. The LLM still sends 2-3 options; the TUI appends the virtual 'Other...' entry at render time
The 'Other...' entry MUST be visually distinct from LLM-provided options — rendered in dim/italic text to indicate it's a fallback, not one of the suggested choices
Empty freeform submission (user hits Enter on blank text after selecting Other) MUST be rejected — show inline hint 'Please type a response or press Esc to go back'

architectureNotes.text: New crate codelet/fspec-core is the future home of the Rust port; this work creates the empty skeleton with stub command modules and a single dispatcher entry point
Dispatcher signature: fn dispatch_command(name: &str, args_json: &str, project_root: &Path) -> FspecResult — pure synchronous fn called from the registered FspecHandler closure

Each command stub file follows the template: pub async fn run(args: &str, ctx: &Context) -> Result<String, FspecCoreError> { Err(FspecCoreError::NotYetPorted { command: "add-rule", work_unit: "RPC-XXX" }) }

Command-name-to-stub mapping uses a static const phf::Map<&'static str, StubFn> or an exhaustive match arm. Phase 1 just maps name → (command, work_unit_id) for the canonical error message; future ports replace the stub with the real implementation.

Child cards under RPC-003 share the epic 'rust-cli-port' and follow naming pattern 'Port <command> command to Rust'. Description references TS source file path and approximate LOC. Estimate based on rpc-003-feasibility.md complexity tiers: trivial (1-2pts), thin-wrapper (2-3pts), top-15 algorithmic (5-13pts).

Source of truth for command list: src/cli/program.ts registerXxxCommand calls + actual .command('name') strings in each command file. 162 commands identified (see grep output and program.ts inspection).

The dispatcher INSIDE codelet_fspec_core decides whether to use the existing chunk-callback path (NAPI present) or serve the stub (NAPI absent). The closure no longer contains the is_global_chunk_callback_registered() branch — it lives one level deeper.
