TOOL-019.description: FspecTool::call (codelet/tools/src/fspec.rs:88-108) always returns Err(ToolError::Execution) because it requires a JS callback (execute_with_js_callback). In the NAPI-free fspec binary there is no JS shell. Since the LLM eagerly picks the Fspec tool on the first turn for almost any prompt, every conversation hangs after the tool_use stream completes: rig dispatches Fspec.call(...), gets an error, and the stream loop never emits Done. Fix: implement direct in-process dispatch — FspecTool::call should route to the same command-execution surface that the tarpc server uses (via Arc<SharedFspecService> or a dyn FspecExecutor trait passed at construction).

The standalone fspec binary cannot execute TypeScript fspec commands.'}, agent loop completes the turn, LLM sees the error and adapts

TOOLS-001.title: Add Multimodal Content Support to Read Tool

userStory.action: read images and PDFs visually in the conversation
userStory.benefit: I can discuss visual content, screenshots, and documents without leaving the agent

architectureNotes.text: VISUAL MODE: Uses pdfium-render crate (Rust wrapper for Google Pdfium C++ library). Renders pages via PdfPage::render_with_config() at 150 DPI to PdfBitmap, converts to image::DynamicImage, encodes as PNG base64. Returns array of {page_number, data, media_type} objects.

TEXT MODE: Uses lopdf crate (pure Rust). Loads via Document::load_mem(), iterates pages with get_pages(), extracts text with extract_text(&[page_num]). Returns paginated string with '--- Page N ---' separators. Already implemented in pdf.rs.

IMAGES MODE: Uses lopdf crate. Iterates PDF objects looking for XObject streams with /Subtype /Image. Extracts raw image bytes, determines format from /Filter (DCTDecode=JPEG, FlateDecode+decode=PNG). Returns array of {data, media_type, width, height} objects.

ENCRYPTION DETECTION: Check raw bytes for /Encrypt dictionary marker BEFORE lopdf parsing. Also check Document::is_encrypted() after load. Return PdfError::Encrypted early to avoid parsing errors on encrypted content streams.

API DESIGN: ReadArgs gains optional pdf_mode: Option<String> field. Values: 'visual' (default), 'text', 'images'. Invalid values fall back to visual. Output varies by mode: visual/images return JSON array of image objects, text returns paginated string.

DEPENDENCY: pdfium-render requires Pdfium C library. Use pdfium-render with 'static' feature to bundle Pdfium, or 'dynamic' to link at runtime. Consider platform-specific builds (pdfium-render supports Linux, macOS, Windows, WASM).

TUI-060.description:
Session header displays work unit ID and status with realtime updates using proper Zustand architecture.

## Architecture Requirements

### Source of Truth
- **Rust session state** is the source of truth for session information (model, work unit ID, status)
- **work-units.json** via singleton Rust watcher (notify crate) updates the board display

### Data Flow
1. Rust session state → AgentView sync effect → sessionStore updated
2. work-units.json → Rust file watcher (BoardView ONLY) → fspecStore.loadData()
3. SessionHeader subscribes to sessionStore directly (NO props for dynamic state)

### Key Constraints
- ONE singleton Rust file watcher for work-units.json at BoardView level
- AgentView does NOT create its own watcher
- SessionHeader uses Zustand hooks, not props, for work unit info

Remove 8 slash commands that are abandoned stubs, speculative NAPI-006 features never adopted by users, or redundant with existing UI.

TUI-078.description: When mouse tracking (?1000h) is active, the terminal hands all mouse button events to the app, which breaks native text selection. The fix: on button-down events (buttonByte 32-34), temporarily disable mouse tracking so the terminal handles the drag natively, then re-enable on button-release (35) or after a 5000ms fallback timeout. Scroll wheel events (96-99) are unaffected and keep working throughout.

Scroll wheel events (96–99) are always handled normally and never trigger ?1000l — the 5000ms fallback window only applies to button-down events

TUI-079.description:
When work-units.json is modified (e.g. by an AI agent changing a work unit status via Fspec tool), the BoardView fails to fully reflect the changes. Work unit ordering within columns is wrong, the last-changed indicator never moves, new attachments don't appear, and deleted work units remain as ghosts. Root cause: TUI-060 moved the file watcher to globalStreamListener which calls updateWorkUnitsFromWatcher() instead of loadData(), losing ordering, stateHistory, attachments, and deletion information.

Additional finding (Gap 8): When the currently-attached work unit is deleted externally, globalStreamListener's session sync logic (lines 68-86) does not clear sessionStore.currentWorkUnitId. The session header continues showing the deleted work unit. This must also be handled — after loadData() completes, if the current work unit no longer exists in the store, session context should be cleared.

architectureNotes.text: Rust footer poller: ONLY call get_current_branch (reads .git/HEAD). Remove get_staged_files, get_unstaged_files, get_untracked_files calls entirely. The FooterStateUpdate chunk drops dirty/untracked fields. TypeScript SessionFooter drops formatBranchDisplay dirty/untracked params.
The footerStore Zustand interface drops git.dirty and git.untracked fields. The SessionFooter formatBranchDisplay function simplifies to just [⎇ branch-name] with no indicators.

Use SessionRegistry<String> in codelet_tools crate to store 'last known CWD' per session (keyed by session UUID). BashTool writes to it after resolve_cwd(). This follows the exact same pattern as BASH_ABORT_FLAGS (BUG-129), TOOL_PROGRESS_CALLBACKS (BUG-126), and PAUSE_HANDLERS (BUG-127) — all per-session globals in the tools crate.

The footer poller (spawn_footer_poller in session_manager.rs) stops using a frozen captured CWD. Instead, each tick reads from the SessionRegistry to get the latest CWD. If the CWD changed since last tick, it recomputes display_path (HOME→~), re-checks git branch for the NEW path, and emits a FooterStateUpdate. Max latency: 5 seconds (existing poll interval).

The SessionRegistry is in codelet_tools — but the footer poller is in codelet_napi (session_manager.rs). codelet_napi already depends on codelet_tools, so it CAN read from the registry directly. The data flow is: BashTool (tools crate) writes → SessionRegistry (tools crate) stores → footer poller (napi crate) reads. No new callback type needed.
Cleanup: SessionRegistry entry must be removed in destroy_session() to prevent memory leaks — same pattern as unregister_bash_abort_flag(session_id).

Initial value: When session is created, seed the registry with the session's effective_cwd (worktree_path or project root). This ensures the footer shows something immediately before any Bash commands run.

When resolve_cwd() returns None (no isolation, no explicit cwd), BashTool writes std::env::current_dir() (the process CWD — typically the project root) to the registry. This ensures the footer always reflects the ACTUAL directory the command ran in, not a stale value from a previous invocation.

VAL-006.description:
src/commands/validate-tags.ts prints '✓ All tags in <file> are registered' for every passing file by default. With ~3000 feature files, every call returns a ~3000-line tool_result which bloats chat_history and triggers PromptCancelled on the next LLM turn. Compaction drops the bloat but the retry often re-invokes validate-tags during DAG rebuild, producing a new bloated tool_result and cascading PromptCancelled up to MAX_COMPACTION_RETRIES=3 → 'Retry error after compaction: PromptCancelled'.

FIX — flip the default. By default, validate-tags prints ONLY failures and the summary counts. Add two opt-in flags for callers who want more/less:
  --verbose  : restore old behaviour (print one ✓ line per passing file)
  --summary  : print ONLY the final count lines (no per-file output at all)
When --summary and --verbose are combined, --summary wins (stricter/quieter flag dominates).

Breaking change scope is tiny: any script that greps 'validate-tags' output for '✓ All tags in ' must now pass --verbose. Documented in help text and release notes.

Running `fspec validate-tags` with no flags and 2 failing files out of 3000 prints exactly 2 ✗ violation blocks plus '✓ 2998 files passed' and '✗ 2 files have tag violations' — no ✓ per-file lines
Running `fspec validate-tags --verbose` on 3 all-valid feature files prints 3 lines starting with '✓ All tags in ' plus the summary line '✓ 3 files passed'
Running `fspec validate-tags --summary` with 2 failing files prints exactly two lines: '✓ 2998 files passed' and '✗ 2 files have tag violations' — no ✓ per-file lines, no ✗ violation blocks
Running `fspec validate-tags spec/features/foo.feature` on a single valid file produces no output (just exit 0) — because there are no failures, no summary is needed for a single file
Running `fspec validate-tags --summary --verbose` with 1 failing file behaves like --summary alone: prints only the two summary count lines, exits 1

rules.text: Exit code behavior unchanged: 0 when all valid, 1 when any invalid, 2 on error — regardless of output flags
Default behavior: print ONLY ✗ violation blocks plus the final summary counts. No per-file ✓ lines are printed by default.
Passing the --verbose flag restores the old behavior: print one ✓ line per passing file plus every ✗ violation block plus the summary
Passing the --summary flag suppresses all per-file output (both ✓ and ✗ blocks) and prints only the final summary counts
Exit code behavior unchanged: 0 when all valid, 1 when any invalid, 2 on unexpected error, regardless of output flags
When --summary and --verbose are both passed, --summary wins (summary is the quietest output, so the stricter flag always dominates)

architectureNotes.text: Root cause analysis: fspec implementation uses panzoom.zoomToPoint() method which doesn't correctly implement zoom-to-cursor behavior. Mindstrike manually calculates viewport offset using formula: newX = viewport.x + (mouseX - viewport.x) * (1 - zoomRatio). This keeps the point under the cursor fixed during zoom. Current implementation passes clientX/clientY to panzoom but library's zoomToPoint doesn't work as expected.

Trackpad jitter cause: Trackpads send many rapid scroll events with tiny deltaY values. Each event triggers immediate zoom state change. Solution: implement debouncing or accumulate deltas over short time window (e.g., 16ms) before applying zoom. Mindstrike may benefit from ReactFlow's internal smoothing.

Implementation approach: Replace panzoom.zoomToPoint() call with manual viewport calculation matching mindstrike's MindMap.tsx lines 1004-1012. Get panzoom's current pan/zoom state, calculate new state with zoom-to-point formula, then apply with panzoom.zoom() and panzoom.pan() separately.

VIEW-002.description: The fullscreen mermaid diagram viewer zoom feature has two critical issues: 1) Zoom does not zoom FROM the mouse position (should keep point under cursor fixed), 2) Trackpad scrolling causes jitter instead of smooth zoom. The implementation relies on panzoom.zoomToPoint() which doesn't match mindstrike's working manual zoom-to-point formula. Trackpad events need debouncing/smoothing.

User positions mouse at center of diagram, scrolls up with mouse wheel, diagram zooms in and point under cursor stays fixed (correct behavior like mindstrike)
User scrolls with trackpad (vertical two-finger swipe), diagram jitters rapidly instead of smooth zoom (many tiny deltaY events cause rapid state changes)
User scrolls with trackpad (horizontal two-finger swipe), diagram pans smoothly left/right (deltaX events work correctly)
User scrolls mouse wheel down, diagram zooms out centered on cursor position (same zoom-to-point formula applies)

rules.text: Zoom must be centered on cursor position (point under cursor stays fixed during zoom)
Mouse wheel events must use deltaMode to correctly calculate zoom delta (supports LINE=1, PAGE=2, PIXEL=0 modes)
Trackpad scroll events must be smoothed/debounced to prevent jittering from rapid tiny deltas
Horizontal scroll (deltaX) must always pan left/right regardless of pan mode
Manual zoom-to-point calculation: newX = viewport.x + (mouseX - viewport.x) * (1 - zoomRatio)

WATCH-001.description: Enable AI 'watcher' sessions that observe a parent session's streaming output in real-time, evaluate against a watching brief, and can inject messages into the parent session. This is the foundational MVP story with child stories for full implementation.

examples.text: User types /watcher, sees 'Watchers for: Main Dev Session (0 watchers)', presses N, configures 'Security Reviewer' with Supervisor authority

User selects message in parent pane (left), corresponding observation highlights in watcher pane (right)
User types /parent in watcher session, switches back to the parent session

rules.text: A watcher session is a fully interactive AI agent with its own LLM connection that observes a parent session
Watchers observe everything from the parent: user input, assistant responses, tool calls, and tool results
Watchers have autonomy over their own context management - they decide what to keep/discard from observations
A watcher has a 'watching brief' that defines what to watch for and when to interject
Each session (parent or watcher) has a defined role with authority level (Supervisor or Peer)
Multiple watchers can observe the same parent session, each with different roles
One watcher can only watch one parent (1:1 relationship from watcher side)
Watcher sessions are ephemeral - watch relationships do not persist across session restarts
Watchers connect to parent via tokio broadcast channel within the same process
Watcher evaluations occur at natural breakpoints: Done, ToolResult, Error, Interrupted chunks
Watcher injections are sent as User messages with structured prefix: [WATCHER: role | Authority: level | Session: id]
Watcher input is displayed in purple (magenta) text in the UI, with the watcher's role name as prefix
The /watcher command opens a Watcher Management overlay for CRUD operations on watchers
Shift+Left/Right in a watcher session navigates between sibling watchers (same parent only)
Watcher sessions display a split view: left pane (parent observation), right pane (watcher conversation)
Cross-pane selection highlighting uses correlation IDs to link parent chunks with watcher observations

Watcher can be in one of three states: Idle (waiting), Observing (accumulating), Processing (running agent)

This matches the architecture intent where the structured format is specifically for evaluation decisions. If user-initiated injection is needed later, add an explicit /inject command as a separate feature.

WATCH-024.description: Rename the entire watcher system terminology from parent/watcher to subordinate/supervisor, replace WatchGraph with ChainOfCommand, and remove the RoleAuthority enum. A subordinate is the session doing the work. A supervisor observes and interjects. The brief field provides all the behavioral instruction — no artificial authority levels needed. Relationships are dynamic (can change at any time) and a subordinate can have multiple supervisors. This is a pure refactoring — no new functionality, just clearer naming that matches the actual architecture.
